title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Unveils Bipartisan Back-to-School Agenda for AI in K-12 Education
text:
AI is a Tool, Not a Replacement for Critical Thinking

New Bipartisan Legislation will Help K-12 Schools Build AI Labs, Train Teachers, Keep Jersey Students Ahead of Curve

Emphasizes Importance of Screen Time Limits In School

Above: Gottheimer announces Bipartisan Back-to-School Agenda on AI and Screen Time in K-12 Education.

RIDGEWOOD, N.J. — Today, September 4, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the House Commission on Artificial Intelligence and the Innovation Economy, unveiled a comprehensive, bipartisan back-to-school agenda to make sure students in the Fifth District and across the country are prepared for a world increasingly shaped by AI. Speaking at George Washington Middle School, Gottheimer announced his new bipartisan AI LABS Act, co-led by Congressman Jay Obernolte (CA-23), to help K-12 schools build dedicated AI labs and train teachers — and paired it with a broader push to keep phones out of the classroom, protect New Jersey’s phone-free schools resources, boost AI literacy in the classroom, and close the digital divide so no community gets left offline.

Watch full remarks here.

“We’re not going to pretend AI doesn’t exist, and we’re not going to ban it and hope it goes away. So, here in Jersey, we need to do this differently,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “AI can be a powerful tool, but it can never replace the fundamentals. Give our schools the tools. Give our teachers the training. And give our children a real head start, instead of a false choice between banning technology outright and drowning in it.”

AI is already reshaping how students study, how teachers plan, and how employers hire, but K-12 schools have unequal access to the tools and curricula students need to learn how to use it responsibly. The bipartisan AI LABS Act tackles that gap head-on.

This legislation directs the Department of Education to create a new federal grant program or make resources from existing grant programs available to help K-12 schools establish dedicated AI labs, much like the computer and typing labs that became a fixture in schools a generation ago. Those labs would give students hands-on curricula on how to use and understand AI, help teachers better understand the technology, and incorporate it into their classrooms. The bill also directs the Department to study who receives the resources, how they are used, and to make recommendations on future investment so students and educators stay ahead on AI education.

Alongside the AI LABS Act, Gottheimer announced additional steps in his AI back-to-school agenda:

Protecting New Jersey’s phone-free schools resources. Gottheimer is sending a letter to Governor Mikie Sherrill and New Jersey Commissioner of Education Dr. Lily Laux that emphasizes the importance of the state’s Phone-Free Schools Grant Program. Public school districts across Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex counties — including eleven here in the Fifth District — received grants to go bell-to-bell phone-free this year.

Boosting AI education in New Jersey. Gottheimer is calling on the State to dedicate K-12 resources specifically to responsibly integrate AI literacy, ethics, and practical skills into K-12 public school curriculum while limiting screen time to ensure fundamentals remain a priority in education.

Keeping phones out of the classroom. Gottheimer is supporting the bipartisan UNPLUGGED Act, introduced by Representatives Eugene Vindman (VA-7) and Jen Kiggans (VA-2), which supports state and local policies that keep personal electronic devices out of the classroom during school hours. It also establishes a Department of Education grant program to help schools purchase secure lock boxes and pouches, with commonsense exceptions for students with medical needs, disabilities, and English learners.

Ensuring Connectivity for All Students and Families. Gottheimer is sending a letter to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) urging the agencies to prioritize broadband deployment to rural and underserved school districts, so the benefits of AI are not concentrated in the wealthiest, most connected communities. This letter builds on Gottheimer’s work fighting for broadband funding for New Jersey, including more than $260 million from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Bill that he helped write, negotiate, and sign into law.

These actions build on Gottheimer’s consistent support for New Jersey schools, including fighting against the Trump administration’s proposed cuts to over $1 billion in education funding for New Jersey, which were fortunately blocked.

Ridgewood Public School District, one of the largest and top-ranked school districts in Bergen County, is implementing a “Return to a Strong Foundation” emphasis this year focused on limiting screens in the classroom and keeping fundamentals front and center in the age of AI.

Gottheimer was joined by Ridgewood Councilman Frank Mortimer, Ridgewood School District Superintendent Dr. Mark Schwarz, George Washington Middle School Principal Dave Bailey, Bergen County Association of School Administrators President Dr. Joseph Cirillo, NJ PTA President Jackie Gibbs, NJ PTA Federal Legislative Chairperson Sharon Roseboro, and NJ PTA Bergen County Council of PTAs President Nancy Wallace. Gottheimer was also joined by four George Washington Middle School students involved in student government – Alaiya Barnes, Landon Ponchak, Karleigh Cadaret, and Druv Kethini.

Below: Gottheimer announces Bipartisan Back-to-School Agenda on AI and Screen Time in K-12 Education.

Read full remarks here:

Good morning, Ridgewood!

As you close out your first week back to school, I want to start by thanking everyone here at George Washington Middle School, including the educators, the administrators and staff, the school board, and especially the students, for having me here today.

Now, I did a little homework before I came, because that’s what you’re supposed to do at school, right? And, I learned a couple of things about this building that I did not know.

First, some of you know the name Willie Geist. He anchors Sunday Today and co-hosts Morning Joe. Willie met his wife, Christina, in their sixth-grade homeroom right here at George Washington Middle School, back in 1986. Forty years later, they’re still together. So, I don’t know exactly what they were teaching in that homeroom, but whatever it was, keep doing it.

Second, Ridgewood’s roots go all the way to the Revolutionary War. George Washington visited this area and wrote letters from right around here, while Patriot and British troops fought nearby. The borough was practically founded during America’s fight for independence. When Washington delivered his first Annual Address to Congress, he said something I think about a lot, especially on a day like today. He said, “Knowledge is in every country the surest basis of public happiness.”

Two hundred and fifty years after our founding, that’s still true, and it’s exactly why we’re here this morning.

I want to give real credit to the Ridgewood School District. While you study the past, you’re not living it. You’re on the cutting edge of education, including how to best use, and not use, technology to learn. This year, you launched your “Return to a Strong Foundation” initiative, cutting back laptop use in the classroom for its nearly 5,500 students, especially for the youngest children. Ridgewood started limiting cell phones in school, too, with phones in lockers, all day, for every student, from elementary school right up through high school. I should add that’s now the state law. No phones in the classroom.

In my opinion, that’s exactly the kind of commonsense, community-driven leadership we need more of, and it’s exactly the balance we need to be talking about in the age of AI. The answer isn’t more screens. The answer is smarter, more purposeful use of technology, alongside real, honest-to-goodness reading, writing, and critical thinking. In other words, technology can’t do your work or your thinking for you. When the calculator showed up to replace the abacus, we still learned how to count. As a kid, I used to look up facts in the World Book Encyclopedia – and then came the Internet.

I still got to read about and learn about the landing on the moon, but I found the information online, not in a book on the shelf. There’s a big difference. We can’t let AI write our papers or do our math assignments, but it can be a tool for helping us learn. We can’t allow AI to replace our educators, but it can certainly help take the busy work off their plate, or allow them to develop more personalized lesson plans for students.

It’s clear that your school system and your educators already get that. Today, I’m here to take that approach across our state and nationwide.

We are at a true inflection point. Technology isn’t slowing down for us. It never has and never will. Just this week, OpenAI introduced Astra, its latest model. This is on the heels of Anthropic’s Mythos – and new Chinese open-weight models that are coming at us nearly every week.

Whether we like it or not, artificial intelligence, or AI, is already in our children’s backpacks, on their laptops, and on their phones. The question isn’t whether our children will encounter AI in their lives – K-12, in college, in their jobs. They will. Just the way we have iPhones and our parents didn’t.

The question is whether we prepare them for it, or just cross our fingers and hope for the best.

Obviously, we can’t take that chance. Our children absolutely need every tool available to compete, not just against others in New Jersey or in the US, but against children in China, India, and all over the world already being trained on this technology. If we sit on our hands, if we don’t have the tools, we will fall behind. That’s just the reality.

But, I want to be really clear about this. AI can be a powerful tool, but it can never replace the fundamentals.

Our students need to learn how to think, solve problems, ask questions, and understand the material for themselves, not through a chatbot. We should use AI to strengthen those skills – not use it as a shortcut around them.

Here’s why I say that. A recent poll found that 45 percent of Jersey students report using AI frequently for schoolwork. But, here’s the number that should get every parent’s attention: nearly two out of three students admit they’ve used AI to cheat in school. And nationally, the majority of teens think AI cheating happens regularly at their own school.

Meanwhile, a lot of parents are flying blind – and, while there are some tools to help, it’s not always easy for an educator to catch a kid using AI to do his or her assignment. In a recent survey from Montclair School District, half of parents said they had no idea how often their own kid uses AI for schoolwork, and 87 percent said they want clearer communication from schools about all of it. So, we’ve got children using a powerful new technology every single day, and we’ve got parents and teachers who, in far too many cases, don’t even know it’s happening, let alone whether it’s helping or hurting their student or child.

Now, some places have looked at all this and panicked. This week, Mayor Mamdani and New York City rolled out a policy banning AI tools outright for every student through eighth grade, with only high schoolers getting restricted access.

I get the instinct. Fewer screens, more critical thinking. I agree with that part, one hundred percent – and I think a lot more of our tests and note-taking should be on a piece of paper, not a computer. But, an outright ban doesn’t teach a single kid how to use AI responsibly, nor does it teach the skills that can help them.

It just guarantees that the first time they really encounter AI with no guardrails and no guidance is the day they get handed a diploma and shoved into a workforce that runs on this stuff. That’s not a plan. That’s sticking your head in the sand and hoping it goes away.

Think about it this way. When I was a kid, we had typing class. Some of you probably did too, pecking away on those big clunky keyboards.

Then by the 80s, and into the ’90s, schools built computer labs because people realized that if children don’t learn a new technology in school that would prepare them for life, in a structured way, with a teacher guiding them, they will learn it somewhere else: badly, unsupervised, and usually too late.

AI technology is the same idea for this generation. We’re not going to pretend it doesn’t exist, and we’re not going to ban it and hope it goes away. So, here in Jersey, we need to do this differently.

We should put AI skills in a classroom, with a curriculum, with an educator, and with guardrails, so that our children grow up to be smart users of AI, not passive victims of it.

That’s why, today, I’m announcing my new bipartisan AI LABS Act, with my colleague Congressman Jay Obernolte of California. This federal legislation directs the U.S. Department of Education to create a new federal grant program to help K-12 public schools set up dedicated AI labs, with real curricula, that teach students how AI actually works, and how to be prepared to utilize it smartly in the new AI world.

This builds on recommendations from the American Federation of Teachers and the National Education Association for real, dedicated curricula that are directed and supervised by educators. There is a reason why AI companies are now hiring college students with philosophy and history degrees, not just those with computer science degrees. They want people who can think critically. The trades also want young people who know how to use AI on the shop floor and in building and manufacturing.

That means learning how to use AI, how to question it, and how to know when to – and not to — trust it. My new legislation will also help teachers get trained up, too, so they’re not scrambling to keep pace with their own students. It also requires a study on how the funds are actually being utilized, so we know what’s working and can keep improving it.

I don’t want to raise a generation of children who can prompt a chatbot, but can’t write a paragraph on their own, or think through what question to ask the chatbot.

I want to raise a generation of children who can use it to genuinely improve their work, because they understand how to use it and know its limits.

That’s the whole idea behind the AI LABS Act. Give our schools the tools. Give our teachers the training. And give our children a real head start, instead of a false choice between banning technology outright and drowning in it.

Second, I’m sending a letter to Governor Sherrill and Education Commissioner Laux on the State’s Phone-Free Schools Grant Program. That program has already helped eighty-six school districts, including eleven right here in the Fifth District. It puts real bell-to-bell cell phone policies in place, with secure pouches, lockers, and the staff training to make it actually work.

Here’s the problem: The current budget for next year includes a record $12.4 billion for K-12 education, but there’s no dedicated earmark in there to keep this program going in the future.

My letter emphasizes the importance of this funding – school districts are just starting to get this right, and we can’t pull the rug out from under them now.

Third, I’m also pushing for new federal funding to help supplement the state’s program. That’s why, I’m very proud to cosponsor the bipartisan UNPLUGGED Act – legislation that directs states and school districts to actually implement phone-free policies during the school day, and it creates a federal grant program to help schools pay for the lockboxes and secure pouches to make it happen.

It includes sensible exceptions too, for children managing a medical condition like Type 1 diabetes, children with disabilities, and English language learners who need translation support.

More resources for this important effort will help implement New Jersey’s new cell phone ban legislation that previous Governor Murphy signed into law in January, which requires all school districts in the state to adopt policies restricting the use of cell phones and other internet-enabled devices in K-12 public schools.

Fourth, I’m working with the state to keep building out real K-12 AI literacy priorities. This builds on New Jersey’s Department of Education’s new core AI principles that were developed with TeachAI, a global partnership that helps schools and governments use AI safely and responsibly in education. These principles will ensure Jersey schools keep people in the loop and put students’ own thinking front and center, not just whatever the AI spits out. This is exactly the kind of approach we need.

We can’t risk losing funding for this program. That’s why, along with others, I successfully fought the Trump Administration’s proposed cuts to New Jersey’s schools. He tried to gut more than $1 billion in federal funding – and we beat him.

And finally, I’m writing to the FCC and the NTIA about broadband access and connectivity. This is an issue that I’ve been working on for years, and, while we’ve made a ton of progress, we still have towns in Northern Jersey with basically dial-up connectivity, and speeds that AI can’t run on. That’s unacceptable.

Right now, there are more than 5,000 homes in Sussex County without dial up, with more than 3,000 more who don’t have access to broadband.

If we don’t get high-speed internet into our rural and disadvantaged school districts, like parts of Sussex County that I represent — net inequality will be permanently baked in. The advantages that AI promises shouldn’t depend on your zip code. I am urging both agencies to prioritize the communities furthest behind, so they get connected first, not last.

This builds on my work getting hundreds of millions in funding for broadband infrastructure right here in Jersey through the American Rescue Plan, the Bipartisan Infrastructure Bill, and the CARES Act, three historic bills that I helped write, negotiate, and sign into law. I’m calling on the state to put to work the money that I fought for in the Care Act. New Jersey was approved for more than $260 million that I helped bring back from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. So far, only $60 million has been deployed to help connect Jersey families, but we have a long way to go.

Right now, the Trump administration is holding up the last $200 million of this critical funding to connect families across Sussex County and the rest of the state. That’s why the FCC and the administration need to release the rest of the funds and get broadband access to every family across the state.

Put it all together, and here’s what we’re doing today: a bill to teach AI the right way, and a push to keep phones out of the way, a push to get real funding for AI literacy, and a push to make sure no community in America gets left offline while the rest of the world races ahead.

I’ll be honest with you: as Co-chair of the House Commission on AI, technology is moving fast, and some days it can feel like it’s moving faster than we can keep up with. But, I have never once bet against American children and Jersey’s incredible educators and schools – and I’m not about to start today.

I promise you, these children will run circles around whatever the future throws at them.

As long as we keep investing in our children and working together, here in the greatest country in the world, I know that our best days will always, always be ahead of us.

Thank you, God bless you, and may God continue to bless and watch over the United States of America.

title: Rep. Grijalva Introduces the Fairness for Farm Workers Act
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva introduced the Fairness for Farm Workers Act, legislation to strengthen federal labor protections for agricultural workers by expanding overtime protections and narrowing exemptions under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).

When the FLSA established the 40-hour work week and overtime pay in 1938, it left out agricultural workers entirely, a carve-out written to appease Southern segregationists who refused labor protections to the Black workers dominating the industry at the time. While farm workers gained partial minimum wage protections in 1966, the overtime exclusion was never fixed. Today, the average farm worker family earns between $25,000 and $29,999 a year, the cost of a law that still doesn't guarantee them overtime pay. This legislation was first introduced by then-Senator Kamala Harris and Rep. Raúl M. Grijalva in 2018. Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA) has introduced the companion bill in the U.S. Senate during this 119th Congress.

“Farm workers play an essential role in the nation’s food and agricultural economy yet remain one of the only groups of workers still excluded from full overtime protections under federal law,” said Rep. Grijalva. “This bill is fundamentally about fairness – ensuring that the workers who keep America fed receive the same workplace protections and benefits as any other worker.”

This legislation comes as the Trump Administration’s attempt to lower wages for farm workers even further was blocked by the courts last week.

“It’s shameful for this administration to try to undercut farm worker wages in order to address a labor shortage of its own making through its cruel immigration agenda,” continued Rep. Grijalva.

“Since 1938, farm workers have been excluded from basic federal wage laws such as the right to overtime pay,” said UFW President Teresa Romero. “Today, with farm worker wages under attack, it is time to finally end this racist Jim Crow exclusion once and for all.”

The Fairness for Farm Workers Act would:

Establish overtime protections for agricultural workers, requiring employers to provide overtime compensation at one-and-a-half times an employee’s regular rate for hours worked above the applicable weekly threshold.

Phase in a lower overtime threshold for agricultural workers, beginning at 55 hours per week in 2027 and reaching 40 hours per week in 2030.

Provide additional time for smaller employers with 25 or fewer employees to comply with the new overtime requirements, with their phase-in beginning in 2030 and reaching a 40-hour threshold in 2033.

Repeal several existing exemptions for agricultural work under the Fair Labor Standards Act, including certain exemptions related to agricultural employees and members of an employer’s immediate family.

Make conforming changes to federal agricultural labor laws, including the Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act, to reflect the changes made by the legislation.

The Fairness for Farm Workers Act has been endorsed by over 100 organizations including United Farm Workers (UFW), American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations (AFL-CIO), United Food and Commercial Workers International Union (UFCW), HEAL, Communication Workers of America (CWA), CRLA Foundation, NAACP, Alianza Nacional de Campesinas, Latino Justice PRLDEF, Farm Labor Organizing Committee, National Center for Law and Economic Justice, Legal Aid Justice Center, Hispanic Federation, Migrant Justice, Farmworker Justice, SEIU, UAW, UnidosUS, National Council of Churches, National Employment Law Project, National Farm Worker Ministry, and Equal Rights Advocates.

Read the full text of the bill here.

title: Hoyer Statement on August Jobs Report
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement on the August jobs report:

“Today’s jobs report continues to demonstrate the urgency with which the current Administration must address the affordability crisis. While our economy saw an increase of 162,000 jobs in August, inflation is rising faster than average household earnings. In fact, wage gains are rising at the slowest pace since the pandemic, leaving families with fewer resources to pay for gas, groceries, and medical care. For months, Americans have faced rising prices, and now, as a result of President Trump’s trade war against Canada, costs will only continue to soar.

“Americans know all too well where the blame lies. President Trump’s approval rating has reached a record low as workers and their families continue to worry about affordability; meanwhile, the majority of Americans disapprove of his handling of the economy and his endless war of choice in Iran, which is driving up gas prices. But rather than actually addressing the concerns of the public, the President has continued to focus on advantaging himself and his billionaire associates and on expensive vanity projects like the White House ballroom.

"President Trump and Republicans in Congress are doing everything they can to distract attention from the real issues facing Americans. While President Trump has said, absurdly, that the current economy is ‘the greatest economy we've ever had, by far,’ Americans know the truth: his claims are nothing but tall tales spun from his gilded halls of Mar-a-Lago. Americans deserve better, and House Democrats are ready to address the affordability crisis from day one if returned to the Majority.”

title: Maryland Delegation Submits Items for Congressional Time Capsule in Celebration of America’s 250th Anniversary
text:
WASHINGTON – In honor of America’s 250th anniversary, this summer, the full Maryland Congressional Delegation – Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05), U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (both D-MD) and U.S. Representatives Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Andy Harris (MD-01), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Glenn Ivey (MD-04), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), and Johnny Olszewski (MD-02) – submitted a Fort McHenry Flag and a Baltimore & Ohio (B&O) Railroad Centenary Souvenir Medal to the Semiquincentennial Congressional Time Capsule. Sealed and buried by the Architect of the Capitol, the Semiquincentennial Congressional Time Capsule contains a joint letter and items of significance from every state and territory reflecting the history and culture of our country. It will be opened by the 224th Congress in celebration of our nation's 500th anniversary on July 4, 2276.

The items selected by the Maryland delegation represent Maryland’s critical role in the history of America:

Fort McHenry Flag: This 15-Star Flag, also known as a Fort McHenry Flag, is a replica of the one that flew above Fort McHenry during the Battle of Baltimore and inspired Francis Scott Key to write the United States national anthem, The Star-Spangled Banner, in 1814. The flag that was flying at Fort McHenry that day was sewn at 844 E. Pratt Street in Baltimore by Mary Pickersgill, members of her family, and indentured and enslaved African-American women – it is now on display at the Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C. The Fort McHenry Flag has 15 stars and 15 stripes to account for Vermont and Kentucky becoming the 14th and 15th states, and was the official flag of the United States from 1795-1818. The Fort McHenry Flag included in the Congressional Time Capsule was flown over 844 E. Pratt Street, now known as the Star-Spangled Banner Flag House, on July 4, 2026, on the occasion of America’s 250th anniversary.

B&O Railroad Centenary Souvenir Medal: This commemorative coin was crafted in honor of the B&O Railroad’s 100th anniversary in 1927. The B&O Souvenir Medal was selected for the Congressional Time Capsule because of the B&O Railroad’s significant impact on both the state of Maryland and the country – chartered on February 28, 1827, it was the first-ever railroad to carry both passengers and freight for a toll. It pioneered railway engineering and spurred industrial opportunity for the United States. Notably, construction of the B&O Railroad began on July 4, 1828, with a groundbreaking event in Baltimore that featured Marylander Charles Carroll, the last living signer of the Declaration of Independence. The Souvenir Medal was donated to this timecapsule by the National Museum of Railroad History and Innovation located in Baltimore.

“It can be difficult to imagine America at 500. What technologies will define the way we live and work? What will our nation celebrate and mourn from its history? How will our people build community and understand the bonds that keep us together? The America 250 Congressional Time Capsule will offer them a window into our nation and our moment in history. I’m proud to join Team Maryland in offering future Marylanders a reminder of what we cherish and how we celebrate our state’s place in American history,” said Congressman Hoyer.

“Marylanders have always played a central role in American history – from the Maryland 400 holding strong against the British Army in 1776, to Baltimore’s own Thurgood Marshall expanding justice under the law, to the countless scientists, innovators, and entrepreneurs pushing our nation forward every day. Inspired by the legacy of these great Marylanders and those still to come, we will continue working to build a nation that lives up to the American promise of equal justice, equal rights, and equal opportunity for all. As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, the items Team Maryland chose for this Congressional Time Capsule showcase the resilience and innovation woven into the histories of both our great state and nation. This time capsule is a reflection on the work our nation has done over the past 250 years to live up to our founding ideals, and a statement of belief that 250 years from now our democracy will be even stronger,” said Senator Van Hollen.

“It was an honor to celebrate America’s 250th Anniversary by looking back at Maryland’s contributions to technology, science, and culture that have transformed our nation forever. And when this timecapsule is opened on July 4, 2276, I hope Marylanders will look back at the mark we are leaving now – how we stood for justice, worked hard to advance society, cured diseases, found solutions to complex problems, and did it all with joy and love for each other,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

"The United States of America's 250th Birthday is a momentous occasion, and with the selection of these items for the Semiquincentennial Congressional Time Capsule, we ensure that Maryland's contributions to American history will be preserved for our nation's Quincentennial," said Congressman Mfume. "The resilience and fortitude represented by this 15-star flag – the same design as flew over Fort McHenry while Francis Scott Key penned our National Anthem – as well as the pioneering spirit and ingenuity embodied by the commemorative B&O Railroad coin, are traits that have characterized Marylanders for generations. Let this capsule carry them forward to those Americans who open it next."

“Maryland’s contributions to our country stretch back to the earliest days of our nation. More than two centuries later, that legacy continues across the Eastern Shore and Chesapeake Bay, where farmers and watermen remain an important part of American agriculture and seafood production, and through the Port of Baltimore, which connects our state to commerce around the world. The items selected by the Maryland delegation capture two defining moments in that history and will carry a piece of Maryland’s past forward as America celebrates its 250th anniversary,” said Congressman Harris.

“From Frederick Douglass to Harriet Tubman to Rachel Carson to Thurgood Marshall, Marylanders have been devoted patriots and fighters for our land, our democracy and our freedom,” said Congressman Raskin. “When this time capsule is opened, future Americans will be reminded of the Free State’s many enduring cultural, scientific and political contributions to our nation’s history and our shared work to build a more perfect union.”

“Maryland has always been at the heart of America’s story, and our contributions to this country extend far beyond the moments we typically see in the history books. The flag that inspired our national anthem was sewn in Baltimore by Mary Pickersgill, her family, and Black women whose contributions were essential to our nation’s history. The B&O Railroad helped launch America’s industrial future from right here in Maryland. As we celebrate 250 years of our nation, these artifacts remind us that America’s story has always been shaped by the people, ingenuity, and perseverance of Marylanders. I’m proud to help preserve that story for Americans 250 years from now,” said Congressman Ivey.

“Home to the oldest State Capitol to remain in use and the only State House to have served as the nation’s Capitol; the place where our Founders met in 1786 and decided we needed a new system of government that led to the Constitution we have today; and the state where our flag flew high after the Battle of Fort McHenry, inspiring our national anthem — Maryland’s role in our nation’s history is undeniable,” said Congresswoman Elfreth. “The artifacts we preserved today tell crucial pieces of Maryland’s story in the last 250 years of our nation’s history, and Team Maryland is committed to preserving this legacy for generations to come.”

“People call Maryland America in miniature. That started as a line about our climate and geography, but I think it says something truer about us: for more than 250 years, Maryland has helped build this country. What our delegation put in this time capsule shows exactly that,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney.

“Maryland has always punched above its weight in shaping the story of America. From the flag that inspired our national anthem to the railroad that helped connect a growing nation, these artifacts help tell the story of Maryland’s role in defending our freedom and creating opportunity,” said Congressman Olszewski. “Now, 250 years later, the fight for these ideals continues in different ways. It is with a spirit of hope that we look to the future -- that generations of Americans will continue our march toward a more perfect union."

title: REP. HOYLE EXPRESSES CONCERN AROUND PROPOSED RAIL MERGER
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representative Val Hoyle (OR-04), alongside over 100 Members of Congress and partners in labor, wrote to federal regulators demanding they consider the consequences of the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Rail merger for workers:

“The proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger would create the largest rail network in this country’s history. Railroad workers are the backbone of our supply chain, and their rights and security must come first. When workers do well, our economy thrives,” said Rep. Hoyle. “I’m leading 100 of my colleagues in demanding that the Surface Transportation Board fully evaluate what this merger could mean for jobs, safety and accountability.”

"This merger could cost thousands of jobs and deny our members their livelihoods, " said TWU Rail Division Director John Feltz. "Norfolk Southern is leaving its workers and everyone else in the dark. We appreciate the members of Congress who have our backs by demanding answers to basic questions about whether this merger will benefit all of us."

“BRS members are on the ground every day maintaining the signal systems and critical infrastructure that keep America’s rail network operating safely. We know firsthand that bigger does not automatically mean better or safer. The proposed Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern merger would create an unprecedented level of consolidation in the freight rail industry, and we have serious concerns about what that could mean for safety, network reliability, competition, and the railroad workforce. Before a transaction of this magnitude is allowed to move forward, the railroads should be required to demonstrate that it will strengthen—not weaken—the safety and reliability of our nation’s rail system. BRS does not believe they have made that case,” said International President, Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen Michael Baldwin

“The proposed $85 billion Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger is the largest railroad merger in history and one of the largest recent corporate consolidations in memory. This merger will have profound impacts on every railroad worker across the railroad industry, including the Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employes Division (BMWED-IBT) members that construction, maintain, repair, and inspect our nation’s railroad tracks, bridges, catenary and other railroad structures. The letter sent to the Surface Transportation Board today by more than 100 Members of Congress highlights important labor considerations and concerns that must be carefully contemplated and satisfied by the Surface Transportation Board when it analyzes the proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger. To date, Union Pacific has not made the labor commitments necessary to protect our membership and we will ask the STB to ensure that our members are protected. We want to thank Congresswoman Val Hoyle for leading this letter and her continued steadfast support for rail labor and our union and all the House members that signed this letter,” said Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employes Division (BMWED-IBT) President Tony Cardwell

“We have seen what railroad mergers and consolidation have done to workers, customers, and communities. The proposed Union Pacific acquisition of Norfolk Southern would create the largest railroad in the country, but bigger does not mean better. These two railroads do not need to merge, and Union Pacific has not shown that this deal is in the public interest.

BLET and BMWED did not rush to judgment. We were the first two rail unions to meet with UP CEO Jim Vena after the announcement, and we listened with an open mind. What we heard did not answer our concerns about jobs, service, safety, or the communities that depend on these railroads.

UP calls its offer ‘Jobs for Life,’ but a slogan is not job protection. Their promise does not protect the jobs that exist today. It allows jobs to disappear through attrition, and it can force workers to move hundreds of miles or accept whatever work the company makes available. That may protect a person from the word ‘furlough,’ but it does not protect that worker’s job, home, or family.

We have already seen the results of doing more with fewer people: limited personal leave, tighter attendance policies, fewer vacation opportunities, and increased discipline aimed at removing employees. If this merger is paid for by eliminating jobs and placing even more work on those who remain, the jobs left will not be the kind of jobs anyone would embrace for a lifetime.

The Surface Transportation Board must look past the slogans and examine what this acquisition would actually mean for farmers, businesses, workers, rail service, safety, and the communities this massive railroad could choose to serve—or abandon.

We thank Representative Val Hoyle for leading this letter and for standing with railroad workers and the customers who depend on reliable rail service. We also thank every member of Congress who signed it and called on the STB to closely examine the real consequences of the proposed UP-NS acquisition,” said Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen (BLET-IBT) National President and Teamsters Rail Conference President Mark Wallace

title: Jayapal Demands Answers on Reports ICE is Weakening Safety Standards at Private, For-Profit Detention Centers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Immigration, Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, is demanding answers from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as reporting indicates that ICE is weakening detention safety standards, even as 56 people have died in these facilities under ICE’s watch. Loosening standards will allow for-profit, private prison operators to continue cutting corners on food, medical care, and safety. ICE Acting Director David Venturella is the former Vice President of GEO Group, the largest of these private, for-profit prison corporations. Reporting suggests that these private contractors were consulted in the adoption of these new standards.

“Detention standards are meant to guide the entities operating immigration detention centers – they should not be written by them. And yet, it appears that that is precisely what occurred here,” wrote the Members. “At a time when there are numerous documented cases of abuse and neglect within the immigration detention system, when deaths of detained people, including at least one homicide, have more than doubled from previous years, and when the oversight mechanisms within the system have been gutted, we should not be lowering detention standards, especially not to pad the bottom line of companies getting rich off of taxpayer funds and human suffering.”

Since the start of the second Trump administration, over 400,000 people have been arrested and sent to immigration detention facilities. From these facilities, there have been reports of inadequate medical care, spoiled food, overcrowded cells, and physical beatings. Guards beat one teenager so badly that he had to be hospitalized. Pregnant women have miscarried inside detention centers because of the appalling conditions, with some reporting receiving no medical care after miscarrying.

Lowering already failing standards will make these facilities less safe and increase profits for the contractors running these facilities, including GEO Group and CoreCivic. These private, for-profit prison corporations have already benefited significantly from the expansion of immigration detention, with both GEO Group and CoreCivic reporting an additional $2 billion in profits in 2025.

Jayapal is demanding information regarding the new standards and what they entail, as well as any communications between DHS officials and officials at GEO Group or CoreCivic.

title: Congressman Joyce Releases Statement as Work Resumes on Brandon Road Project
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Dave Joyce (OH-14) released the following statement after the stop-work order for the Brandon Road Interbasin Project was lifted. The Brandon Road project is a $1.15 billion federal-local partnership intended to stop the continued spread of invasive carp up the Mississippi River Basin toward the Great Lakes. The project has received support from President Trump, who signed a presidential memorandum in 2025 directing federal agencies to expedite support and infrastructure for the project.

“The Great Lakes are one of our region’s greatest assets, and we have a responsibility to protect them. That means taking the threat of invasive carp seriously and making sure the Brandon Road Interbasin Project moves forward. The Great Lakes Task Force Co-Chairs and I sent letters to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and the Army Corps urging them to lift the stop-work order, while I also spoke directly with OMB Director Russell Vought about the project. I appreciate the Director’s attention to this issue and his willingness to work with us. I will continue working with my colleagues and the Administration to find a path forward that protects the Great Lakes and the communities that rely on them.”

“Addressing the threat of invasive carp is about more than one project. It is about preserving a resource that defines our region and supports millions of people. We have an opportunity to get this right, and we should seize it.”

title: Kennedy, Ranking Member Thompson, Homeland Security Dems Demand DHS Cooperate with Homicide Investigation into Death of Nurul Amin Shah Alam
text:
After Thorough Review, AG James Determined her Office Lacked Authority to Prosecute, Referred Case to Erie County DA

BUFFALO, N.Y. – Standing feet from where Mr. Nurul Amin Shah Alam was found, Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) was joined today by House Committee on Homeland Security Ranking Member Bennie G. Thompson (MS-02), Border Security Subcommittee Ranking Member Lou Correa (CA-46), and Rep. Nellie Pou (NJ-09) to demand that the Department of Homeland Security fully comply with the Erie County District Attorney’s investigation into the death of Mr. Shah Alam. Shah Alam was a Rohingya refugee with legal status who was found dead in Buffalo in February after being released from DHS custody. In April, the Erie County Medical Examiner determined Shah Alam’s death to be a homicide and an investigation remains ongoing. In a letter sent this week to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Kennedy and Thompson demanded the Department turn over any and all information requested by Erie County law enforcement, arguing that DHS has a legal and moral obligation to cooperate with a local homicide investigation within the District Attorney’s jurisdiction.

In their letter, they noted that there has been a clear pattern by the Department to obfuscate facts and block meaningful oversight. Despite multiple letters as well as several instances of questioning by members of Congress on the Homeland Security Committee and other committees, all inquiries have been met with silence.

“It has been more than six months since Nurul Amin Shah Alam died after DHS left him, blind and disabled, outside of a closed coffee shop in the middle of winter without the proper footwear or clothing needed for the Buffalo climate and no way to call for help,” said Congressman Kennedy. “The Erie County Medical Examiner has ruled his death a homicide, yet DHS still won’t hand over a single meaningful record. Not to my office, not to Attorney General James, and not to the Erie County District Attorney. Simply put, they are obstructing the pursuit of justice by local law enforcement. Mr. Shah Alam’s family deserves to see justice served by our legal system. I won’t stop demanding it until DHS complies.”

“A man died after being released from DHS custody, and his family deserves to know what exactly happened. DHS does not get to run out the clock and hope folks stop asking questions,” said Ranking Member Thompson. “If DHS has nothing to hide, then they need to turn over the records and cooperate fully with the Erie County law enforcement. It is that simple.”

“DHS dropped off a blind, disabled man outside a closed coffee shop in the dead of winter in New York with no coat and no call to his family. Six months later, there is an ongoing homicide investigation into his death, and DHS won’t cooperate. His family deserves answers. DHS owes Erie County the truth,” said Congressman Correa.

“Nurul Amin Shah Alam’s death was a tragic injustice that the Department of Homeland Security wants to sweep under the rug,” said Congresswoman Pou (NJ-09). “As Members of Congress, we have taken an oath to act in the best interest of the American people, however, consistent efforts from the Department of Homeland Security undermine this crucial work. I am proud to join Congressman Kennedy here in Buffalo to make clear that we will never forget what happened to Mr. Shah Alam and we will never stop fighting for justice for his family and this community.”

On February 19, 2026, DHS agents released Shah Alam, who was disabled, largely blind, and spoke little to no English, outside a closed Tim Hortons in Buffalo’s Black Rock neighborhood without proper footwear or appropriate clothing for Buffalo’s winter weather, and without notifying his family or attorney. He was reported missing and was found dead on February 24, miles from where he was released. DHS initially claimed he had been dropped off at a “warm, safe location” and showed no signs of distress, which has since been proven to be false by video evidence. Kennedy, Thompson, and their colleagues have since sent multiple oversight letters to DHS. Kennedy directly questioned Secretary Mullin on the topic as well, and was met with hostility. To date, no substantive response has been received. Attorney General James opened her own inquiry into the death, but has since reported that CBP has declined to share information and records, and she has determined that proper jurisdiction lies with the Erie County District Attorney.

Kennedy introduced the DHS Release Transparency Act in response to Shah Alam’s death, which would require ICE and CBP to notify a detainee’s designated point of contact before releasing them from custody.

Full text of the letter here.

title: Krishnamoorthi, Budzinski, Pappas Lead 97 Members Demanding USPS Halt Trump-Backed Mail Ballot Rule
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), together with Representatives Nikki Budzinski (D-IL) and Chris Pappas (D-NH), today led 97 Members of Congress in demanding that Postmaster General David Steiner halt implementation of a new U.S. Postal Service rule carrying out President Donald Trump’s executive order restricting mail ballot delivery. The lawmakers warned that the rule could throw the nation’s election system into uncertainty and chaos just weeks before states begin sending mail-in ballots to millions of Americans. The rule would require USPS employees to cross-reference mail ballots against voter information supplied by states, effectively asking postal workers to act as election judges.

In their letter, the lawmakers wrote:

“The evidence is clear: voting by mail is safe, effective, and helps to ensure everyone is able to execute their constitutional right to vote. USPS has played an essential role in elections for generations – and it is our fear that this final rule risks harming the democratic process and severely damaging USPS’s relationship with the millions of Americans who rely on USPS to deliver ballots every election cycle.”

The lawmakers pointed to USPS’s longstanding record of successfully delivering election mail and the extremely low incidence of mail-voting fraud. During the 2024 election cycle, USPS delivered 99.22 million ballots, including ballots for servicemembers overseas, and delivered 99.88 percent of election mail within seven days. A 2025 Brookings Institution study cited in the letter found an average of just four cases of voter fraud for every 10 million mail-in votes cast.

The letter also raises serious questions about USPS’s compliance with court orders governing the Trump Administration’s mail-ballot policy. An anonymous whistleblower alleged that USPS resumed development of its Federal Ballot Mail Portal around July 29 while an injunction remained in effect and that work continued even after an August 27 temporary restraining order barred further preparatory steps. The lawmakers wrote that those allegations are difficult to square with USPS’s representation that it would take no action to implement the rule while the injunctions remained in place.

The lawmakers wrote:

“This rule is a solution in search of a problem. For these reasons, we respectfully ask that you halt the implementation of this final rule.”

Krishnamoorthi, Budzinski, Pappas, and their colleagues are demanding answers from Steiner by September 10, including whether USPS conducted a financial analysis of the rule, whether development of the Federal Ballot Mail Portal continued while court orders were in effect, whether USPS coordinated with the White House in developing the rule, how many postal employees would participate in ballot verification, and how USPS plans to handle ballots in states that have already printed envelopes that do not comply with the new requirements.

title: Krishnamoorthi Continues National Push to Combat Rising Hate Against South Asian Americans at Georgia Event
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) participated Thursday in the first stop of Indian American Impact’s national listening tour in Norcross, Georgia, where South Asian elected officials, community leaders, and residents gathered to address the rise in hate, harassment, and violence targeting South Asian Americans. The Georgia gathering followed Wednesday’s national roundtable on Capitol Hill and focused on what communities are experiencing and how federal, state, and local leaders can strengthen prevention, reporting, and accountability.

“The rise in hate, harassment, and violence against South Asian Americans demands a response across the country,” Krishnamoorthi said. “After bringing South Asian leaders together in Washington, we are continuing that work here in Georgia with community members and public officials to improve prevention, reporting, and accountability for hate crimes. South Asian Americans have built their lives here, raised their families here, and strengthened communities across this country. We have to stand shoulder to shoulder against hate and violence whenever our communities are targeted.”

The listening session included Krishnamoorthi, Virginia Lieutenant Governor Ghazala Hashmi, Georgia State Senator Sheikh Rahman, Georgia State Representative Akbar Ali, Indian American Impact Executive Director Chintan Patel, SAATH founder Rohan Soni, and community leaders and advocates from across Georgia. Participants discussed what South Asian Americans are seeing and experiencing, how government is responding, and what additional steps could help communities confronting hate and discrimination. The Georgia gathering marked the beginning of Indian American Impact’s national listening tour, which is intended to hear directly from community members about their experiences and what additional steps are needed to confront hate targeting South Asian Americans.

Earlier this year, Krishnamoorthi reintroduced the bipartisan Hate Crimes Commission Act, which would establish a bipartisan commission to examine what is driving hate crimes, including the role of social media and technology, assess barriers to complete reporting, and identify successful prevention and response strategies.

title: Krishnamoorthi Demands Trump Disclose Whether He, His Family, or Allies Stand to Profit from Venezuela Oil Deal
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a senior member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, today demanded President Donald Trump disclose whether he, members of his family, political allies, major donors, or business associates stand to financially benefit from his Administration’s Venezuela oil deal before substantial U.S. taxpayer resources are committed.

Trump announced the deal on August 28, claiming it would give the United States “majority U.S. control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves” in Venezuela. According to the White House, the agreement includes a 35 percent U.S. stake in the corporate parent of North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), a private company led by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt, as well as preferential rights to purchase a portion of its oil production.

In the letter, Krishnamoorthi writes:

“Given the limited information your Administration has made public, conflicting statements from Venezuela’s acting President, and questions of the legality of the agreement, I have serious concerns, including whether you, members of your family, your political allies, or major donors stand to financially benefit from this arrangement. Therefore, I urge you to provide greater transparency regarding this deal before the United States commits substantial capital to Venezuela’s energy sector.”

Krishnamoorthi raised particular concerns about Betancourt, who has reportedly faced investigations in Switzerland, Spain, and the United States involving alleged money laundering. Betancourt was identified as a conspirator in a Miami criminal complaint detailing a billion-dollar scheme involving funds from Venezuela’s state-owned oil company PDVSA. Rudy Giuliani, Trump’s personal lawyer at the time, represented Betancourt in discussions with Justice Department officials. Betancourt was also arrested twice in Britain in 2025 at the requests of Spain and Switzerland.

The letter also raises questions about other potential beneficiaries of the deal, including oil magnate Harry Sargeant III, a Republican donor with longstanding connections to Trump who reportedly advised the Administration on Venezuela. Sargeant agreed last month to sell the company through which he held a minority stake in NABEP to an unidentified buyer for $300 million.

Krishnamoorthi writes:

“The public requires meaningful transparency when government decisions have the potential to create substantial financial benefits for individuals with close connections to the President. Your family members and business associates have extensive investments and commercial relationships around the world. If any individual or entity connected to you stands to benefit from the development, financing, refining, transportation, sale, or export of Venezuelan oil—or from companies receiving U.S. government contracts, financing, licenses, or other benefits as a result of this agreement—the public deserves to know before American taxpayers and U.S. government resources are committed.”

Krishnamoorthi is demanding answers to the following questions:

Do you, any member of your immediate family, or any entity in which you or your immediate family has a direct or indirect financial interest have any financial interest in any entity involved in the Venezuela agreement or in the development, financing, refining, transportation, or sale of Venezuelan oil? If so, please identify each interest and its estimated value.

Do any current or former Administration officials, campaign officials, major political donors, business associates, or other individuals with a personal or professional relationship with you have a direct or indirect financial interest in any entity participating in the agreement? If so, please identify those individuals and entities.

What U.S. government agencies, funds, financing mechanisms, or other taxpayer-supported resources will be used to finance, guarantee, insure, or otherwise support the Venezuela oil agreement?

What ethics reviews, conflict-of-interest analyses, recusals, disclosure requirements, or other safeguards have the Administration undertaken to ensure that the agreement does not provide an improper financial benefit to you, your family, your political allies, or your business associates?

What mechanisms are in place to ensure that individuals with connections to you or your family cannot acquire interests in Venezuelan oil assets or companies participating in the agreement after the agreement has been announced?

title: Krishnamoorthi, Garcia, Frost Demand Census Bureau Rescind Sham Noncitizen Voting Report
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Health Care and Financial Services, House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Ranking Member Robert Garcia (D-CA), and Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs Subcommittee Ranking Member Maxwell Frost (D-FL) today demanded that the U.S. Census Bureau immediately rescind a deeply flawed, defective, and politically motivated report on noncitizen voting in the 2020 election.

The lawmakers also demanded answers about who was involved in producing the report, how it was developed, what outside individuals or organizations participated in the effort, and what federal resources were used.

“Donald Trump lost the 2020 election, and no deeply flawed, politically motivated Census Bureau report can rewrite that fact. The Census Bureau should be producing rigorous, nonpartisan data, not spending taxpayer resources to prop up Trump’s election lies. Our letter demands that the Bureau rescind this report and provide answers about who was behind it and how it was produced,” said Ranking Member Krishnamoorthi.

“Donald Trump is a loser and a liar who is misusing government resources to cover up the fact that he lost the 2020 election. In the process, he is politicizing and undermining the credibility of the Census, with serious consequences for our country. We need to find out how Trump’s allies were involved in this and what federal funds were wasted on this worthless report,” said Ranking Member Garcia.

“The Census Bureau is supposed to give the American people reliable information, not help Donald Trump relitigate an election he lost six years ago. Using taxpayer resources to produce a report that serves a political agenda is unacceptable. The Bureau should withdraw this report and be transparent about who commissioned it, who worked on it, and how it was produced,” said Ranking Member Frost.

In their letter to George M. Cook, Deputy Under Secretary of the U.S. Census Bureau, Krishnamoorthi, Garcia, and Frost raised concerns about the Bureau’s publication of Noncitizen Voting in the 2020 Election, A Beginning Analysis, including questions about the report’s methodology, the individuals involved in producing it, and the use of federal resources.

The lawmakers wrote:

“The mere publication of the Beginning Analysis in service of Trump’s big lie threatens to undermine trust in the independence and credibility of the Bureau. The Bureau has been historically regarded as a public institution that employs rigor and integrity in each of its statistical quality standards and operations. As stated by former Census Bureau Director Rob Santos, ‘[t]he scientific reputation of the Bureau has been beyond reproach. And as long as that document sits on the Census Bureau's website, that's no longer the case.’ To one policy expert, ‘[t]his is the weakest methodology description I’ve ever seen in a Census Bureau publication.’ Despite clear indicators that the Beginning Analysis lacks thoroughness and integrity, Trump falsely claimed that this initial review proved he ‘WON THE ELECTION’ in 2020 another attempt to further instigate Trump’s embarrassing hyper fixation on the 2020 presidential election.”

Krishnamoorthi, Garcia, and Frost are demanding that the Census Bureau rescind the report and provide documents and information concerning its production, including the individuals involved, the data and methodology used, communications with outside organizations, the legal authorities relied upon, and the federal funding used to produce the analysis.

title: Krishnamoorthi Sounds Alarm as Trump Administration Continues to Threaten to Deploy Armed Federal Agents to Polling Places
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a senior member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, today sounded the alarm as the Trump Administration continues to threaten the deployment of ICE, CBP, or other armed federal agents at or near polling places during the 2026 midterm elections, warning that their presence could intimidate voters and suppress lawful participation.

In a letter to Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Krishnamoorthi demanded a definitive statement of DHS policy after Mullin’s latest comments again left open the possibility of ICE appearing at polling places. President Trump has also said he would “do anything necessary” when asked whether he would send ICE or the National Guard to voting sites.

In the letter, Krishnamoorthi writes:

“With early voting and Election Day fast approaching, voters should not have to wonder whether federal immigration agents could appear at or near their polling place while they are casting their ballots. The presence of armed federal agents at or near a polling location—even when ostensibly responding to a separate law-enforcement matter—could create confusion, fear, or intimidation and could discourage eligible voters from exercising their constitutional right to vote.”

Krishnamoorthi warned that the threat is no longer theoretical. Republican candidates in Georgia, Maine, and Michigan have publicly discussed sending law enforcement, including ICE agents, U.S. Marshals, retired police officers, and the National Guard, to polling places in November. One candidate for governor of Maine has said he intends to ask the Trump Administration to send ICE agents and U.S. Marshals to voting sites.

The letter also points to the extraordinary volume of DHS records concerning possible federal deployments at election sites. ICE and CBP have told a federal court that they identified more than 127,000 pages of potentially responsive records concerning possible deployments of federal agents near polling places, ballot drop boxes, or election offices, yet neither agency had produced a single page as of the most recent filing.

Federal law sharply restricts the presence of armed personnel at polling places and separately prohibits federal officials from intimidating voters. Krishnamoorthi noted that election officials in at least eight states have already moved to establish buffer zones and other restrictions on federal agents near polling places in response to the Administration’s refusal to rule out such deployments.

Krishnamoorthi writes:

“The Department cannot simultaneously maintain, on one hand, that ICE has ‘no reason’ to be near a polling place, and on the other, that its Special Response Teams stand ready to deploy there. As the Department's Secretary, you are uniquely positioned to end this ambiguity.”

Krishnamoorthi is demanding that DHS provide:

A definitive, unqualified statement of Department policy on whether ICE, CBP, or any other DHS component will deploy personnel to, or within sight of, any polling place, ballot drop box, or election office during the early voting period or on Election Day 2026.

All guidance, directives, memoranda, or operational plans — including any related to Special Response Team deployment — concerning the presence of DHS personnel at or near polling locations for the 2026 elections.

A precise definition of the “specific threat” standard you have described publicly, including who within the Department is authorized to determine that the standard has been met and what review, if any, occurs before agents are dispatched to a polling site.

A status update on ICE's and CBP's document production in the pending Democratic National Committee FOIA litigation, including a timeline for completing review and release of the identified records.

Copies of any communications between Department leadership and the White House, the Department of Justice, the Department of Defense, or outside political advisers regarding the potential deployment of federal personnel to polling places in 2026.

Confirmation of what guidance, if any, the Department has issued to field offices regarding compliance with state buffer-zone laws that restrict federal agents' proximity to polling places.

title: Congressman Langworthy Announces $76.2 Million Investment to Strengthen Rural Health Care
text:
Washington D.C.—September 3rd… Congressman Nick Langworthy today announced a $76.2 million investment through New York’s Rural Community Health Integration Initiative to strengthen health care services and expand access for rural communities across the state, including seven counties in New York’s 23rd Congressional District.

The investment is part of the broader Rural Health Transformation Program, which was established to provide resources to states to strengthen rural health care systems and improve the availability and quality of services in rural communities. The funding includes approximately $22.7 million in planning awards and $53.5 million in implementation awards, with an additional $1 million dedicated to increasing the number of School-Based Health Centers.

Within NY-23, Allegany, Cattaraugus, Chautauqua, Chemung, Schuyler, Steuben, and Tioga counties have been identified as areas of focus under New York’s program and are expected to directly benefit from the initiative.

“When we created the Rural Health Transformation Program, it was to acknowledge that our rural communities face unique healthcare challenges and demand a unique approach to improving access and quality of care,” said Congressman Nick Langworthy. “This significant $76 million investment in New York is proof that we are delivering on that promise. By strengthening partnerships among rural hospitals, health centers, and community providers, we are breaking down barriers to care, improving coordination, and building a stronger rural health care system that improves health outcomes, expands access, and delivers the kind of care that Americans in rural communities deserve just as much as those in urban and suburban settings. Delivering on this commitment will continue to be one of my top priorities for the residents of Western New York and the Southern Tier."

New York has identified 47 of the state’s 62 counties as rural for purposes of its program application, using criteria established by the Health Resources and Services Administration’s Federal Office of Rural Health Policy. The state’s initiative will support partnerships among rural hospitals, health centers, and community providers to improve care coordination and expand access to health and social services.

title: REPS LIEU, SUBRAMANYAM, AND NEGUSE INTRODUCE THE NO PARDON PAYDAYS ACT
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representatives Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA), Ted Lieu (D-Los Angeles County), and Joe Neguse (D-CO) introduced the No Pardon Paydays Act.

Trump has handed out blanket pardons to January 6th insurrectionists and those who padded his pockets – including those who engaged in acts of violence. Many of the January 6th insurrectionists who received pardons have since committed new crimes.

The No Pardon Paydays Act would prevent corruption in the pardon process by requiring the Pardon Attorney to submit a review to Congress of any criminal history of the pardon recipient. It would also prohibit pardon recipients from making high dollar contributions to political committees associated with the President who granted the pardon.

“Time and time again, trump uses pardons as favors for his pals and donors. This blatant corruption is dangerous to our democracy and our communities,” said Congressman Lieu. “I am pleased to partner with Rep. Subramanyam on the No Pardon Paydays Act, which would mitigate the perverse practice of paying for Presidential pardons. You should not be able to buy your way out of justice, no matter how much money you donate to the President.”

“This administration is the most corrupt in modern American history. Every American is paying the price while this administration lines their pockets and dishes out favors to their friends. We refuse to stand by and watch this unfold. There must be consequences for this corruption while we work to restore the American people’s trust,”

said Congressman Subramanyam.

“Donald Trump has repeatedly abused the presidential pardon power to give get out of jail free cards to violent, convicted felons who assaulted Capitol Police officers on January 6th, and benefit close political allies and the members of his inner circle. This cannot stand. That’s why I’m proud to join Rep. Subramanyam’s effort to put a commonsense check on presidential pardons, ensuring regardless of who’s in the White House, the power is used fairly and responsibly,” said Congressman Neguse.

title: Malliotakis Honors Good Samaritan Who Helped Staffer Struck by Lightning
text:
(STATEN ISLAND, NY) — Today, Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) met with Stefanie Homan, the Good Samaritan who came to the aid of staff member Thomas Fahmy after he was struck by lightning last week. Malliotakis presented Homan with a Congressional Commendation in recognition of her quick thinking and compassion during the frightening incident.

“We are incredibly grateful that Thomas, a valued member of our Staten Island office, is doing well after this horrifying experience, and we thank Stefanie Homan for her heroic actions. Her quick response is an example of the kindness and compassion that make Staten Island such a special community,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. “We also thank the first responders and the medical team at Staten Island University Hospital for treating Thomas.”

"I heard Thomas say 'help me, help me' so I ran to my door and I opened it and I saw him on the ground," said Stefanie Homan, Good Samaritan. "I am just so happy that I was able to help you and you were able to get up and that you're okay."

“I am extremely grateful to the Good Samaritan, Stefanie Homan, who so selflessly came to my aid during last Thursday’s thunderstorm. After I was struck by lightning, fell to the ground, and cried out for help, Stefanie opened the front door of her home while holding and comforting her baby son, who was understandably frightened by the lightning and what had just occurred. While caring for her son, she immediately called 911 and welcomed me into her home until emergency services arrived. This is Staten Island at its finest. I will always be grateful for Stefanie’s extraordinary selflessness and compassion in opening her home to a complete stranger in need," said Thomas Fahmy.

title: Representative John W. Mannion Secures $1,031,000 for Onondaga Community College to Expand Advanced Manufacturing and Semiconductor Workforce Training
text:
SYRACUSE, NY - Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today announced that $1,031,000 in federal Community Project Funding he secured for Onondaga Community College’s Innovating Manufacturing Programs for Advanced Career Training (IMPACT) project has been formally awarded through the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Representative John W. Mannion said, “The growth of advanced manufacturing and the semiconductor industry is creating new demand for skilled workers. I’ll continue working with strong partners like Onondaga Community College to make sure local residents have the tools and training they need to succeed in these high-demand and good-paying jobs. With over a million dollars in new equipment, OCC students and apprentices will be training on the same modern equipment they’ll use in their careers, giving manufacturers the workforce pipeline they need to grow and succeed.”

Dr. Warren Hilton, Onondaga Community College President, said, “Onondaga Community College is proud to be Central New York’s Partner in Education for Success and to play a critical role in preparing the skilled workforce our region needs. We are grateful to Representative Mannion for his leadership and investment in our students and our community. His support will help OCC expand opportunities for students to gain the skills they need for rewarding careers while helping employers meet the growing demand for a highly skilled workforce.”

OCC will use the funding to purchase and install advanced equipment and software focused on electrical technology, mechanical technology, semiconductor systems, welding, and thermodynamics.

The workforce training will be incorporated into OCC’s degree, certificate, and apprenticeship programs, expanding hands-on instruction in precision manufacturing, material analysis, and quality control. More than 250 students and apprentices annually will benefit from this investment, strengthening the local pipeline of skilled workers for the manufacturing, semiconductor, construction, automotive, and industrial machinery sectors.

The OCC funding is part of 15 Community Project Funding priorities advanced by Representative Mannion during his first year in office in partnership with local leaders across Central New York and the Mohawk Valley. All 15 projects have passed Congress and been signed into law, delivering a total of more than $15 million in federal funding to address locally identified needs - including public safety improvements, lead service line replacement, water and wastewater modernization, workforce training, airport infrastructure upgrades, and research critical to America’s economic and national security.

title: McClain Delaney Statement on Reports of Ongoing ICE Presence Across Frederick Communities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman April McClain Delaney (MD-06) today issued the following statement in response to reports of a heavy and ongoing presence of federal immigration agents across several Frederick communities:

“I am closely monitoring reports that ICE agents and multiple vehicles have maintained a sustained presence across residential neighborhoods in Frederick for more than 30 hours. According to community members, residents have consistently observed between two and eight vehicles in the area since this activity began.

“Families—including many with lawful immigration status—are staying inside and scared to come out. No family should feel unsafe simply living in their own neighborhood.

“I’ve reached out to local officials for a full accounting of what’s happening on the ground, and I’ll have more to say once I know the facts. In the meantime, my office is available to any constituent who needs help or has questions about their rights.”
