title: Representatives DeSaulnier and Patronis Introduce Legislation to Hold Tech Companies Accountable and Protect Young Americans
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Representatives Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10) and Jimmy Patronis (FL-01) introduced the Sunset Section 230 Act, which would repeal Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act of 1996, making it possible for Americans to bring legal action against big tech companies responsible for online harm.

“With one in five American teenagers reporting harm to their mental health from social media sites, it is critical and urgent that we take action to rein in the big tech companies that are allowing the dissemination of harmful material on their platforms. These companies have been profiting at the expense of young people, who have been harassed and subjected to harmful content,” said Congressman DeSaulnier. “This legislation combined with the recent legal action against companies like Meta should send a loud message: Big Tech’s days of acting with impunity, wreaking havoc, and then asking for forgiveness once the damage has been done are over.”

“Big Tech has become a crooked dealer, pushing digital fentanyl to our kids while profiting from their addiction. Enough is enough. I’m proud to partner with Congressman DeSaulnier to co-lead the Sunset Section 230 Act and fight to repeal Section 230 once and for all. It’s time to hold Big Tech accountable and put our kids’ safety ahead of Big Tech’s profits,” said Congressman Patronis.

Section 230 was created in 1996 as part of the Communications Decency Act to help encourage innovation and growth among new social media companies, but 30 years later as these companies have become inordinately powerful, Section 230 has become obsolete and dangerous. By sunsetting Section 230 after two years, this bill would provide much needed reform to our tech policy that would protect all users of social media, particularly children, from harmful content and hold companies responsible for demonstrated injury to users of their platforms.

Introduction of this legislation comes as Meta agreed this summer to pay up to $18 billion to settle claims brought by 29 U.S. states that the company had contributed to the national youth mental health crisis. The deal also mandates that Meta introduce new guardrails for young users of its platforms, including default daily time limits and nighttime blocks that can only be lifted by a parent, an enhanced mechanism for teens to report potentially harmful content and a requirement that Meta respond to 90% of those reports within six hours, and bans on features such as cosmetic procedure image filters and the display of the numbers of likes on posts. Earlier this year, Meta suffered additional losses in court over claims it created addictive products that harmed young Americans.

Full text of the bill can be found here.

Congressman DeSaulnier is a senior member of the House Committee on Education & Workforce and a longtime advocate for consumer safety and the health and wellbeing of young people, having sponsored legislation to hold e-cigarette companies accountable for their role in the youth vaping crisis and to increase access to supports, services, and resources for children, students, workers, and families by strengthening school-based behavioral health care, bolstering mental health parity protections, and ensuring access to mental health and substance use disorder benefits for workers and families.

title: Dexter, Ruiz Condemn Lack of Due Process for Imprisoned Palestinian Pediatrician Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya and Demand His Release by Netanyahu’s Government
text:
Lawmakers: “We write with urgent concern about the life-threatening conditions facing Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, a Palestinian pediatrician being badly mistreated in Israeli custody.”

Netanyahu’s government has filed no formal charges against Dr. Abu Safiya, nor has he received a trial.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03), and Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. (CA-25), led 69 of their colleagues in calling on U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to engage his counterparts in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government to secure the release of imprisoned Palestinian pediatrician Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya. The lawmakers emphasized the lack of due process afforded to Dr. Abu Safiya, who has yet to receive formal charges, and highlighted his worsening physical condition.

“We write with urgent concern about the life-threatening conditions facing Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, a Palestinian pediatrician being badly mistreated in Israeli custody,” the lawmakers wrote. “As recently as last month, Dr. Abu Safiya’s lawyer warned that his physical condition had deteriorated to the point of near-death.”

Dr. Abu Safiya is the longtime director of Kamal Adwan hospital in Gaza City. During the war in Gaza, he played a critical role in providing wounded civilians with vital medical care. Among his most notable contributions was the construction of a malnutrition unit that treated hundreds of children.

On December 27, 2024, Dr. Abu Safiya was arrested while on duty at his hospital and remains in Israeli custody. No formal charges were ever presented against him, and to this day, he has yet to receive a trial.

“For over 18 months, Dr. Abu Safiya has languished in Israeli jails, including an underground facility previously shut down due to the poor conditions its detainees faced,” the lawmakers continued. “According to his lawyer, authorities have repeatedly denied him adequate access to medical care, food and toiletries, causing him to lose significant weight.”

On July 2, 2026, Dr. Abu Safiya’s lawyer visited him in jail and found that the severity of his injuries had rendered him nearly unrecognizable. His body bore fresh bruises, and he struggled to remain conscious. The lawmakers urged Secretary Rubio to do everything in the Trump Administration’s power to free Dr. Abu Safiya before he dies in custody.

The letter is cosigned in the House by 66 Members.

The letter is cosigned in the Senate by 3 Senators.

title: Fischbach, Minnesota Republican Delegation Confront Walz on recent Minnesota Fraud Report
text:
Washington, DC - Congresswoman Michelle Fischbach (MN-07), Congressman Tom Emmer (MN-06), Congressman Pete Stauber (MN-08), joined Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) in sending a letter to Governor Walz on the recent findings of more fraud in Minnesota, this time involving a Liberian government official who is connected to at least two dozen Minnesota group homes that have collected $36 million of taxpayer funds over the last ten years.

“Minnesotans work hard for their money, and they have every right to expect that their tax dollars are supporting vulnerable families, not being lost to fraud due to a lack of state oversight,” said Rep. Fischbach. “The Walz Administration has shown a complete lack of accountability. Minnesotans deserve answers and corrective action to protect their tax dollars.”

To address the oversight failures highlighted by cases like this, Congresswoman Fischbach recently introduced the Federal Funds Whistleblower Protection Extension Act. The legislation stops whistleblower retaliation that often prevents fraud reporting by extending federal protections to state and local government employees, contractors, and subcontractors. Her bill follows a House Oversight Committee hearing where Minnesota State Representatives confirmed there are currently no criminal penalties for government officials who retaliate against individuals who speak out about fraud. The legislation would make it a federal crime for any state official who knowingly tries to ruin a whistleblower's life to protect a political narrative, with penalties of up to five years in federal prison.

Background

Recently, a Minnesota news outlet released the findings of its investigation into several group homes with reports of neglect and even investigations into the deaths of several residents. At the center of this investigation is Sekou Dukuly, a man who relocated to Africa from Minnesota in 2024 to become the director of Liberia’s government-owned port system while remaining the director of three Minnesota group homes.

title: Reps. Foushee, Thompson Lead Opposition to Removal of Bike Safety Resources and Bike Safety Project Funding
text:
WASHINGTON, DC (September 10, 2026) — Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) and Congressman Mike Thompson (CA-04) sent a letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) Administrator Sean McMaster opposing the removal of programs for road safety, specifically those mentioning bike safety.

In the letter, the Congressmembers wrote, “The U.S. is experiencing a roadway safety crisis, with more than 36,000 people killed on our streets in 2025. One in five traffic deaths is a person walking or biking. Since 2010, bicyclist fatalities in the U.S. have risen by 87 percent.”

“The removal of several PSCM related to protecting vulnerable road users coincides with the USDOT’s recent cancellation of grants that include bicycling facilities and stated intention to limit funding for bike lanes within the Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development (BUILD) Grant Program. Ignoring multimodal transportation networks, rejecting projects that prioritize the safety of people biking and walking, and eliminating funding for bike lanes goes against the express congressional intent for these funding sources. Furthermore, DOT’s actions only make our roads less safe for American families,” continued the lawmakers. “We therefore strongly urge you to restore all PSCM pages recently removed from the FHWA website, as well as funding eligibility for bike projects within BUILD and any other grant program for which they are eligible. Please provide us with a written response to explain the Administration’s rationale, your process for these actions, and how these actions support the Department’s mission to “Advance safety.””

The letter was signed by 28 Democratic lawmakers, including: Reps. Rick Larsen (WA-02), Sharice Davids (KS-03), Betty McCollum (MN-04), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Jake Auchincloss (MA-04), Gwen Moore (WI-04), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Andre Carson (IN-07), Dina Titus (NV-01), Ed Case (HI-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Dave Min (CA-47), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Jim Himes (CT-04), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Steve Cohen (TN-09), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) and Sara Jacobs (CA-51).

“My granddaughter Allie was just five years old when she was killed riding her bike through a crosswalk near her home,” said Philip Hart, a Durham resident and constituent of Rep. Foushee. “Every proven safety countermeasure removed from FHWA's website risks costing lives that could otherwise have been saved. Families for Safe Streets was founded by people who buried loved ones killed by dangerous road design — we know firsthand that these aren't abstract policy debates, they're the difference between a child making it home from school on a bike lane and a family getting a knock on the door. We're grateful to Representatives Thompson and Foushee for standing up for the data-backed tools that save lives, and we urge the Department of Transportation to restore this guidance and the funding that puts it into practice.”

“Bike lanes, road diets, and speed management are called Proven Safety Countermeasures because the evidence is clear: they work to improve safety for everyone. Whether you are walking, biking, taking transit, or in a car, these are safety interventions that save lives. Removing these Proven Safety Countermeasures from engineers' and planners' toolbox signals that this administration is putting political whims over the safety of Americans,” said Bill Nesper, Executive Director of the League of American Bicyclists.

“Rails To Trails Conservancy thanks Representatives Foushee and Thompson for their leadership organizing this letter and standing up for the vast majority of Americans who support trails, walking, and biking infrastructure. Removing the proven safety countermeasures endangers bicyclists, pedestrians, and drivers, and denies decades of research and experience in all types of American communities. By limiting funding for bicycle projects through the BUILD program, USDOT is undercutting bipartisan Congressional intent and denying Americans the infrastructure they need to safely and affordably get where they need to go,” said Scott Goldstein, Senior Director of Government Relations of Rails To Trails Conservancy.

“One of The 6 E’s of Safe Routes to School is evaluation: using evidence-based strategies to improve safety and get kids and families where they need to go. Proven Safety Countermeasures have been rigorously evaluated to show they keep kids and families safe on our roadways,” said Marisa Jones, Executive Director of Safe Routes Partnership. “We encourage FHWA to follow the evidence on what keeps kids and communities safe, and reinstate all Proven Safety Countermeasures. No family should mourn the death of a child on our roadways over the politics of transportation modes. Communities need every tool available to them to make American streets safer for kids and families.”

title: Evans’ Bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act Set for House Vote
text:
WASHINGTON — Gabe Evans’ bipartisan legislation protecting ratepayers from rising costs associated with the increased energy demand will receive a vote next week — marking one of the final bills to be considered by the House prior to the midterm elections.

The bill ensures American families are not left footing the bill for the grid upgrades and new energy generation required to operate large data centers. More specifically, it requires state utility regulators, like the Colorado Public Utilities Commission, to consider implementing rules for large-load data centers and hyperscalers to cover the full costs of power generation, transmission lines, and other energy infrastructure upgrades needed to meet their immense energy demand. Without this bill, families and small businesses in communities where data center development occurs could see higher electricity bills at the end of every month.

The Ratepayer Protection Act was introduced amid our nation’s increasing energy needs and heightened scrutiny regarding how data centers affect consumer costs. The legislation has gained significant bipartisan support with 41 cosponsors in the House and it unanimously passed the Energy and Commerce Committee in July by a vote of 52-0.

“This bill coming to the House Floor proves that House Republicans are responding to the needs of the American people. As the United States competes to win the global AI race and outcompete adversaries like Communist China, we must ensure that growth does not come at the expense of hardworking families. I’m proud to lead the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act to keep energy affordable and ensure American innovation can move forward without leaving families and small businesses to foot the bill.” — Congressman Gabe Evans

Background

If enacted, the legislation would establish a federal standard for state regulators to consider when reviewing proposals for new large-load customers with an electricity demand of 100 megawatts or more to come onto the grid. The bill recommends:

Requiring financial assurances that large-load customers will pay for the generation, transmission, and other infrastructure necessary to serve their demand, preventing those costs from being shifted onto families and local businesses through higher electricity rates.

Recovering the full incremental cost of grid upgrades from the large-load customer over time through special rate structures or other agreements, ensuring utilities and existing ratepayers are not left paying for infrastructure if a customer later scales back operations or leaves the system.

The Ratepayer Protection Act builds on the principles of President Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge, under which major data center developers, utilities, and governors committed to covering the full energy and infrastructure costs associated with new data center development.

title: Evans, Peters Unveil Bill to Address Transmission Project Bottlenecks and Lower Electricity Costs
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Gabe Evans (R-CO) and Scott Peters (D-CA) introduced the Certainty in Litigation for Electric Asset Reliability (CLEAR) Act of 2026, legislation to streamline the buildout of big power line projects. The CLEAR Act would fix the legislative ambiguity that currently leaves Department of Energy (DOE)-coordinated transmission projects prone to excessive litigation and outright obstructionism that can stall critical infrastructure development, kill jobs, and drive up costs for utility ratepayers.

“As America’s demand for energy continues to rise, it is crucial that we find new and innovative ways to successfully transfer power in an affordable, safe and timely manner. The CLEAR Act will boost energy production, cut red tape and expedite project timelines, and reduce costs related to transmission projects across our country. I’m proud to help lead this important legislation, and look forward to continuing to prioritize permitting reform as I work to make energy and life more affordable for Coloradans and our nation.” — Congressman Gabe Evans

"Californians pay some of the highest electricity rates in the country, and part of the reason is that we can't get transmission projects through the litigation process and built on time. Our grid is too old and too slow to meet our skyrocketing energy demand. We can't wait years for badly needed infrastructure to be built. The CLEAR Act would accelerate the review process for large energy infrastructure projects and establish clear rules for stalled transmission projects, giving developers and local stakeholders the certainty to plan along with relief for ratepayers from rising costs." — Congressman Scott Peters

The CLEAR Act would align judicial review standards for DOE-coordinated transmission projects with those already used for hydropower and natural gas pipelines under the Federal Power Act, ensuring projects are built on time, without unnecessary legal delays.

The Federal Power Act governs the regulation of electricity and interstate power lines and empowers the DOE to act as a coordinating entity between Federal agencies, states, and local governments responsible for siting and permitting transmission lines. However, for DOE-coordinated transmission projects, parties have up to six years to sue, which drags cases through multiple, lengthy legal battles. This leads to confusion and uncertainty for companies who want to plan and invest with confidence, or local stakeholders who want to engage efficiently in the review process.

For example, the North Plains Connector, a proposed 420-mile, high-voltage transmission line connecting the western and eastern electric grids—currently subject to lengthy deadlines — has dealt with unpredictable litigation timelines under the Federal Power Act.

Under the CLEAR Act, projects would have to follow Federal Power Act judicial review standards, including:

A 120-day statute of limitations for filing suit

A requirement that petitioners participate in the environmental review process before litigating, improving upfront engagement and making projects better during the review process, instead of on the back end; and

Direct elevation of challenges to the U.S. Court of Appeals, ensuring stakeholders can reach a final decision faster

Read a one-pager here. Read bill text here.

Background:

As leaders of the Problem Solvers Caucus’ Permitting Energy & Environment Working Group, and members of the House Energy and Environment Committee, Reps. Evans and Peters have led several major bipartisan efforts in Congress to overhaul and streamline the federal permitting process for energy and infrastructure projects.

title: Rep. Gabe Evans, Acting United States Secretary of Labor, Keith Sonderling, Highlight Colorado’s Manufacturing and Skilled Workforce
text:
DENVER, CO — Congressman Gabe Evans welcomed Acting U.S. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling back to Colorado’s Eighth Congressional District for two site visits and workforce roundtables highlighting the manufacturers, skilled trades, truckers, and small businesses powering Northern Colorado’s economy.

The visit comes just days after the August jobs report showed the U.S. economy added 162,000 jobs—tripling expectations—while unemployment remained steady at 4.1 percent.

“Hardworking Coloradans are leading America’s manufacturing comeback. The August jobs report tripled expectations, American manufacturing is growing, and right here in CO-08, businesses are ready to hire and workers are ready to work.

I’m proud to partner with Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling to highlight Colorado’s entrepreneurs, skilled tradesmen and women, and frontline workforce that are the backbone of our economy and our communities. These conversations are essential to ensuring we find ways to strengthen and support our skilled workforce, and continue bringing high-paying jobs back to the United States.” –– Congressman Gabe Evans

“America runs on trucking. Companies like JFW Trucking keep our supply chains moving, support local economies, and create pathways to the American Dream for hardworking Americans. I appreciated the opportunity to join Congressman Evans and the Colorado Industrial Property Owners Consortium to hear directly about what it takes to keep trucks on the road and how the Trump Administration can continue to help small businesses grow.

America will need an estimated 300,000 new electricians over the next decade — and apprenticeships are how we meet that demand. Congressman Evans and I met with apprentices and IECRM leadership to discuss expanding apprenticeships to train more Americans faster and with zero debt for the jobs powering America’s Industrial Renaissance.” — Acting Secretary Keith Sonderling

Congressman Gabe Evans and Sonderling began the day in Commerce City at JFW Trucking, a family-owned Colorado company with roots dating back to 1935. Following a tour of the facility, Evans and Sonderling joined members of the Industrial Property Owners Consortium (IPOC) for the first workforce roundtable of the day.

The discussion brought together Colorado business and industrial leaders to talk directly with Evans and Sonderling about the challenges facing employers and what it will take to continue growing Colorado’s industrial and manufacturing economy.

The second stop took Rep. Evans and Sonderling to Independent Electrical Contractors Rocky Mountain (IECRM) in Northglenn, where they toured one of the country’s largest electrical apprenticeship training programs before hosting a second roundtable with apprentices, instructors, contractors, and industry leaders.

IECRM trains thousands of apprentices and licensed electricians each year, helping prepare Coloradans for careers in high-demand industries—new manufacturing facilities, housing, data centers, energy infrastructure, and other major projects being built across the state.

Background

Colorado’s Eighth District has become an important hub for manufacturing, energy, construction, and advanced technology, while major investments across northern Colorado are creating new demand for skilled workers.

Nationally, that momentum is reflected in the latest employment numbers. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported manufacturing employment increased by 16,000 in August, including gains in machinery and fabricated metal products. Manufacturing employment has increased by 58,000 since December 2025.

Acting Secretary Sonderling said that manufacturing and construction have now added jobs for three consecutive months following the release of the August report.

Wednesday marked Sonderling’s second workforce-focused visit to Colorado’s Eighth District with Evans. In July 2025, Evans welcomed then-Deputy Secretary Sonderling to Aims Community College in Fort Lupton for a tour and roundtable focused on artificial intelligence, workforce training, and preparing students for the jobs of the future.

A year later, Evans and Sonderling returned to CO-08 as Colorado helps lead the nation’s manufacturing comeback — this time taking the conversation directly to the businesses, workers, and apprentices building it.

title: Gallagher Introduces Bill to Strengthen Drone Safety as Airspace Risks Rise
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) and Congresswoman Dina Titus (NV-01) together introduced H.R. 10304, the Drone Safety Statement Modernization Act, legislation to make sure drone operators know the rules before they take off. The bill would modernize federal safety requirements as drones become increasingly common in America’s skies.

“When a wildfire is burning, our firefighters should be focused on putting it out, not worrying about a drone getting in their flight path. We’ve already seen aerial firefighting operations delayed or grounded because drones were in the airspace over the Dixie and Palisades Fires,” Rep. Gallagher said. “Firefighters need to reach these fires in their early stages and launch air attacks without interruption. This bill ensures drone operators know the rules before they take off and is a commonsense step in keeping our skies and firefighters safe.”

"The Drone Safety Statement Modernization Act will help Southern Nevada prepare for major events like Formula One and the Super Bowl," said Congresswoman Dina Titus (NV-01). "This legislation would require drone operators to receive the most-up-to-date safety information on this quickly evolving technology. As Co-Chair of the Congressional Unmanned Systems Caucus, one of my top priorities is maintaining the United States's global leadership in the development and deployment of unmanned systems while also keeping our skies and communities safe. This legislation does just that."

The legislation would require small drone manufacturers to provide operators with up to date safety information when a drone is first activated and require the operator to acknowledge that they have read and understand it. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) would be responsible for developing and regularly updating the safety requirements.

The danger is not hypothetical. A single drone in restricted airspace can ground firefighting aircraft and delay critical operations while a wildfire continues to burn. During the 2025 Palisades Fire, a civilian drone collided with a water-dropping Super Scooper, leaving a football-sized hole in its wing and grounding the aircraft.

Read more about the Palisades Fire incident

“Flying a drone comes with a responsibility to know where you can fly and how to do it safely," Rep. Gallagher continued. "We've seen what can happen when a drone gets somewhere it shouldn't be. It can put pilots in danger and even force firefighters out of the sky when every second matters. This bill is pretty simple: know the rules before you take off."

Unauthorized drones have also created challenges around major events. During the 2026 FIFA World Cup, federal authorities seized more than 700 unauthorized drones operating in restricted airspace across 11 U.S. host cities. The FAA established nearly 250 temporary flight restrictions as part of the security operation.

Read the FAA’s World Cup report

Under the Drone Safety Statement Modernization Act, safety statements would provide operators with information about applicable flight rules and airspace restrictions, as well as how to determine whether a flight is lawful. Operators would also receive information about the potential consequences of unsafe or unlawful drone operations.

The bill directs the FAA to review the safety requirements annually and update them when necessary to keep pace with changing technology and airspace risks.

title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Testifies on Her Bills to Clean Up Congress
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Last week, Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez attended a hearing held by the House Committee on Rules to advocate for changes to House rules for next Congress. She urged the committee to enact a number of reforms within the U.S. House of Representatives. Among these reforms were an effort to create cognitive standards for members of the House, to form a Select Committee to explore Electoral Reform options, allow for remote committee testimonies, and to expand the code of conduct to ban Members of Congress from sleeping with House staff.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez testifies in front of the Rules Committee

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez opened her testimony asking committee members to consider the adoption of her BRIDGE to Congress Resolution to allow remote witness testimony at Congressional hearings. The Congresswoman noted that for too long everyday people and people who live far from the Capitol face significant burdens in coming to DC to speak in front of their representatives. This provision hopes to bring local issues into committee spotlights and reduce the influence of lobbyists and paid policy professionals.

“For a constituent in Southwest Washington, testifying in person can mean taking time off work, finding child or elder care, and paying for a plane ticket and hotel in Washington, D.C. Most working families I know simply can’t afford that,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “The result is a witness pool that lacks geographic, economic, and lived-experience diversity. Instead of hearing directly from a fisherman in Pacific County or a shop teacher in Skamania County, Congress gets a feedback-loop from people paid to discuss policy. That leads to bad policy and erodes public trust.”

The Congresswoman continued her testimony by urging the adoption of her resolution establishing a bipartisan Select Committee on Electoral Reform. Throughout her time in congress, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez has pursued options for making Congress a more representative body to the average American. The Electoral Reform Select Committee Act was the first piece of legislation she introduced in the 119th Congress. If formed, the bipartisan Select Committee would investigate options such as multi-member districts with proportional representation, expanding the House, and independent redistricting commissions to improve the responsibility members of Congress have to their constituents.

“Regardless of party or ideology, more and more Americans feel that our democracy isn’t working for them. Americans feel unrepresented and are losing faith in a government that they view as unreflective of their communities and values.” Said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “As Members of Congress, we need to take a step back, reexamine how we got here, and work toward what we can do to fix it.”

Video of the Congresswoman’s remarks can be found here:

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez continued her testimony by reminding the committee that accountability and trust in Congress demands they take action on the instances of sexual misconduct that have plagued this Congress.

“This is about trust, accountability, and not giving powerful people a free pass to continue perpetuating a culture of sexual assault and misconduct. Americans deserve to know that their elected officials are held to high standards–and that their representatives are hellbent on making this institution work better for the American people,” Said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “As members, we are here to work – not date. The next rules package should include a code of conduct that prohibits Members of Congress from having sexual relationships with House staff, no matter where that staffer works—whether in another Member’s personal office, a committee, or a caucus.”

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez ended her testimony by once again raising her mental acuity standards provision to her colleagues in the House. She has made repeated efforts to urge the Office of Congressional Conduct to create a standard of conduct as it relates to members suffering from significant and irreversible cognitive decline. Recently she offered this provision in the Appropriations Committee as an amendment to the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act. The amendment failed overwhelmingly, with Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez casting the only yes vote on the entire committee.

“Americans elect Members of Congress to be their voice in Washington, and that responsibility comes with a clear standard of conduct. Clause 1 of Rule XXIII of the Rules of the House requires Members to ‘behave at all times in a manner that shall reflect creditably on the House.’” Said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “When a Member is no longer able to fulfill the responsibilities of the office because of a significant and irreversible cognitive impairment, and unelected staff are effectively running the office on that Member’s behalf, we have to establish a process to evaluate and address it.”

title: Congressman Dan Goldman Presents $354,000 Grant Award to Kings County District Attorney’s Office
text:
New York, NY - U.S. Representative Dan Goldman (NY-10) presented the Kings County District Attorney’s Office with a $354,000 Community Project funding award. The award will be used to bolster the Outreach and Assistance Response (SOAR) program. The program is designed to conduct immediate outreach to violent crime victims and their families.

Rep. Goldman requested and secured funding for the project, which was included in a package of bills to fund the federal government. Goldman secured $13,756,000 for 15 community projects in NY-10 in the FY 2026 appropriations process.

Rep. Goldman presented the award to Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez.

“Violent crime often leaves lasting trauma for victims and their families, who benefit greatly from immediate assistance,” said Congressman Dan Goldman. “I am proud to have secured $354,000 to fund the Kings County District Attorney’s Office’s program that does just that – from financial help to mental health assistance.. Thank you to District Attorney Gonzalez for his leadership on this issue to provide Brooklyn families with the respect and care they deserve."

Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said, “While Brooklyn is experiencing a public safety renaissance with historic lows in homicides and shootings, there are still too many families dealing with the trauma of a shooting, an assault or the loss of a loved one. And even when there has not yet been an arrest or a criminal case, victims and families may need immediate support. The new SOAR program will offer just that and fill gaps that traditional compensation programs cannot always cover, allowing our counselors to assist and stand with every victim of serious violence and their families. I am grateful for Congressman Dan Goldman who secured the grant that will allow us to launch this important initiative.”

Kings County District Attorney’s SOAR (Support Outreach and Assistance Response) conducts outreach and provides support to victims of violent assaults and homicides regardless of whether anyone has been arrested for the crime. Typically the victim’s services staff in a DA’s office only comes into contact with a victim once an arrest has been made and a case generated. The SOAR team responds to violent crimes even when there is no case in the DA’s office. The response team provides assistance with victim compensation, counseling, and relevant case related information. The SOAR team also engages in community outreach to inform the public of KCDA’s services and commitment to public safety.

Immediately following a violent incident or homicide, usually within the first 24 to 48 hours, SOAR counselors work with the NYC Police Department to obtain contact information of survivors or surviving family members. In cases where other agencies or organizations, such as the offices of elected officials or community-based organizations, have already had contact with the victim or family, SOAR counselors work with those agencies to ensure a warm handoff from those organizations to our experts in trauma, crime victim’s rights, and criminal justice.

The funds will assist with building the SOAR team by covering the salary for a program coordinator and four new staff members dedicated to the program.

title: Goldman Leads More Than 200 Members in Bipartisan Resolution Marking 25th Anniversary of September 11th Attacks
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Dan Goldman (NY-10), a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, introduced a bipartisan resolution recognizing the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, honoring the 2,977 innocent lives lost, and reaffirming the nation’s commitment to never forget.

The resolution is co-led by Representatives Andrew Garbarino (NY-2), Mike Lawler (NY-17), and Jerry Nadler (NY-12) and is cosponsored by more than 200 Members of the House of Representatives.

“As we approach the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks, our commitment to honoring the courage and sacrifice demonstrated by so many brave Americans endures. I am honored to co-lead this resolution, which not only commemorates the sacrifice of the 2,977 lives lost that tragic day, but reaffirms our obligation to those who continue to suffer from illnesses caused by the attacks. May we never forget it,” said Congressman Goldman.

“Twenty-five years later, the impact of September 11th is still deeply personal for New Yorkers and for families across our country,” said Congressman Garbarino. “We remember the 2,977 innocent lives taken from us, the first responders who ran toward danger, and the thousands we have lost in the years since to 9/11-related illnesses, as well as those who continue to suffer today. I am proud that more than 200 of my colleagues have joined together to honor their sacrifice and reaffirm a promise that must endure for generations: we will never forget.”

“On a clear September morning with an unusually blue sky, our nation was attacked. And our community was forever changed. In Congress, I have worked to make sure the Hudson Valley, and our nation, never forgets. Twenty-five years later, we remember the lives we lost, the heroes we honor, and the duty that remains: care for the living, teach the next generation, and never forget,” said Congressman Lawler.

“25 years ago, New Yorkers and Americans across our nation experienced the deepest tragedy. 2,977 lives were lost, thousands were injured, and many more were sickened. We will never forget the lives we lost, and we must continue to serve those who have been afflicted from the toxic air at Ground Zero and in their homes, schools, and offices. We thank the first responders and everyday citizens who committed incredible acts of heroism, and we promise to honor their legacy by never forgetting their sacrifice,” said Congressman Nadler.

The resolution honors the victims killed at the World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, as well as the extraordinary courage of the first responders, members of the Armed Forces, passengers and crew of United Airlines Flight 93, medical professionals, rescue and recovery workers, volunteers, and countless others who responded to the attacks and their aftermath.

It also recognizes the lasting consequences of September 11th for responders and survivors who continue to suffer from 9/11-related illnesses and acknowledges the organizations that have spent the past 25 years supporting survivors and victims’ families.

The resolution further recognizes the service and sacrifice of the members of the Armed Forces who defended the United States in the years following the attacks and emphasizes the importance of teaching future generations the history and lessons of September 11th.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Claws Back More than $1.7 Million in Federal Security Funding for NJ Houses of Worship
text:
Above: Gottheimer visits Bris Avrohom of Fair Lawn ahead of the High Holidays.

NORTH JERSEY — Today, September 10, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced $1.7 million clawed-back for eight nonprofit organizations across North Jersey for Fiscal Year 2025 Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) funding, delivering critical resources to help churches, synagogues, temples, and faith-based schools in the Fifth District protect their communities from the growing threat of hate and violence. Gottheimer also announced the funding at Bris Avrohom of Fair Lawn and visited Rabbi Mendel Zaltzman and Rabbi Mordechai Kanelsky ahead of the High Holidays.

See video of Gottheimer’s visit here.

Gottheimer also hosted a briefing with the New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness (NJOHSP) and Jewish faith leaders from across North Jersey to address the security threats facing the Jewish community as they prepare for the High Holidays. The meeting brought together NJOHSP Director Hauck, state leadership, and Jewish faith leaders to discuss the current threat landscape, coordination between law enforcement and religious institutions, and the urgent need to deliver federal security resources to houses of worship — the very resources this NSGP funding provides.

Gottheimer has been pushing for the long-delayed resources, passed in 2024, to be distributed after clawing it back for the district. The Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP), administered by the U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), provides funding to nonprofits at high risk of terrorist attacks or hate-related incidents, with a particular focus on houses of worship and other faith-based institutions like schools and community centers. The funding allows organizations to invest in physical security upgrades like cameras, gates, bollards, and blast-resistant film, and to provide training that helps staff and congregants recognize and respond to threats.

Anti-Jewish hate crimes account for nearly two-thirds of all religion-based hate crimes reported to the FBI nationwide. Antisemitic incidents in the United States have increased by 68% since 2022, before October 7. In 2025, ADL recorded 6,274 antisemitic incidents across the United States. That means Jewish Americans were targeted an average of 17 times per day. New Jersey recorded the third-highest total of antisemitic incidents across the nation in 2025, with Bergen County ranking first in highest rates of antisemitic incidents in New Jersey.

Gottheimer has been a vocal advocate for this vital funding to be distributed. Last year, Gottheimer led a bipartisan group of 78 colleagues in urging the Administration to reverse its decision to pause the drawdown of federal grant funding at FEMA, which includes the Nonprofit Security Grant Program.

“No one should ever have to worry about their safety while praying, learning, or gathering with their community,” said Congressman Gottheimer (NJ-5). “With hate crimes and antisemitic incidents spiking at historical levels, this funding is crucial. It gives our religious communities the resources they need to strengthen their security and protect the people who walk through their doors every day. I’ll keep fighting in Washington to make sure North Jersey’s nonprofits and religious institutions get every dollar they need to stay safe.”

The following North Jersey organizations were awarded funding:

Bris Avrohom of Fair Lawn (Fair Lawn) — $380,000

Young Israel of Fort Lee (Fort Lee) — $190,000

Grace Redeemer Church (Glen Rock) — $190,000

Hindu Samaj Temple of Mahwah (Mahwah) — $175,750

The Frisch School (Paramus) — $380,000

The Church Gathered and Scattered (Teaneck) — $95,000

The Young Israel of Teaneck (Teaneck) — $190,000

Temple Emanuel of the Pascack Valley (Woodcliff Lake) — $190,000

Gottheimer will continue working in Congress to protect and expand funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program and push FEMA for faster turnaround and greater transparency so that at-risk organizations can plan and receive their security investments with confidence.

title: Congresswoman Gwen Moore Visits Midwest Regional Reception to Conduct Welfare Check on Constituents
text:
Yesterday, Congresswoman Gwen Moore (WI-04) visited the U.S. Immigration and Custom Enforcement’s (ICE) Midwest Regional Reception Center in Leavenworth, Kansas to conduct a welfare check on her constituents. At this facility, individuals detained have reported numerous instances of abuse and neglect.

Two of her constituents are detained here after being caught up in ICE’s reckless surge in Milwaukee earlier this summer. At that time, Congresswoman Gwen Moore held a press conference in Milwaukee condemning ICE’s reckless, escalating presence in Milwaukee and its excessive force on residents.

After her recent visit to the ICE facility in Kansas, she held a conference with immigration rights advocates from Milwaukee and Kansas to discuss what she saw and heard.

As part of her oversight responsibilities, Congresswoman Moore has traveled to ICE detention facilities across the nation to check on her constituents’ safety and well-being. She released the following statement:

“While I was relieved that my constituents are being treated with dignity and respect, I was puzzled as to why these women were detained in the first place. Then I learned about the massive profit machine driving detainments of individuals with no criminal records.

The Trump administration isn’t targeting violent criminals, but anyone they choose, while private companies are getting rich and taxpayers foot the bill. That’s why I will continue these important oversight responsibilities. I thank advocates from Milwaukee and Kansas for bringing my attention to this facility and my constituents who are being detained,” said Congresswoman Moore, (WI-04).

“We thank Congresswoman Moore for her leadership in protecting the rights of immigrants like her constituents, Estenderly Marte Polanco and Reyna Elizabeth Garcia, and for using congressional oversight to hold ICE and the Department of Homeland Security accountable. ICE is using excessive force, separating families, and spending billions of taxpayer dollars on immigration enforcement. The American people deserve to know how that money is being spent and how companies like CoreCivic are profiting from a system that harms immigrant families and communities. It was an honor to stand with Congresswoman Moore and community partners in Kansas and Missouri to demand the reunification of families, the closure of these modern-day concentration camps, and humane immigration reform,” said Christine Neumann-Ortiz, Executive Director, Voces de la Frontera.

"As an immigrant myself, I was lucky enough to enter the United States over 40 years ago, as a white European, without having to go through the harrowing experience our immigrant neighbors of color are facing now. I am from Germany, and I am worried and horrified that my adopted country is going down the same slippery slope that my country of origin did in the 1930s and 40s. I would like to ask our elected officials to come and regularly visit their constituents in this ICE detention center, and ask them to call for the closure of this detention center," said Angelika Schafer with Advocates for Immigrant Rights and Reconciliation (AIRR).

About the Facility

Last month, the Midwest Regional Reception Center, owned by CoreCivic, was sold to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for $238 million. CoreCivic reported $684 million in revenue in the spring quarter, a dramatic spike in revenue from last year. In an earnings call, the CEO of CoreCivic said that selling several of its detention facilities generated $1.6 billion, amounting to $307,000 per bed. During the press conference, Congresswoman Moore drew attention to how much profitability is motivating reckless ICE operations across the country.

title: Congressman Hamadeh Condemns Iranian-Backed Houthis for Seizing Red Sea Port
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Abraham Hamadeh (AZ-08) condemns the Iranian-backed Houthis and is calling for swift action in response to their terroristic seizure of the port of Mocha.

“The seizure of the strategic port of Mocha in the Red Sea by the Iranian-backed Houthi terrorists from Yemeni control is a direct assault on regional security, freedom of navigation, and the global economy. The Houthis are an armed extension of the Islamic Republic of Iran. The seizure of this port puts Saudi Arabia directly in harm’s way and we must stand with our allies in the region,” sated Congressman Hamadeh. “The Houthis must face decisive consequences, and Tehran must understand that the era of attacking America and our allies through proxies is over. America First doesn't mean America alone.

Congressman Hamadeh, a former U.S. Army Intelligence Officer, knows first-hand the ravages committed by the Houthi terrorists from his service time in Saudi Arabia. In 2021, then-Captain Hamadeh was deployed to the Middle East when the Houthis conducted multiple high-profile attacks against civilian Saudi Arabian and coalition targets in the Gulf.

In February 2025, Congressman Hamadeh introduced H.R. 1250, requiring the imposition of sanctions with respect to the officials, agents, or affiliates of Ansarallah, commonly known as the Houthis, for acts of international terrorism.

In April 2025, Congressman Hamadeh reached across the aisle to work with Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) to introduce the Promoting Education on the Abraham Accords for Comprehensive Engagement (PEACE) Act, which will strengthen U.S. diplomatic engagement by institutionalizing training on the Abraham Accords and other normalization agreements at the U.S. State Department.

BACKGROUND

"Yemen's Tehran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in the south of U.S. ally Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding more than 70 people and setting oil installations ablaze in what appeared to be a major expansion of the six-month-old Middle East war," reported USAToday. "The Houthis, who control most of Yemen's populated areas including the capital, said they had launched a broad operation deep into Saudi territory. They used drones and missiles to strike a Saudi airbase in the southern city of Khamis Mushait, and targets belonging to Saudi Arabia's state oil company in nearby Abha, Najran on the Yemeni border, and Jazan, a major Red Sea port city that houses a large refinery and power plant."

title: Harshbarger Introduces Legislation to Fix Outdated FDA Drug Preclusion Rules, Protect Access to Dietary Supplements
text:
“Ambiguous FDA standards can leave manufacturers without guidance and consumers guessing about which products are available,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger. “For decades, this broken drug preclusion process has allowed Washington bureaucrats to threaten lawful dietary supplements that have safely been purchased over the counter for years, stifling innovation and denying Americans access to products they already trust. My bill delivers the regulatory certainty manufacturers need to innovate and invest with confidence, while establishing transparency and predictability within the drug preclusion framework and preserving consumer access to dietary supplements.”

“Representative Harshbarger has introduced exactly the kind of thoughtful, balanced legislation this issue has needed for years,” said Steve Mister, President & CEO of the Council for Responsible Nutrition. “This bill doesn't weaken FDA or undermine pharmaceutical innovation. Instead, it restores the balance Congress intended when it enacted DSHEA by creating evenhanded, transparent, or predictable rules that allow both industries to innovate while protecting consumer access to safe dietary supplements. We commend Representative Harshbarger for her leadership and strongly urge Congress to advance this legislation.”

“We applaud Representative Harshbarger for introducing this important legislation, which modernizes an outdated provision of law, provides much-needed regulatory certainty, and helps ensure consumer access keeps pace with innovation,” said Consumer Healthcare Products Association (CHPA) President and CEO Scott Melville.

title: Comisionado se opone a cambio propuesto a Medicare que podría dificultar aún más el acceso a servicios médicos en Puerto Rico
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente, Pablo José Hernández, expresó su oposición, mediante unacarta enviada a los Centros de Servicios de Medicare y Medicaid (CMS), a una propuesta que podría dificultar aún más el acceso a servicios médicos para pacientes en Puerto Rico.

La propuesta reduciría en 50% el pago a médicos por ciertas evaluaciones realizadas el mismo día que un procedimiento. Hernández advirtió que este cambio podría hacer que servicios que actualmente pueden ofrecerse durante una misma visita médica tengan que realizarse en citas separadas.

“En Puerto Rico ya es difícil conseguir una cita médica. No podemos aprobar políticas que hagan el proceso todavía más complicado para nuestros pacientes o que añadan presión a los médicos que queremos mantener en la Isla. Si un paciente puede ser evaluado y recibir un procedimiento necesario en una sola visita, el gobierno federal no debe crear barreras adicionales que lo obliguen a regresar otro día”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Para los pacientes, esto podría significar más viajes, más copagos y más tiempo esperando para recibir atención, particularmente para quienes viven en comunidades donde ya existen dificultades para acceder a médicos y especialistas.

El cambio podría afectar situaciones que surgen durante una misma cita. Por ejemplo, un dermatólogo podría estar evaluando una condición de la piel y detectar durante esa visita una lesión que requiere una biopsia. Bajo la propuesta, el médico recibiría un pago reducido por parte de la evaluación realizada ese mismo día, aun cuando ambos servicios sean distintos y médicamente necesarios.

Hernández señaló que la propuesta también podría añadir presión sobre las prácticas médicas que atienden pacientes de Medicare en Puerto Rico, en un momento en que la Isla ya enfrenta dificultades para mantener y atraer médicos y especialistas.

“Los pacientes no deben cargar con las consecuencias de una política que haga más difícil que los médicos puedan atenderlos en una sola visita cuando eso es clínicamente apropiado. Nuestra prioridad debe ser facilitar el acceso a la atención, no crear nuevas barreras”, añadió Hernández.

La preocupación fue planteada al Comisionado por la Sociedad Dermatológica de Puerto Rico y la Sociedad Puertorriqueña de Oftalmología. Además, Hernández exhorta a las organizaciones médicas, hospitales y ciudadanos, a someter sus comentarios sobre esta propuesta haciendo clic: AQUÍ

title: Hudson Announces 2026 Congressional App Challenge
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Richard Hudson (NC-09) announced the 2026 Congressional App Challenge is open to students in North Carolina’s Ninth District.

“North Carolina’s students have the creativity and talent to build the next generation of technology,” said Rep. Hudson. “The Congressional App Challenge gives them an opportunity to turn an idea into something real. I look forward to seeing this year’s submissions, and I encourage every eligible student in our district to participate, whether they are an experienced coder or just getting started.”

The Congressional App Challenge is the official student Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) competition of the U.S. House of Representatives. The nationwide competition encourages students to explore coding and computer science through hands-on experience creating their own app.

The competition is open to students who are enrolled in middle or high school and live or attend school in North Carolina’s Ninth District. Students may compete individually or in teams of up to four. At least half of the members of a team must live or attend school in the Ninth District. Submissions will be evaluated by a panel of industry professionals from North Carolina’s Ninth District. The winning app will be featured online and may be displayed in the U.S. Capitol.

Students must register and submit their app through CongressionalAppChallenge.us by 12:00 p.m. ET on Monday, October 26, 2026. The official rules and requirements for the 2026 Congressional App Challenge are available here.

title: Hudson Secures New AT&T Service in Continued Push for Better Cell Coverage
text:
SOUTHERN PINES, N.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Richard Hudson (NC-09), Chairman of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology, shares the news of AT&T's expanded wireless service to areas of Moore County following his continued push for better cell service across the community.

“Folks in Moore County have been asking for better cell service, and I’m glad we’re continuing to see progress,” said Rep. Hudson. “This new coverage will help families, businesses, and especially our first responders stay connected when it matters most. I appreciate AT&T working with us after our meeting last month, and I’ll keep working with providers to bring better service to more of our community.”

Beginning Thursday, September 10, AT&T customers will benefit from a new roaming agreement that expands wireless coverage into parts of Moore County where AT&T previously did not provide service. The expanded coverage will serve both AT&T customers and FirstNet subscribers, including first responders who rely on FirstNet to stay connected, especially during emergencies.

This comes just weeks after Hudson met with AT&T officials in Moore County to discuss areas where residents, businesses, and visitors experience weak signal, dropped calls, and unreliable service. Hudson also discussed opportunities to improve connectivity for first responders and other AT&T customers.

Hudson’s work with AT&T follows similar efforts with Verizon. In July, he brought Verizon officials to Moore County to see problem areas firsthand, including a small cell site in Aberdeen and a cell tower near Moore County Airport. In August, Verizon activated the site near Moore County Airport, improving service for customers in the surrounding area.

As Chairman of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology, Hudson will continue working with AT&T, Verizon, and other providers to improve reliable cell service across Moore County and the Ninth District.

title: Huizenga Announces $1.6 Million in New Mental Health Funding for Kalamazoo, Ottawa, and Van Buren Counties
text:
Today, Congressman Bill Huizenga (R-MI) announced that Ottawa County, Van Buren County, and Western Michigan University will receive new grant funding through the Department of Health and Human Services to strengthen mental health services and support substance abuse recovery. These federal grant funds are a direct result of legislation supported by Congressman Huizenga.

“Connecting children, parents, and families across Southwest Michigan with mental health resources creates positive outcomes, strengthens our community, and makes Southwest Michigan an even better place to call home,” said Congressman Bill Huizenga. “I am committed to ensuring that those facing mental health and substance use challenges—some of life’s hardest struggles—have access to the best possible care, support, and resources.”

Western Michigan University in Kalamazoo is being awarded a $599,999 grant for their Family Trauma Assessment of Children and Caregivers work

Ottawa County Community Mental Health in Holland is being awarded a $616,685 grant for mental health & substance abuse services.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES IN DENVER: “PEOPLE ARE DROWNING IN THE TRUMP ECONOMY”
text:
Yesterday, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries spoke to reporters following a roundtable in Denver with Assistant Democratic Leader Joe Neguse (CO-02), local elected officials and members of the Greater Metro Denver Ministerial Alliance about how House Democrats are united in the fight to make life better for everyday Americans and reverse the toxic policies of Donald Trump and extreme MAGA Republicans. Below are excerpts of his remarks during the gaggle and the roundtable.

LEADER JEFFRIES ON THE ROUNDTABLE: We had a wonderful, thoughtful, powerful conversation with the Denver Ministerial Alliance as well as elected officials and community leaders. We discussed a host of issues, including a lot of the challenges that relate to the extremism that’s been unleashed on the people of Colorado and this nation by the Trump administration, including the cuts to Medicaid and SNAP, the attacks on healthcare, the out-of-control ICE activity and the assault on voting rights. I look forward to continuing to stay in close touch with the leadership here in Denver, in the greater Denver area and beyond. I’m so thankful, of course, for Congressman Joe Neguse for extending this invitation to me and for the great work that he continues to do as Assistant Leader in the United States House of Representatives.

LEADER JEFFRIES ON THE AFFORDABILITY CRISIS: We’re committed to addressing the affordability crisis that we know is impacting the people here in Denver and throughout Colorado. Life is far too expensive. There are too many people in this state and across the country who are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive and they can barely survive. The affordability crisis is not a hoax. It is very real. People are drowning in the Trump economy, and we’re committed to lowering the high cost of living in the United States of America. At the same period of time, we’ve seen record levels of corruption be unleashed on the American people. And when you have people in high office, including the President and all of his minions who are part of the Trump cartel, who are so focused on enriching themselves, their family, their friends and their donors, then it means they’re not focused on making life more affordable for the people of Colorado or throughout this great country, and we need to address it.

LEADER JEFFRIES ON ACCOUNTABILITY AGENDA: What we’ve committed to doing is to make sure that beginning on day one, if folks have been stealing from the American people, shortchanging the American people or screwing over the American people, we’re going to hold the crooks accountable. And the effort as it relates to oversight, investigations and accountability, as I’ve indicated, that’s going to be led by Congressman Jamie Raskin and House Judiciary Committee Democrats, including Congressman Joe Neguse as well as Congressman Robert Garcia and House Oversight Committee Democrats. Here’s what we’re going to do: we’re going to follow the facts, we’re going to apply the law, we’re going to be guided by the Constitution and we’re going to let the chips fall where they may in terms of conducting the oversight that is part of being a separate and co-equal branch of government.

LEADER JEFFRIES ON REINING IN ICE: We’ve made clear that Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine doesn’t get a dime, and we’ve done that in the minority…because we think taxpayer dollars should be spent to make life more affordable for the American people, not brutalize or kill American citizens or, finally, target law-abiding immigrant families, including African immigrants.

LEADER JEFFRIES ON RACISM IN POLICYMAKING: Some of what we talked about with some of the African American leaders related to the policy violence that’s going to have a disproportionate impact on the African American community, including the assault on healthcare, the attacks on Medicaid, the dramatic cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, continuing challenges as it relates to the lingering impact of mass incarceration and, of course, just the naked, blatant attack on Black political opportunity as a result of the Supreme Court’s egregious decision in gutting the Voting Rights Act, as well as the attack led by Pete Hegseth, of all people, on diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives, and the adverse impact that has had on Black women in particular. So these were all very incredibly well-articulated, thoughtful, passionate observations and points that were made that I think Congressman Neguse and myself are going to take to heart and take back with us to Washington as we shape public policy into the future.

###

title: Remembering 9/11: Kean Commemorates the 25th Anniversary of the September 11th Terrorist Attacks
text:
(SEPTEMBER 10, 2026) WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) introduced two pieces of legislation to honor the 25th anniversary of the September 11th terrorist attacks.

Congressman Kean said: “September 11th is deeply personal to New Jersey. For families across our state, that day still has a name, a face, an empty chair at the table. Hundreds of our neighbors left home that morning and never came back. Twenty-five years later, we carry their memory with us, along with the courage of the first responders who ran toward danger and the service members who answered the call to defend our country.

“The truth of September 11th is clear. Innocent Americans were murdered in an act of evil against our country and our way of life. Our responsibility is to tell that story with honesty, to honor the people we lost, to stand with the families who still carry that loss, and to make sure every generation understands what happened that day and what followed.

“This package is about fulfilling that responsibility to preserve the firsthand voices of September 11th, honoring the Americans who brought justice to the terrorists responsible in the years that followed, and supporting the victims and families. A quarter-century has passed, but our promise remains the same. We remember them. We honor them. America will never forget.”

The 9/11 Legacy Preservation Act of 2026:

The 9/11 Legacy Preservation Act that Congressman Kean introduced with Representative Don Beyer (VA-08), would direct the Director of the American Folklife Center at the Library of Congress to establish an oral history program to collect video and audio recordings of personal histories from survivors of September 11, 2001.

Read the text of the bill HERE.

The Seal Team Six Congressional Gold Medal Act:

The Seal Team Six Congressional Gold Medal Act would award a Congressional Gold Medal to SEAL Team Six in recognition of their critical role in bringing Osama bin Laden to justice. Congressman Kean introduced the bill with Representatives Madeline Dean (PA-04), Mike Lawler (NY-17), and Bill Keating (MA-09).

Read the text of the bill HERE.

Congressman Kean is also a cosponsor of a resolution to commemorate the 25th anniversary of 9/11 and a resolution to recognize New Jersey’s first responders who carried out rescue, recovery, and medical relief efforts following September 11, 2001.

title: Kennedy Sends Oversight Letter to EPA & Army Corps of Engineers Seeking Answers and Transparency in Ongoing NECRA Project
text:
Kennedy Presses Federal Agencies for Clarity on Contamination, Testing Timeline, Resident Protections, Relocation Assistance, and Financial Impacts on Affected Families

BUFFALO, N.Y. – Congressman Tim Kennedy sent a letter to U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Commanding General Lieutenant General William H. Graham, Jr. to solicit answers on the ongoing Niagara and Erie County Radiological Assessment (NECRA) and the federal government’s role in responding to elevated levels of radioactive material discovered on properties in Niagara and Erie Counties.

“As the elected federal representative of the families directly impacted by this situation, I am deeply concerned that the pace, transparency, and scope of the joint federal and state response have not adequately matched the urgent concerns facing affected residents,” wrote Congressman Kennedy. “These families deserve clear answers, timely action, and confidence that all levels of their government are doing everything possible to protect them.”

Kennedy’s letter comes as affected residents continue to face uncertainty about the safety of their homes, their health, and their financial futures. Kennedy called on EPA and USACE to provide written answers on the scope and pace of the investigation, sampling and laboratory analysis, risk assessments, health and safety protections, temporary relocation assistance, property values, and the origins of the radioactive contamination.

The full text of Kennedy’s letter can be found here.
