title: Congressman Riley M. Moore Presents $1 Million for Watson Fire Station Renovation
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Riley M. Moore presented a $1 million check to City of Fairmont officials in support of Fairmont’s renovation of the Watson Fire Station.

Congressman Riley M. Moore released the following statement:

“Fairmont’s first responders put their lives on the line every day to protect their neighbors. They deserve a facility that ensures they have the tools and resources necessary to do their jobs safely and effectively. I’m proud to have secured this $1 million in federal funding through my work on the House Appropriations Committee to help modernize the Watson Fire Station and ensure Fairmont’s firefighters and EMS personnel have a safe, efficient, and mission-ready facility for years to come.”

The Watson Fire Station has provided essential fire and EMS services to the Watson neighborhood, Fairmont State University, and the Fairmont Technology Park for nearly 50 years. However, the aging facility no longer meets the operational needs of the Fairmont Fire Department or the growing needs of the surrounding community.

The funding will help the City of Fairmont transform the outdated station into a modern, mission-ready facility. Planned improvements include converting the original apparatus bay into sleeping and living quarters and constructing a new, energy-efficient apparatus bay to house fire vehicles, turnout gear, SCBA equipment, a hose washer and dryer, and other essential infrastructure. The upgrades will improve response capabilities, support staffing needs, ensure compliance with current codes, and allow the department to expand technical rescue and EMS services.

The project represents a significant investment in Fairmont’s public safety infrastructure and will help ensure the Fairmont Fire Department is equipped to continue providing critical services to the community for decades to come.

###

title: SCHNEIDER JOINS BIPARTISAN GROUP OF OVER 250 CURRENT AND FORMER MEMBERS OF CONGRESS URGING THE SUPREME COURT TO BLOCK TRUMP’S EXECUTIVE ORDER LIMITING VOTING BY MAIL
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) joined a bipartisan group of over 250 current and former Members of Congress in urging the Supreme Court to block President Trump’s executive order that would require states to provide a citizenship verification list to the Department of Homeland Security and give the Postal Service control over who can vote by mail. Millions of Americans utilize mail-in voting including deployed service members, seniors, and disabled Americans. Trump himself voted by mail last month.

“The right to vote is a critical pillar of our democracy,” said Schneider. “Every single American deserves the opportunity to cast their ballot how they wish – whether that is in-person or by mail. This executive order is a blatant attempt to sow doubt in the integrity of our elections and disenfranchise eligible voters.

“Trump’s continued attacks on mail-in voting are un-American and anti-democratic. I’m glad to join a bipartisan group of over 250 current and former lawmakers to urge the Court to stand up for the right to vote and stand against any and all attacks that undermine this sacred right,” Schneider concluded. “We will continue fighting to protect free and fair elections for everyone.”

title: Peters Statement on Reported ICE Activity Near San Diego Schools
text:
San Diego, CA — Today, Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) released the following statement after San Diego Unified School District (SDUSD) and San Diego City College both informed the Congressman's office of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrest activity outside their schools within the past week:

"I am deeply troubled by reports that students and parents were detained without warning while trying to attend classes or bring kids to school. Schools are supposed to be a safe place for young people to learn. Yet this Administration exploits the places we trust most—schools, childcare facilities, hospitals, courthouses, and places of worship. President Trump has turned these places into hunting grounds.

“ICE isn’t going after the 'worst of the worst,' as President Trump promised. We saw this at Buona Forchetta, when ICE agents threw the owner against a wall, handcuffed employees, and used flash-bang grenades on bystanders. These people weren't drug lords or violent criminals; they were workers trying to make a living.

“Parents and children should not have to worry about ICE agents waiting outside a classroom or a doctor's office. That's why I led introduction of the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, which would bar immigration enforcement within 1,000 feet of schools, hospitals, and churches except in true emergencies. I will also continue working with SDUSD and City College to make sure San Diegans have the resources they need to stay informed and protected.

"Until ICE operates responsibly and reasonably to target dangerous criminals instead of hardworking families, I will push for real reforms from ICE and hold them accountable for the fear they have inflicted on my constituents and communities across the country. I urge all state and local elected officials to express their support for the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act and my Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act so we can deliver commonsense reforms that keep our communities safe."

Background:

Last year, Rep. Peters led the Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act, a bill to make our communities safer by establishing a stronger standard for Federal immigration agents' use of force. The bill would also restrict use of crowd munitions like tear gas and create greater transparency in enforcement by requiring the use of body cameras and strictly limiting the use of masks. Rep. Peters has pushed Congress to pass these common sense reforms, but they have been blocked by the Republican majority.

###

title: Congressman Brad Sherman Statement on the North Korea Travel Ban
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32), senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued the following statement:

“To the dismay of many Korean Americans, Secretary Rubio recently renewed the ban on U.S. citizen travel to North Korea for the 10th consecutive year. About 100,000 Korean Americans still hope to have family reunification meetings with aging relatives in North Korea, and the ban makes it impossible for them to do so. It is time for the State Department to revise its policy so that Korean Americans can have the opportunity to attend funerals or burials in North Korea and to heal the wounds of years-long separations.”

title: Brown Announces $20 Million Dollar Grant for GCRTA Platform Renovations Funded by Bipartisan Infrastructure Law
text:
Cleveland, OH – Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) is proud to announce that the Greater Cleveland Regional Transit Authority (GCRTA) has been awarded a $20 million dollar grant to fund renovations to Green Line light rail platforms. The Department of Transportation has awarded GCRTA with an All Stations Accessibility Program (ASAP) grant. The ASAP grant program was created and funded by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which Brown voted for in 2021. Congresswoman Brown also supported GCRTA’s funding request with an official letter of support in April.

“I’m proud to announce more federal funding is coming to Northeast Ohio thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. This is a big win for our community: $20 million for our transit system that thousands of Ohioans rely on. I was proud to advocate for this funding because this federal grant will help make GCRTA platforms more accessible, allowing more passengers and their families use the Rapid to get where they need to go. It’s another example of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law delivering for Northeast Ohio,” said Congresswoman Brown.

“Accessibility is about more than platforms and sidewalks; it represents independence, dignity and ensuring everyone can fully participate in our community. Once this project is complete, every rail station in our system will be ADA accessible, which is a major milestone for our network. For our riders, that translates into improved access to jobs, health care, education and everything Greater Cleveland has to offer. We appreciate the unwavering support of Congresswoman Shontel Brown, as a steadfast supporter of public transportation, through legislative advocacy and measurable action," said India L. Birdsong Terry, GCRTA General Manager and CEO.

The DOT’s ASAP program provides federal competitive grants to assist eligible entities in financing capital projects to upgrade the accessibility of legacy rail fixed guideway public transportation systems for people with disabilities.

###

title: Rep. Steube, Sen. Moody Urge Army Corps to Preserve Charlotte County Septic-to-Sewer Authorization
text:
WASHINGTON—Representative Greg Steube (R-Fla.) and Senator Ashley Moody (R-Fla.) today sent a joint letter to Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works Adam Telle urging the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to preserve Charlotte County’s eligibility to seek federal funding for septic-to-sewer conversion projects.

Rep. Steube worked to increase the amount in federal funding that Charlotte County could seek from $3 million to $33 million in 2022 to address nearly 2,600 failing septic systems harming water quality in the Charlotte Harbor National Estuary and the Gulf of America. Federal funds have yet to be dispersed for the project, but the lawmakers say that reflects bureaucratic delay, not a lapse in need. Charlotte County has since completed the Manasota Key Shoreline Protection Study and is now positioned to pursue a roughly $400 million wastewater conversion program, with the county planning to request Congressional support for septic-to-sewer conversions in the upcoming funding cycle.

Rep. Steube and Sen. Moody warn that removing Charlotte County’s eligibility for federal support now would strip the county of its ability to seek funding for this work going forward, undoing years of Congressional effort to address failing septic systems and improve water quality throughout Southwest Florida.

The full letter is attached here.

title: Rep. Haley Stevens Champions Bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act to Prepare Students for Data-Driven Economy
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Michigan Congresswoman Haley Stevens alongside Reps. Jim Baird (R-IN), Don Beyer (D-VA), and Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) introduced the Bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act, to expand access to data science education and make sure Michigan students have the skills needed to compete in an increasingly data-driven economy.

Data science draws on statistics, computer science, and mathematics to analyze and derive insights from data. Yet many students graduate from high school without these foundational skills, even as nearly one in four jobs requires data science skills.

“Data is powering the technologies and jobs that will define America’s economic future, and our students deserve the skills to lead that future,” said Rep. Haley Stevens. “Whether a student goes on to work on the factory floor, in a research lab, at a small business, or developing the next breakthrough technology, the ability to understand and use data will be increasingly important. This legislation is about making sure Michigan students are ready.”

“Data science education can be the catalyst that launches American scientific leadership into the stratosphere. Introducing children to STEM early gives them a foundation to continually build upon, preparing them to tackle increasingly advanced concepts as they reach higher education and enter the workforce. This is how we compound our scientific knowledge and foster the next generation of American innovation. Start early, build upon that knowledge, and grow our nation’s understanding of STEM,” said Rep. Jim Baird.

“Data is one of the most powerful tools shaping our society today. It helps businesses streamline supply chain operations, public health officials track and prevent disease, and Americans navigate nearly every aspect of modern life. Yet too many students lack access to the education they need to understand and use data effectively. Our bill would provide educators with the resources necessary to expand access to a quality data science education and prepare students for 21st century jobs,” said Rep. Don Beyer.

“Every generation has a responsibility to prepare the next for the world they will inherit. As data becomes foundational across nearly every field, our classrooms must keep pace. This legislation builds on the work we have led here in PA-1 to strengthen career and technical education, expand pathways into high-demand fields, and better connect learning with opportunity. The bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act will carry that mission forward—equipping more students with the skills to succeed, strengthening our workforce, and ensuring America continues to lead,” said Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick.

The Data Science and Literacy Act establishes a grant program at the U.S. Department of Education to expand access to data science education nationwide. The program would support data science instruction from pre-K through community college, strengthen students’ data literacy, and provide professional development opportunities for educators. The legislation also improves federal data collection and establishes evaluation and reporting requirements to guide future investments.

Specifically, the Data Science and Literacy Act authorizes educational grants for the following purposes:

Curriculum Development: Developing, implementing, and expanding data science curricula and instructional materials.

Student Support: Improving student outcomes in data science education, including targeted support for students historically underrepresented in the field.

Professional Development: Providing evidence-based training and recruitment support for educators to effectively teach data science and related subjects.

Partnerships: Supporting collaboration with community colleges, institutions of higher education, and other relevant organizations to strengthen data science education pathways.

Text of the bill can be found here.

The legislation is backed by Data Science 4 Everyone (DS4E), Alliance for Data Science & AI (ADSA), Alliance for Learning Innovation (ALI), American Mathematical Association of Two-Year Colleges (AMATYC), American Statistical Association (AmStat), Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators (AMTE), Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA), Digital Promise, INFORMS, Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR), National Council of Teachers of Mathematics (NCTM), and National Science Teaching Association (NSTA).

“The average school experience is becoming disconnected from the fast-changing world our students are graduating into,” said Zarek Drozda, Executive Director of Data Science 4 Everyone (DS4E). “The question ‘why am I learning this?’ needs to have a better answer. Engaging in data science activities allows students to connect their academic subjects to the real-world, and learn a toolkit for navigating (and questioning) AI at the same time.”

“ADSA works with more than 100 institutions of higher education, from R1 universities, community colleges, HBCUs, and Hispanic-serving institutions. One thing we hear consistently is that they want to be better partners to the K-12 schools in their regions,” said Dr. Micaela Parker, Founder and Executive Director of Alliance for Data Science and AI (ADSA). “The Data Science and Literacy Act creates that opportunity by putting flexible resources into district, community college, and university partnerships to update curricula for the modern age. This bill reflects how students actually use data: across their whole education, not in a single elective. ADSA is proud to support it.”

“Too often, promising education investments go unmeasured, leaving us guessing about what actually works. The Data Science and Literacy Act gets this right by building evaluation into the bill from the start by directing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES) to rigorously assess grant effectiveness and requiring grantees to continuously monitor their own progress. That commitment to evidence, not just access, is exactly what we want to see in federal education investments,” Sara Schapiro, Executive Director of Alliance for Learning Innovation (ALI). “At the Alliance for Learning Innovation (ALI), we believe every student deserves the tools to make sense of data and put it to work solving real problems. We're proud to endorse this bipartisan legislation and thank Representatives Stevens, Beyer, Kim, and Baird for their leadership in building a stronger STEM pipeline for the next generation."

“H.G. Wells once said ‘Statistical thinking will one day be as necessary for efficient citizenship as the ability to read and write.’ (c. 1903) That day is today. This bill is the right step forward,” said Eddie Tchertchian, President of the American Mathematical Association of Two-Year Colleges (AMATYC).

“The presence of AI in our everyday lives and work has made statistical thinking more critical than ever, so I applaud Representative Stevens and her cosponsors for reintroducing this bill, " said Jeri Mulrow, President of the American Statistical Association (AmStat). “Statistical thinking, a core component of data literacy, is essential for today's students to effectively use AI, critically assess its outputs, and succeed in today's job market.”

“In continuing AMTE efforts to bring diverse mathematics teacher education communities together, our organization continues to support educators, coaches, consultants, specialists, and university and community college faculty to share and disseminate research, teaching, and community partnerships in different educational contexts,” said Farshid Safi, President of Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators (AMTE). “AMTE, intentionally and toward a more comprehensive and inclusive lens, adopts an expansive view of the term mathematics education to include intersections with fields such as data science and statistics education, mathematical modeling, STEM education while partnering with those engaged in early childhood, PK-12, and post-secondary contexts.”

“Data shapes the technologies students use, the decisions they encounter, and the world they will help create. The 2026 CSTA PK–12 Computer Science Standards identify Data & Analysis as a core concept in foundational computer science education, calling on students to use data to solve problems, make discoveries, and express ideas while critically examining its quality, representation, privacy, and impact,” said Bryan Twarek, Head of Research and Innovation of the Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA). “The Data Science and Literacy Act would invest in the curricula, professional development, and partnerships teachers need to prepare their students to become critical consumers, responsible creators, and informed participants in a world powered by computing.”

“Data literacy is a foundational tool for real-world agency. Preparing students for a changing economy requires updating what and how we teach, moving away from narrow metrics of success to build practical skills across disciplines,” said Jean-Claude Brizard, Chief Executive Officer of Digital Promise. “The Data Science and Literacy Act delivers flexible resources that allow school systems and postsecondary partners to strengthen teacher capacity and create powerful learning experiences for every student. Digital Promise strongly supports this legislation as a crucial investment in long-term economic mobility.”

“Ensuring that data literacy is a foundational aspect of education is a cornerstone of the United States’ long-term economic and national security. Data is everywhere and the ideas and demands to create more of it, and the evermore complex ways to deploy it, are growing more significant by the day,” said Jeff Cohen, Chief External Affairs Officer at INFORMS. “This bill is a key part of addressing the substantial shortfall of STEM-prepared students for the workforce of tomorrow. Operations research, analytics, and the science and technology of decision-making is predicated on the sound and ethical use of data. INFORMS strongly supports the bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act of 2026 and looks forward to working to ensure its passage and effective implementation.”

“Our students are graduating into a world where the ability to understand, interpret, and use data is no longer optional; it is essential. Science and STEM education provide powerful opportunities for students to develop these skills as they use data to ask questions and make sense of the world around them,” said Brianna Reilly Oliveira, Director of Professional Learning for the National Science Teaching Association. “NSTA strongly supports the Data Science and Literacy Act and its investment in educators and students. By equipping educators with the confidence, tools and strategies to integrate data literacy into science and STEM instruction, we can better prepare all students to thrive in a data-rich world.”

###

title: Suozzi Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Crack Down on Health Care Fraud
text:
Washington, D.C.—Congressman Tom Suozzi (D-NY) today introduced the bipartisan Health Care Fraud Prevention and Enforcement Act with Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (R-NY) to strengthen the federal government’s efforts to combat waste, fraud, and abuse across government healthcare programs. The legislation would increase funding for the Health Care Fraud and Abuse Control Program (HCFAC), a joint agency program involving the Department of Health and Human Services, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), Office of Inspector General (OIG), Department of Justice, and FBI. HCFAC coordinates federal, state, and local efforts to identify and prosecute health care fraud across programs including Medicare, Medicaid, and other government health care programs.

“Taxpayers bear the cost of every dollar lost to fraud, ultimately making healthcare more expensive. If we want to lower healthcare costs, we need to start by going after waste, fraud, and abuse wherever it’s happening. HCFAC is a tremendously successful program helping us do just that,” said Congressman Suozzi. “Fighting fraud is not a partisan issue; it’s common sense. The Health Care Fraud Prevention and Enforcement Act is about protecting taxpayers, rooting out fraud, and helping keep health care costs down. I’m proud to introduce this important bill to protect taxpayers and the healthcare programs that so many patients depend on.”

“Every dollar stolen through health care fraud is a dollar taken from taxpayers and the patients who depend on these programs,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “Fraudsters are becoming more sophisticated, and the federal government must have the tools and resources to find them, stop them, and hold them accountable. The Health Care Fraud Prevention and Enforcement Act strengthens the investigators and watchdogs on the front lines of this fight and improves oversight across federal health care programs. Protecting Medicare, Medicaid, and other critical programs from fraud will safeguard taxpayer dollars and help ensure these resources are there for the Americans who truly need them.”

Every dollar lost to fraud costs not only the government, but trickles down to consumers through higher premiums and costs on other health care expenses. HCFAC is a highly effective federal program, returning $3 to taxpayers for every dollar spent. By increasing the funding for this successful and worthwhile program, this legislation fights fraud responsibly, by equipping federal agencies with additional resources to prevent fraudulent payments, hold bad actors accountable, lower costs for patients, and recover taxpayer dollars.

Since 2010, the scope of HCFAC’s work has expanded significantly. Medicare and Medicaid spending has far outpaced inflation, enrollment has skyrocketed, and fraudsters have become savvier. The funding for HCFAC has not kept up. As a result, the network of agencies involved have had to police a broader and more complex system without adequate resources. To address this, the Health Care Fraud Prevention and Enforcement Act would rebase HCFAC’s funding, raising it to $490,000,000 for FY2027, $520,000,000 for FY2028, $57,000,000 for FY2029, and ensuring it continues to increase commensurate with inflation in FY2030 and beyond.

###

title: Suozzi, Leader DeRiggi-Whitton, and Mayor Villafane Announce Expansion of Sea Cliff  Sewer System
text:
Glen Cove, NY—Congressman Suozzi (D-NY) today joined Nassau County Legislature Minority Leader DeRiggi-Whitton (D-Glen Cove), Sea Cliff Mayor Elena Villafane, and local residents in Sea Cliff to announce the expansion of the Sea Cliff sewer system. The $6.5 million expansion will utilize more than $1.1 million in funds Congressman Suozzi secured in the FY2026 Community Project Funding grants. Nassau County Legislature Minority Leader Delia DeRiggi-Whitton secured an additional $4 million in bond authorization over the next two years to support the expansion of the sanitary sewer system in Sea Cliff, and local resources will cover the balance.

“This is a major accomplishment by Legislator DeRiggi-Whitton to help sewer critical areas in Sea Cliff and protect our precious Hempstead Harbor,” Congressman Suozzi said. “The continued success of Sea Cliff’s sewer expansion initiative is an outstanding illustration of what can be accomplished when all levels of government work collaboratively to solve problems for the communities we serve. I am excited to see how the $1 million in federal funding that I secured from the federal government has become a catalyst for millions more in County-level support spearheaded by Legislator DeRiggi-Whitton in partnership with Village leaders. This is transformational.”

The funds will be applied toward sewering a total of 2,860 linear feet on these streets:

• Prospect Avenue between Carpenter Avenue & Albin Street (900 linear feet, 20 service connections)

• Winding Way between 7th Avenue and Prospect Avenue (860 linear feet, 12 service connections)

• The Drive between Park Way and Carpenter Avenue (370 linear feet, five service connections)

• Park Way between 7th Avenue and Prospect Avenue (730 feet, eight service connections)

The forthcoming project will build upon previous work, completed during the summer of 2021, which sewered portions of Prospect, Maple, 12th, Sea Cliff, Summit, Central, 8th, and 7th Avenues, as well as all of Fairview Place. The expansion will also play a key role in the continued effort to clean up the Long Island Sound. By converting septic systems to sewer systems, this project will reduce nitrogen pollution into the Sound, helping impove the water quality of one of our nation’s great treasures.

Congressman Suozzi has long been a champion for protecting Long Island's environment, advocating for clean water, open space preservation, and investments that improve the health of the Long Island Sound, including delivering a 1000% increase in funding to improve the Long Island Sound since he came to Congress in 2017. His leadership has earned recognition from the New York League of Conservation Voters, which this year named him a Clean Water Champion for his decades-long commitment to safeguarding Long Island's water quality and securing federal support for critical environmental projects.

“Since Sea Cliff Village officials received their first funding for sewer expansion in 2014, Sea Cliff Avenue was our first area to focus on. Completing that was, in and of itself, a major accomplishment because it opened the doors for businesses to flourish and grow without having to consider the limitations of septic systems,” Minority Leader DeRiggi-Whitton said. “The fact remains that, of the 10 percent of Nassau County that is not sewered, about 90 percent falls within District 11, and that is why it was so important to pursue a vision that expands the initial project to connect additional streets to the gravity line that was completed five years ago. With critical support from Congressman Suozzi and this new County infrastructure funding, we are a major step closer to making those plans a reality.”

“This is exactly the kind of intergovernmental partnership that produces lasting results for our residents and our environment,” Sea Cliff Mayor Elena Villafane said. “Legislator Delia DeRiggi-Whitton’s success in securing $4 million in Nassau County capital funding, combined with Congressman Tom Suozzi’s $1 million commitment, brings us significantly closer to extending public sewers to areas of Sea Cliff that have relied on aging cesspools for generations. Protecting Hempstead Harbor is one of our highest priorities, and expanding sewer service is one of the most meaningful steps we can take toward that goal. On behalf of the Village, I thank Legislator DeRiggi-Whitton and Congressman Suozzi for investing in Sea Cliff’s future.”

title: Congressman Shri Thanedar Leads Bipartisan Resolution Designating September as National Suicide Prevention Month
text:
Washington, DC - Today, Congressman Shri Thanedar (D-MI-13), along with Congressmen Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) and Mike Lawler (R-NY-17), introduced a bipartisan resolution recognizing September as “National Suicide Prevention Month” and September 10, 2026, as “World Suicide Prevention Day”. This resolution will bring awareness to the mental health battles that many face silently every day and decrease the stigma behind seeking treatment for mental illness.

“In 1996, I lost my first wife to her battle with mental illness,” said Congressman Shri Thanedar. The pain my young boys and I suffered was devastating and has stayed with me ever since. Her loss has inspired my work in Congress to ensure everyone has access to high-quality mental health care. By partnering in a bipartisan fashion with Representatives Bell and Lawler, we will bring awareness to this devastating issue and ensure that no more lives are lost to mental illness.”

"Suicide is an epidemic plaguing our youth that demands urgent attention, because behind every statistic is a family forever changed by a loss words can't capture," said Congressman Bell. "In Missouri and across the nation, too many people are suffering in silence, believing they have nowhere to turn. National Suicide Prevention Month is about changing that. We must meet this crisis head-on by investing in mental health care, breaking down the stigma that keeps people from asking for help, and making clear that reaching out is a sign of strength, not weakness. Mental health is health, and no one should have to face their darkest moments alone. If you're struggling, help is always within reach — call or text 988."

“Suicide is a devastating public health crisis, but it is not inevitable. We have a responsibility to ensure that people who are struggling know they are not alone and have access to the mental health care and support they need. During National Suicide Prevention Month and on World Suicide Prevention Day, we must recommit ourselves to breaking the stigma around mental health, expanding access to care, and doing everything we can to prevent the loss of another life,” said Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17).

This resolution is supported by a broad range of mental health stakeholders, including the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, saying “Suicide is the 10th leading cause of death in the United States, with nearly 49,000 Americans dying by suicide in 2024 and an estimated 2.2 million suicide attempts,” said Laurel Stine, J.D., M.A., Executive Vice President and Chief Policy and Advocacy Officer at the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (AFSP). “AFSP commends Representatives Thanedar, Bell, and Lawler for introducing this bipartisan resolution recognizing September as National Suicide Prevention Month and September 10 as World Suicide Prevention Day. By raising awareness about suicide and the critical need to expand access to quality mental health, substance use, and suicide prevention services and care, we can help save lives and create a future where everyone has the support and resources they need to thrive.”

Another supporter, the National Alliance on Mental Illness, said the following about Thanedar’s resolution: “Every life lost to suicide is a tragedy, and every effort to prevent suicide must begin with ensuring people have access to the mental health care and support they need," said Hannah Wesolowski, Chief Advocacy Officer at the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI). “National Suicide Prevention Month and World Suicide Prevention Day are important opportunities to raise awareness, spread hope, and spark meaningful action. NAMI thanks Rep. Thanedar for recognizing suicide prevention as a national priority.”

Congressman Shri Thanedar proudly represents Michigan's 13th Congressional District, which includes Detroit, Downriver, and the Grosse Pointes. As a champion for working families, Shri is committed to advancing economic opportunities, education, healthcare access, and entrepreneurship for underserved communities. Drawing from his journey from poverty to success, he works tirelessly to uplift Metro Detroit, ensuring every resident has the resources and support they need to thrive.

title: Representatives Torres and Rutherford Secure First Federal Recognition of Blue Envelope Programs in House Appropriations Report
text:
Washington, D.C. – Representatives Norma Torres (CA-35) and John Rutherford (FL-05), both members of the House Appropriations Committee that oversees government spending, celebrated the inclusion of a provision in the Fiscal Year 2027 Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies (CJS) Appropriations Report recognizing Blue Envelope Programs as an eligible use of Byrne Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) funding and to highlight these programs nationwide. The report was reported out of the Appropriations Committee last month, and now awaits consideration by the full House.

Blue Envelope programs help improve communication between law enforcement and public safety personnel with individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (I/DD), or others who may face communication challenges.

The report language notes that Blue Envelope Programs are consistent with existing Byrne JAG funding priorities, including law enforcement training and community engagement initiatives. The report also directs the Department of Justice to provide Congress with a report within 180 days on efforts to highlight Blue Envelope Programs to grant recipients.

"This is an important step toward expanding Blue Envelope Programs across the country and ensuring that individuals with autism, developmental disabilities, and communication challenges can have safer and more positive interactions with law enforcement," said Congresswoman Torres. "The inclusion of this language in the House Appropriations report recognizes the value of these programs and encourages awareness and support nationwide. While this progress is worth celebrating, I will continue working with Congressman Rutherford to pass our bipartisan legislation and create a dedicated federal funding stream to help communities establish and expand Blue Envelope Programs."

“As a former sheriff and lifelong law enforcement officer, I know that effective communication is essential to keeping both officers and the people they serve safe,” said Congressman Rutherford. “Recognizing Blue Envelope Programs as an eligible use of Byrne JAG funding is an important step toward helping more law enforcement agencies reduce misunderstandings and improve interactions with individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (I/DD), and others who may face communication challenges. I am proud to work with my colleague Congresswoman Torres to advance this bipartisan effort."

Last December, Congresswoman Torres and Congressman Rutherford introduced the bipartisan Supporting Blue Envelope Programs Act (H.R.6602) to establish a federal grant program that would support the creation, expansion, and implementation of Blue Envelope Programs, which already exist in 29 states, including in California and Florida. Senator Coons (DE) and Schmitt (MO) lead the companion bill in the Senate (S.4089). The bill is supported by numerous law enforcement organizations, stakeholders, and community advocates.

Blue Envelope Programs provide individuals with a clearly identifiable blue envelope that can hold driver's licenses, vehicle registrations, emergency contact information, and other materials that help first responders better understand a person's communication needs during traffic stops and other interactions. Programs may also provide additional tools and training to support effective communication between law enforcement officers and individuals with disabilities.

Background

The FY 2027 Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies Appropriations Report (House Report 119-652) includes language recognizing Blue Envelope Programs as an allowable use of Byrne Justice Assistance Grant funding. The report encourages the Department of Justice to highlight these programs in guidance provided to Byrne JAG grantees and directs the Department to report to Congress within 180 days on its efforts.

In FY 2026, Congresswoman Torres secured $1.031 million in Community Project Funding for the Autism Society Inland Empire, in partnership with the Pomona Police Department, Fontana Police Department, Ontario Police Department, and Chino Police Department, to support specialized law enforcement training for interactions with individuals with ASD, ISD, and other communication challenges.

title: Trahan Tours New Dracut Housing Project Made Possible by Significant Federal Investments
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03) toured The Avenue at Greenmont, a new housing development in Dracut featuring 56 newly built apartment homes designed for adults aged 62 and older and non-elderly individuals with disabilities. All units are fully affordable to households earning at or below 60% of the Area Median Income (AMI). The project was made possible in part through nearly $7 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds, awarded by the Massachusetts Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities (EOHLC) through its Community-Based Housing program.

“These 56 homes show what's possible when private partners and every level of government row in the same direction,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “Federal resources like ARPA dollars and Low-Income Housing Tax Credits helped make The Avenue at Greenmont a reality, but we can't stop here. We must continue advancing commonsense legislation like the recently passed 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act so more families can afford a home of their own.”

The project also received $3 million from the Town of Dracut's Community Preservation Act, $1.4 million from EOHLC's Housing Stabilization Fund, $825,000 in federal HOME funds, $630,000 through the state's MassWorks program, more than $5.5 million in Massachusetts Housing Tax Credits, and nearly $11.4 million in federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits.

The United States continues to face a severe affordable housing and homelessness crisis. According to experts, the U.S. has an estimated shortage of 3.7 million to 5.5 million homes for rent and purchase. The lack of housing, along with other factors, is driving up costs and making housing the single largest expense for Americans across the country. According to a recent poll, half of Massachusetts residents say housing is unaffordable for their household, making it the single biggest financial pressure point.

In 2021, Trahan supported passage of the American Rescue Plan Act to respond directly to the challenges created and worsened by the COVID-19 pandemic. The law invested billions of dollars to expand affordable housing and support Americans experiencing or at risk of homelessness. In Massachusetts, EOHLC put those federal dollars to work through programs like Community-Based Housing, which helped make The Avenue at Greenmont possible.

Earlier this year, Trahan supported passage of the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. The new law, which took effect despite President Donald Trump’s refusal to sign it, makes it easier to build new homes, expand financing opportunities for housing, and provide new protections for renters. The bipartisan legislation also reduces unnecessary regulatory barriers to new home construction, authorizes the use of federal funds to support the development of affordable housing, and establishes a maximum limit for affordable rents.

title: Vindman Hears from the 84% of Virginians Who Support Keeping the Government Open
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) heard from more than 850 Virginians in a district-wide survey, and the results were clear: respondents overwhelmingly believe that Congress should fight to keep the government open.

“Virginians know that federal workers are the backbone of our economy and our government,” said Vindman. “With tens of thousands of federal workers and contractors in Virginia’s Seventh District, I was proud to vote to keep the government open. I will continue working to deliver a budget that funds the government responsibly, aligns with our values, and tackles the out-of-control corruption we are seeing in Washington.”

Last week, the House of Representatives voted on a Senate Amendment to H.R. 6500 that would keep the government open. Vindman was proud to vote in favor of this amendment and stand with the dedicated federal workers and contractors who keep our government running.

The survey asked constituents whether they support keeping the government open and how concerned they would be about the impact of a government shutdown on federal workers and contractors in Virginia’s Seventh District.

Below are responses submitted by Virginia’s Seventh District residents who took the survey:

—

“My husband is a government worker and primary income earner. We do not have the financial wherewithal to handle another government shutdown.” — Caitlin, Prince William

“Our elected officials have a duty to ensure all essential services remain open. Federal employees should not have to live in fear of partisan politics.” — Richard, Spotsylvania

“I am very concerned about how the people of Virginia would survive another government shut down.” — Dorothy, Caroline

“I retired last year to avoid being RIFed. I went through two long shutdowns as a federal employee. It is very stressful not knowing when you are going back to work and will be paid. These shutdowns have to stop.” — Dinna, Spotsylvania

BACKGROUND

Vindman has long been a champion for federal workers and contractors.

During the October 2025 government shutdown, Vindman asked the U.S. House of Representatives’ Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) to withhold his salary for the duration of the shutdown.

In March 2025, Vindman introduced bipartisan legislation that would block Members of Congress from receiving their pay during a government shutdown.

title: Rep. Watson Coleman Addresses Housing Affordability and Equity at Panel Event in Trenton
text:
Today, Representative Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12) spoke to the Capital Region Minority Chamber of Commerce (CRMCC) about housing affordability. Joined by CRMCC President Herb Ames and industry experts, the Congresswoman highlighted the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a comprehensive bipartisan package passed earlier this year that addresses many dimensions of housing policy.

Over the past few years, Americans have dealt with rising housing costs, putting a strain on millions of families looking to pay their bills and in 2023, the Brookings Institute estimated that there is a shortage of about 4.9 million housing units. This highlights the importance of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which is the largest bipartisan housing law in a generation. President Trump did not sign it into law, however, calling it “a big yawn.” Per the United States Constitution, the bill eventually became law on July 11th, 2026 after the President failed to sign it or veto it within the 10 days following its delivery by Congress. Based on track-record, there is reason to be concerned that the Trump Administration may ignore the law.

The Congresswoman gave the following remarks:

It's been over 50 years since the New Jersey Supreme Court handed down the Mount Laurel Doctrine that said exclusionary zoning practices that prevent low- and moderate-income families from living in a town are unconstitutional. Yet today, safe, affordable housing remains out of reach for so many. Fewer than four in ten non-homeowning families can afford a typical starter home.

It is not enough to remove legal barriers to the middle class while leaving socioeconomic barriers in place. Economic predators have filled the vacuum left behind by the law. Money is like water; it'll find the cracks.

The result is that young people and Black people suffer. The homeownership rate for Black households is barely half that of white households, at about 41%. Meanwhile, over 4.2 million young people experience homelessness each year. This astonishing number consists of a disproportionate number of people of color and LGBTQ+ individuals. Not coincidentally, in 2023 the Brookings Institute estimated that there is a shortage of about 4.9 million housing units.

This is not only immoral - it is unsustainable in an economy in which homeownership plays such an important role in wealth accumulation. Housing is a right; it is not a privilege. Shelter is as fundamental a need as food and water. And, in a country as wealthy as ours, the difference between a housing crisis and a roof over everyone's head is a policy choice.

The policy choices of the Trump administration have been clear. After passing their latest round of tax cuts for the mega rich and corporate donors, they had the gall to cut the HUD budget by 51%. That included a $27.25 billion cut to rental and homeless assistance programs- or 40%. A $53 billion cut to Section 8. An $8.8 billion cut to public housing. And a $1.25 billion cut to the HOME program, to name a few.

In addition, HUD withdrew legal guidance for the Fair Housing Act's coverage of appraisal discrimination of undervalued homes in majority-black neighborhoods. They also disbanded the Property Appraisal and Valuation Equity taskforce and repealed the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing subregulatory policies, removing federal requirements for local governments to proactively desegregate their communities.

Now I've worked to fight back on these abysmal policies, including during Appropriations hearings with Secretary Scott Turner, and through legislation like my Homes for Young Adults Act and Rep. Omar's Homes for All Act. But the biggest dent we've made was with the 21st Century Road to Housing Act, which passed earlier this summer.

This new law is not perfect, but it does some important things like prohibiting large institutional investors, like BlackRock, from purchasing new single-family homes, a practice that has priced millions out of their own neighborhoods, forcing people who rent who would otherwise buy, and leaving many homes vacant in the process.

It also increases grants to local governments that successfully increase housing supply through zoning reform and density bonuses. And it raises the public welfare investment cap for community development banks.

Incorporated into the final package were six Democratic priorities including, the Reforming Disaster Recovery Act to codify the Community Development Block Grants for Disaster Recovery, the PRICE Act to help manufactured communities preserve affordability, the VALID Act to improve transparency for veteran homebuyers, the Build Now Act to incentivize housing development in certain CDBG jurisdictions while protecting disaster-hit areas, a Moving to Work provision to add up to 25 Public Housing Authorities while prohibiting these PHAs from imposing overwhelming work requirements, and a provision to codify Rental Assistance Demonstration to help convert aging public housing into long-term Section 8 contracts to fund critical property repairs.

This bill passed the Senate 85 - 5 and the House 358 - 32. The president did not sign it, but he also did not veto it, so it became law on July 11th this year. We have the law passed now. But Trump’s refusal to engage with the bill, even just to sign it, hints at the likelihood that he will ignore the law.

He’s done this before and his administration is filled, at the highest levels, with people who believe a President can simply ignore a law he doesn’t agree with. So, we need a Congress that will hold the Administration accountable. That starts this November.

During his testimony last summer, HUD Secretary Turner repeatedly referred to the administration's efforts at dismantling housing assistance as a so-called “paradigm shift.” However, the real shift we've seen is how Americans of vastly different stripes and political persuasions view housing.

People are fed up. They see their grown children unable to afford homes, they see rents skyrocketing, and they see more and more of their budgets going to rent and mortgage payments while they struggle to stay afloat.

We are at the precipice of a revolution in how people view housing. And while I may not be in Congress to see universal housing become a reality, I am confident that if we keep working in this space, it will.

Thank you and God bless.

title: Rep. Watson Coleman Celebrates Grand Opening of Revitalized Reading Center for Trenton Community

title: Reps. George Whitesides, Maria Salazar, and Don Davis Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect Seniors From Wire Fraud
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Reps. George Whitesides (CA-27), Maria Salazar (FL-27), and Don Davis (NC-01) introduced the bipartisan Protecting Elders from Wire Fraud Act, legislation that would require financial institutions place holds on suspicious wire transactions leaving a senior’s account where financial exploitation is suspected.

As scams become more sophisticated and convincing, Congress has a responsibility to act to better protect Americans from financial exploitation. According to the FTC, $334 million was reported lost to fraudulent wire transfers in 2025 alone. As scams are typically underreported, the true total amount of money lost is likely much higher.

“We have a duty to protect our nation’s seniors from the epidemic of scams that threaten their financial security,” said Rep. Whitesides. “The Protecting Elders from Wire Fraud Act does just that, by allowing banks to hold suspicious wire transactions to determine their legitimacy.”

“Many seniors are spending their golden years on a fixed income. With the cost of living continuing to rise in places like Miami, every dollar matters, so accidental wire transfers can be especially devastating,” said Rep. Salazar. “Accidental wire transfers are nearly impossible to stop once a transaction has been fully completed, which is why I am proud to co-lead the Protecting Elders from Wire Fraud Act, to proactively protect seniors from bad actors and help them keep the money they worked so hard for.”

“As scams become more sophisticated, we cannot allow criminals to stay a step ahead. The Protecting Elders from Wire Fraud Act would give financial institutions stronger tools to act quickly when they suspect fraud, including temporarily holding suspicious transactions and reporting suspected exploitation to the appropriate authorities. We must give families and law enforcement the tools they need to protect our seniors from exploitation and safeguard not only their financial security but their independence and peace of mind,” said Rep. Don Davis. “Seniors across eastern North Carolina worked hard for what they have, and we have a responsibility to protect the savings they have spent a lifetime building from criminals looking to exploit them.”

“Scams are a scourge on the American consumer, and every year scammers are stealing more and more money from the pockets of our nation’s seniors,” said Brady Finta, founder and CEO of the National Elder Fraud Coordination Center. “We need concrete action from both the public and private sectors to address this crisis, which is why I’m proud to support Rep. George Whitesides’ legislation to better protect seniors from financial exploitation.”

The Protecting Elders from Wire Fraud Act would:

Require covered financial institutions to place holds up to 90 days on transactions leaving a senior’s account where financial exploitation is suspected to allow for the legitimacy of the transaction to be determined.

Direct financial institutions to reach out to trusted contacts associated with the senior’s account when a hold is placed.

Provide safe harbor for financial institutions acting in good faith.

This legislation is endorsed by AARP and the National Elder Fraud Coordination Center.

title: Baldwin Urges Supreme Court to Block Trump’s Effort to Restrict Mail-In Voting
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) and her colleagues are urging the U.S. Supreme Court to block President Trump’s unconstitutional Executive Order and U.S. Postal Service rule that attempts to restrict Wisconsinites’ ability to vote by mail ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

Specifically, Baldwin joined a bipartisan group of 261 current and former lawmakers in filing an amicus brief with the U.S. Supreme Court in the matter of State of California, et al. v. United States Postal Service, et al., a lawsuit brought by a coalition of State Attorneys General against the U.S. Postal Service (USPS). The court case challenges a final rule issued by the USPS in response to Trump’s directive that imposes unconstitutional and unworkable restrictions on mail-in voting, including requiring states to provide a “citizenship verification list” and attempting to give USPS control over who can vote by mail.

“The President is trying to meddle in the elections because he knows that Americans are going to hold him accountable in November,” said Senator Baldwin. “Instead of changing course and doing what he said he would to lower costs, he is trying to silence Americans from having their voice heard at the ballot box. This effort to stop Americans from voting by mail – despite many Wisconsinites already having their ballots on their counters – is cut and dry unconstitutional, and the Supreme Court needs to say just that and protect Americans’ right to vote.”

Nearly one-third of Americans have voted by mail in recent elections, including over 500,000 Wisconsinites in the 2024 election — a voting practice Trump himself used as recently as August 2026, when he voted in Florida’s Republican primary.

In the court filing, the lawmakers argue that Trump’s Executive Order 14399 and USPS’s final rule violate the separation of powers and usurp congressional authorities outlined in Article I of the U.S. Constitution, which gives the States and Congress exclusive authority over election administration.

The lawmakers also pointed to a recent federal court ruling blocking the USPS from implementing its newly finalized mail ballot rule for the midterm elections, saying the agency lacked the authority to implement the rule and that its actions are “substantively unconstitutional and contrary to law.”

The lawmakers concluded by asserting States’ power to administer elections and Congress’s power to make or alter rules regulating elections, which the Supreme Court itself has described as an “override” authority. Trump’s illegal incursion on this authority is an attempt to disenfranchise people who depend on mail-in ballots to vote.

Senator Baldwin has repeatedly pushed back against the Trump Administration’s efforts to restrict mail-in voting and disenfranchise Wisconsin voters. In June, Baldwin demanded that the USPS abandon the rule, and in July, she called on the USPS to immediately address severe mail delays that caused hundreds of Wisconsinites’ ballots to arrive after Election Day in April.

The lawmakers’ demands come as President Trump has taken an all-of-the-above approach to try to interfere in the upcoming 2026 elections. In addition to his attempt to curtail legal mail-in voting, the President has repeatedly threatened to send federal agents to states’ polling places, repeated his claim about “rigged” elections more than 100 times, and sent FBI agents into Milwaukee to relitigate his 2020 election loss.

The amicus brief was led by Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Dick Durbin (D-IL), and Gary Peters (D-MI) and joined by the entire Senate Democratic Caucus.

The full brief is available here.

title: Bennet, Hickenlooper, Wyden, Padilla, Schiff Sound the Alarm on Lack of Firefighting Resources During the 2026 Wildfire Season
text:
Denver — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a senior member of the U.S. Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, led Senators John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) to express serious concerns about the U.S. Department of Interior (DOI) and U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) preparedness and ability to adequately respond to the 2026 fire season. Colorado has faced one of the most severe wildfire seasons to date, with over 240,000 acres burned and loss of wildland firefighting personnel.

“[…] Record-breaking high temperatures and historic drought have led to catastrophic fires across the West, destroying thousands of homes, wreaking havoc on the economies of rural communities, stressing the budgets of local governments, and leading to the loss of four wildland firefighters and two pilots,”began the senators.

Between July 18 and September 4, 2026, the national firefighting force was at preparedness level 5 with federal resources fully committed to combating wildland fires across the country. So far this year, the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) and U.S. Wildland Fire Service has dedicated over $6 billion to fire suppression budget authority, spending nearly the entire fire suppression budget as of September 2, 2026. The West is expected to remain in peak fire season with hot, dry, and windy conditions for at least the next two months, raising concerns that federal wildfire resources and suppression funds could run out entirely.

“In light of these concerns, the capacity of the federal government to sustain operations is critical. We are concerned that the agencies simply do not have enough highly qualified personnel, Incident Management Teams, and supervisory staff to sustain operations. Our offices have received reports that teams have worked more fires than is safe, using temporary supervisory structures because fully qualified personnel are not available. We have also heard that locally-led initial attack was affected by national mobilization, and that personnel have worked repeated or extended assignments. This is exceptionally concerning given that the worst of the fire season is likely yet to come and the high wildland firefighter fatality rate this season,”continued the senators.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Subcommittee on Conservation, Forestry, Natural Resources, and Biotechnology, Bennet has fought for adequate support for Colorado’s forests during wildfire seasons. In August 2026, Bennet and Representative Jeff Hurd (R-Colo.) led the entire Colorado Congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump expressing strong support for Governor Jared Polis’ request for a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration following massively destructive wildfires in Pueblo, Custer, and Ouray Counties. Additionally, Bennet led Senators Hickenlooper, Mike Lee (R-Utah), and John Curtis (R-Utah) to introduce a bipartisan resolution honoring this season’s wildfire casualties and all those who serve on the front lines of wildland firefighting efforts in the United States. Bennet and Hickenlooper also introduced the Emergency Mountain Pine Beetle Response and Coordination Act to mitigate the growing mountain pine beetle outbreak in Colorado.

Bennet has also consistently pushed USFS to respond to drought, prioritize hazardous fuels reduction, and reduce wildfire risk. In March 2026, Bennet urged USFS Chief Tom Schultz to prioritize proactive wildfire mitigation efforts in the West. In December 2025, Bennet urged Schultz to address persistent staffing shortages and mounting setbacks to wildfire risk reduction efforts across the West and the country.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Dear Secretaries Burgum and Rollins:

We write with serious concern about the U.S. Department of Interior (DOI) and U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) continued preparedness to respond to the 2026 fire season. Record- breaking high temperatures and historic drought have led to catastrophic fires across the West, destroying thousands of homes, wreaking havoc on the economies of rural communities, stressing the budgets of local governments, and leading to the loss of four wildland firefighters and two pilots. The national firefighting force was at preparedness Level 5 between July 18 and September 4, meaning that federal resources were fully committed for nearly seven weeks. With several weeks remaining in peak fire season, fire conditions could continue to strain an already stretched system.

In light of these concerns, the capacity of the federal government to sustain operations is critical. We are concerned that the agencies simply do not have enough highly qualified personnel, Incident Management Teams, and supervisory staff to sustain operations. Our offices have received reports that teams have worked more fires than is safe, using temporary supervisory structures because fully qualified personnel are not available. We have also heard that locally led initial attack was affected by national mobilization, and that personnel have worked repeated or extended assignments. This is exceptionally concerning given the high wildland firefighter fatality rate this season.

We are also concerned that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) and U.S. Wildland Fire Service (USWFS) may run out of fire suppression funds this year. As you know, these two agencies had over $6 billion in fire suppression budget authority for Fiscal Year 2026. However, as of September 2, nearly the entire fire suppression budget has been spent. With over four weeks left in the fiscal year, USFS and USWFS may need to borrow funding from other accounts to pay for fire suppression.

Please respond to the following questions within 10 days:

Every day of this fire season, wildland fire personnel have put themselves in harm’s way as they work to suppress fires. Tragically, 9 first responders have given their lives this summer responding to fires. Now, more than ever, we must do everything possible to support those who have returned to the front lines after watching their colleagues fall.

Why are we seeing so many firefighter fatalities, entrapments, and shelter deployments this year? To what extent has the full suppression policy contributed to a higher rate of injuries and fatalities this summer?

In response to the deaths of so many response personnel, what resources are USFS and USWFS deploying to ensure the safety of wildland firefighters?

How are DOI and USDA prioritizing safety?

How many hours of overtime have wildland firefighters, and specifically Hotshot and Type 1 crews, accumulated so far this year? How does that compare to the past?

In 2025, DOI and USDA cut nearly 8,700 public servants, USFS alone reducing its staff by 16% (approximately 6,000 full-time equivalents) nationwide. We are especially concerned about the loss of highly-qualified personnel, supervisory capacity, and red- card holders in high-level fire management positions. We are now hearing from communities across the West that requests for crews are going unfilled.

How many complex incident management teams are operating this year? Please also provide data on the number of complex incident management teams for the last ten years.

How many personnel are working repeated or extended assignments?

Describe how DOI and USDA are managing current shortfalls in wildland firefighting teams and supervisory capacity.

What, if any, plans do DOI and USDA have to increase the number of Incident Management Teams to historic (or greater) levels?

How does the number of contract federal wildland firefighter crews compare this year to previous years?

In Fiscal Year 2025, USFS and DOI spent a combined $5.9 billion on suppression, a $1.5 billion increase from the previous most expensive year. As stated previously, the agencies have already spent over 70% of their $6 billion FY26 budget authority. As of August 31, 2026, fires have already burned nearly twice the acreage compared to 2025 (8,238,284 acres in 2026, up from 4,142,738 over the same window in 2025).

Explain why there was such a dramatic increase in spending in FY25 and how FY25 spending informed FY26 operations.

How are USDA and DOI ensuring that, after record spending in FY25, FY26 dollars are being spent as efficiently as possible to account for the significant increase in burning acres?

Going into the 2026 fire season, did USDA and DOI expect to have spent 70% of their budget authority by this point in the summer?

With the potential exhaustion of fire suppression funding this year, the federal agencies will likely be forced to use appropriated funding from other accounts to pay for fire suppression, a practice known as “fire borrowing.”

To what extent are USDA and DOI rationing other resources this summer in preparation for potential fire borrowing?

Describe the appropriated accounts that USFS and USWFS would borrow from in order to fund fire suppression.

Will USFS and USWFS borrow from accounts that fund hazardous fuels reduction, watershed restoration, state and Tribal forestry, Burned Area Emergency Response, Emergency Response, or other similar accounts focused on reducing the threat of and responding to wildland fire?

We have been glad to work with the agencies to raise pay for federal wildland firefighters. Temporary wildland firefighters (1039) continue to face pay caps and limitations on their employment. Given the extreme fire season, the Administration, in partnership with Congress, must take all necessary steps to compensate all front-line first responders.

Describe to what extent the agency has had, if any, ongoing discussions to extend the federal temporary 1039 appointment, allowing seasonal workers greater flexibility to continue fighting fires. To what extent are seasonal workers approaching the caps associated with 1039 appointments?

5 U.S.C. § 5545(c)(iii), passed in March 2025, requires USDA, DOI, and the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to ensure that the compensation paid to wildfire personnel is consistent with FY2023 levels. What steps have you taken to implement this law?

At the beginning of the 2026 fire season, agency officials discussed the successes of fighting fires in 2025.

To what extent does weather factor into the differences between the 2025 wildland fire season and the 2026 wildland fire season?

Describe how the organizational changes and restructuring of the wildland fire organizations address the issues associated with prolonged drought and extreme weather.

Thank you for your prompt response to our questions.

title: Blackburn, Duckworth Reintroduce Bipartisan Legislation to Improve Life-Saving Emergency Communication Technology
text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. – U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) and Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), members of the U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation, reintroduced legislation to improve emergency communication technology and help save lives. The ITS Codification Act would codify the Institute for Telecommunication Sciences (ITS), which currently serves as the research and engineering laboratory at the National Telecommunications and Information Administration, and require ITS to develop emergency communication and tracking technologies to help locate trapped individuals in confined spaces where conventional radio communication is limited.

“First responders in Tennessee need access to reliable technology that will help them locate trapped individuals in confined spaces where radio signals fail,” said Senator Blackburn. “Our bipartisan ITS Codification Act would drive the development of advanced communication technologies to help first responders save more lives when every second counts.”

title: Blumenthal Calls on DHS Inspector General to Investigate ICE Tactics Following Surge Targeting Connecticut Residents at Schools, Workplaces
text:
[WASHINGTON, DC] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) wrote Department of Homeland Security Inspector General Joseph Cuffari seeking “a formal investigation into the recent surge of [Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)] arrests and activity in Connecticut.”

The surge has focused on Danbury and nearby towns, where people have been targeted dropping their children off at school and going to work. “In one of the largest immigration operations in Connecticut history, ICE agents reportedly apprehended nearly 100 individuals — many of whom likely have legal status and no apparent serious criminal history — throughout the course of just one week in August,” Blumenthal wrote.

“Individuals observed: an ICE agent kicking and tasing a man while other agents were on top of him, sending the man to the hospital; ICE agents breaking car windows; removing detainees in chains; blocking attorney access to detainees in Hartford; the deployment of masked agents to locations that children frequent in Danbury, including parks, an elementary school, and a daycare center; the detention of a father walking his child to a bus stop; and a threat by ICE agents to pepper spray a man detained in front of a preschool.”

Earlier this week, Blumenthal attended Hartford Immigration Court to observe the court’s operations and demand oversight and accountability if the proper legal processes are not being followed.

Last week, Blumenthal wrote Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin and the Acting Director of ICE David Venturella requesting a meeting and demanding information about a dramatic increase in immigration enforcement activity in Connecticut. The full text of Blumenthal’s letter to Mullin and Venturella is available here.

Blumenthal also hosted a public forum to receive testimony from the Danbury community about ICE’s destructive and indiscriminate detentions. Blumenthal was joined by Mayor Roberto Alves; attorney Glenn Formica with the American Legal Immigrant Clinic; and members of Danbury United for Immigrants.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, Blumenthal has led an investigation into DHS’s abuses. Over the last year, Blumenthal and U.S. Representative Robert Garcia (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, have hosted four public forums on Capitol Hill as part of their ongoing inquiry into the lawless and abusive tactics used by federal immigration agents.

The full text of Blumenthal’s letter to Cuffari is available here and copied below.

Dear Inspector General Cuffari,

Over the past several months, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has engaged in increased enforcement activity in communities across the United States.[1] Two weeks ago, this surge came to Connecticut, where Immigration and Customs Enforcement (“ICE”) agents fanned out across towns in Connecticut, sowing fear, engaging in violent and threatening tactics, and detaining residents in the presence of their own children.[2] These troubling tactics follow similar reports from communities across the nation and come in the wake of two recent shooting deaths by immigration agents in Maine and Houston, Texas.[3] Given these troubling reports and the irreparable harm that DHS’s actions are having on communities in our nation, I write to request that you initiate a formal investigation into the recent surge of ICE arrests and activity in Connecticut.

In one of the largest immigration operations in Connecticut history, ICE agents reportedly apprehended nearly 100 individuals — many of whom likely have legal status and no apparent serious criminal history — throughout the course of just one week in August.[4] Individuals observed: an ICE agent kicking and tasing a man while other agents were on top of him, sending the man to the hospital;[5] ICE agents breaking car windows; removing detainees in chains; blocking attorney access to detainees in Hartford;[6] the deployment of masked agents to locations that children frequent in Danbury, including parks, an elementary school, and a daycare center;[7] the detention of a father walking his child to a bus stop;[8] and a threat by ICE agents to pepper spray a man detained in front of a preschool.[9]

Nationwide reporting indicates that this surge in Connecticut follows similar increases in ICE enforcement across the country, which led to the arrests of nearly 50,000 individuals in July alone, the highest single monthly total since President Trump returned to office.[10] This summer, ICE has arrested more immigrants without a criminal conviction than at any other point during this administration.[11]

This surge in enforcement activity is especially concerning in the wake of reports regarding ICE’s failure to properly vet new agents and officers who may be carrying out these enforcement operations. According to recent reporting, a whistleblower within DHS has raised serious concerns regarding the systemic breakdown of ICE’s vetting of agents, abbreviated training programs, and the fast-tracking of unqualified candidates before they even pass basic fingerprint, identity, or credit checks.[12] These concerns closely mirror testimony that the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (“PSI”) heard earlier this year from a former ICE Academy instructor, who disclosed that ICE had drastically reduced its training requirements and testified that the ICE Basic Immigration Enforcement Training Program is “deficient, defective, and broken.”[13]

As the deployment of ICE agents to communities across America continues to surge and place residents at risk — including deployments like those recently seen in Connecticut — I request that your office promptly initiate a full, fair, and impartial investigation into DHS’s recent enforcement activity including:

Whether DHS is currently employing a quota system or other metrics that dictate goals for daily or monthly arrests of immigrants that must be met.

How ICE is identifying and targeting individuals for arrest, and what steps it is taking, if any, to prioritize those with serious criminal backgrounds.

Whether any of the enforcement operations in Connecticut were undertaken in sensitive locations or in other locations where children were either present or where children are known to frequent.

Whether any of those detained during recent enforcement activities in Connecticut were U.S. Citizens or held any other legal status, and what steps agents took to ensure that those with legal status were not detained.

Whether any detained individuals in Connecticut were injured during the course of ICE’s operations.

Whether DHS or ICE received any complaints, formal or otherwise, against ICE agents for use of force during operations in Connecticut or in any other state since January 1, 2026. To the extent that complaints have been lodged, please thoroughly investigate all allegations, as well as the extent to which DHS properly implemented any necessary punishment for misconduct.

Whether ICE agents involved in operations were following protocol for the use of body cameras during enforcement operations in Connecticut.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Named Federal Champion by American Flood Coalition
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) was named a Federal Champion by the American Flood Coalition (AFC) for her leadership, public service, and commitment to finding solutions to challenges posed by flooding.

“Alabama is home to world-class federal research institutions that are leading the country in advancing flood forecasting and mapping capabilities,” said Senator Britt. “I am proud to support their work to deliver accurate, updated rainfall and flood data that engineers, planners, and communities need to build more resilient infrastructure and flood-ready communities. As a Federal Champion, I look forward to working with the American Flood Coalition to ensure those investments reach communities across Alabama and the nation.”

“Whether supporting FEMA funding as a senior appropriator or fighting for NOAA facilities in her state, Senator Britt understands that flood resilience starts long before a storm makes landfall,” said Melissa Roberts, AFC Founder and Executive Director. “Her support for effective National Weather Service programs and products means engineers and planners will finally have the data necessary to design roads, bridges, and communities that can withstand today and tomorrow’s storms. We are proud to recognize her leadership as a Federal Champion.”

Senator Britt is the lead sponsor of the bipartisan Water Research Optimization Act of 2025 to streamline hydrological forecast modeling within the National Weather Service. She has also been a strong supporter of the Cooperative Institute for Research to Operations in Hydrology (CIROH), a partnership between NOAA, The University of Alabama, and 28 different institutions committed to advancing water prediction and building community resilience to water-related challenges. Additionally, Senator Britt has been a key proponent of NOAA’s forthcoming Atlas 15 nationwide rainfall dataset, among other key tools in development by the Office of Water Prediction. In Fiscal Year 2026 Appropriations funding, Senator Britt secured tens of millions in funding for both CIROH and the National Water Center.

Senator Britt serves as Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee’s Subcommittee on Homeland Security, where she oversees FEMA’s budget and the Department of Homeland Security’s disaster preparedness and response programs. She also serves on the Appropriations Committee’s Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, which oversees the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ Civil Works program. Additionally, as a member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, Senator Britt oversees the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and the Department of Housing and Urban Development’s Community Development Block Grant for Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) program.
