title: House Passes Hudson, Knott Bill to Clear Way for New Veterans Home Near Fort Bragg
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the U.S. House of Representatives passed legislation led by U.S. Representatives Richard Hudson (NC-09), Fort Bragg’s Congressman, and Brad Knott (NC-13) to clear the way for construction of a new state veterans home near Fort Bragg.

“Our veterans sacrificed to take care of us, and we have a responsibility to take care of them,” said Rep. Hudson. “After the Fayetteville State Veterans Home closed, 85 veterans were forced to leave their home and relocate across the state, many far away from their families. Today’s passage brings us one step closer to building a new home near Fort Bragg and bringing that care back to our community.”

"Tens of thousands of veterans call North Carolina’s 13th District home, and they’ve earned care worthy of their service,” said Rep. Knott. "Since the Fayetteville veterans' home closed in 2024, our state's heroes in central North Carolina have been without a home built for their care. I am proud to work with Congressman Hudson on this bill to advance a new veterans' home in Harnett County, which will provide quality, long-term care for those who served our country.”

The legislation transfers 20 acres off installation at Fort Bragg to the State of North Carolina, allowing the state to move forward with the permitting and construction process for the new veterans home.

The former Fayetteville State Veterans Home closed in 2024, displacing 85 veterans, including many with dementia and other disabilities. Hudson has worked with members of the North Carolina congressional delegation and the North Carolina Department of Military and Veterans Affairs to advance plans for a replacement facility, and the legislation is a necessary step in that effort.

Hudson spoke on the House floor ahead of passage, urging his colleagues to support the legislation and highlighting the need to restore a veterans home to the Fayetteville and Fort Bragg community.

Hudson and Knott were joined by Reps. David Rouzer (NC-07), Don Davis (NC-01), Deborah Ross (NC-02), Greg Murphy (NC-03), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Virginia Foxx (NC-05), Addison McDowell (NC-06), Mark Harris (NC-08), Pat Harrigan (NC-10), Chuck Edwards (NC-11), Alma Adams (NC-12), and Tim Moore (NC-14) in cosponsoring the legislation.

title: Congressman Issa Introduces Digital Asset Inventory and Audit Act to Find and Protect Digital Assets in Federal Custody
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.– Congressman Darrell Issa (CA-48) recently introduced the Digital Asset Inventory and Audit Act of 2026, legislation to ensure the federal government identifies, secures, and accounts for cryptocurrency and other digital assets that come into its custody.

As federal law enforcement agencies routinely seize computers, phones, and other electronic evidence during investigations, those devices can contain private keys, seed phrases, digital wallets, and other cryptographic information that provide access to digital assets that may be related to criminal activity. What’s missing is a uniform government-wide requirement to identify and account for those assets.

“The federal government cannot protect, recover, or account for assets it does not know it possesses,” said Congressman Issa. “When law enforcement seizes an electronic device, it may also be taking custody of the keys to digital assets that should also be seized. It’s time to recognize and remedy that reality.”

Congressman Lance Gooden (TX-5), an original co-sponsor of H.R. 10317, added “As criminals increasingly use digital assets to move and conceal illicit funds, our law enforcement agencies must keep pace. This bill ensures federal agencies have the tools, standards, and accountability necessary to properly identify and safeguard digital assets in government custody.”

Specifically, the legislation requires federal agencies to identify, secure, and account for digital assets discovered in electronic evidence. It also directs DOJ and NIST to establish government-wide standards for handling those assets and requires regular audits and oversight. The legislation creates no new search or seizure authorities and preserves existing legal and privacy protections.

“The Digital Chamber applauds Reps. Lance Gooden and Darrell Issa for introducing the Digital Asset Inventory and Audit Act of 2026. As digital assets play a growing role in law enforcement investigations and federal asset management, agencies need modern, consistent standards for identifying, securing, and accounting for them. This legislation is an important step toward that goal, and we look forward to working with these Co-Sponsors and Congress to advance it.”

And the Epstein survivors deserve accountability and transparency, and that’s why House Democrats are continuing to push back aggressively against the Department of Justice’s ongoing cover-up of the Epstein files. The explosive growth of artificial intelligence and the challenges that are therein presented—that’s not a hoax. It’s very real, despite what Donald Trump has to say about that issue as well, and it requires decisive congressional action immediately in a manner consistent with what some of the leading AI voices in the country are now saying needs to happen as it relates to slowing things down to protect the health, the safety and the well-being of the American people.

There are 50 days until the American people will have an ability to move things in this country in a different direction. We have a president right now uninterested in solving the challenges confronting the American people. Instead, he continues to publicly and brazenly make the unhinged observation that these challenges, including the affordability crisis and the safety concerns related to artificial intelligence, are hoaxes. They are not. They are very real issues. Republicans should stop burying their heads in the sand. Democrats will never make that mistake.

title: Kamlager-Dove to Run for Co-Chair of House Democrats’ Messaging Apparatus
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) announced her candidacy for Co-Chair of the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee (DPCC), a key leadership position within the caucus that helps develop messaging and communication strategies for House Democrats.

Rep. Kamlager-Dove announced her intentions in the following letter to colleagues:

Dear Colleague:

As this week will likely be our last together before the critical November elections, I wanted to respectfully ask for your support in serving as Co-Chair of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee (DPCC). After what I believe will be a historic election for our caucus, Americans will look to House Democrats for leadership through the remaining years of the dreadful Trump presidency. I want to serve as a bridge between leadership and my fellow colleagues as we face the monumental challenges ahead.

My decision to run for DPCC Co-Chair was born from the misery and anguish of the 2024 presidential election. A major lesson from that loss was that our party did not do enough to communicate with voters where they were through the new media landscape of social media, creators, independent journalists, podcasts, and other emerging platforms. So I threw myself into all of it to learn, experiment, and most importantly, break through. After Trump’s illegal actions in his first months in office, I launched Is This Sh*t Legal? to cut through the noise and explain what made those actions illegal, why they mattered, and how Democrats were fighting back. My favorite part of this series was bringing so many of you in and watching your authenticity and passion shine through. I’ve also prioritized building lasting relationships with creators, podcasters, and independent journalists so we’re consistently reaching their audiences and making sure our message is part of the conversation year-round.

What’s important to me as a member of this caucus is ensuring that any progress we make benefits all of us. Because I know our strength and success as a caucus depends on our unity. We cannot create an affordable America or hold Trump accountable as solo actors on a stage. That’s why I have made it a priority to collaborate with so many of you, proudly filming with more than a quarter of our caucus this term–with some members joining me two, three, even four times.

Building on this unity framework, one of my biggest goals, if elected Co-Chair, is to connect the incredible creative talent in my home city of Los Angeles to the Democratic Caucus. Hollywood understands how to tell complicated stories in compelling, accessible ways that meet people where they are. I want to build a stronger bridge between our members and the writers, producers, storytellers, and digital creators who can help us communicate our agenda, connect with voters, and move people to action.

Our caucus has an opportunity to meet this moment with clarity, creativity, and unity. I am ready to bring my experience, relationships, and perspective from Los Angeles to help strengthen how we communicate, collaborate, and deliver for the American people. Above all, I’m committed to being a trusted voice for every member of this caucus and to ensuring that you and your districts are represented when decisions are made and messaging is shaped.

I would be honored to serve alongside each of you as Co-Chair of DPCC, and I respectfully ask for your support as we work together to build a stronger, more effective Democratic Caucus.

Sincerely,

Sydney Kamlager-Dove

Member of Congress

Rep. Kamlager-Dove is in her second term serving California’s 37th Congressional District. She is a member of the House Judiciary Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee, where she serves as Ranking Member on the South and Central Asia Subcommittee, and is Whip of the Congressional Black Caucus and Policy Co-Chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus.

title: Kean Visits Somerville to Highlight $1,942,000 Secured in Federal Funding
text:

The funding will be used for two complementary capital improvement projects: the Division Street Arts Plaza and the Giardina Walk Improvements. Together, these projects will transform two heavily traveled public corridors into vibrant, safe, and fully accessible pedestrian spaces that anchor Downtown Somerville’s arts and cultural identity.

“Downtown Somerville is truly the heart of Somerset County, and this investment will help make it an even better place to live, work, shop, and dine,” said Congressman Kean. “I fought for this funding because Somerville deserves a downtown that reflects the energy, character, and pride of this special community. title: Kiggans’ Bill to Ensure Proper Lifeguard Staffing on Public Beaches Passes the House with Bipartisan Support
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) announced the House passage of her bill, H.R. 5063, the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act, which passed the House by voice. This bill would direct the Secretary of the Interior to work with local governments to ensure there is proper lifeguard coverage in the event of a lifeguard shortage.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “As the representative of a coastal district, keeping our beaches safe for the families who live here and the millions of people who visit them every year is incredibly important to me. Last summer, communities on Virginia’s Eastern Shore were forced to step up when a federal lifeguard shortage left Chincoteague without the assurance our families deserve. Our local leaders did the right thing, but they should never be left scrambling to solve a federal staffing problem or pay the bill to keep a federal beach safe.

“The Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act provides a commonsense solution by allowing the Department of the Interior to partner with local governments when lifeguard shortages occur and ensuring those communities are reimbursed for the costs they take on. I’m incredibly proud to see this bipartisan bill pass the House today, and I want to thank Mayor Denise Bowden and our local leaders on the Eastern Shore for working with us to turn a challenge we experienced at home into a solution that can help keep families safe at federal beaches across the country.”

“Families visiting America’s vast federal beaches and swimming areas should be able to count on properly staffed shores. H.R. 5063 allows the Department of the Interior to partner with local governments during lifeguard shortages and guarantees those communities are reimbursed for the costs they incur, ensuring federal responsibilities are not shifted to local taxpayers. I commend Rep. Kiggans for developing a practical solution that strengthens visitor safety and supports the coastal communities in Virginia welcoming millions of Americans each year,” said Chairman Bruce Westerman.

Watch Rep. Kiggans’ speech from the House Floor here.

Read Rep. Kiggans’ remarks from the House Floor prior to the bill’s passage as prepared for delivery:

Thank you, Mr. Speaker.

I rise today in support of my bill, H.R. 5063, the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act.

I have the privilege of representing a district that lives on the beach and the Bay. For families across Coastal Virginia, and the millions of Americans who visit our federal beaches every year, water safety is incredibly important.

Last year, we saw firsthand what can happen when the federal government fails to adequately staff these beaches.

Following a federal hiring freeze, Assateague Island National Seashore was unable to provide its normal lifeguard coverage at the federal beach in Chincoteague, Virginia.

Families continued visiting and swimming, but the lifeguards they had come to rely on were not there.

Our local leaders stepped up. The Town of Chincoteague and Accomack County took on unforeseen costs to make sure lifeguards returned to the beach and families could safely enjoy the water.

But our local governments should never be left scrambling to solve a federal staffing problem on their own.

That is why I introduced the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act.

My bill provides a commonsense solution. When the Department of the Interior determines that a federal swimming area is facing a lifeguard staffing shortage, it can partner with local governments to provide the necessary coverage. And importantly, when a local government steps up to provide those lifeguards, the federal government will reimburse it for the reasonable costs it incurs.

This applies to designated swimming areas managed by the National Park Service, Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, and Bureau of Reclamation that are normally monitored by federal lifeguards.

Mr. Speaker, this bill is about public safety, accountability, and giving our communities a solution when Washington falls short.

I am grateful to the local leaders on the Eastern Shore who worked with us after seeing this problem firsthand, and I am proud that we now have an opportunity to make sure communities across the country have another tool to keep their beaches safe.

No family visiting a federal beach should have to wonder whether a lifeguard will be there when an emergency happens.

I urge my colleagues to support the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act, and I yield back.

The Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act now moves to the Senate for consideration.

Background:

In June 2025, Congresswoman Kiggans questioned Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum in the House Committee on Natural Resources regarding recent federal hiring freezes and whether temporary hires, including lifeguards, would receive an exemption. Watch the Congresswoman’s questioning here and coverage from Shore Daily News here.

Following the hearing, Congresswoman Kiggans sent a letter to Secretary Burgum reaffirming concern for the federal hiring freeze and its impact on the lifeguard shortage. Read her letter here.

In September 2025, Rep. Kiggans introduced the Safe Beaches, Safe Swimmers Act in response to lifeguard shortages on Chincoteague Island and across the Eastern Shore of Virginia in the Summer of 2025. Read her press release here.

Watch Rep. Kiggans’ interview with CBS News following the bill’s introduction here.

title: Kiggans Welcomes Federal Highway Administrator Sean McMaster to Hampton Roads, Highlights Major Hampton Roads Projects
text:
NORFOLK, VA — Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) joined Federal Highway Administrator Sean McMaster and local transportation leaders to highlight major infrastructure projects underway in Hampton Roads and discuss continued efforts to improve transportation throughout Coastal Virginia.

Congresswoman Kiggans and Administrator McMaster received a briefing from representatives of the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT), and the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel (HRBT) Expansion Project on ongoing work related to the HRBT Expansion and Hampton Roads Express Lanes.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “Everyone from Hampton Roads knows how critical our tunnels, roads, and bridges are to everyday life. However, transportation infrastructure is more important than just getting from Point A to Point B. Not only does it support operations on our military installations and the movement of goods through the Port of Virginia, but it also keeps our shipyards and ship repair industry moving, connects our local businesses, and helps hardworking families get where they need to go.”

“At nearly $4 billion, the HRBT Expansion project is the largest highway construction undertaking in the Commonwealth’s history, and a great example of what we can accomplish with federal, state, and local collaboration. I’m grateful to Administrator McMaster for coming to Hampton Roads to witness the project firsthand and I look forward to continuing working with the Federal Highway Administration to ensure our region has the safe and reliable infrastructure it needs to thrive,” Kiggans concluded.

The HRBT Expansion Project is widening approximately 10 miles of Interstate 64 between Norfolk and Hampton and constructing two new two-lane bored tunnels alongside the existing tunnels. Once completed, the corridor will expand from four lanes to eight lanes, including six general-purpose lanes and two Express Lanes. The project will help address one of the region’s most significant transportation bottlenecks while improving connectivity for commuters, freight, military personnel, and visitors.

Kiggans’ Work to Secure Transportation Priorities for Hampton Roads:

Since entering Congress, Congresswoman Kiggans has also worked to secure federal funding for transportation priorities throughout Virginia’s Second District, including:

$3 million for Laskin Road Phase I-B in Virginia Beach,

$3.04 million for preliminary engineering and environmental work for the King’s Highway Bridge replacement in Suffolk,

And $1 million for flood-resiliency improvements to Pungo Ferry Road in Virginia Beach.

Through the Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (TIFIA) program, the Hampton Roads Transportation Accountability Commission (HRTAC) applied for a loan of $310 million to finance related express lane projects. By December 2025, the loan had reached the final approval stages, but had yet to receive approval from the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT). Following contact from Congresswoman Kiggans’ office, USDOT announced in September 2026 that the loan would proceed, saving local taxpayers roughly $11 million.

Via FY26 federal-aid highway formula funding through FHWA, Virginia received approximately $1.46 billion to support highway construction, bridge improvements, safety, congestion reduction, and other transportation projects across the Commonwealth.

Other FY26 Virginia allocations include:

Approximately $795 million through the National Highway Performance Program,

$387 million through the Surface Transportation Block Grant Program,

And $85 million through the Highway Safety Improvement Program.

As of September 30, 2025, there were 149 new federal-aid highway project commitments in Virginia’s Second Congressional District totaling approximately $219 million, according to the American Road & Transportation Builders Association’s district-level analysis of federal highway data. Major commitments include:

$23.15 million for I-64 Southside widening/High Rise Bridge work,

$19.92 million for Elbow Road Phase 2C,

$13.22 million for Laskin Road Phase 1-A,

And $13.14 million for Hampton Roads districtwide paving.

title: $7.1M to HSEM to Support Sinlaku Emergency Response
text: Congratulations to the CNMI Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Management on receiving $7,076,132.78 in FEMA grant funding to support emergency protective measures following Super Typhoon Sinlaku. This award is funded at a 100% federal cost share under Section 403 of the Robert T. Stafford Act. The funding will reimburse and support critical emergency response activities carried out between April 12 and July 9, 2026, including personnel costs, contract services, and the operation of the Emergency Operations Center. This federal assistance recognizes the significant resources the CNMI deployed during the disaster and helps ensure our local agencies have the support they need to respond effectively.

title: Ensuring Economic Benefits and Protections from Seabed Mining
text:
On September 8, I introduced H.R. 10318, the Pacific Minerals Economic Security Act (PACMESA), to ensure the Northern Mariana Islands and other U.S. Pacific territories directly affected by potential seabed mining receive meaningful economic benefits and a stronger voice in decisions that could impact our communities. PACMESA would direct 50 percent of revenues from covered seabed mining leases to eligible adjacent territorial governments, creating a significant source of revenue for the CNMI if seabed mining occurs offshore. The bill would also strengthen environmental bonding requirements to help ensure companies are financially accountable for potential impacts and expand notification and consultation requirements for territorial governments. Critical minerals are increasingly important to America’s economic competitiveness and national security. If seabed mining occurs offshore our communities, the CNMI should not bear the risks without receiving a meaningful share of the benefits and having a seat at the table. PACMESA provides those protections and helps close important gaps in existing federal law governing hard mineral development on the Outer Continental Shelf.

title: Talking about Connecting Local Business to a Larger Pacific Strategy
text: As the United States seeks to increase both its presence and its influence in the Pacific region, it is critical that our nation’s foreign policy does not overlook one of its most productive assets, its Pacific territories. I firmly believe the territories can be influential voices in our country’s diplomacy with our neighbors, but official diplomacy is only one part of that role. Commerce, investment, transportation, and business relationships also help strengthen America’s presence across the region. Last week, I met with Del Benson and Nathan Benson at the District Office to talk about the role CNMI businesses can play in advancing American interests in the Pacific and the steps we can take, both in the private sector and through the federal government, to help create more opportunities for our local businesses to participate in regional growth. The CNMI sits in the middle of a region that is becoming increasingly important to the United States. We should be thinking seriously about how our businesses, our people, and our location can contribute to that strategy while also creating new opportunities here at home. Thanks Del and Nathan for stopping by and for the great conversation.

title: Talking Constituent Casework with Rotary
text: I came almost straight from the airport to join the Rotary Club of Saipan last week for a conversation about one of the most important services we provide to the people of the Commonwealth, congressional casework. Since January 3, 2025, we have handled at least 612 formal cases and resolved 377 of them. This year alone, we have received more than 370 new cases and resolved a little more than 210. Immigration represents about 48 percent of our casework, Social Security about 20 percent, and FEMA another 20 percent this year because of disaster-related assistance. The central point of my remarks, and what I want to share with all of you, is simple. If you need assistance with the federal government, reach out. Whether it is Social Security, immigration, FEMA, veterans benefits, passports, or another federal issue, our team is here to help you navigate the process and work toward a resolution. Thank you to Rotary for having me and for giving me the opportunity to talk about this important part of the work we do for you.

title: Their Memory Lives On
text: Last week, our office joined the community for the annual We Will Never Forget ceremony and the 11th Annual Field of Heroes as we remembered the lives lost on September 11, 2001, and honored the first responders, service members, and community servants who continue to serve others every day. Thank you to all of the sponsors, organizers, volunteers, and community servants who come together each year to make this commemoration possible. Twenty-five years later, the promise remains the same. We will never forget.

title: Working Together to Support Our Schools
text: When the economy struggles, government revenues fall. That means austerity, reduced services, and difficult decisions about how limited local resources are used. One of the places where those pressures are felt most directly is in our public school system. The CNMI Public School System educates thousands of our children, and federal funding already supports a significant share of its operating budget. I am grateful that we have been able to protect those federal resources, but with local revenues continuing to shrink, we also need to think creatively about how every available resource can be used to support our schools. That is why I sincerely appreciate PSS Board Chair Maisie Tenorio and PSS Director Donna Flores for coming by and having a frank and productive conversation about needs, opportunities, and how we can develop a shared strategy for leveraging federal and local resources to give our children the strong educational foundation they deserve. Thank you Maisie and Donna for stopping by and for your service to our students!

title: Knott, Hudson Bill to Advance a New Veterans’ Home in Harnett County Passes the House
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. - Congressman Brad Knott (NC-13) issued the following statement after the House passed H.R. 10159, a bill he co-led with Congressman Richard Hudson (NC-09) to transfer land facilitating the construction of a new state veterans' home in Harnett County.

"Tens of thousands of veterans call North Carolina’s 13th District home, and they’ve earned care worthy of their service,” said Congressman Knott. "Since the Fayetteville veterans' home closed in 2024, our state's heroes in central North Carolina have been without a home built for their care. I am proud to work with Congressman Hudson on this bill to advance a new veterans' home in Harnett County, which will provide quality, long-term care for those who served our country."

“Our veterans kept their promise to serve, and we have a responsibility to keep our promise to take care of them,” said Congressman Hudson. “After the Fayetteville State Veterans Home closed, veterans were forced to relocate across the state, many far away from their families. Today’s passage brings us one step closer to building a new home near Fort Bragg and bringing that care back to our community.”

Background:

The North Carolina State Veterans Home in Fayetteville closed in 2024 due to disrepair and health and safety concerns.

H.R. 10159 transfers a 20-acre parcel of land from the Fort Bragg Training Area to the State of North Carolina to build a replacement facility.

The new site sits roughly 15 miles from the original Fayetteville location, along the western access road to Fort Bragg.

Congressmen Knott and Hudson were joined by Reps. David Rouzer (NC-07), Don Davis (NC-01), Deborah Ross (NC-02), Greg Murphy (NC-03), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Virginia Foxx (NC-05), Addison McDowell (NC-06), Mark Harris (NC-08), Pat Harrigan (NC-10), Chuck Edwards (NC-11), Alma Adams (NC-12), and Tim Moore (NC-14) in cosponsoring the legislation.

title: Congressman Langworthy Announces Nearly $13.6 Million in Federal Aviation Grants for Airports Across New York’s 23rd Congressional District
text:
Washington, D.C.—September 14th… Congressman Nick Langworthy today announced $13,532,819 in federal Airport Improvement Program (AIP) grants from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) for critical infrastructure improvements at three airports across New York’s 23rd Congressional District.

The grants will support runway and taxiway rehabilitation projects designed to maintain the structural integrity of existing pavement, improve safety and reliability, and extend the useful life of critical airport infrastructure.

“This significant $13.6 million investment will help ensure our airports across the Southern Tier and Western New York have the safe, reliable infrastructure they need to serve our communities and support economic growth,” said Congressman Nick Langworthy. “Strong aviation infrastructure is essential for connecting our communities, supporting local businesses and keeping our region competitive. I’m proud to help bring these federal resources home and will continue working to make sure our region gets its fair share.”

The specific grants include:

$11,080,483 for Elmira/Corning Regional Airport in Elmira, awarded to Chemung County. The funding will support the second phase of construction to rehabilitate 8,000 feet of existing paved Runway 6/24, which has reached the end of its useful life, as well as reconstruct its runway lighting. The project will help maintain the structural integrity of the runway and minimize foreign object debris.

$1,619,172 for Wellsville Municipal/Tarantine Field in Wellsville, awarded to the Town of Wellsville. The funding will support the final construction phase of a project to rehabilitate 5,700 feet of existing paved Taxiway A, maintaining pavement integrity, minimizing foreign object debris and extending its useful life.

$833,164 for Akron/Jesson Field in Akron, awarded to Christian Airmen Inc. The funding will support the final construction phase of a project to rehabilitate 3,268 feet of existing paved Runway 7/25, helping maintain its structural integrity, minimize foreign object debris and extend the runway’s useful life.

The funding was awarded through the Federal Aviation Administration’s FY2026 Airport Improvement Program, which provides federal resources for airport infrastructure projects.

title: McCaul Introduces Legislation to Accelerate Breakthroughs in Pediatric Cancer by Leveraging AI
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Michael McCaul (R-Texas) — founder and co-chair of the Congressional Childhood Cancer Caucus — introduced the Ailani Myers Accelerating Innovation in Medicine (AIM) to Cure Kids with Cancer Act with caucus co-chairs Ami Bera, M.D. (D-Calif.) and Mike Kelly (R-Pa.). The legislation, which is named after a brave young cancer patient and advocate, will accelerate the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to improve and transform pediatric cancer research, treatment options, and data storage.

McCaul said, "Since I founded the Childhood Cancer Caucus 17 years ago, advancements in technology have radically expanded the frontiers of healthcare. We owe it to our nation's children to leverage cutting-edge AI to improve their care and treatment options. I'm proud to introduce this bill, which codifies and builds on President Trump's executive order to unlock cures for pediatric cancer patients. By empowering AI to continuously drive research forward, we move one step closer to beating this heartbreaking disease once and for all.

"I'm also proud to have named this bill after Ailani Myers, a beautiful young cancer fighter. Like so many of the children I've met, she is far more courageous than most adults. Even a rare form of Leukemia can't steal her smile! Ailani has fiercely advocated for the childhood cancer community and recently attended the signing of President Trump's executive order accelerating AI use for pediatric cancer cures. It's fitting that this bill carry her name and her legacy forward."

Image

McCaul and Ailani in 2013

“Pediatric cancer remains one of the most heartbreaking diagnoses any family can face, and we have a responsibility to use every tool available to improve outcomes for children,” said Bera. “The bipartisan Accelerating Innovation in Medicine for Kids with Cancer Act would leverage cutting-edge AI and data tools to transform pediatric cancer research, improve clinical trial design and access, and deliver more personalized treatment options for young patients. I am proud to support this effort to accelerate innovation, strengthen the Childhood Kelly Data Initiative, and move us closer to ending cancer as we know it.”

“Congress should always consider new, initiative ways not only to treat cancer, but to defeat cancer. This legislation would leverage artificial intelligence to strengthen patient care and patient outcomes,” said Kelly.“I’m proud to sponsor the bipartisan Accelerating Innovation in Medicine for Kids with Cancer Act as we work to ensure pediatric cancer patients and their families have every tool at their disposal to receive the care and cures they deserve.”

The Ailani Myers AIM to Cure Kids with Cancer Act would:

Codify and strengthen the National Cancer Institute’s Childhood Cancer Data Initiative, authorizing federal support to collect, connect, and share pediatric cancer data;

Establish an AI coordinator to align pediatric cancer efforts across the White House, federal agencies, and private-sector partners; and

Harness AI to accelerate pediatric cancer research and treatment by improving data sharing, strengthening predictive modeling, and modernizing clinical trials.

title: House Passes Chairwoman McClain's Common Cents Act to End Wasteful Penny Production
text:
WASHINGTON— Today, the House passed H.R. 10167, the Common Cents Act, legislation led by House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.), to permanently end production of the penny for general circulation and modernize America’s coinage system.

“Washington has a spending problem, and it shows up in places big and small,” Chairwoman McClain said. “If the federal government is spending nearly four cents to make a penny worth one cent, something is broken. House Republicans are proving that common sense still has a place in government by cutting waste and protecting taxpayer dollars.”

The Common Cents Act ends production of pennies for general circulation while keeping existing pennies legal tender and allowing the U.S. Mint to continue producing collectible coins. It also establishes uniform guidance allowing cash transactions to be rounded to the nearest five cents when exact change is unavailable. Electronic payments and other non-cash transactions will continue to be charged to the exact cent.

The legislation also directs the Federal Reserve to develop a national transition plan for the hundreds of billions of pennies already in circulation and requires Treasury to notify Congress before discontinuing any other circulating coin. It also authorizes a lower-cost nickel composition if testing shows it will reduce production costs without significantly disrupting coin-operated machines.

title: The Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange Act Approved by House of Representatives
text:
September 14, 2026

Washington, D.C. – The Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange Act, H.R. 8454, has passed the House of Representatives by a voice vote. The legislation by Congressman McClintock, H.R. 8454, has companion legislation in the Senate authored by Senator Padilla, S. 288.

The legislation addresses a familiar problem in federal land management in the Sierra Nevada: the checkerboard of boundary lines that makes land management disjointed and inefficient. The legislation consolidates land jurisdictions between the National Park System and the National Forest System and will help to eliminate confusion caused by split jurisdiction.

“Jurisdictional boundaries should not stand in the way of effective land management. H.R. 8454 transfers administrative jurisdiction over federal parcels in Ackerson Meadow, helping establish a more logical and efficient approach to managing and restoring this vital ecosystem,” remarked House Natural Resources Committee Chairman Bruce Westerman. “I commend Rep. McClintock for pursuing a targeted solution that improves government efficiency and advances responsible land management in California.”

Congressman McClintock delivered the following remarks today on the House floor in support of the legislation:

Floor Statement (Video Link)

H.R. 8454

Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange Act

September 14, 2026

Mr. Speaker:

The Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange Act is a simple proposal to transfer administrative jurisdiction over approximately 160 acres of National Forest System land to Yosemite National Park. It would also transfer approximately 170 acres of National Park System land to be a part of the Stanislaus National Forest.

Senator Padilla is carrying identical legislation in the Senate. We don’t agree on much, but we certainly agree on this.

This legislation addresses a familiar problem in federal land management in the Sierra Nevada: the checkerboard of boundary lines that makes land management disjointed and inefficient. This bill simply consolidates land jurisdictions between the National Park System and the National Forest System, without increasing the federal footprint.

At issue is the Ackerson Meadow. This meadow supports livestock grazing operations that have been part of the history and economy of the region. These operations are essential for brush control and fire suppression, maintaining meadow conditions and sustaining the rural economy that depends on the productive use of these lands.

Federal agencies, conservation organizations, and local ranchers have worked together to improve the meadow while maintaining grazing opportunities. Restoration projects have improved wetland conditions, enhanced water storage, improved habitat, and supported continued public uses, including grazing.

The proposed land exchange would make that cooperative approach easier by eliminating the confusion caused by split jurisdiction. Ranchers need to know where their permits apply, where infrastructure can be maintained, and who is responsible for decisions affecting their operations.

The bill also protects existing rights and authorizations. It specifically provides that valid existing rights, including rights-of-way, easements, leases, licenses, and permits, remain protected after the transfer. This ensures that current users, including grazing permit holders, are not unfairly disrupted by a change in administrative jurisdiction.

It also appropriately maintains federal responsibilities for hazardous substance cleanup and other obligations.

This bill reflects a principle that should guide federal land policy, management decisions should be based on the realities of the landscape, not simply the boundaries drawn on a map decades ago.

Our national forests and parks serve many purposes. They preserve wildlife habitat, protect watersheds, provide recreation, and support rural economies. A balanced approach recognizes all of these values.

I urge adoption of this measure and yield back the balance of my time.

title: Amid NYFW, Nadler & Gillibrand Reintroduce FABRIC Act To Support Garment Workers And Revitalize The US Fashion Industry
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Jerry Nadler (NY-12) and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) announced the reintroduction of their Fashioning Accountability and Building Real Institutional Change (FABRIC) Act.

In New York State, there are approximately 130,000 people employed by the fashion industry, including thousands working in apparel manufacturing. Garment workers are a cornerstone of the American economy, and for far too long, they have faced unsafe working conditions, wage theft, and piecework pay, which often prioritizes fast fashion over the safety of workers. Nadler and Gillibrand's FABRIC Act would protect over 75,000 American garment workers and help revitalize the garment manufacturing industry in the United States by improving working conditions and reforming the piece-rate pay scale.

“America's garment workers have been undervalued and subjected to unfair labor practices for far too long, due to weak regulations across the fashion industry and the rise of fast fashion. With more than 100,000 New Yorkers contributing their labor to a billion-dollar garment industry, it is time to protect these workers and others across our nation and make historic investments in domestic manufacturing by passing the FABRIC Act,” said Congressman Jerrold Nadler. “I’m proud to work with Senator Gillibrand to protect workers’ rights, bring jobs back from overseas, and revitalize the American fashion industry.”

“Garment workers are the backbone of a multibillion-dollar industry, yet for far too long, their labor has been undervalued and exploited,” said Senator Gillibrand. “We cannot champion American innovation while turning a blind eye to abusive labor practices in our own backyard. It’s time to take bold action at the federal level to change the fabric of the American garment industry. The United States was once home to a booming apparel manufacturing industry, and it’s time to reexamine how this industry has evolved over the past 50 years and change how we treat our workers. With the FABRIC Act, we can curb wage theft, protect our workers, and revitalize domestic manufacturing so that 'Made in America' also means ethically made.”

The FABRIC Act proposes to address these issues by:

Restructuring pay rates for garment workers and providing minimum wage as a floor with productivity incentives on top.

Establishing new liability measures that compel major retailers to become allies in combating workplace violations.

Introducing recordkeeping and transparency measures, including requiring garment manufacturers and contractors operating in the U.S. to register with the Department of Labor.

Incentivizing reshoring by creating a domestic garment manufacturing grant program aimed at revitalizing the industry.

In addition to Nadler and Gillibrand, the bill is cosponsored by Reps. Deborah Ross (D-NC), Don Beyer (D-VA), Maxwell Frost (D-FL), Robert Garcia (D-CA), Dan Goldman (D-NY), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), and Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), as well as Senators Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Tammy Duckworth (D-IL). The bill is also endorsed by AFL-CIO, UNITE HERE, Workers United, and RWDSU.

title: House Passes Nehls' National Law Enforcement Officers Remembrance, Support, and Community Outreach Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Troy E. Nehls (R-TX-22) announced that his bill, H.R. 309, the National Law Enforcement Officers Remembrance, Support, and Community Outreach Act, passed the U.S. House of Representatives by a voice vote.

"I am proud that the U.S. House of Representatives unanimously passed my bipartisan legislation to honor our brave law enforcement officers and raise public awareness of their service," said Congressman Nehls. "As a former law enforcement officer and Texas sheriff, I know firsthand the sacrifices our men and women in blue make, often without receiving the recognition and gratitude they deserve. Our law enforcement officers risk their lives every day to keep our communities safe, and I urge the Senate to swiftly pass this legislation."

"America’s law enforcement officers put their lives on the line each day with courage, resolve and an unwavering commitment to their communities," said House Natural Resources Committee Chairman Bruce Westerman. "H.R. 309 supports the National Law Enforcement Museum’s public education, community outreach, and officer wellness initiatives, helping more Americans understand the demands of this noble profession. Rep. Nehls brings firsthand experience to this effort, and I commend his continued leadership on behalf of our nation’s law enforcement officers."

This bipartisan legislation seeks to establish a formal program within the U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) that will enhance community outreach, public education, and officer safety and wellness initiatives at the National Law Enforcement Museum. The program will offer grants to the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund (NLEOMF). Its goals include honoring law enforcement officers, collecting data on officer fatalities and injuries, increasing public understanding and support for law enforcement, improving officer safety and wellness, and strengthening the bond between law enforcement and the communities they serve.

title: Omar, Scott, Casar Introduce Legislation to Protect Workers’ Hard-Earned Wages from Medical Debt Collection
text:
WASHINGTON— Today, House Committee on Education and Workforce Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), Subcommittee on Workforce Protections Ranking Member Rep. Ilhan Omar (MN-05), and Vice Ranking Member Rep. Greg Casar (TX-35), introduced the Protecting Workers’ Wages from Medical Debt Act. This bill would prohibit workers’ wages from being garnished to pay for medical debt.

Right now, approximately 100 million Americans are trapped with $220 billion in medical debt. Looming unpaid medical bills can devastate working families, whether they have health insurance or not. Unfortunately, the medical debt crisis has become more dire as millions of Americans are being stripped of their health care due to President Trump and Congressional Republicans’ disastrous “Big, Ugly Bill.”

Over the last several years, new reports of hospitals and debt collectors suing patients for outstanding bills and forcibly cutting their wages to repay the debt have highlighted the predatory nature of wage garnishments.

Currently, federal law allows up to 25 percent of a worker’s take-home pay to be garnished each workweek. Over 30 states have taken action to better protect consumers and have added additional protections to prevent workers’ wages from being unnecessarily garnished. However, when workers are struggling, these constraints are not enough.

The Protecting Workers’ Wages from Medical Debt Act protects workers, many of whom are struggling to make ends meet, by prohibiting wages from being garnished for the payment of medical debt. Specifically, the bill:

Bans any amount of a worker’s wage from being subject to garnishment for medical debt, and

Prohibits any state or court from issuing or enforcing a wage garnishment order for medical debt.

“In the richest country in the world, medical debt should not be a threat to working people’s livelihood. The American people should not have to slash spending on necessities to pay for life-saving care and no one should be denied future health care because of unpaid medical bills. Unfortunately, that is the reality many Americans are facing right now,” said Ranking Member Scott. “I am proud to work with Reps. Omar and Casar on this commonsense legislation, which will ensure families are not thrown into further hardship simply because they got sick and needed care.”

“In 45 states, some workers have a portion of their take-home pay forcibly cut to pay off medical debt,” said Subcommittee on Workforce Protections Ranking Member Omar. “I'm partnering with Ranking Member Bobby Scott (D-VA) and Rep. Greg Casar (D-TX) to ban this practice and ensure no worker is thrown into further financial hardship over often-predatory debt.”

“Nobody should lose their wages because they got sick,” said Vice Ranking Member Greg Casar (D-TX). “Trump and Republicans ripped health care away from millions of Americans to pay for tax cuts for billionaires. Now families who get sick are being hit with bills they can't pay, and in most states a hospital or debt collector can take a cut of their paycheck before they ever see it. This needs to end, and our bill would stop it.”

The Protecting Workers’ Wages from Medical Debt Act is endorsed by: American Federation of Teachers (AFT); Center for Health and Democracy; Families USA; Public Citizen; and Service Employees International Union (SEIU).

title: Rep. Panetta Continues Legal Push Challenging  Administration’s Efforts to Restart Sable Offshore Pipeline
text:
Washington, D.C. – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joined Rep. Salud Carbajal (CA-24) and 18 other members of Congress in filing an amicus brief in California v. Wright, pending in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, in support of California’s challenge to the Trump Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA) to facilitate the restart of the Sable Offshore oil pipeline system along California’s Central Coast. U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) also led the filing.

The brief argues that the Administration has failed to identify a legitimate national defense need for Sable’s crude oil and that the DPA order does not satisfy the statutory requirements for invoking this extraordinary authority. Sable produces crude oil, not finished fuels used by the military, and the order does not establish a connection between Sable’s production and an unmet military fuel requirement.

“This Administration’s efforts to restart the Sable Offshore pipeline system in Santa Barbara could do damage to our environment and economy,” said Rep. Panetta. “That’s why I joined this amicus brief challenging its use of the Defense Production Act to force this pipeline system back into operation and open our waters back up to offshore oil production. The order fails to establish a legitimate national defense need or genuine emergency that would justify using this extraordinary authority on behalf of a single oil company. We must continue to support each other and stand together from the courtroom to the coastline to protect our environment and economy.”

“The Sable pipeline restart is a classic example of the Trump administration abusing power to benefit political allies at the expense of local communities,” said Rep. Carbajal. “As our brief outlines, there was no legitimate national security justification for invoking the Defense Production Act on behalf of Sable. This Administration is clearly fixated on boosting the fossil fuel industry, even when doing so risks putting our environment and public health in harm’s way. The people of Santa Barbara County and California have every right to be concerned about the pipeline restart given its role in the 2015 Refugio oil spill. I will keep fighting alongside my colleagues to hold the Administration accountable for this overreach and protect our communities’ right to a safe environment.”

“Californians have been clear: we don’t want oil infrastructure off our coast,” said Sen. Padilla. “The Trump Administration is using a bogus justification to open our waters to their Big Oil donors, jeopardizing our environment and our economy. It’s corrupt, it’s dangerous, and I’ll do everything in my power to stop it.”

“The idea that reopening a damaged pipeline on the Central Coast of California is somehow imperative to our national defense – when killing other renewable energy sources is just fine, when data centers are demanding new energy and we’re taking offline 90 to 95% of the new energy coming into the grid – tells you this has nothing to do with national security. It has nothing to do with your price at the pump. It only has to do with the president keeping a promise to the big oil companies, and we are all paying the price,” said Sen. Schiff.

Sable Offshore acquired the Santa Ynez Unit from ExxonMobil in 2024. The pipeline had been out of service since the 2015 Refugio oil spill. In March 2026, Energy Secretary Chris Wright invoked the DPA and ordered Sable to restore pipeline operations. The brief argues that the Administration used national defense as a pretext to advance domestic energy policy and benefit a specific company.

“This case is not about national defense. It is about a heavily leveraged, crude oil company asking the President to transform the Defense Production Act (DPA) from a statute designed to ‘assure the availability of domestic energy supplies for national defense needs,’ 50 U.S.C. § 4502(a)(5), into a corporate rescue operation for political allies; a rescue that advances the Administration’s political preference for fossil-fuel development at the expense of all other concerns,” wrote the lawmakers. “The Department of Energy’s (‘DOE’) March 13, 2026 order (the ‘Wright Order’) comes nowhere close to identifying a need for Sable crude oil or pipelines in the Order’s generalized invocation of California’s military presence and increased reliance on foreign crude. DOE never explains why those general circumstances create a national-defense need for Sable’s crude, much less how restarting its beleaguered pipelines would meet one.”

“Merely invoking ‘national defense’ or an ‘emergency’ does not insulate executive action from the statutory prerequisites that Congress imposed in the DPA on the exercise of delegated authority,” continued the lawmakers. “Enforcing these requirements, i.e., that the Secretary establish the statutory predicates for invoking the DPA, does not amount to second-guessing genuine executive judgments about national defense. Instead, enforcement honors the conditions precedent Congress imposed to prevent abuse of the DPA. DOE’s failure to satisfy these statutory prerequisites invalidates the Wright Order.”

In addition to Reps. Panetta and Carbajal and Sens. Padilla, Schiff, and Whitehouse, the amicus brief was filed by U.S. Representatives Jared Huffman (CA-02), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Laura Friedman (CA-30), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Mike Levin (CA-49), Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Doris Matsui (CA-07), Dave Min (CA-47), and Kevin Mullin (CA-15), as well as U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Tammy Duckworth (D-IL).

“Trump is turning the Defense Production Act into a blank check for Big Oil,” said Rep. Huffman. “Emergency national security powers exist to protect this country in a crisis. They were never meant to force open an oil pipeline that has sat idle for more than a decade after fouling our coast. This is a fossil fuel giveaway dressed up as national security, designed to enrich Trump and reward his political allies. But it’s our beaches, our coastal communities, and the businesses that depend on a clean, healthy ocean that will face the consequences if we let his sham continue. We have cleaned up this company’s mess once already. Californians have defended this coast for decades, and we are not backing down.”

“The Trump Administration’s abuse of the Defense Production Act to revive the Sable pipeline is an unlawful corporate giveaway masquerading as a national security measure,” said Speaker Emerita Pelosi. “California communities know the devastating consequences of offshore oil spills. Congress created the Defense Production Act to protect our national security—not to reward political allies, endanger our coastline and override vital environmental safeguards.”

“As Chair of the California Democratic Congressional Delegation, we have been united against this Administration’s illegal attempts to force fossil fuel projects at the expense of our state’s environment and public health,” said Rep. Lofgren. “Trump has always put oil company profits above Americans’ well-being, but invoking the Defense Production Act for this pipeline is ridiculous. Californians don’t want a repeat of the 2015 oil spill, and the Administration is overstepping its authority to put our environment and coastal economy at risk.”

In May 2026, Rep. Panetta joined his colleagues to request an investigation into Sable Offshore Corp.’s politicized efforts to restart oil drilling operations off the Santa Barbara coast and demanded answers about the company’s collaboration with the Trump Administration to invoke the Defense Production Act in relation to this project. Last year, members of the California congressional delegation demanded answers from the Trump Administration on its involvement in Sable Offshore Corporation’s attempts to restart offshore oil drilling using the same pipelines that caused the Refugio State Beach oil spill of 2015.

The full amicus brief is available here.

title: Pfluger, Houlahan Introduce the Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) introduced the bipartisan Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act alongside Congresswoman Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06) to keep dangerous actors from misusing DNA synthesis technology while keeping America at the forefront of biotechnology.

Gene synthesis has transformed medicine, agriculture, and manufacturing, helping scientists build lifesaving treatments and develop hardier crops. However, these same tools could be misused to create dangerous pathogens if left unchecked. Currently, screening of nucleic acid orders is voluntary, leaving a gap that bad actors could exploit, especially as new desktop machines make it easier to generate genetic material outside the traditional supply chain.

The Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act would close this dangerous gap by requiring companies that sell synthetic DNA, as well as the manufacturers of the machines that produce it, to know their customers and exactly what they're being asked to make.

"Biotechnology is one of America's greatest strategic advantages. Right now, there's a dangerous gap between how fast this technology is moving and the safeguards we have in place to keep it out of the wrong hands. The Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act closes this gap without slowing down the innovation saving lives while strengthening our economy," said Rep. August Pfluger (TX-11).

“Biotechnology is creating enormous opportunities to improve lives and transform our economy, but like all emerging technologies, the related security policies must keep pace,” said Rep. Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06). “The Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act is an important step toward ensuring that the federal government has the flexibility and agility to respond to new technologies and emerging threats as they evolve. As Co-Chair of the bipartisan BIOTech Caucus, I am committed to ensuring that we strengthen our biosecurity posture while preserving the responsible innovation that keeps America at the forefront of biotechnology.”

The legislation is a House companion to bipartisan legislation introduced by Senator Tom Cotton (AR-R) and Senator Amy Klobuchar (MN-D) and was developed in consultation with key industry stakeholders in the biotechnology and gene-synthesis sector.

title: CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CELEBRATES HOUSE PASSAGE OF LEGISLATION TO HONOR VIRGIN ISLANDS MUSIC LEGEND PETER G. THURLAND SR.
text:
For Immediate Release Contact: Tionee Scotland

September 14, 2026 202-808-6129

PRESS RELEASE

CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CELEBRATES HOUSE PASSAGE OF LEGISLATION TO HONOR VIRGIN ISLANDS MUSIC LEGEND PETER G. THURLAND SR.

Washington, D.C. — The U.S. House of Representatives today passed H.R. 8121, legislation introduced by Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett (D-VI) to designate the Christiansted Bandstand in Christiansted, St. Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands, as the “Peter G. Thurland, Sr., Bandstand.”

“I am pleased that the House has passed H.R. 8121 to designate the Christiansted Bandstand as the Peter G. Thurland, Sr., Bandstand,” said Congresswoman Plaskett. “The Christiansted Bandstand is one of the most significant cultural landmarks in the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Peter Thurland helped build it, served his country with distinction, and dedicated decades of his life to the cultural life of St. Croix. I thank Chairman Westerman (R-AK), Ranking Member Huffman (D-CA), and the Members and staff of the House Committee on Natural Resources for their expeditious consideration of this bill, and I thank my House colleagues on both sides of the aisle for their support.”

The Christiansted Bandstand has served for over a century as a gathering place for residents and visitors and as the center of St. Croix’s musical and civic life. Peter Gregory Thurland, Sr., was born on February 19, 1892, in Christiansted, St. Croix, and performed with the Christiansted Industrial Brass Band at the March 31, 1917, ceremony that marked the transfer of the Virgin Islands to the United States. He went on to enlist in the U.S. Navy, where he was instrumental in the physical construction and design of the Bandstand and performed there with the Christiansted Naval Band until his honorable discharge in 1921. In 1938, Mr. Thurland founded the St. Croix Community Band, leading free monthly concerts at the Bandstand for three decades and training generations of young musicians until 1968.

This legislation was first introduced by Congressman Ron de Lugo in the 103rd Congress. Congresswoman Plaskett is proud to carry it forward in the 119th Congress on behalf of the Thurland family, who have long advocated for this recognition. This bill now moves to the U.S. Senate for consideration, and if passed, it will proceed to the President's desk to be signed into law.

title: Congresswoman Pou Calls on United to Save Nonstop Newark→Lima Flights
text:
PATERSON, NJ – Congressmember Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09), the Vice Ranking Member of the House Subcommittee on Aviation, today called on United Airlines to reconsider its plan to eliminate a popular direct route between Newark Liberty International Airport and Lima, Peru, long relied on by New Jersey’s large Peruvian-American community.

“I write to express my concern about United Airlines’ recent decision to eliminate nonstop service between Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) and Jorge Chávez International Airport (LIM) in Lima, Peru. Ending this longstanding route would have a serious impact on New Jersey communities that rely on direct service to Peru, while potentially leaving travelers with fewer choices and higher costs,” Congresswoman Pou writes United CEO Scott Kirby.

United announced earlier this month that it will end nonstop service between Newark and Lima on March 27, 2027, ending a route that has operated since 1996, first under Continental Airlines and later United following its merger. United plans to double its Houston-Lima service to two daily flights when the Newark route ends.

“Given the impact this decision would have for New Jersey’s Peruvian community and for travelers across the Tristate area, I am asking United Airlines to pause its plan to eliminate the Newark–Lima route and consider alternatives that could preserve direct service, including operating the route on a reduced schedule,” Pou concludes in her call to United’s CEO.

According to Census data, New Jersey has roughly 95,000 people of Peruvian origin living in the state. New Jersey’s Ninth District is home to one of the largest Peruvian communities in the United States. At the heart of this community is Paterson’s “Little Lima,” which is full of Peruvian bakeries, salons, restaurants, and other small businesses.

Congresswoman Pou is the lead sponsor of the PERU Act (H.R. 5335) which seeks to strengthen ties between the U.S. and Peru by adding Peru to the list of countries eligible to obtain E1 and E2 visas, so long as the Peruvian government treats United States nationals similarly.

The text of Congresswoman Pou’s letter is below.

Dear Mr. Kirby:

I write to express my concern about United Airlines’ recent decision to eliminate nonstop service between Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) and Jorge Chávez International Airport (LIM) in Lima, Peru. Ending this longstanding route would have a serious impact on New Jersey communities that rely on direct service to Peru, while potentially leaving travelers with fewer choices and higher costs.

New Jersey has deep-rooted ties with Peru, with roughly 95,000 people of Peruvian origin living in the state, the third largest Peruvian population in the country. New Jersey’s Ninth Congressional District, and Paterson in particular, is home to one of the largest Peruvian communities in the United States. At the heart of this community is Paterson’s “Little Lima,” which is full of Peruvian bakeries, salons, restaurants, and other businesses. These ties led Paterson to establish “sister city” partnerships with Machu Picchu and the Municipality of Lurigancho-Chosica in 2024 and 2025, respectively. For decades, our local community members have also worked to strengthen ties between Peru and the United States and rallied to support Peru in times of crisis, including the devastating 2007 earthquake.

For over 30 years, United Airlines and its predecessor Continental Airlines have maintained direct service between Newark and Lima. This route is far more than a convenience. It connects New Jersey families with loved ones in Peru and supports business, tourism, and trade between our two countries. Eliminating it would force many travelers to take connecting flights or travel to other airports, adding time and expense to trips that are already prohibitively expensive.

I recognize that rising fuel prices have created new challenges for the airline industry this year. United Airlines must make business decisions that reflect fast-changing market conditions. However, United has also reported increased revenues and strong passenger demand while announcing plans to expand its network. Given the company’s strong business performance over the last two quarters, United Airlines should provide greater clarity about when a long-established route serving a major New Jersey community is being eliminated. This is particularly true given that United has told investors that it expects to recover 100% of higher fuel cost by the fourth quarter.

The decision to eliminate the non-stop Newark-Lima route comes as United Airlines is announcing new routes to destinations in Luxemburg, Slovenia, France, and elsewhere. This growth is exciting for travelers, but new service should not come at the expense of a route that has served New Jersey’s Peruvian community for decades, particularly when the Newark-Lima route has continued to see strong demand and frequently full flights. United Airlines should be able to expand its network without leaving behind communities that have relied on established routes for decades.

Given the impact this decision would have for New Jersey’s Peruvian community and for travelers across the Tristate area, I am asking United Airlines to pause its plan to eliminate the Newark–Lima route and consider alternatives that could preserve direct service, including operating the route on a reduced schedule.

I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and would welcome the opportunity to meet with you, along with representatives of our large Peruvian community, to discuss this decision and explore ways to preserve direct service between Newark and Lima. I hope we can work together toward a solution that keeps this important connection in place.

Sincerely,

###

Congresista Pou hace un llamado a United para mantener los vuelos entre Newark y Lima

La congresista hace un impulso para pausar la cancelación de una ruta con 30 años de servicio que atiende a la numerosa comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey

PATERSON, NJ – La congresista Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09), vicepresidenta de mayor rango de la Subcomisión de Aviación de la Cámara de Representantes, pidió hoy a United Airlines que reconsideren la decisión de eliminar la popular ruta directa entre el Aeropuerto de Newark y Lima, Perú, de la cual la numerosa comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey ha dependido durante décadas.

“Le escribo para expresar mi preocupación por la reciente decisión de United Airlines de eliminar el servicio sin escalas entre el Aeropuerto Internacional Newark Liberty (EWR) y el Aeropuerto Internacional Jorge Chávez (LIM) en Lima, Perú. El fin de esta histórica ruta tendría un grave impacto en las comunidades de Nueva Jersey que dependen del servicio directo a Perú, y podría dejar a los viajeros con menos opciones y costos más altos”, escribió la congresista Pou al director ejecutivo de United, Scott Kirby.

United anunció a principios de este mes que pondrá fin al servicio sin escalas entre Newark y Lima el 27 de marzo de 2027, terminando así una ruta que ha operado desde 1996, primero a través de Continental Airlines y posteriormente de United. United planea duplicar su servicio entre Houston y Lima a dos vuelos diarios cuando finalice la ruta desde Newark.

“Dado el impacto que esta decisión tendría en la comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey y en los viajeros de toda el área triestatal, estoy pidiendo a United Airlines que suspenda su plan de eliminar la ruta Newark-Lima y considere alternativas que permitan preservar el servicio directo, incluida la posibilidad de operar la ruta con una frecuencia reducida”, concluyó Pou en su llamado al director ejecutivo de United.

De acuerdo con el Censo, Nueva Jersey cuenta con aproximadamente 95,000 residentes de origen peruano. El Noveno Distrito Congresional de Nueva Jersey alberga una de las comunidades peruanas más grandes de Estados Unidos. En el corazón de esta comunidad se encuentra Little Lima en Paterson, donde abundan panaderías, salones de belleza, restaurantes y otros pequeños negocios peruanos.

La congresista Pou es la principal patrocinadora de la Ley PERU (H.R. 5335), que busca fortalecer los lazos entre Estados Unidos y Perú al agregar a Perú a la lista de países cuyos ciudadanos pueden solicitar visas E-1 y E-2, siempre que el gobierno peruano otorgue un trato similar a los ciudadanos estadounidenses.

El texto de la carta de la congresista Pou se encuentra a continuación.

Estimado Sr. Kirby:

Le escribo para expresar mi preocupación por la reciente decisión de United Airlines de eliminar el servicio sin escalas entre el Aeropuerto Internacional Newark Liberty (EWR) y el Aeropuerto Internacional Jorge Chávez (LIM) en Lima, Perú. El fin de esta histórica ruta tendría un grave impacto en las comunidades de Nueva Jersey que dependen del servicio directo a Perú, y podría dejar a los viajeros con menos opciones y costos más altos.

Nueva Jersey tiene profundos lazos con Perú, con aproximadamente 95,000 residentes de origen peruano, la tercera población peruana más grande del país. El Noveno Distrito Congresional de Nueva Jersey, y Paterson en particular, alberga una de las comunidades peruanas más grandes de Estados Unidos. En el corazón de esta comunidad se encuentra Little Lima en Paterson, donde abundan panaderías, salones de belleza, restaurantes y otros negocios peruanos. Estos vínculos llevaron a Paterson a establecer relaciones de “ciudades hermanas” con Machu Picchu y la Municipalidad de Lurigancho-Chosica en 2024 y 2025, respectivamente. Durante décadas, miembros de nuestra comunidad local también han trabajado para fortalecer los lazos entre Perú y Estados Unidos y se han movilizado para apoyar a Perú en momentos de crisis, incluido el devastador terremoto de 2007.

Durante más de 30 años, United Airlines y su predecesora, Continental Airlines, han mantenido un servicio directo entre Newark y Lima. Esta ruta es mucho más que una comodidad. Conecta a familias de Nueva Jersey con sus seres queridos en Perú y apoya los negocios, el turismo y el comercio entre nuestros dos países. Eliminarla obligaría a muchos viajeros a tomar vuelos con conexiones o trasladarse a otros aeropuertos, agregando tiempo y gastos a viajes que ya tienen costos prohibitivos.

Reconozco que el aumento de los precios del combustible ha creado nuevos desafíos para la industria aérea este año. United Airlines debe tomar decisiones comerciales que reflejen las condiciones rápidamente cambiantes del mercado. Sin embargo, United también ha reportado un aumento en sus ingresos y una fuerte demanda de pasajeros mientras anuncia planes para ampliar su red. Dado el sólido desempeño comercial de la compañía durante los últimos dos trimestres, United Airlines debería ofrecer mayor claridad cuando decide eliminar una ruta de larga trayectoria que presta servicio a una importante comunidad de Nueva Jersey. Esto es particularmente cierto dado que United ha dicho a sus inversionistas que espera recuperar el 100 por ciento del aumento en los costos del combustible para el cuarto trimestre.

La decisión de eliminar la ruta sin escalas Newark-Lima se produce mientras United Airlines anuncia nuevas rutas a destinos en Luxemburgo, Eslovenia, Francia y otros lugares. Este crecimiento es una buena noticia para los viajeros, pero los nuevos servicios no deberían implementarse a costa de una ruta que ha servido durante décadas a la comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey, especialmente cuando la ruta Newark-Lima continúa registrando una fuerte demanda y vuelos que con frecuencia están llenos. United Airlines debería poder ampliar su red sin dejar atrás a comunidades que han dependido de rutas establecidas durante décadas.

Dado el impacto que esta decisión tendría en la comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey y en los viajeros de toda el área triestatal, estoy pidiendo a United Airlines que suspenda su plan de eliminar la ruta Newark-Lima y considere alternativas que permitan preservar el servicio directo, incluida la posibilidad de operar la ruta con una frecuencia reducida.

Agradezco su pronta atención a este asunto y agradecería la oportunidad de reunirme con usted, junto con representantes de nuestra numerosa comunidad peruana, para hablar sobre esta decisión y explorar maneras de preservar el servicio directo entre Newark y Lima. Espero que podamos trabajar juntos para encontrar una solución que mantenga esta importante conexión.

Atentamente,

Nellie Pou

Miembro del Congreso

title: Amata Attends Defense MIA Briefing to Honor Veterans and Military Families
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata attended a special meeting Saturday for the families of U.S. personnel missing from the Vietnam War, Cold War, Korean War, and World War II. The Family Member Update, held in Dover, Delaware, by the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA), included over 400 Gold Star family members.

Vice Chairman Amata attended the DPAA Family Member Update to honor Veterans

Amata, who is Vice Chairman of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee, traveled from DC to be there in honor of these patriotic families and all U.S. Veterans. Amata and Fred Radewagen have a personal connection to the effort, as a cousin’s family is among these U.S. military families seeking long-awaited closure regarding missing loved ones. Additionally, this agency has twice in recent years brought important closure to families in American Samoa who sought information about a Service Member from past wars.

Amata attended DPAA briefing

“It is moving to see a large room full of families that sacrificed a loved one for our country and the cause of freedom,” said HVAC Vice Chairman Amata. “The DPAA is doing an important service to those who served, and it’s a special mission that is deserving of support. One case at a time, they bring a sense of closure to a family, often providing the ability to visit a loved one’s gravesite. I admire the resolve of these dear families, and our earnest prayer is that they will be blessed with clear results to put their questions and uncertainty to rest. To the U.S. personnel engaged in this research, I just want to say from the bottom of my heart thank you for your dedication.”

The full day’s agenda in Dover included a briefing on the U.S. global efforts to account for Americans missing from past conflicts, where they also made research experts available to meet with families, and offered families tours of the Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory in Delaware for insight into this effort.

Amata has previously visited the Agency’s main Pacific office in Honolulu with the world’s largest forensic anthropology laboratory for an informational tour and briefing. In multiple locations, the agency continuously studies archives and records, and sends expert teams worldwide to recover remains. The DPAA is led by Director Kelly McKeague, a retired Major General from the U.S. Air Force.
