title: ICYMI: In Letter to SEC and CFTC, Fetterman Urges Private Credit Market Transparency
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) penned a July letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) urging them to begin enforcing an existing rule requiring greater disclosures in private credit markets.

“The private credit industry is far too opaque to regulators and the rest of the financial system. Because these firms have never been through a downturn at their current size, markets do not know how to properly value private credit loans and assets in a crisis. As with all financial crises, the panic of not knowing where the floor is makes it far worse. It is important that regulators have the knowledge and the tools to prevent crises before they happen, but that is not possible if they do not know enough about the market,” wrote Senator Fetterman.

Big banks, insurance companies, and pension funds are all exposed to private credit — a market of unregulated lending to struggling companies — which is showing signs of much higher risk than investors anticipated. Form PF is a disclosure form that unregulated entities like private credit funds must submit to the SEC and CFTC. The agencies’ proposed updates to Form PF would greatly improve their understanding of the risks in private credit, but have yet to start enforcing them.

“The updates to Form PF, as originally proposed, would ensure regulators and investors better understand the leverage, interconnectedness, loan quality, and liquidity of this market. It is concerning, therefore, that your agencies have chosen to delay the enforcement of these requirements three times since taking office,” continued the senator. “Now is not the time for regulators to be in the dark.”

Read the full text of the letter below and here.

–

Dear Chairman Atkins and Chairman Selig:

I write to urge you to begin enforcing compliance with the updates to Form PF as initially proposed. It is critically important that regulators have a better understanding of the risks in private markets, in order to protect investors and prevent disruptions to the broader financial system.

I am deeply concerned about the mounting risks in private credit markets. Now $3 trillion in size, the private credit industry is making increasingly bad loans to subprime companies. The failures of First Brands and Tricolor, increasing reliance on payments-in-kind among borrowers, and concerns around AI disruption to the software industry all demonstrate poor underwriting over the past several years. In reaction, investors have been rushing to get their money out of these souring investments, but have often been trapped.

Even more concerning is the exposure America’s traditional financial system has to this market. The big banks have lent almost $300 billion to the private credit industry, much of which lacks covenants that protect the banks in times of crisis. Moreover, the insurance industry is not only exposed to $1 trillion in risk but also is among the largest purchasers of the low-tranche collateralized loan obligations (CLOs) that would get wiped out in a downturn.

The private credit industry is far too opaque to regulators and the rest of the financial system. Because these firms have never been through a downturn at their current size, markets do not know how to properly value private credit loans and assets in a crisis. As with all financial crises, the panic of not knowing where the floor is makes it far worse. It is important that regulators have the knowledge and the tools to prevent crises before they happen, but that is not possible if they do not know enough about the market.

The updates to Form PF, as originally proposed, would ensure regulators and investors better understand the leverage, interconnectedness, loan quality, and liquidity of this market. It is concerning, therefore, that your agencies have chosen to delay the enforcement of these requirements three times since taking office. Your recent April 24th announcement seeking comments on an extreme watering down of the changes is even more concerning. Beyond these updates, it is critical that you better enforce annual reporting requirements and punish market actors who fail to follow their obligations.

I urge you to move forward with robust, detailed transparency through Form PF by October 1st. Now is not the time for regulators to be in the dark.

Sincerely,

title: Gallego, Kelly, Stanton, Ansari, Announce $2 Million Federal Investment to Advance Water Reuse Technology for Semiconductor Manufacturing at ASU
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) along with Representatives Greg Stanton (AZ-04) and Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) announced $2,062,000 in federal funding for Arizona State University to develop, test, and demonstrate innovative water reuse technologies designed for semiconductor manufacturing. The award, made through the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), was secured as congressionally directed spending championed by the Arizona delegation.

The project will test emerging water treatment technologies and validate them at ASU’s Macro Technology Works (MTW) facility in Tempe, generating the real-world performance data industry needs to adopt water-saving solutions at scale. The work aims to help fabs improve conservation while strengthening the reliability of domestic semiconductor production.

“Making Arizona’s semiconductor manufacturing industry even more water efficient will allow us to continue to create good-paying jobs and protect our state’s water supply,” said Senator Gallego. “Thanks to this project, Arizona will continue to lead the nation in community-beneficial innovation.”

“Arizona is a national leader in chip manufacturing, and we know how to manage water responsibly,” said Senator Kelly. “This investment builds on that leadership by developing water reuse technology, creating good-paying jobs, strengthening American manufacturing, and protecting our water supply. It’s a win for Arizona.”

“Arizona is proving that you can lead the nation in semiconductor manufacturing and be a responsible steward of every drop of water,” said Rep. Stanton. “This investment puts ASU’s researchers to work on exactly the right challenge: making sure the industry driving our economic future can grow without straining the water resources our communities depend on. That’s how we keep chip production strong and sustainable right here in Arizona.”

“In Arizona, water is our most precious and sacred resource. As our state continues to lead the nation in innovation and build the economy of the future through advanced semiconductor manufacturing, we must ensure that growth is sustainable,” said Rep. Ansari. “The federal dollars my colleagues and I secured will help do exactly that and ASU is a critical partner in driving the research, innovation, and commercialization needed to reduce water use and strengthen our resilience. Our future depends on it.”

“ASU looks forward to putting this federal investment to work advancing technologies that can help semiconductor manufacturers use water more efficiently and strengthen the resilience of chip production in Arizona,” said Arizona State University President Michael Crow. “Arizona’s water security and the nation’s focus on semiconductor manufacturing capacity depends on the leadership of policymakers and we appreciate the support from Senators Kelly and Gallego and Representatives Stanton and Ansari in recognizing the importance of this work. By developing and testing promising water reuse technologies in a semiconductor manufacturing environment, ASU can help advance these solutions for commercial use.”

The project will advance promising technologies from early-stage research toward commercial readiness through two phases: developing and integrating emerging treatment technologies into a mobile, pilot-scale demonstration testbed, and validating them in manufacturing-representative conditions at the MTW facility. Quarterly stakeholder reviews will guide which technologies advance to pilot-scale demonstration, where researchers will quantify water savings, cost reductions, and operational benefits.

By bridging the gap between fundamental research and commercial deployment, the project is expected to benefit semiconductor fabs seeking to reduce water use and improve resilience, while generating new intellectual property that can be licensed to start ups and established water-technology firms.

title: WATCH: Gallego Calls for Immediate Congressional Oversight and Regulation on AI
text:
‘This is more akin to Dr. Frankenstein telling us the monster is loose. Help me stop the monster.’

WASHINGTON – In response to former Anthropic researcher quitting his role and warning of an industrywide rush to build AI systems that can improve themselves and, in turn, destroy humanity, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) has spoken out on the need for immediate congressional oversight.

WATCH: State of the Union with Jake Tapper

On the imminent danger of artificial intelligence: “This is not previous tech. Previous tech could not make a decision to kill us. When we turned on the internet it did not have autonomy. When we created the nuclear weapon, the nuclear weapon did not have the decision-making power to drop a nuclear weapon. AI has the capability and will have the capability to make decisions like that. This is more akin to Dr. Frankenstein telling us the monster is loose. Help me stop the monster.”

On the need of his proposed bipartisan Senate Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence: “Speaker Johnson is not meeting the moment. Trump’s not meeting the moment. The Senate and Congress are not meeting the moment. We need to get together as fast as possible with the smartest people, with the skeptics, with the people that want to regulate, the people that want to actually deal with this, people that are going to figure out how to actually have the perfect balance. We can’t just use this idea that if we do this, we’re somehow going to lose to China because AI does not care once it becomes fully dangerous whether we are Chinese or American. That’s the danger of this. Everyone’s thinking about this in a way that is based on old tech and not what’s going towards the future. This is why we need to get the people in the room.

“The way we are going about this is that we are hoping that some committee in the House or the Senate is just going to come together with some staffers and put together the framework that’s going to go into place maybe three years from now. We don’t have that time. Dr. Frankenstein is telling us the monster has escaped. Help us stop this.”

title: What They Are Saying: Senator Gallego Unveils his Plan to Strengthen America’s Education System
text:
WASHINGTON – Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) released his new plan to reform and strengthen America’s public education system. The four-pillar plan, “Class in Session: A Plan to Fix America’s Public Education System,” provides a pathway to bolster public education for every American student — especially those in rural, tribal, and high-poverty communities who often face barriers that extend beyond the classroom.

Read the full plan HERE.

If Democrats take control of one or both chambers of Congress in November, U.S. Sen. Ruben Gallego wants to be ready.

title: Amid New York Fashion Week, Gillibrand, Nadler Reintroduce FABRIC Act To Bring Accountability And Transparency To The Fashion Industry
text:
Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Congressman Jerry Nadler (D-NY-12) announced the reintroduction of their Fashioning Accountability and Building Real Institutional Change (FABRIC) Act. In New York State, there are approximately 130,000 people employed by the fashion industry, including thousands working in apparel manufacturing. Garment workers are a cornerstone of the American economy, and for far too long, they have faced unsafe working conditions, wage theft, and piecework pay, which often prioritizes fast fashion over the safety of workers. Gillibrand and Nadler’s FABRIC Act would protect over 75,000 American garment workers and help revitalize the garment manufacturing industry in the United States by improving working conditions and reforming the piece-rate pay scale.

“Garment workers are the backbone of a multibillion-dollar industry, yet for far too long, their labor has been undervalued and exploited,” said Senator Gillibrand. “We cannot champion American innovation while turning a blind eye to abusive labor practices in our own backyard. It’s time to take bold action at the federal level to change the fabric of the American garment industry. The United States was once home to a booming apparel manufacturing industry, and it’s time to reexamine how this industry has evolved over the past 50 years and change how we treat our workers. With the FABRIC Act, we can curb wage theft, protect our workers, and revitalize domestic manufacturing so that ‘Made in America’ also means ethically made.”

“America’s garment workers have been undervalued and subjected to unfair labor practices for far too long, due to weak regulations across the fashion industry and the rise of fast fashion. With more than 100,000 New Yorkers contributing their labor to a billion-dollar garment industry, it is time to protect these workers and others across our nation and make historic investments in domestic manufacturing by passing the FABRIC Act,” said Congressman Jerrold Nadler. “I’m proud to work with Senator Gillibrand to protect workers’ rights, bring jobs back from overseas, and revitalize the American fashion industry.”

The FABRIC Act proposes to address these issues by:

Restructuring pay rates for garment workers and providing minimum wage as a floor with productivity incentives on top.

Establishing new liability measures that compel major retailers to become allies in combating workplace violations.

Introducing recordkeeping and transparency measures, including requiring garment manufacturers and contractors operating in the U.S. to register with the Department of Labor.

Incentivizing reshoring by creating a domestic garment manufacturing grant program aimed at revitalizing the industry.

In addition to Gillibrand and Nadler, the bill is cosponsored by Senators Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), as well as Reps. Deborah Ross (D-NC), Don Beyer (D-VA), Maxwell Frost (D-FL), Robert Garcia (D-CA), Dan Goldman (D-NY), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), and Rashida Tlaib (D-MI). The bill is also endorsed by AFL-CIO, UNITE HERE, Workers United, and RWDSU.

The full text of the FABRIC Act can be found here.

title: In Rochester: Gillibrand Raises Alarm On Trump Administration Slashing Federal Funding For SNAP And Threatening New Yorkers’ Benefits
text:
New York State Will Be Responsible for Estimated $168 Million More Annually as SNAP Cost Responsibilities Shift to State and Local Governments

Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand held a press conference calling out the change in Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill” that will imminently shift billions of dollars in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) cost responsibilities from the federal government onto state and local governments, resulting in major financial burdens on New York State. This comes as President Trump’s reckless war in Iran and chaotic tariffs have raised grocery prices for New York families and made it increasingly difficult to put food on the table.

“President Trump has consistently threatened and cut the essential services that serve as the backbone of our nation,” said Senator Gillibrand. “At a time when people can barely afford a cart of groceries or a tank of gas, this president is making states and localities bear excruciating cost burdens for SNAP programming while he is funding tax cuts for the richest people in the country and pouring billions into a war overseas.”

“No one should confuse the federal shift in SNAP funding with a reduction in our local commitment to people who rely on SNAP. Monroe County will continue to ensure eligible residents receive their benefits,” said Monroe County Executive Adam Bello. “However, every dollar we have to spend covering what used to be a federal responsibility is a dollar we have less available for other critical services and investments here at home. Thank you to Senator Gillibrand for hearing our voice and advocating for local county taxpayers.”

“At 1199SEIU, our fight is about more than contracts and wages. It is about dignity, fairness, and ensuring that every person has the opportunity to live a healthy and secure life. When children go hungry, seniors struggle to afford food, and working families are pushed deeper into poverty, we have a responsibility to speak out and demand change,” said Tracey Harrison, 1199SEIU Vice President for the Rochester and Corning Area. “That is why we will continue to stand together and advocate for policies that strengthen families and communities, not just the wealthiest among us. Restore the SNAP benefits now!

The change, which is slated to take effect on October 1 and is part of a broader slate of harmful cuts to the SNAP program, will reduce the federal share of SNAP administrative expenses from 50% to 25%, with states and localities now responsible for covering 75% costs. Counties in New York State are expected to be on the hook for $168 million annually as a result, with Monroe County being responsible for an additional $3 million to keep SNAP-supported programs running. Nearly 100,000 people in Monroe County rely on SNAP to feed their families each month. Without this additional federal support, counties may be forced to raise local taxes or slow down the review of SNAP applications.

Senator Gillibrand has led the fight against hunger in New York and across the nation. Through legislative efforts like the Closing the Meal Gap Act and the Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act, she has consistently worked to expand SNAP benefit amounts, remove administrative red tape, and protect low-income families from electronic benefit theft. Her commitment to expanding and protecting SNAP benefits has helped ensure that federal nutrition programs remain a strong and accessible lifeline for millions of Americans.

title: In Schenectady, Gillibrand Rails Against Closure of Veterans Affairs Community Based Outpatient Clinic
text:
1,500 Capital Region Veterans’ Care Disrupted

Despite Repeated Requests for Answers, the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Has Provided Little Transparency and Communication on the Future of Capital Region Veterans’ Services

Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, held a press conference addressing the recent closure of the Schenectady Veterans Affairs (VA) Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC). This is the region’s second CBOC closure in five years, following the shutdown of the Troy CBOC in July 2021, forcing veterans to seek alternative healthcare in places that may be far from their homes.

“The Schenectady VA provided access to care for more than 1,500 veterans in the Capital Region who put their lives on the line to protect our nation,” said Senator Gillibrand. “The decision to close this facility with little communication on alternative care could have devastating consequences. Veterans served our country, and we have a duty and responsibility to ensure their care. I have repeatedly demanded answers from VA Secretary Doug Collins, and I want to reiterate that any plans going forward must include the veterans who have relied on the care of the Schenectady VA.”

“The federal VA closed our Schenectady Clinic despite months of warnings from veterans and repeated calls to stop this decision,” said Assemblyman Angelo Santabarbara. “The VA’s own records show that cost and projected savings were part of the plan. The bottom line is our veterans should never be asked to pay the price for federal cost-cutting. The lack of answers and communication throughout this process was unacceptable. Veterans deserved answers, not excuses, and access to care, not another barrier standing in their way. At the very least, the VA should have paused the closure, met with us and listened to the veterans who depended on this clinic. The doors may be closed, but the fight is not over. I will continue standing with our veterans and fighting to restore the local access to health care that this closure stripped away.”

“As Rotterdam Town Supervisor, I stand firmly against the closing of the Schenectady VA Clinic,” said Rotterdam Town Supervisor John Polimeni. “This decision, overseen by VA Secretary Doug Collins, abandons the men and women who wore our nation’s uniform and now face greater barriers to the care they were promised. I have repeatedly requested meetings with VA staff and have offered practical solutions to keep services accessible locally, yet those concerns have gone unanswered. Our veterans deserve better than to be pushed farther from care and treated as a budget line instead of as heroes who have earned our unwavering support.”

The closure of the Schenectady VA Clinic is a slap in the face to those who sacrifice everything for this country and runs contradictory to our shared commitment to caring for all of our veterans when they return home,” said State Senator Patricia Fahy. “Schenectady County veterans should not have to travel further or pay more to access the basic services afforded to them after their service is complete. Our community has not been and will not be silent while this federal administration rips away healthcare from veterans at a time when access to quality, affordable healthcare is dwindling. Our message is clear: reverse this decision and continue your commitment to serving our Schenectady County veterans and meet them where they are in our community.”

“The closure of the Schenectady VA clinic is a serious concern for Veterans across the Capital Region who relied on that facility for their care,” said Albany County Executive Daniel P. McCoy. “Our Veterans should not face additional barriers or uncertainty when it comes to accessing the health care they earned through their service. I share Senator Gillibrand’s concerns and believe the VA must provide clear answers and a plan that ensures continuity of care for every Veteran affected by this closure.”

“The VA clinic in Rotterdam provided care to more than 1,500 veterans. Now, those veterans are dealing with the impact of its closure, including challenges finding transportation to get to another clinic and uncertainty about who will provide their care going forward,” said Schenectady County Legislature Chairman Gary Hughes. “Our veterans served and sacrificed for our country. They earned these benefits, and we have a responsibility to make sure they can access the care they need. We thank Senator Gillibrand for standing up for our veterans and bringing us together to make sure their voices are heard.”

When the closure was announced in March 2026, Gillibrand immediately called on the Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins to halt the closure and provide immediate answers to ensure that healthcare would not be disrupted for the over 1,500 Capital Region veterans who relied on this clinic. Now, six months following the original letter, and after a subsequent follow-up letter in August, few questions have been answered, even as the VA has closed the clinic.

title: During National Truck Driver Appreciation Week, Grassley Celebrates Efforts to Deliver Safer Roads for Families and Industry
text:
WASHINGTON – Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) is welcoming improvements to roadway safety amid National Truck Driver Appreciation Week (September 13-19).

In a response to a Grassley oversight letter, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) touted their recent actions to prevent drivers from violating Department of Transportation (DOT) and FMCSA regulations. Additionally, the Trump administration recently announced a historic crackdown on fraud in the trucking industry, including stronger enforcement of English language proficiency requirements. The announcement comes after Grassley and other elected officials pressed for action.

“Truck drivers put in the miles to keep our economy moving and bring Iowa’s world-class goods to market. I appreciate the Trump administration taking this issue seriously and responding to my oversight letters. By cracking down on fraudsters trying to game the system, this administration is standing with our truckers and working to keep America’s roads safe,” Grassley said.

“The state of Iowa is proud to support the truck drivers and motor carriers who build our economy,” said Scott Marler, Director of the Iowa Department of Transportation. “Our commercial driver licensing programs, truck parking facilities, and highway improvements provide an environment where truckers can deliver for Iowans and across the nation.”

Helping drivers get safely back on the road:

In April, Grassley pressed FMCSA regarding allegations that a network of scammers was abusing the Return-to-Duty (RTD) program to circumvent FMCSA’s legally mandated recovery process and to fraudulently collect fees from truck drivers.

In its response to Grassley, FMCSA reported its recent actions to protect the integrity of the RTD program and hold fraudsters accountable for violating DOT and FMCSA regulations. This includes new identity verification requirements and plans to discontinue the self-certification process later this year.

Curbing CDL fraud:

Grassley and others pressed the Trump administration to prevent illegal immigrants and fraudsters from obtaining commercial driver's licenses (CDLs) and ensure CDL holders meet English language proficiency requirements. Numerous news reports have shown dangerous illegal immigrant drivers causing serious accidents that leave Americans severely injured or killed.

In August, DOT Secretary Sean Duffy and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin joined other federal partners to announce a historic interagency effort to crack down on fraud in the trucking industry. The coalition is launching a nationwide audit of CDL testing and is removing over 110 CDL schools associated with thousands of drivers who failed English proficiency tests.

Combating organized retail crime:

Grassley and Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) are leading the Combating Organized Retail Crime Act to crack down on cargo theft and intricate retail theft schemes. Their bipartisan legislation strengthens the federal response to organized retail crime and establishes new tools to recover stolen goods and illicit proceeds. It’s estimated that approximately $35 billion is lost to cargo theft each year.

title: Hagerty, TN Delegation Urge Swift Approval of Major Disaster Declaration Requests After Severe Weather Impacts West Tennessee
text:
WASHINGTON—On Friday, United States Senator Bill Hagerty (R-TN) joined the Tennessee delegation in sending a letter to President Donald Trump urging his swift approval of Governor Bill Lee’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration following severe storms that affected areas of West Tennessee.

Co-signers of the letter include Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-TN), along with Representatives Diana Harshbarger (R-TN-01), Tim Burchett (R-TN-02), Chuck Fleischmann (R-TN-03), Scott DesJarlais (R-TN-04), Matt Van Epps (R-TN-07), David Kustoff (R-TN-08), and Steve Cohen (D-TN-09).

A copy of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Mr. President:

We write to urge swift approval of Governor Bill Lee’s request for a major disaster declaration pursuant to the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act due to severe weather occurring on August 22, 2026.

On August 22, a severe thunderstorm moved through the Mid-South and into West Tennessee, producing widespread damaging straight-line winds. Severe weather, including prolific straight-line winds and hail, caused significant damage to the power grid, particularly in Shelby County. The National Weather Service reported that more than 130,000 customers were without power, in addition to extensive tree damage, downed power lines, and road closures. Peak wind speeds were estimated between 60 and 80 miles per hour, with the storm lasting approximately 45 minutes in Shelby County and 90 minutes across the entire affected area. Ongoing extreme heat following the storm also posed serious risks to vulnerable residents, including seniors, young children, people with disabilities, low-income households, and those without access to cooling.

To respond to this disaster, Governor Lee is specifically requesting a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance and Public Assistance for Shelby County and Hazard Mitigation statewide. The State is also requesting direct Federal assistance for debris management support, including technical monitoring and mentoring to affected areas. On behalf of the State of Tennessee, we urge you to approve this request as soon as possible.

Our offices can provide you with any additional information you need.

Sincerely,

title: Senator Hassan Raises Alarm Bells Over ICE’s Neglect of Counter-Fentanyl Responsibilities
Hickenlooper, Bennet, Colleagues Challenge Trump Efforts to Restrict Mail-In Voting
text:
261 current and former lawmakers joined together to file amicus brief in SCOTUS Mail-In Voting Case

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper, Michael Bennet, the entire Senate Democratic Caucus, and members of the U.S. House of Representatives filed an amicus brief challenging the legality of President Trump’s executive order and U.S. Postal Service (USPS) rule that imposes unconstitutional, unworkable restrictions on mail-in voting, including requiring states to provide a “citizenship verification list” and attempting to give USPS control over who can vote by mail.

“Mail-in voting is safe, secure, and makes our elections more accessible,” said Hickenlooper. “The Trump administration continues throwing everything at the wall to restrict the fundamental right of every American to choose their leaders. It’s an unconstitutional, authoritarian attack that we won’t let them get away with.”

“Since the beginning of his administration, President Trump and Congressional Republicans have done everything they can to make our voting system less safe and secure,” said Bennet. “The Supreme Court must stand firm against this latest unconstitutional attempt to supersede the authority of states and Congress when it comes to our elections, all in an effort to make it harder for Coloradans to cast a vote by mail.”

Colorado’s vote-by-mail system produced a turnout rate of 73.4% in the 2024 general election, nearly 10% higher than the national average. Of these voters, 92.2% chose to return a mail ballot. In Colorado, 90% of Colorado Republicans voted by mail during the 2024 Presidential election and 98% of Colorado Republicans voted by mail in 2025.

Nearly one-third of Americans have voted by mail in recent elections — a voting practice Trump himself used as recently as August 2026, when he voted in Florida’s Republican primary.

In the court filing, the group argued that Trump’s Executive Order and USPS’s final rule violate the separation of powers and steal congressional authorities outlined in Article I of the U.S. Constitution, which gives the States and Congress exclusive authority over administering elections.

“As current and former legislators, amici took an oath to uphold and defend the Constitution of the United States — including its guarantee of the separation of powers,” wrote the lawmakers. “The Constitution does not contemplate the Executive Branch acting unilaterally to assert power over federal elections. Yet that is what the Order and Final Rule do.”

The lawmakers concluded by asserting States’ power to administer elections and Congress’s power to make or alter rules regulating elections, which the Supreme Court itself has described as an “override” authority. Trump’s illegal attack on this authority is an attempt to disenfranchise people who depend on mail-in ballots to vote.

“The integrity of our constitutional system depends on each branch keeping to its assigned role,” concluded the lawmakers. “The Framers set up a two-part system that gave the States default authority to regulate federal elections subject to Congress’s authority to override the States. The Framers did not provide the President with any authority to interfere in that system, nor has Congress subsequently imbued the President or the Executive Branch with any such authority by statute.”

U.S. Representative Joe Neguse led the effort in the U.S. House of Representatives.

Hickenlooper and Bennet previously demanded that the USPS abandon the rule and have been staunch opposition to the Trump administration’s efforts to restrict voting rights. Both senators also introduced the Mail and Absentee Voter Protection Act to nullify Trump’s executive order.

As governor, Hickenlooper helped create the gold standard mail-in voting system alongside Republican county clerks.Under Hickenlooper’s leadership, Colorado became the first in the nation to conduct a bipartisan statewide audit after every election. Results from the audit over the last six years show Colorado vote-counting systems were more than 99.99% accurate.

Hickenlooper has consistently fought efforts by MAGA and Trump to restrict voting, including the SAVE Act, which he took to the senate floor to oppose. He also cosponsors several pieces of voting rights legislation, including the For the People Act, the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, and the Freedom to Vote Act.

The full amicus brief is available HERE.

title: Hoeven Makes Case With Senators Cruz, Cantwell For the Protect College Sports Act
text:
WASHINGTON – Senator John Hoeven (R-N.D.) today made the case for the Protect College Sports Act (PCSA), bipartisan legislation to improve fairness and stability in college athletics. Hoeven outlined the importance of the legislation at a press conference led by Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), with college sports leaders and athletes from across the country, including former North Dakota State University (NDSU) head football coach Craig Bohl and Adam Dugger, a current NDSU track and field athlete. Hoeven, a cosponsor of the legislation, is working with his colleagues to bring the bill up for a vote by the full Senate as soon as this week.

The PCSA seeks to address issues created by the patchwork of state laws and court cases regulating college athletics, including a settlement reached in 2025 under House v. NCAA that allows schools to pay student athletes directly. This settlement has put schools with fewer financial resources at a competitive disadvantage and encourages gaming of the transfer portal. It also pressures schools to channel more funding into football and basketball, reducing resources available for students who participate in other sports programs. Accordingly, the legislation would:

Better protect and benefit student athletes by:

Preventing deceptive practices by agents or schools.

Protecting students’ Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) rights.

Ensuring pro athletes can’t compete in college sports.

Helping preserve support for women’s and Olympic sports.

Level the playing field in college sports across all schools. The bill:

Limits what schools can pay athletes.

Prevents player- or coach-poaching.

Curbs excessive transfers.

Stops Super League consolidation.

Secure access for local broadcasters to ensure a free option for fans to watch games.

“With the college football season underway, the problems facing student athletic programs are in clear focus. Across the country, small athletic programs are disappearing, student athletes are left vulnerable to exploitative contracts and college rosters are being hollowed out by a system that awards excessive transfers. That’s why we’re working to advance the Protect College Sports Act, which will establish a common-sense, bipartisan framework to protect competition, restore fairness and bring much-needed stability to college athletic programs,” said Hoeven. “It’s great to have Coach Bohl and NDSU track and field student athlete Adam Dugger here in Washington to help make the case for this legislation. We’re going to keep moving this bill forward, with the goal of securing a vote by the full Senate as soon as this week.”

The PCSA was introduced by Cruz and Cantwell, who serve as the Senate Commerce Committee Chairman and Ranking Member, respectively. Additional bill details include:

Improve Fairness for Student Athletes

Protect NIL rights by ensuring students can enter into NIL agreements and retain agents without losing scholarships or institutional support.

Stop fraudulent agents and deceptive contracts by establishing a registry of certified agents and allowing sanctions against agents that exploit student athletes.

Create uniform, enforceable eligibility rules for college athletes, including:

Setting a cap of 5 years of playing time starting from the time of enrollment or the academic year following a student’s 19th birthday, whichever comes first.

Loss of eligibility for participation in professional sports and poor academic performance, among other issues.

Create new funding incentives and revenue streams to preserve support for women’s and Olympic sports.

Require Division I schools to cover out-of-pocket medical costs for sports-related injuries and require all athletic programs to follow health and safety standards.

Restore Fair Competition for Schools

Limit compensation for student athletes and create enforceable standards on recruitment, tampering and NIL disclosures.

Prevent player- and coach-poaching by:

Allowing sanctions against agents that facilitate player poaching or recruit tampering.

Prohibiting football coaches from quitting mid-season to be hired by another program.

Curbing excessive transfers.

Student athletes are guaranteed one transfer as an undergraduate without losing eligibility with certain exceptions.

Stop Super League consolidation by:

Prohibiting conferences with more than $700 million in revenue from consolidating with or acquiring other conferences.

Limiting conference expansion to 19 entities.

Allow schools to voluntarily pool media rights across conference lines.

The bill also requires at least one free local broadcast option for football and basketball games in the local market of each participating school to preserve fan access to games.

title: Hoeven Statement After EPA Repeals Biden-Era Clean Power Plan 2.0
text:
WASHINGTON – Senator John Hoeven, a member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, issued the following statement after the Environmental Protection Agency repealed the Biden-era Clean Power Plan 2.0, an overreaching regulation that threatened the reliability of the electrical grid and premature closure of the nation’s coal-fired power plants.

“Repealing this overreaching rule is a win for U.S. energy dominance and will help American families have access to the affordable and reliable baseload power provided by coal,” said Hoeven. “The Supreme Court found that this regulation falls far outside of the legal authority provided to the EPA by Congress. That’s why we continually pushed back on this federal overreach, and we appreciate the Trump administration and EPA Administrator Zeldin for working with us to repeal this harmful rule.”

Specifically, the Clean Power Plan 2.0 would have forced states to change their fuel source for electricity. The Biden administration advanced the rule despite a Supreme Court ruling in 2022, which found the administration overstepped its authority in imposing the sector-wide regulation.

Last year, Hoeven joined President Trump as he signed executive orders to initiate the process of repealing the rule and other harmful regulations imposed by the Biden administration. The senator has also worked with EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin to roll-back the rule.

title: Husted, Walberg lead bicameral bill to protect college sports opportunities for American student-athletes
text:
“If the U.S. Congress is being asked to ‘save college sports’ we should save it for American student-athletes.”

WASHINGTON – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) today joined House Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Rep. Tim Walberg (R-Mich.) in introducing the Training and Education for Americans Members in University Sports and Athletics (TEAM USA) Act.

The bill would protect opportunities for American student-athletes by limiting international student-athlete (ISA) participation to no more than 20% of each varsity sports team.

“As Congress considers the future of NIL and college sports, protecting opportunities for American student-athletes must come first. American colleges and universities are increasingly giving scholarships and limited roster spots to foreign athletes, and the growth of NIL money only creates more incentive for foreign athletes to cash in on the American system. If the U.S. Congress is being asked to ‘save college sports’ we should save it for American student-athletes,” said Husted.

“American colleges and universities should first and foremost provide opportunities for American students. College athletics provides a pathway to world-class education and opportunities that last a lifetime. This bill restores balance by protecting roster spots for American student-athletes. America has built the strongest collegiate athletic system in the world, and we should make sure it continues to develop the next generation of American students and American Olympians,” said Walberg.

Each year, NCAA Division I and II schools provide more than $4 billion in athletic scholarships to over 197,000 student-athletes. Since 2001, the number of ISAs receiving scholarships has nearly tripled, from approximately 8,945 to roughly 25,000 today.

Only about 2% of American high school athletes receive an athletic scholarship. In several Division I sports, ISAs account for more than a third of participants, with some exceeding 60%.

The TEAM USA Act would:

Amend the Higher Education Act of 1965 to require colleges and universities participating in Title IV federal student aid programs to limit ISA participation to no more than 20% of each varsity team’s roster. Schools would also be required to report ISA participation on each team annually to the U.S. Department of Education and the applicable athletic association.

Aim to strengthen the American Olympic development pipeline. At the 2024 Paris Olympics, 65% of Team USA were current, former or incoming NCAA student-athletes. However, of the 1,036 NCAA-affiliated athletes who competed in Paris, only 385 represented the United States, with the other 63% competing for other nations.

Ensure that every team can roster at least 1 ISA if they so choose.

Take effect beginning with the 2029-2030 academic year, to minimize disruption to current student athletes already on campus and giving schools and athletic programs time to adjust recruiting practices.

title: Kelly, Gallego, Stanton, Ansari Announce $2 Million Federal Investment to Advance Water Reuse Technology for Semiconductor Manufacturing at ASU
text:
Today, Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), along with Representatives Greg Stanton (D-AZ-04) and Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ-03), announced $2,062,000 in federal funding for Arizona State University (ASU) to develop, test, and demonstrate innovative water reuse technologies designed for semiconductor manufacturing. The award, made through the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), was secured as congressionally directed spending championed by the Arizona delegation.

The project tests emerging water treatment technologies and validates them at ASU’s Macro Technology Works (MTW) facility in Tempe, generating the real-world performance data industry needs to adopt water-saving solutions at scale. The work aims to help fabs improve conservation while strengthening the reliability of domestic semiconductor production.

The legislation builds on Kelly’s work to bring manufacturing back to America. In 2022, Kelly’s CHIPS and Science Act was signed into law, which has significantly boosted domestic semiconductor manufacturing.

“Arizona is a national leader in chip manufacturing, and we know how to manage water responsibly,” said Sen. Kelly. “This investment builds on that leadership by developing water reuse technology, creating good-paying jobs, strengthening American manufacturing, and protecting our water supply. It’s a win for Arizona.”

“Making Arizona’s semiconductor manufacturing industry even more water efficient will allow us to continue to create good-paying jobs and protect our state’s water supply,” said Sen. Gallego. “Thanks to this project, Arizona will continue to lead the nation in community-beneficial innovation.”

“Arizona is proving that you can lead the nation in semiconductor manufacturing and be a responsible steward of every drop of water,” said Rep. Stanton. “This investment puts ASU’s researchers to work on exactly the right challenge: making sure the industry driving our economic future can grow without straining the water resources our communities depend on. That’s how we keep chip production strong and sustainable right here in Arizona.”

“In Arizona, water is our most precious and sacred resource. As our state continues to lead the nation in innovation and build the economy of the future through advanced semiconductor manufacturing, we must ensure that growth is sustainable,” said Rep. Ansari. “The federal dollars my colleagues and I secured will help do exactly that and ASU is a critical partner in driving the research, innovation, and commercialization needed to reduce water use and strengthen our resilience. Our future depends on it.”

“ASU looks forward to putting this federal investment to work advancing technologies that can help semiconductor manufacturers use water more efficiently and strengthen the resilience of chip production in Arizona,” said Arizona State University President Michael Crow. “Arizona’s water security and the nation’s focus on semiconductor manufacturing capacity depends on the leadership of policymakers and we appreciate the support from Senators Kelly and Gallego and Representatives Stanton and Ansari in recognizing the importance of this work. By developing and testing promising water reuse technologies in a semiconductor manufacturing environment, ASU can help advance these solutions for commercial use.”

Background:

The project will advance promising technologies from early-stage research toward commercial readiness through two phases: developing and integrating emerging treatment technologies into a mobile, pilot-scale demonstration testbed, and validating them in manufacturing-representative conditions at the MTW facility. Quarterly stakeholder reviews will guide which technologies advance to pilot-scale demonstration, where researchers will quantify water savings, cost reductions, and operational benefits.

By bridging the gap between fundamental research and commercial deployment, the project is expected to benefit semiconductor fabs seeking to reduce water use and improve resilience, while generating new intellectual property that can be licensed to start-ups and established water-technology firms.

title: Senator Kim Calls on Senate to Reassert Control over AI
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Andy Kim (D-NJ) released the following statement:

“AI is moving faster than anyone – including its creators – can understand or control. We need to act and act now to ensure that humans remain in control of this technology and that all people – not just the elite few – benefit from it.

“The warnings we’ve gotten after multiple concerning AI incidents need to serve as a wake-up call to establish a comprehensive approach including government action to put guardrails on our own technology, and ensure that our competitors and adversaries aren’t able to develop dangerous technologies.

“Technology and innovation must move forward; it’s what has powered our nation’s economy and kept us safe. But moving forward recklessly without sensible controls is a recipe for chaos and danger. The American people don’t want this technology to advance without rules that they have a say in writing.

“The Senate will reconvene this week. We should call together a Senate wide discussion on next steps and set out to pass critical bipartisan legislation that we can get done before the end of the year like the MATCH Act and BLADE Act that I’ve put forward along with other legislation to protect our kids. I’ve also pushed to develop a protocol to “Mythos-proof” our critical infrastructure and financial/healthcare sectors from AI-driven attacks and vulnerabilities. These are steps we can take right now as we build out broader solutions and regulations.

“It should be a focus of ours to discuss how to reassert control over AI for the American people. Control based on a set of principles, enforced by a set of rules, all built for a common purpose: to ensure the technology and innovation that moves us forward never leaves us behind. And controls to ensure our competitors and adversaries aren’t able to proceed recklessly while we take sensible steps.”

title: Lankford Leads Oklahoma Delegation in Push for Federal Disaster Assistance Following July 4 Storms
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — US Senator James Lankford (R-OK) led the Oklahoma congressional delegation in urging President Trump to approve Governor Kevin Stitt’s request for a major disaster declaration to help Oklahoma communities recover from severe storms, high winds, flooding, and widespread power outages that struck the state on July 4.

The delegation requested Public Assistance for Cleveland, Nowata, Osage, and Washington Counties, as well as Hazard Mitigation Grant Program assistance statewide.

Read the full letter HERE and below.

Mr. President,

We write in support of the formal request from the State of Oklahoma, through the office of Governor Kevin Stitt, that was submitted on September 2, 2026, for a major disaster declaration, including Public Assistance for Cleveland, Nowata, Osage, and Washington Counties to recover from severe storms, high winds, flooding, and widespread power outages that occurred on the evening of Saturday, July 4, as well as Hazard Mitigation Grant Program assistance statewide. An Executive Order declaring a State of Emergency in these counties (E.O. 2026-23) was issued on July 5, 2026.

Severe storms, high winds, and flooding impacted the State of Oklahoma on the evening of Saturday, July 4 and caused damage to public property within the State. As usual, Oklahomans demonstrated the Oklahoma Standard when they stepped up to help their families and neighbors as they began the process of cleaning up the debris and repairing damage to schools, businesses, and neighborhoods.

State and local officials have informed us that this incident is of such severity and magnitude that effective response and recovery is beyond the combined capability of the state and local governments, and that federal assistance is necessary to lessen the threat of disaster, protect property, and to ensure the safety of these communities.

As such, we respectfully urge you to approve the Governor’s request for the counties listed above and to provide Hazard Mitigation Grant Program assistance statewide. We stand ready to provide any assistance needed to ensure the prompt evaluation of this request. Please reach out to our offices with any questions on this matter.

Sincerely,

/x/

Background

Lankford has consistently worked to ensure Oklahoma communities have access to federal resources following severe weather and natural disasters.

In July, Lankford announced more than $12.3 million in FEMA Public Assistance grants to help Oklahoma communities repair electrical infrastructure, roads, and public buildings damaged by severe storms, tornadoes, and winter weather.

In June, Lankford highlighted more than $2.8 million in FEMA assistance for recovery from severe storms, tornadoes, flooding, and wildfires after working with FEMA leadership to finalize the grants.

Earlier this year, Lankford helped secure more than $20 million in FEMA funding for flood mitigation in Tulsa County and severe-weather recovery efforts in Shawnee, Sulphur, and other Oklahoma communities.

Lankford has also repeatedly worked with the Oklahoma congressional delegation to support major disaster declarations following severe weather, including leading the delegation’s request for federal assistance after the April 2024 tornado outbreak.

Lankford has introduced bipartisan legislation to improve federal disaster response and recovery, including the POWER Act, which would allow FEMA funding to be used to strengthen electrical infrastructure while it is rebuilt following a disaster.

title: Lummis, Boozman, Scott Release Final Clarity Act Text
text:
Washington, D.C.— U.S. Senate Banking Digital Assets Subcommittee Chair Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) alongside Chairmen John Boozman (R-AR) and Tim Scott (R-SC) released a final draft of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act before Tuesday’s vote, reflecting over a year of bipartisan negotiations and 126 substantive changes made at the request of Democrats.

The final text includes new ethics language which reflects substantially all of the Tillis-Gallego ethics proposal, including a meaningful role for state attorneys general in enforcement. It also gives the Secretary of the Treasury new authority to prevent deposit flight tied to payment stablecoins, providing a strong circuit-breaker to protect community banks and the farmers and small businesses who rely on them. The draft also includes edits to the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA) to shield developers from money transmission registration requirements and establish a strong civil safe harbor. On the Agriculture Committee’s provisions, this language protects consumers with new guardrails on affiliate trading and conflicts of interest, clarifies the applicability of state consumer protection laws, and protects software developers without impacting derivatives regulation and existing Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) authority.

If cloture is invoked on the motion to proceed on Tuesday afternoon, this legislative text would be offered as an Amendment in the Nature of a Substitute.

“After a year of intense daily bipartisan negotiations, this bill is ready,” said Lummis.“President Trump voluntarily agreed to unprecedented ethics restrictions, holding every federally elected official, judge, and their spouses to some of the toughest ethics restrictions in U.S. history. This text is truly bipartisan and includes more than 120 of Democrats’ demands. A no vote on Tuesday means opposing real ethics reforms on politicians’ personal investments, handing American leadership in digital assets to our foreign competitors, and leaving Americans with zero protections in the digital asset markets. Democrats got what they wanted; now they need to take yes for an answer.”

Chairman Boozman, who led the Agriculture Committee portion said:

“We have an opportunity to establish clear rules of the road that will protect consumers, strengthen our markets, and ensure we remain a global leader in digital asset innovation. We cannot afford to wait any longer. This legislation is the result of more than a year of negotiations with our colleagues and conversations with stakeholders to get the details right. Senator Lummis has been a steadfast leader on this issue, and I appreciate her continued efforts to get this across the finish line.”

Chairman Scott, who led the Banking Committee portion said:

“Growing up with a single mom in South Carolina, I learned that every dollar matters. The Clarity Act will protect Americans’ hard-earned money, keep innovation and jobs in America, and strengthen our national security. This final text further empowers law enforcement and gives the Treasury Secretary the tools to protect community banks, farmers, and rural Americans. I am grateful to Chairman Boozman and Senator Lummis for their partnership. After over a year of bipartisan negotiations and over 100 changes requested by Democrats, it is time for the Senate to move this strong, bipartisan bill forward.”

In 2022, Senator Lummis and Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) introduced the Responsible Financial Innovation Act, a comprehensive bipartisan bill to establish the first regulatory framework for digital assets in the United States, dividing oversight jurisdiction between the SEC and CFTC.

In 2023, Senators Lummis and Gillibrand reintroduced the legislation.

In July of 2025, Senator Lummis, Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott (R-SC), and Senators Bill Hagerty (R-TN) and Bernie Moreno (R-OH) released a Senate discussion draft of the Responsible Financial Innovation Act of 2025.

In May 2026, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act passed out of the Banking Committee by a 15 to 9 bipartisan vote.

In July, Senator Lummis led her colleagues in reintroducing text that included an unprecedented and serious ethics agreement where President Trump agreed to voluntarily impose the strictest ethics measures in U.S. history on himself, the Vice President, judges, every federally elected official, and their spouses. This was a serious demonstration of the President’s commitment to getting this legislation across the finish line and ensuring the United States leads the world in digital assets.

The Clarity Act has earned support from major financial institutions like BlackRock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, Goldman Sachs, Charles Schwab, and SoFi, and law enforcement organizations like the National Fraternal Order of Police and the National Organization of Black Law Enforcement Executives. The National Sheriffs Association and the Majority County Sheriffs Association, representing law enforcement which protects more than 130 million Americans, both dropped their opposition recently to the Clarity Act, recognizing that this legislation gives law enforcement the tools it needs to fight crime.

title: Senator Markey Statement on EPA’s Repeal of Power Plant Greenhouse Gas Emission Standards and Proposal to Abdicate Responsibility for Addressing the Danger of Climate Change from the Power Sector
text:
Washington (September 14, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), a member of the Environment and Public Works Committee and a co-chair of the Senate Environmental Justice Caucus, today released the following statement after the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) finalized its repeal of the 2024 greenhouse gas emission standards for existing coal-fired and new natural gas-fired power plants and announced that it no longer plans to regulate greenhouse gas pollution from power plants, a major driver of climate change.

“By rejecting the EPA’s responsibility to regulate climate change caused by greenhouse gas pollution from power plants, Trump and Zeldin are defying the laws of this country, the laws of physics, and the law of common sense. Their Polluters First Agenda passes the very real costs of a more dangerous environment and a more extreme climate onto working families. This is a slap in the face to anyone who has lost their home to wildfires or was washed out by an extreme storm. It is a slap in the face to parents who want their kids to breathe clean air, not suffer from asthma or heat stroke. And it is a slap in the face to anyone who put trust into the Environmental Protection Agency to uphold its mission to protect human health and the environment, not protect corporate polluter profits. We don’t need dirty power when we have the solutions and can get cheap, clean megawatts on the grid, and we don’t need dirty politicians overruling the scientific necessity of action.”

This move follows the Trump EPA’s elimination of the Endangerment Finding, the determination that affirms the scientific risks of climate change and requires federal action to protect Americans from harm. The Trump EPA has also eliminated greenhouse gas emission standards for cars and trucks and slashed protections against mercury, soot, and other dangerous emissions from the power sector. In addition to specific rollbacks of statutorily-required protections, the EPA has also stopped accounting for the public health benefits of regulatory action—valuing human health at zero, compared to compliance costs for profitable polluting industries.

In April 2024, the Biden administration finalized standards to reduce pollution from fossil fuel-fired power plants, which are the largest source of greenhouse gas emissions from the energy sector in the United States. If it were a country, the American power sector would be the fifth-largest emitter of climate pollution in the world.

title: Senator Marshall Applauds Nearly $17 Million in New CMS Funding for Rural Kansas
text:
Washington – U.S. Senator Roger Marshall, M.D. (R-Kansas), applauded today’s announcement from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) of nearly $17 million in new federal funding to strengthen rural healthcare across Kansas through the Rural Health Transformation Program.

As part of today’s announcement, $16 million will be allocated to Emerging Technology Grants to help 14 rural providers adopt technologies like diagnostic tools and remote patient monitoring. An additional $780,000 will support the Interfacility Transport Project to improve regional transportation coordination, helping rural patients safely reach specialty and behavioral healthcare faster. These investments build on the more than $80 million in RHTP funding previously announced to strengthen rural healthcare across Kansas, including support for prevention and chronic disease management, healthcare workforce recruitment and development, technology and infrastructure upgrades, and nutrition-focused initiatives.

“Technology is playing a bigger and bigger role in the future of rural health care,” said Senator Marshall.“Telemedicine, remote patient monitoring, and new diagnostic tools can help our rural doctors and nurses deliver more care close to home, while better transportation helps patients who still have to travel hours to see a specialist. I’m thrilled CMS is working with Kansas to make sure these Rural Health Transformation dollars are making a real difference in our rural communities.”

The investment was made possible through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act — passed by Republicans in Congress and unanimously opposed by Democrats — delivering a historic $50 billion investment to help states transform the way healthcare is delivered in America.

Today’s announcement is one part of the larger overall funding amount awarded to Kansas for fiscal year 2026.

Projects supported by this funding include:

Advancing technology-enabled healthcare: Expanding telehealth, remote patient monitoring, data analytics, and emerging technologies, including new awards supporting diagnostic, surgical, AI-enabled, and assistive technologies across rural Kansas.

Strengthening prevention and chronic disease management: Supporting earlier screening and community-based prevention to improve health outcomes and reduce preventable hospitalizations.

Building a sustainable rural healthcare workforce: Investing in recruitment, training, career pathways, and retention strategies to strengthen the pipeline of healthcare professionals serving rural communities.

Improving access to rural healthcare: Strengthening local providers, regional partnerships, and innovative care models, including new interfacility transportation projects to help patients reach needed care more quickly.

title: Senator Marshall Completes 120 Stops Across 59 Kansas Counties
text:
Olathe – U.S. Senator Roger Marshall, M.D. (R-Kansas), wrapped up his “120 Stops to Strengthen Rural Kansas” Tour, traveling across 59 Kansas counties during the August recess to meet directly with Kansans and highlight the people, industries, and policies that are strengthening communities across the state.

Over the course of the tour, Senator Marshall visited hospitals and healthcare providers, manufacturers, family farms and ranches, small businesses, technical schools, community organizations, local leaders, and Kansans working every day to keep rural communities strong.

“Over the past month, I’ve traveled to 59 counties and made 120 stops across our great state. I’ve sat down with farmers and ranchers, doctors and nurses, manufacturers, small business owners, and families to hear what’s happening in their communities,” said Senator Marshall. “We’ve got a lot to be proud of — from cutting taxes for working families and growing Kansas manufacturing to delivering real resources for our rural hospitals. But there’s still work to do. I’m going back to Washington with what I heard from Kansans, and I’ll keep fighting to deliver results for the people who sent me there.”

Senator Marshall wrapped up the tour at the Kansas State Fair, where he participated in a Kansas agriculture leadership breakfast hosted Kansas Farm Bureau, the voice of Kansas agriculture. He discussed his time working in agriculture as a child and his continued fight to get the Farm Bill across the finish line, which includes 23 Kansas priorities authored by Senator Marshall.

Throughout the tour, Senator Marshall highlighted key deliverables that are helping strengthen Kansas communities and create new opportunities across the state, including:

Working Families Tax Cuts: Senator Marshall highlighted the tax relief now putting more money back in Kansans’ pockets, including No Tax on Overtime legislation he authored and fought to include in the final bill, as well as no tax on tips, full expensing for domestic research and development, and a permanent 20% small business deduction. These provisions are helping Kansas workers keep more of their paychecks while giving farmers, ranchers, manufacturers, and Main Street businesses more resources to invest, expand, and hire.

Growing Kansas Manufacturing: Senator Marshall highlighted how new tax provisions, including 100% bonus depreciation and full expensing, are helping Kansas manufacturers immediately write off investments in new machinery and equipment. Those incentives are making it easier for Kansas companies to expand their facilities, invest in their workforce, and bring more manufacturing jobs home.

Strengthening Rural Health Care: Senator Marshall highlighted more than $220 million in Rural Health Transformation funding coming to Kansas, supporting rural hospitals and providers with resources to expand access, recruit and retain health care workers, improve technology and patient care, and keep more Kansans from having to travel hours for treatment.

Supporting Kansas Agriculture: Senator Marshall heard directly from farmers and ranchers about the need for a stronger farm safety net and greater certainty. He highlighted his fight for crop insurance, higher reference prices, year-round E15, rural broadband, childcare, and farmers’ mental health, including 23 Kansas priorities he brought directly into the Farm Bill.

Investing in Rural Communities: Senator Marshall also highlighted investments in infrastructure, workforce development, and rural economic growth, including expanded access to private capital for rural communities and small businesses and greater opportunities for Kansans pursuing technical and skilled-trades education.

The “120 Stops to Strengthen Rural Kansas” Tour built on Senator Marshall’s commitment to meeting Kansans where they are and ensuring that the voices of rural communities are heard in Washington.

From one end of Kansas to the other, the tour reinforced his message that strong rural communities make up a stronger Kansas.

title: Senator Marshall Urges USDA to Provide Diesel Relief for Farmers During Harvest
text:
Wichita – U.S. Senator Roger Marshall, M.D. (R-Kansas), sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins urging the Trump Administration to work with Congress to provide temporary, targeted relief for farmers and ranchers facing rapidly rising diesel costs during the 2026 harvest season.

With the national average retail price of diesel reaching $5.967 per gallon as of September 7, producers are being hit with significant, unplanned fuel costs during one of the most diesel-intensive times of the year.

In the letter, Senator Marshall wrote:

“Most producers made their planting, financing, and marketing decisions months ago, before this latest price spike, and they must now absorb substantial unplanned fuel costs during one of the most diesel-intensive periods of the year.”

“A stable and secure food supply depends on financially viable farmers and ranchers. Helping producers withstand this sudden and largely unforeseen cost shock is therefore both an agricultural and national-security imperative.”

Background:

Diesel prices are approaching $6 per gallon. The national average retail price reached $5.967 per gallon as of September 7, hitting producers as harvest gets underway.

Diesel supplies remain exceptionally tight. The U.S. Energy Information Administration forecasts domestic distillate inventories will fall below 100 million barrels in September and remain below the five-year low through the end of 2026 and most of 2027.

Refineries have little room to increase production. U.S. refineries operated at 97.8 percent of capacity during the week ending September 4, limiting the ability to quickly boost diesel supplies.

Senator Marshall is calling on USDA to work with the Administration and Congress to provide temporary, targeted relief for farmers and ranchers facing extraordinary diesel costs during the 2026 harvest and production year.

Senator Marshall has worked on expanding ethanol and biodiesel supply through expansion of the RFS, and incentivizing production through the 45Z tax credit. These actions offer an affordable option at the pump for consumers and increases on-road transportation fuel supply.
