title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Helps Launch Bipartisan Hydropower Caucus
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) joined Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) to launch the bipartisan Congressional Hydropower Caucus, a new forum focused on expanding reliable American energy production, strengthening the electric grid, and lowering costs for families and businesses.

The Hydropower Caucus will bring Members of Congress together with hydropower and marine energy experts from federal agencies, industry, and stakeholder organizations to address permitting and licensing reform, tax policy, research and development, and deployment of new technologies. The caucus will focus on practical ways to make better use of existing infrastructure, remove barriers to new generation, and bring more American power onto the grid.

“America’s electricity needs are growing fast, and meeting that demand is going to require us to produce more power from every reliable resource we have here at home,” said Congressman Harrigan. “Hydropower has been powering American communities for generations, and there is still tremendous potential to build on what already works. This caucus gives us a place to bring the right people together, cut through outdated barriers, and find practical ways to get more power onto the grid. If we want to bring manufacturing home, lead the next generation of technology, and keep energy affordable, America needs an energy system built for growth.”

“Hydropower is at the heart of lowering energy costs for hardworking Granite Staters and making America the world’s clean energy superpower. For generations, hydropower has delivered reliable, homegrown energy to communities across New Hampshire and our country. Our bipartisan caucus will bring together the people with the expertise and ideas we need to cut red tape, invest in innovation, and get more affordable American energy online. I’m proud to lead this effort with Congressman Harrigan, and I will keep working across the aisle to lower costs and build an energy future that works for the people we serve,” said Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander.

“Hydropower is a reliable, carbon-free energy resource that plays an important role in supporting grid reliability and meeting growing electricity demand. Duke Energy looks forward to working with the Caucus on policies that support the continued operation and modernization of America's hydropower fleet, and I thank Representatives Pat Harrigan and Maggie Goodlander for their leadership in creating this bipartisan forum,” said Kendal Bowman, president of Duke Energy’s utility operations in North Carolina.

"NHA applauds Representatives Goodlander and Harrigan for launching the bipartisan Hydropower Caucus. Hydropower is America’s first renewable energy resource, operating in 48 states and providing reliable power to nearly 30 million Americans. Yet too few people understand its benefits and the policy challenges it faces. The Hydropower Caucus can help change that by educating lawmakers and stakeholders about the many ways hydropower supports our communities—not only through affordable, reliable electricity, but also through irrigation, flood control, recreation, and good-paying jobs. We thank Representatives Goodlander and Harrigan for their leadership in advancing this important effort,” said Matthew Allen, Senior Director of Legislative Affairs, National Hydropower Association.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Introduces REACH Act to Strengthen Rural Health Care Workforce
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10), alongside co-leads Congressmen Tom Barrett (R-MI-07) and Don Davis (D-NC-01), introduced the Resources for Essential Access to Community Health (REACH) Act, legislation to address the shortage of health care providers in rural communities by offering a refundable $10,000 annual tax credit to doctors, nurses, mental health professionals, and medical residents who choose to work in rural areas.

“Too many families in rural North Carolina have to drive farther and wait longer just to see a doctor because there simply aren’t enough health care professionals nearby. If we want to change that, we have to make it easier for doctors, nurses, and mental health professionals to choose these communities and stay there,” said Congressman Harrigan. “The REACH Act puts a real incentive behind that choice, giving providers a $10,000 tax credit to serve rural communities and helping more families get the care they need closer to home.”

“Too many of our rural communities don’t have enough doctors and nurses to provide essential care for the local residents who need it,” said Congressman Barrett. “Where you live should never be a barrier to accessing quality care. By providing an incentive to attract these professionals to our communities, our bipartisan REACH Act will make health care more affordable and accessible for families in rural mid-Michigan.”

"Every patient deserves the same standard of care, no matter their zip code. That's especially true in rural North Carolina, where shortages of physicians, nurses, and mental health providers make access to care more challenging than it should be. As an academic health system, training the next generation of healthcare professionals is central to our mission, and we welcome Congressman Harrigan's efforts to strengthen the rural healthcare workforce and encourage more providers to serve the communities that need them most,” said Dr. David Zaas, Chief Executive Officer, Duke University Health System.

“As the largest provider of rural health care in North Carolina, Atrium Health understands firsthand the importance of attracting and retaining providers in underserved areas. We applaud Representatives Pat Harrigan and Don Davis for introducing the REACH Act and for their leadership in addressing the unique health care challenges facing rural communities. This legislation is an important step toward strengthening the rural health care workforce, expanding access to care, and ensuring patients can receive high-quality healthcare services close to home. We appreciate them for their bipartisan commitment to supporting the health and well-being of rural North Carolina communities,” said Steve Moot, President North Carolina & Georgia Division, Atrium Health.

“Rural hospitals and health systems are working every day to recruit and retain the healthcare professionals their communities need. The REACH Act would give rural providers another tool to compete for talented professionals and strengthen access to care in communities across North Carolina," said Josh Dobson, President and CEO of NCHA.

Under the REACH Act, eligible providers who work at least 900 hours per year in a rural area would qualify for the $10,000 credit. The legislation covers primary care practitioners, including OB-GYNs, as well as mental health professionals, nurses, and residents participating in approved medical residency programs.

The credit would begin to phase out for providers with adjusted gross incomes above $170,000 and would remain available for qualifying rural employment through 2033. The legislation would take effect beginning with the 2027 tax year.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Secures $20 Million Authorization for Mooresville Water Infrastructure
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) voted for H.R. 9497, the Water Resources Development Act of 2026, bipartisan legislation that includes a major win he secured for Mooresville, increasing the city’s federal authorization for water and wastewater infrastructure from $4 million to $20 million.

“Mooresville is one of the fastest-growing communities in our region, and I worked to make sure this bill reflects what that growth actually requires,” said Congressman Harrigan. “Increasing Mooresville’s authorization from $4 million to $20 million gives our community significantly more capacity to pursue the water and wastewater infrastructure families and businesses will depend on for decades. This is exactly the kind of work I came to Congress to do, taking the needs I hear about at home and turning them into results in Washington.”

Beyond Mooresville, the Water Resources Development Act authorizes and improves U.S. Army Corps of Engineers projects and programs across the country, covering water and wastewater infrastructure, flood risk management, ports and harbors, inland waterways, dam safety, and other critical water resources needs. The legislation also includes reforms aimed at speeding project delivery, improving contracting and permitting processes, and making it easier for local communities to navigate and access Army Corps programs.

Having passed the House, the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 now heads to the Senate for consideration.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Votes to Block California Shipping Mandate
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) voted for H.J. Res. 210, a Congressional Review Act resolution overturning an Environmental Protection Agency action allowing California to enforce its own emissions requirements for ocean-going vessels while they are docked at ports.

“California should not get to write the rules for an industry that moves goods across the entire country,” said Congressman Harrigan. “When one state is allowed to impose its own requirements on ships moving through our ports and supply chains, the consequences do not stop at the California border. Congress has a responsibility to push back when state regulations reach far beyond the state itself and affect how the rest of the country does business.”

H.J. Res. 210 disapproves the EPA’s decision regarding California’s nonroad engine pollution control standards for ocean-going vessels at berth. Under the Congressional Review Act, the resolution would nullify the EPA action and prevent it from having force or effect.

Following House passage, H.J. Res. 210 now moves to the Senate for consideration.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Votes to Crack Down on Fraud in Federal Programs
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) voted for H.R. 10326, the Preventing Rip-offs and Obtaining Oversight of Funds (PROOF) Act, legislation strengthening information sharing between federal law enforcement and state agencies to help identify, investigate, and prosecute fraud involving taxpayer-funded programs.

“Every dollar stolen through fraud is a dollar taken from an American who earned it and a program someone genuinely depends on,” said Congressman Harrigan. “We know criminals look for gaps between agencies, jurisdictions, and systems because those gaps make it easier to hide. The PROOF Act gives law enforcement a better way to connect the dots and go after the people stealing from taxpayers, with strong protections in place for Americans’ private information.”

The PROOF Act allows the Attorney General, as part of a fraud investigation or prosecution, to request relevant records from states administering programs including Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, unemployment insurance, disaster assistance, emergency rental assistance, broadband funding, and certain small business programs. The bill requires transferred information to be encrypted, limits access to authorized personnel, restricts its use to fraud-related law enforcement purposes, and requires the information to be permanently removed after the relevant investigation or legal proceeding concludes.

Having passed the House, the PROOF Act now heads to the Senate for consideration.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Votes to Strengthen Federal Fraud Enforcement
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) voted for H.R. 9576, the National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026, legislation establishing a dedicated National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice to strengthen the federal government’s ability to combat fraud and protect taxpayer dollars.

“Fraud has changed dramatically, but the way the government goes after it hasn’t kept pace,” said Congressman Harrigan. “Criminals can move money, steal identities, and exploit weaknesses in our systems faster than ever before, while federal enforcement is often spread across different offices and agencies. Americans deserve a government that can keep up, and creating a dedicated fraud division at the Department of Justice is a commonsense step toward doing that.”

The National Fraud Enforcement Division Act establishes a permanent National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice under the authority of the Attorney General. The division will be led by an Assistant Attorney General for National Fraud Enforcement, appointed by the President, providing a dedicated leadership structure within DOJ for federal fraud enforcement. The legislation also subjects the new division to federal restrictions on political activity, ensuring the officials responsible for carrying out its work are held to the same standards governing political activity that apply to other key components of the Department of Justice.

Having passed the House, the National Fraud Enforcement Division Act now heads to the Senate for consideration.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Votes to Strengthen Sanctions Against Russia and Iran
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) voted for the Senate Amendment to H.R. 5334, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, legislation imposing sweeping economic pressure on Russia and those helping finance, supply, and sustain its war machine.

“America’s adversaries pay attention to what we are willing to tolerate, and there has to be a real cost for threatening our interests and fueling aggression,” said Congressman Harrigan. “Russia has used its energy exports, financial system, and networks around the world to sustain its war machine and evade pressure from the West. This legislation goes after those lifelines directly, including the countries and companies helping keep them open. Peace through strength means making clear that aggression comes with consequences.”

The legislation targets senior Russian officials, state-controlled entities and financial institutions, defense suppliers, energy interests, and vessels used to evade sanctions. It restricts U.S. investment in Russia, prohibits certain financial transactions and energy exports, blocks purchases of Russian sovereign debt, and strengthens restrictions on Russian uranium. The bill also authorizes tariffs of up to 500 percent on Russian goods and duties of up to 100 percent on goods from certain countries that continue purchasing Russian oil or natural gas or facilitate Russian sanctions evasion.

The bill also extends the Iran Sanctions Act through 2031, maintaining a key tool for applying economic pressure on the Iranian regime.

title: CT House Delegation Statement On Russia Sanctions Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Representative Jahana Hayes (CT-05), John Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), and Jim Himes (CT-04) issued the following statement after voting “no” on H.R. 10076, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026.

“Last June, the U.S. House passed a bipartisan Russian sanctions bill, H.R. 2913, to support the brave nation of Ukraine along with new military assistance to Ukraine, which is critically needed. The sanctions provisions in H.R. 2913 provided enforcement language that would ensure President Trump implemented the bill. The Lindsay Graham Senate bill, H.R. 10076, removed the sanctions enforcement language and left the decision to sanction totally within the discretion of the President, who has repeatedly demonstrated bias towards Russia’s war goals of seizing the eastern Donbas.

Furthermore, this bill would only enable the President’s penchant for imposing reckless tariffs at the expense of the American consumer – effectively handing the President the power to raise costs on American workers and families by more than $8,000 a year– while providing zero additional military assistance for Ukraine. Our delegation has staunchly supported Ukraine and are determined to provide tangible assistance as well as enforceable sanctions against Putin’s war machine.

We recognize the Senate’s hard work and applaud Senator Blumenthal and his colleagues for their efforts. Due to our concerns, we could not vote for this bill in its current form and remain committed to continuing to stand unwaveringly with the Ukrainian people and enacting tough sanctions that hold the Putin regime accountable.

The Senate bill falls short of those goals, and we believe it is time to redouble efforts to pass the original House bill.”

title: Cámara federal aprueba 11 medidas del Comisionado Residente para atender la crisis de agua en Puerto Rico
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, anunció que la Cámara de Representantes aprobó la Ley de Desarrollo de Recursos Hídricos de 2026 (WRDA), que incluye 11 de sus prioridades para atender la crisis de agua, fortalecer la infraestructura crítica y proteger a comunidades vulnerables a inundaciones y erosión costera en Puerto Rico.

“Estamos dando pasos concretos para atender lo básico. Puerto Rico necesita un sistema de infraestructura de agua que funcione y comunidades mejor protegidas contra inundaciones y tormentas,” dijo el Comisionado Residente.“Estas 11 prioridades fueron presentadas por nuestra oficina, incluidas en el proyecto, y no son asignaciones automáticas. Es un logro del cual nos sentimos muy satisfechos.”

La Ley de Desarrollo de Recursos Hídricos de 2026 (WRDA) autoriza al Cuerpo de Ingenieros del Ejército de Estados Unidos a avanzar proyectos y estudios relacionados con infraestructura de agua, control de inundaciones y protección costera. Los proyectos que requieran fondos deberán pasar posteriormente por el proceso de asignaciones del Congreso.

Las 11 prioridades que el Comisionado Residente aseguró para Puerto Rico son:

Más recursos para infraestructura de agua en Puerto Rico: El proyecto aumenta de $35 millones a $75 millones la autorización federal disponible para apoyar proyectos de agua potable y alcantarillado.

Humacao: Incluye el Río Antón Ruiz y sus diques para desarrollar mejoras que reduzcan las inundaciones y protejan a Río Verde Mar, Punta Santiago y comunidades cercanas.

Corozal: Autoriza $10 millones para mejorar los sistemas de agua y alcantarillado, incluidos acueductos comunitarios que sirven a familias con acceso limitado al agua.

Vega Baja: Autoriza un estudio de la Laguna Puerto Nuevo, o Laguna Quintín Valle, para evaluar dragado y otras soluciones contra inundaciones.

Loíza: Autoriza un estudio para combatir la erosión costera, reducir los daños por marejadas y proteger hogares y comunidades cercanas a la costa.

Ceiba: Permite estudiar soluciones para proteger la costa y las comunidades frente a tormentas, inundaciones y erosión.

Yabucoa: Autoriza un estudio para reducir los daños por marejadas y fortalecer la protección de las comunidades costeras.

Río Puerto Nuevo: Incluye lenguaje para realizar nuevos estudios de impacto que atiendan las preocupaciones de las comunidades aledañas.

Naguabo: Autoriza un estudio para proteger la costa, reducir la erosión y disminuir los riesgos para las comunidades durante eventos atmosféricos.

Fajardo: Permite evaluar proyectos para proteger viviendas, infraestructura y recursos naturales frente a la erosión y las tormentas costeras.

Acceso de Puerto Rico a un programa federal de protección de costas y ríos: El proyecto añade expresamente a Puerto Rico al Programa de Protección y Restauración de Costas y Ríos (Shoreline and Riverine Protection Program), permitiendo que la isla sea considerada para futuros estudios y proyectos dirigidos a reducir daños por inundaciones, huracanes y tormentas.

Tras su aprobación en la Cámara, el Comisionado Residente continuará trabajando para que las 11 prioridades de Puerto Rico permanezcan en la legislación final durante el proceso legislativo con el Senado.

title: Horsford Delivers FULL HOUSE Act to Protect Nevadans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) today secured House Ways and Means Committee approval of his bipartisan FULL HOUSE Act to restore the full deduction for gambling losses, advancing relief for taxpayers and helping protect the Nevada jobs that depend on gaming and tourism.

“At a time of economic uncertainty, my job is to protect Nevadans and their jobs,” said Rep. Horsford. “From dealers and housekeepers to restaurant workers and small business owners, families across our state depend on visitors choosing Nevada. This unfair tax puts their livelihoods at risk. That’s why I fought to advance my FULL HOUSE Act, and I won’t stop until we get this relief signed into law.”

For decades, taxpayers could deduct 100 percent of their gambling losses against their winnings, up to the amount won. Last year’s “One Big Beautiful Bill” reduced that deduction to 90 percent, creating a “phantom tax” that can force people to pay taxes even when their losses equal their winnings.

Following months of bipartisan negotiations, Horsford secured inclusion of his FULL HOUSE Act’s full repeal of that restriction in the tax package approved by the committee.

“No one should pay taxes on money they never earned,” said Rep. Horsford. “This is about the workers supporting their families, the small businesses keeping their doors open, and the communities that make Nevada home. I stayed at the table because they deserve results. Today, we moved closer to delivering.”

While we all recognize the work is not yet done, today’s Committee action marks a critically important step toward protecting our workforce and restoring fairness to the tax code,” noted Craig Billings, Chief Executive Officer to Las Vegas-based Wynn Resorts. “It has taken bi-partisan leadership from Chairman Smith and hometown Congressman Horsford to get us to this point. We commend them for their efforts, and we look forward to supporting them as they work to pass this important legislation before this Congress comes to a close.”

“The American Gaming Association is grateful for this critical step forward in restoring the 100% gambling tax deduction. We encourage Congress to pass the FULL HOUSE Act to ensure that consumers choose the legal market where protections exist and are not taxed on phantom income. Thank you to the Ways and Means Committee as well as Representatives Horsford and Miller for their leadership in advocating for this bi-partisan measure. We look forward to working with our partners in Congress to get this passed.” Said Bill Miller, President and CEO, American Gaming Association

The bipartisan legislation passed overwhelmingly with 38 Members in favor, 5 opposed. The legislation now awaits consideration by the full House. Horsford will continue building bipartisan support to get this relief passed and signed into law.

title: Houchin Bill to Name American Mastodon and T. Rex National Symbols Passes House
text:
September 16, 2026

WASHINGTON—Today, H.R. 9191, the National Fossil Act, led by Congresswoman Erin Houchin (R-IN-09) and Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) passed the House of Representatives. The bill designates the American mastodon (Mammut americanum) as the national fossil mammal and the Tyrannosaurus rex as the national fossil dinosaur of the United States.

If enacted, the American mastodon and Tyrannosaurus rex would join the bald eagle, bison, rose, and oak tree as official national symbols of the United States.

“The mastodon has been Indiana's state fossil since 2022, and today the House voted to give it a place among our national symbols," said Rep. Houchin. "As our country marks its 250th year, this is a fitting way to honor a piece of America's story and to get the next generation curious about science, geology, and paleontology. I'm grateful to Rep. Dingell for her partnership and to my colleagues on both sides of the aisle for sending this bill forward."

“America’s story didn’t begin in 1776. It began thousands and even millions of years earlier, with creatures like the mastodon and T. rex roaming the land we now call home,” said Rep. Dingell. “The mastodon is the state fossil of Michigan, and recognizing them as a national symbol alongside the T. rex is a reminder that discovery is part of who we are as a country. From backyard discoveries to museum exhibits that have inspired generations of kids, this bipartisan effort is a way to celebrate America’s prehistoric past and spark curiosity about science and exploration. I am proud to work with Congresswoman Houchin to advance this legislation, and we will keep working together until it is law.”

The American mastodon is the official state fossil of both Indiana and Michigan and has been discovered at sites throughout both states. The Tyrannosaurus rex remains one of the most recognizable dinosaurs in the world and an enduring symbol of American paleontological discovery.

The legislation is supported by Dr. Stanley Totten, curator of the Hanover College Museum of Natural History and professor emeritus of geology at Hanover College, where he taught for 40 years.

"Recognizing these two amazing animals as representative of America’s historic past would be the perfect present for a Nation celebrating its 250th birthday,” said Dr. Totten.

title: Rep. Houchin Bill to Improve Literacy Education Practices Passes House
text:
September 16, 2026

WASHINGTON—Today, the House of Representatives passed H.R. 7890, the Science of Reading Act of 2026. This bill would prioritize the Science of Reading in the deployment of federal literacy funds. This brings federal policy into alignment with advancements in scientific understanding of how children learn to read, and reserves grant funding to the most impactful and effective methods of instruction.

American schoolchildren at all levels have faced declining literacy skills for nearly a decade. This is a quiet crisis that has significant economic, social, and behavioral impacts for the rest of each student’s life, and for the communities that they live in.

Fortunately, we have a clear path forward. The Science of Reading is a body of research that emphasizes phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension as pillars of instructional principles. Implementation of Science of Reading in states across the country has yielded significant improvements in reading acquisition on all levels, including in Indiana.

“Reading is the foundation of learning, and we cannot accept declining literacy rates as the status quo. The Science of Reading Act will equip classrooms with proven methods to ensure every student can read. Indiana has shown that the Science of Reading works, and I’m proud to see this important legislation pass the House.”

– Rep. Erin Houchin (IN-09)

"It’s time to move away from failed theories and restore evidence-based reading instruction that actually works. Our children deserve an education grounded in what the evidence tells us, not the latest educational fad. I applaud Rep. Houchin for her leadership to improve our nation’s child literacy rates.”

- ‎House Education & Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg (MI-05)

“As a former teacher and Chair of the K-12 Education Subcommittee, I am grateful the House has come together in a bipartisan way to promote literacy. Perhaps nothing is more vital to a child's academic success than receiving proper literacy instruction from an early age. This legislation will promote best practices, rooted in the science of reading, and help more students develop the reading skills needed to reach their full potential.”

– Rep. Kevin Kiley (CA-03)

"As a teacher for nearly three decades - and the husband of a literacy expert - I know that strong reading skills are the foundation for success in the classroom, in the workplace, and throughout life. The Science of Reading Act gives teachers and students access to proven, evidence-based approaches that help kids become stronger readers. I’m proud that Republicans and Democrats came together to pass this legislation and move us one step closer to improving reading outcomes for students in NY-22 and across the country. Strong schools and strong readers are essential to America’s ability to compete and win globally.”

- ‎Rep. John Mannion (NY-22)

“Indiana continues to invest historic resources to ensure the science of reading is used in every Hoosier classroom. Through this intentional focus, we’ve seen two consecutive years of historic literacy gains, with nearly 90 percent of third graders now reading proficiently. This legislation reinforces our work in Indiana, ensures taxpayer dollars are only used on what we know works, and will help more students across the country to become strong readers.”

– Indiana Governor Mike Braun

“Literacy is the key to unlocking future success for our students, which is why it is absolutely essential that we use instructional strategies proven to help children learn to read. Through Indiana’s focus on the science of reading, we have more Hoosier third graders reading today than even before the pandemic. By doubling down on these evidence-based strategies, we can ensure students across Indiana and the nation have the best possible chance for literacy success, and thus lifelong opportunities.”

– Indiana Secretary of Education Dr. Katie Jenner

"We are already seeing the impact of the Science of Reading research in Indiana, with literacy rates among Hoosier children showing significant improvement since 2022. As one of Indiana’s largest producers of teachers, IU acted swiftly to align our programs with science of reading practices, ensuring our graduates enter classrooms prepared to meet the needs of every student. The Science of Reading Act will further support this work and inspire a new generation of confident readers.”

– Leah Michele Nellis, Assistant Vice President for School Partnerships, Indiana University

“We appreciate Representatives Houchin, Mannion, and Kiley for their leadership on the Science of Reading Act of 2026 and for engaging Save the Children on this important effort. Every child deserves the opportunity to become a confident reader. This legislation is an important step toward closing literacy gaps by promoting evidence-based instruction grounded in decades of research. We welcome this investment in early literacy and support continued efforts to ensure children in rural and underserved communities have access to high-quality reading instruction. By equipping educators with proven tools and training, we can help more children develop the foundational skills they need to thrive.”

- ‎Allison Dembeck, Head of Policy, Save the Children

title: Warren, Hoyle, Wyden, Merkley, Ocasio-Cortez, Subramanyam Introduce Bill to Ban the Corporate Practice of Medicine
text:
The Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act would ban corporations and private equity from owning physicians.

The bill is modeled on the landmark Oregon law that physicians have already used to successfully challenge corporate takeovers.

Text of Bill (PDF)|One-Pager (PDF)

Washington, D.C. – Today, Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), and Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), along with Representatives Val Hoyle (D-Ore.), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.), introduced the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act to ban the corporate practice of medicine.

Over 80 percent of doctors in the United States are employed by corporate entities—including private equity firms and insurers—up from 62 percent in 2019. Despite prohibitions on the corporate practice of medicine in over thirty states, private equity firms, insurers, and other corporate entities have exploited legal loopholes that allow them to circumvent these restrictions to the detriment of clinicians and patients.

Management services organizations (MSOs) have become vehicles for exercising corporate control over physicians. MSOs contract with physician practices to handle ostensibly purely administrative tasks, but these actors often challenge the autonomy of acquired physicians once in control. For example, corporate entities often assume control over clinical operations, management and staffing decisions, and billing and coding practices—all of which can exert pressure on physicians to change care delivery.

The Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act ensures health care decisions are made by physicians—not private equity firms, insurance companies, or other corporate actors. The legislation:

Bans the corporate practice of medicine by making it illegal for private equity funds, insurance companies, and other for-profit corporations to own or control medical practices;

Closes the “friendly physician” loophole that has allowed investor-backed corporations to evade state-level bans on the corporate practice of medicine and control medical practices through MSOs;

Prohibits an MSO from controlling a medical practice through a “friendly” or “captive” physician, or by taking over business, administrative, and clinical functions such as hiring and firing, work schedules, compensation, disbursement of revenue or setting of revenue targets, billing practices, contracting, and other services;

Ensures that physicians retain ultimate control of medical practices by requiring that physician owners are meaningfully engaged in providing medical care in the state in which their practice is located; and

Protects physician independence by prohibiting corporate interference with clinical decisions and banning restrictive contract terms, such as non-compete agreements, nondisclosure agreements, and non-disparagement agreements.

“Patients want to know that decisions about their health are being made by their doctors, not by Wall Street investors,” said Senator Warren. “If we’re going to lower costs and un-rig the health care system, we need to stop the corporate takeover of medicine.”

“Billionaire corporations are using sick patients to turn healthy profits, and Americans are fed up,” said Senator Merkley. “In Oregon, we passed one of the most comprehensive corporate practice of medicine laws in the country, standing up for patients and health care providers. It’s time we take on corporate greed in health care at the federal level by passing our Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act, cracking down on these takeovers that are destroying our health care system.”

“Americans want medical decisions to stay between patients and their doctor, not dictated by corporate actors and private equity firms focused on maximizing profits,”said Senator Wyden. “I’m proud of Oregon’s pioneering state law that has been used by doctors to protect their independence, and it’s time to take that model to the federal level. Corporate medicine is making health care more expensive for everyone, and safeguards must be put in place to ensure health care decisions stay in the hands of physicians.”

“80% of doctors in the U.S. are employed by corporate entities, up from 62% in 2019,” said Representative Hoyle. “Healthcare should not be a line item in a spreadsheet. The Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act will ensure proper protections are in place, so our healthcare systems serve the best interests of our patients, not corporations.”

“Americans want medical decisions to stay between patients and their doctors, not dictated solely by the pursuit of maximizing profits. States have passed laws to protect the independence of physicians, and it’s time to take that model to the federal level. Corporate medicine is making health care more expensive for everyone, and safeguards must be put in place to ensure health care decisions stay in the hands of physicians,”?said Representative Subramanyam.

“Across the country, private equity firms and corporate conglomerates are buying up American physician offices. To increase shareholder profits, these entities often cut corners, leading to patients paying more for significantly worse care,” said Representative Ocasio-Cortez. “I’m proud to co-lead the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act to get Wall Street out of Americans’ doctors’ offices and ban predatory noncompete agreements for healthcare workers.”

“With big bipartisan majorities, Oregon passed the strongest ban on the corporate practice of medicine in the country,” Oregon House Majority Leader Ben Bowman said, the author and chief sponsor of Oregon Senate Bill 951 (2025). “Oregon has shown that it’s possible to stand up to corporate profiteering in healthcare and win. Now it’s time to take that fight nationwide.”

The bill is modeled on a landmark law in Oregon that physicians have already used to successfully challenge corporate takeovers in the state. Most recently, Eugene Emergency Physicians beat back efforts by Peace Health to replace local physicians with a private equity-backed staffing company.

This legislation is also supported by Representatives Yassamin Ansari (D-Az.), Yvette Clarke (D-N.Y.), Chris Deluzio (D-Pa.), Maxine Dexter (D-Ore.), Maxwell Frost (D-Fl.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), and Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), and has been endorsed by the American Academy of Emergency Medicine, American Economic Liberties Project (AELP), Coalition for Patient Centered Care, Bull Moose Project, OrthoForum, Alliance of Independent Dentists, Private Equity Stakeholder Project, Center for Health and Democracy, Association for Independent Medicine, OnCARE Alliance, Families USA, Committee to Protect Health Care, and Social Security Works.

"The American Academy of Emergency Medicine (AAEM) believes that local physician ownership of their practice is the best arrangement for the physicians, the medical staff, the hospital and, most importantly, for the patient,” said Vicki Norton, MD, FAAEM, President of the AAEM. “That’s why the AAEM strongly supports The Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act of 2026. The bill would prohibit the corporate practice of medicine and allow physicians to work unencumbered, focusing on patients. There is no greater policy imperative for AAEM than protecting patient safety and quality of care in emergency departments through efforts such as this bill.”

"The Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act will strengthen long-standing bans on the corporate practice of medicine, ensuring clinical decisions are made by licensed professionals sworn to care for patients, not corporations beholden to shareholders," said Emma Freer, Senior Fellow for Health Care at the American Economic Liberties Project. "It's an essential step toward breaking up Big Medicine, which drives costs up, quality down, and independent practitioners out of business."

"States established prohibitions against the corporate practice of medicine a century ago for a simple reason: when corporations start making medical decisions instead of doctors, everyone loses. Care gets worse and more expensive for patients, working conditions get worse for doctors and their staff, and communities lose the unique benefits of high-quality, independent care,"?said Joe Van Wye, Policy Director at Coalition for Patient-Centered Care.?"We commend the sponsors of the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act for introducing today’s legislation, which will enshrine our nation’s strongest and most effective protections against the corporate practice of medicine into federal law for the benefit of all Americans, and hope it is enacted quickly."

"Across America, physician's private practices have been bought up by shadowy corporations and private equity groups with the sole goal of profit. Putting patients first is out — monopolizing local physician services, driving up fees, and shortening hours is in. This has made life worse for Americans across the country. The Bull Moose Project has long sounded the alarm about these shady practices, such as in cancer care. The ‘‘Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act of 2026" can halt these appalling practices once and for all by making it illegal for big corporations to vacuum up private clinics,"said Aiden Buzzetti, President, Bull Moose Project.

"The Association for Independent Medicine strongly supports the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act, and we're grateful to Senators Warren, Wyden, and Merkley and Representatives Hoyle, Subramanyam, and Ocasio-Cortez for championing it. A prohibition is only as strong as its enforcement, and this bill backs its corporate practice of medicine prohibition with three enforcement paths: the FTC, state attorneys general suing on behalf of residents, and physicians themselves through a private right of action with treble damages. That layered enforcement, paired with mandatory divestment, is what gives this bill teeth that earlier CPOM laws have often lacked," said Dr. Marco Fernandez, President and Co-Founder, Association for Independent Medicine.

“Patients are best served when clinical decisions and practice operations remain under the control of licensed healthcare professionals, not private equity firms or management companies whose primary obligation may be to investors,” says Dr. Jill Tanzi, President of the Alliance of Independent Dentists. "The threats posed by corporate consolidation are not unique to medicine; dentists and their patients deserve these same protections. This bill’s protections against corporate control and interference are critical safeguards for both clinicians and patients, and we commend its sponsors for working to protect independent medicine."

“Private equity firms and other corporate investors should not get to decide how doctors practice medicine. When investors dictate staffing levels or how much time doctors can spend with patients, they are directing patient care. Doctors need the authority to make those decisions based on what their patients need. We support the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act and urge Congress to put enforceable limits on corporate control of medical practices,” said Michael Fenne, Senior Policy Coordinator at the Private Equity Stakeholder Project.

“For too long, private corporations have overridden physicians' clinical judgment, prioritizing shareholder returns and profits over patient care. This legislation would end that practice. Patients deserve care decisions made by clinicians, not by investors managing a portfolio. We thank Senators Warren, Wyden, and Merkley and Representatives Hoyle, Subramanyam, and Ocasio-Cortez for introducing this vital legislation and urge Congress to pass it without delay,” said Rachel Madley, PhD, Executive Director, Center for Health and Democracy

"Our health care system is perfectly designed to concentrate wealth and power into corporate entities and increasingly badly designed to actually care for patients. The Oncology Practices of ONCare Alliance are dedicated to helping oncologists remain independent of private equity and other corporate structures that pull needed resources away from patient care into their profit margins," said Barbara McAneny, Co-Chair of the OnCARE Alliance. "We strongly oppose the corporate practice of medicine and commend the sponsors of the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act for introducing this important bill that will help doctors design our practices to make the best treatment plans with our patients."

"As doctors, we have a duty to put the needs of our patients first," said Hugh Bassewitz, M.D., the OrthoForum. "That's much harder when a practice is run by corporate executives focused on increasing returns for their shareholders, not by physicians focused on helping people who need us. We're glad to see Congress acting to help doctors provide patient-centric care, and thank the sponsors for their work on this important legislation."

“This groundbreaking legislation is absolutely needed to give health providers and patients a fighting chance against corporate greed. Congress must stop private equity from ripping the copper wires out of American healthcare and put patients first. Social Security Works is proud to endorse this legislation,” said Alex Lawson, Executive Director, Social Security Works.

title: Hudson-Backed Bill to Keep AM Radio in New Vehicles Passes House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Richard Hudson (NC-09), Chairman of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology, applauded House passage of bipartisan legislation he championed to keep free AM radio available in new vehicles.

“AM radio is about more than what you listen to on the drive home. For millions of Americans, especially folks in rural communities, it is a trusted source for local news, weather, and critical information during emergencies,” said Rep. Hudson. “I’ve pushed hard to keep AM radio available in our cars, and I’m glad the House has finally passed this bipartisan bill.”

Background

The legislation directs the Department of Transportation to require AM radio access as standard equipment in new passenger vehicles. Consumers would not be charged an additional fee to access AM radio.

AM radio continues to play an important role in emergency communications, particularly in rural areas and during hurricanes, tornadoes, wildfires, and other disasters when cellular and internet service can be disrupted. Firefighters, law enforcement officers, sheriffs, emergency medical organizations, and farmers have backed keeping AM radio available in vehicles because of its role in delivering emergency information.

As Chairman of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology, Hudson has continued working with local broadcasters and public safety leaders to preserve access to AM radio for drivers across the country.

Hudson was one of the earliest cosponsors of the legislation and has pushed for its passage throughout the 119th Congress.

title: Huffman Demands Answers After Park Service Quietly Hires Contractors for Trump Golf Course
text:
Contracts were found buried in a federal procurement database days before Congress leaves town; one construction contract worth up to $49 million is forecast for January 2027

Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) revealed during a committee hearing that the National Park Service awarded contracts on Sept. 10, with no notice to Congress, to begin work on Donald Trump’s planned takeover of the East Potomac Golf Course.

“Democrats on this committee just learned that a couple of days ago, the Park Service hired a company to start working on the historic public golf course at East Potomac Park without any announcement, without a word to any of us, without a single public hearing,” said Ranking Member Huffman. “Now, this is not just any old golf course. This is a beloved public space with huge historic significance. […] Donald Trump is systematically moving to take this historic, publicly accessible resource and turn it into another gilded private golf club for the mega-rich. That’s what’s going on here, folks. This is a methodical, deliberate effort to take a public park away from the people. Taxpayers are going to foot the bill to rebuild this golf course to Donald Trump’s specifications. He might even sell it to himself, or just gift it to himself as a trophy, as another tribute to himself on his way out the door of the White House.”

“Congress leaves town today, and I don’t think it’s any coincidence that this is the exact moment the administration has chosen to line up contracts, setting the stage to roll equipment into the park and start tearing up public land for a Trump golf course,” said Ranking Member Huffman. “Democrats on this committee are tracking all of this. We’re going to keep dragging it all into the daylight until the public gets the answers we deserve. We’re not going to let Donald Trump walk off with our public lands. That park belongs to the American people, and I’m not willing to sit here and watch him simply steal it.”

The $389,355 award to Vanasse Hangen Brustlin, Inc. covers environmental and historic preservation compliance work at the course. The Park Service has since posted a forecasted construction contract worth up to $49 million, with a projected solicitation date of Jan. 31, 2027. Together the contracts commit at least $50 million in federal funds, lined up the same week Congress leaves Washington.

The contracts follow months of activity at the park. Recent reports confirm the administration has reached an agreement with Fazio Design and undisclosed private and public partners to begin major construction, and the President has said his goal is to turn the public course into a major championship or Ryder Cup venue. Crews have already cut down more than sixty trees while a court is still deciding whether the project is lawful.

In light of this information, Ranking Member Huffman, House Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), Rep. Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Rep. Don Beyer (D-Va.), and Rep. Glenn Ivey (D-Md.) also sent a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Acting National Park Service Director Jessica Bowron demanding every document, communication, and record on the project.

“East Potomac Park does not belong to Donald Trump,” the lawmakers wrote. “It belongs to the American people, and it has for more than a century.”

The letter also questions the timing of a separate seawall project. The Department left the East Potomac Park seawall crumbling for a decade, then opened procurement for repairs in August 2026 and expanded the funding documents for the Tidal Basin and West Potomac Park to cover additional stretches of the seawall. “But the question is why a project the Department never prioritized has suddenly become urgent at the precise moment separate contracts for Donald Trump’s makeover are going out,” the lawmakers wrote.

“Executed in small pieces, the President’s plans for the course appear designed to evade accountability at the expense of the American taxpayer,” the lawmakers wrote. “We refuse to let this grotesque desecration of public land and waste of American tax-dollars go unaccounted.”

The lawmakers requested all documents and communications since Jan. 20, 2025, on plans, cost estimates and funding sources for the golf course; the forecasted construction contract; the seawall project and its cost estimates; the tree removal; environmental and historic preservation compliance; and any proposed transfer of any part of East Potomac Park to the Trump Organization, Trump Golf Management or any Trump-affiliated entity. They also asked for all communications between the Department or the Park Service and Fazio Golf Designers, Meredith O’Rourke and Abby Matthis of Forward Strategies, the National Garden of American Heroes Foundation, the White House, the Trump Organization, Trump Golf Management and any member of the President’s family.

title: Bipartisan Members of Congress Found Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

September 16, 2026

Contact: Anna Claire Stietenroth

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, September 16, 2026, U.S. Representatives Brian Jack (GA-03), Laura Friedman (CA-30), Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11), and Tom Suozzi (NY-03) founded the bipartisan Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus.

The bipartisan Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus will work to revitalize, strengthen, and expand film production across the United States.

For nearly a century, the United States was the undisputed global leader in film and television production, creating stories that inspired generations of Americans, from Rocky to Top Gun.

However, our nation has lost more than 100,000 film and television production jobs since the industry's 2022 peak, more than a third of the workforce. Last year alone, U.S. productionspending fell 20 percent while the U.K. grew 15 percent and Eastern Europe grew 78 percent.

In recent years, individual state incentives have been outpaced by subsidies offered by foreign countries, leading to an exodus of film production overseas out of the country. No single state can outbid a foreign government on its own. America should be competing for this work at the national level, and American crews, small businesses, and local economies should be the ones who benefit.

Last month, President Donald J. Trump voiced his support for a bipartisan legislative approach to revitalizing the American film industry, posting on Truth Social, “Republicans and Democrats [should] get together, and immediately craft Legislation to save the Movie, Television, and Entertainment Business in America. Congress should approve, immediately, a Federal Production Incentive to create Entertainment Jobs in America.”

The Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus is eager to partner with President Trump and his Administration to educate Members of Congress on the economic and cultural importance of American filmmaking and to propose legislative solutions to address the loss of domestic film production.

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairman Congressman Brian Jack (GA-03) said, “I am honored to co-found and co-chair the Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus. My Congressional District is home to Trilith Studios, and I proudly represent the craftsmen, electricians, and carpenters who work hard to create movies that inspire generations of Americans. I commend President Trump’s leadership in calling for a legislative solution to bring film production back to the United States, and I look forward to working with him and my colleagues in Congress to achieve this important goal.”

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairwoman Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) said, “We're launching this caucus to show that bringing film and television production back to the United States isn't a partisan fight. Film and television work is leaving this country because 65 other nations decided to compete for these hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs. A national film tax credit is how we bring that work home, and this caucus is a key step to build support for it.”

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairman Congressman Nathaniel Moran (TX-01) said, "For too long, we've watched jobs in the film and television industry move overseas to the detriment of local communities across America who were the backbone of American storytelling. The American Film & TV Production Caucus is committed to bringing that production back home—back to our sound stages, our small businesses, our caterers, carpenters, electricians, and camera crews who make this industry run in all of our 50 states. Every production that sets up here ripples out, supporting the businesses around it and pumping money into local communities. We need to keep that going and keep American storytelling in America."

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairwoman Congresswoman Linda Sánchez (CA-38) said, “The film and television industry doesn’t just make the shows and movies we all love. It’s an economic engine that employs 2 million American jobs throughout the United States. I’m proud to help launch this bipartisan caucus to support the workers and small businesses who make this industry run, and to find new ways to maintain those jobs and bring more of them back home.”

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairwoman Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) said, “I am proud to serve as Co-Chair of the Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus and work on a bipartisan basis to strengthen film and television production here at home. Productions like Blue Bloods, Boardwalk Empire, Ray Donovan, Gotham, and Fallout have supported jobs and economic activity in my district, and we must ensure those opportunities remain in the United States. This caucus will focus on supporting American workers, strengthening domestic production, and keeping America the global leader in film and television.”

Caucus Co-Founder and Co-Chairman Congressman Tom Suozzi (NY-03) said, “The film industry is an economic engine in New York, contributing tens of billions of dollars to the state’s economy every year. I'm proud to help launch the Congressional American Film and TV Production Caucus to promote film production in the United States and continue advocating for an industry that supports thousands of jobs and enriches the cultural fabric of my district.”

Congressman Nathaniel Moran, Congresswoman Linda Sánchez, Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis, and Congressman Tom Suozzi are members of the House Committee on Ways and Means, the chief tax-writing committee in Congress.

Congressman Brian Jack serves on the House Committee on Rules, which controls the flow of legislation.

And, Congresswoman Laura Friedman is one of the only credited film producers ever elected to Congress.

Congressional Caucuses, officially known as Congressional Member Organizations, are administered through theHouse Committee on Administration.

title: ICYMI: Rep. Ronny Jackson Highlights Need to Accelerate U.S. Drone Testing
text:
WASHINGTON — In an opinion editorial published by The Defense Post, Representative Ronny Jackson (TX-13) warned that America cannot afford to test and field drone technology at peacetime speed while our adversaries innovate at wartime speed.

In case you missed it…

America Can’t Afford to Test Drones at Peacetime Speed

Defense Post

Rep. Ronny Jackson

15 September 2026

A US Army Apache helicopter goes down near the Strait of Hormuz, reportedly hit by an Iranian drone. The crew is recovered not by another helicopter, but by an unmanned surface vessel — the first time a robotic boat has ever pulled a downed US aircrew from the water. That’s not a preview of future warfare. That’s three months ago.

Small, inexpensive drones are transforming the battlefield. From the trenches of Ukraine to conflicts across the Middle East, they are no longer specialized technologies but essential tools for reconnaissance, targeting, electronic warfare, logistics, and tactical assaults.

Drones costing only a few thousand dollars are destroying equipment worth millions. Our adversaries have recognized this and are adapting rapidly. The United States must do the same.

The Hormuz rescue is a case in point. Rather than relying solely on traditional rescue assets, the US military deployed a Saronic “Corsair” autonomous drone boat to locate and recover the downed crew. The vessel carried the aircrew to safety, where they were recovered by helicopter.

It showed how quickly autonomous systems are moving from experimental technology to operational force multiplier, becoming indispensable tools for combat, logistics, and intelligence collection, and even personnel recovery.

The same technologies will be called on to conduct reconnaissance, deliver supplies, overwhelm enemy defenses, and protect critical infrastructure.

America’s competitors are integrating drones and autonomous systems into every part of military operations. If we want to keep our battlefield advantage, we cannot afford an acquisition and testing system that moves at peacetime speed while adversaries innovate at wartime speed with real-time feedback.

That’s the gap Section 221 of the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act — a provision I led through the House Armed Services Committee — is built to close.

It authorizes the Secretary of War to establish dedicated test and training corridors for small unmanned aerial systems (UAS), where operators can run realistic electronic warfare and high-energy scenarios instead of sanitized lab conditions.

It also directs the Department to identify the regulatory barriers slowing that testing down. In practice, that means operators can troubleshoot, add new payloads, and develop new tactics against real conditions before a system ever reaches a unit rather than discovering its limits in combat. Without that kind of test and training space, even the most advanced prototype can still fail against a live threat.

The future battlefield will belong to the military that can test, adapt, and field autonomous systems fastest. America must lead that race — not follow it.

America has always maintained its military advantage by anticipating the next battlefield rather than reacting to it. We invested in airpower before others understood its potential. We pioneered precision-guided weapons. We led the world in stealth technology, space capabilities, and networked warfare.

Drone warfare represents the next major evolution in military operations. Through the Pentagon’s Drone Dominance Program, the Department of War is moving to equip combat units with low-cost attack drones and rapidly synchronize counter-UAS efforts across the services.

By 2027, the Department intends to field more than 200,000 lethal, AI-enabled drones as part of this program, with 30,000 already ordered and being delivered now.

Section 221 builds on this momentum by allowing the Department of War to establish the infrastructure and regulatory fast lanes necessary to support the testing and integration of these systems and ensure that enduring technological advantage belongs to the United States.

Our servicemembers should never enter a fight equipped with yesterday’s technology or trained for yesterday’s battlefield. By expanding realistic drone testing, accelerating innovation, and preparing our forces for the fight we’re actually likely to face, we can keep America ready to deter aggression and protect our national security.

The future of warfare is already here. It’s our responsibility to make sure America is prepared for it.

title: Congressman Smith Hosts Annual Academy Day for High School Students
text:
HILLSBORO, Mo. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08), joined by members of the Missouri delegation, recently hosted an Academy Day event at Jefferson College in Hillsboro, where hundreds of high school students and parents came to hear from admissions representatives from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, the U.S. Naval Academy, the U.S. Air Force Academy, and the U.S. Coast Guard Academy.

Congressman Smith said, “Nominating Missouri Students to a U.S. Service Academy is one of my favorite parts of this job because it’s a clear reminder that our rising generation is carrying a strong sense of patriotism as they look to their next chapter. This is especially true across Missouri, as this year’s Academy Day had more attendees than we’ve seen in a long time show up to learn more about how to serve their country.

“Serving in our nation’s military is one of the most admirable things one can do, and attending a U.S. military service academy is a high honor that sets Missouri students up for success throughout their lives. It takes selflessness, discipline, integrity, and most of all, a love for your country. Thank you to all of the students and parents who showed up to learn more about our service academies, and thank you to each of the academy representatives for taking part in this special event.”

Background:

The event was co-sponsored by U.S. Senators Eric Schmitt and Josh Hawley, and U.S. Representatives Ann Wagner (MO-02), Bob Onder (MO-03), and Wesley Bell (MO-01).

Congressman Smith has co-sponsored the annual Academy Day since 2019, and this year’s event saw the highest turnout ever with 275 students, family members, and educators in attendance.

Each member of Congress has the privilege of nominating gifted students each year to attend a service academy.

Selection is based on a review process by the respective service academy evaluating academic performance, extracurricular activities, leadership skills, physical aptitude, and letters of recommendation.

Last year, five of Congressman Smith’s nominees received appointments, and since his election in 2013, 46 students from Missouri’s 8th District have been appointed.

Students can begin applying in the spring semester of their junior year of high school.

For more information on the nomination process or to apply for a service academy nomination, please contact Congressman Smith’s Service Academy Coordinator at donna.hickman@mail.house.gov or all 573-756-9755.

title: Jayapal Statement on Vote for Ratepayer Protection Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) released the following statement after voting for the Ratepayer Protection Act.

“I voted for this bill because there is nothing objectionable in it, and at least it makes slight headway in proposing regulatory standards for data centers to operate and not push costs onto consumers. But I want to be clear: this bill has no teeth to it—it does not require states to do anything. It is merely a suggested standard that states are not required to adopt. It does absolutely nothing to address the very real concerns that voters have around AI, data centers, and the safety and accessibility of their water and air. And importantly, it does nothing to actually hold AI companies responsible for the havoc that they are wreaking on communities across the country.

“Let’s remember that Donald Trump continues to call the threats of AI a ‘hoax’ and that this Administration — right now — has laws that could be enforced against the AI companies to hold them accountable for the threats they have unleashed in surveillance, scraping knowledge, and creating models that could very seriously cause the extinction of the human race, in the words of their own researchers and CEOs.

“We need real solutions to rising costs of energy, like the Energy Bills Relief Act, rather than backroom deals that help to shield big polluters and data centers while doing very little to address the affordability crisis that people are facing. I intend to continue doing that work.”

title: JOINT DEMOCRATIC LEADERSHIP STATEMENT ON H.R. 5334
text:
UPDATE: Termination of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Syrians

On Tuesday, June 25, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration could move forward with its plans to rip legal status away from nearly 350,000 current Haitian and Syrian Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders. Following this decision, the Department of Homeland Security announced the termination of TPS for Haitians and Syrians, effective July 27, 2026.

Individuals who have lost TPS may be impacted in different ways, including loss of protection from deportation and loss of work authorization. However, there may be alternative legal pathways to remain and work in the United States. To learn more about what the end of TPS means for you and your family:

All TPS holders regardless of designation should visit the USCIS website for the latest updates on their TPS status.

Visit the NYC Mayor’s Office of Immigration Affairs website to learn more about what the expiration of TPS status means for impacted New Yorkers. Resource documents are available in English, Arabic, French and Haitian Creole.

Contact the Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA), whose Legal Support Centers offer free, confidential immigration legal help. Free, safe and confidential immigration legal services are available regardless of your immigration status and in your language by calling the MOIA legal support hotline at 800-354-0365 or visiting nyc.gov/knowyourrights.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON HOUSE FLOOR: “WE WILL CONTINUE TO STAND WITH THE UKRAINIAN PEOPLE UNTIL VICTORY IS WON”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries spoke on the House Floor in opposition to legislation that would expand Donald Trump’s authority to impose tariffs and continue his failed global trade war that is making life far too expensive for everyday Americans.

LEADER JEFFRIES: I rise in strong support of the underlying bill to honor the heroic, brave, patriotic Tuskegee Airmen, part of the Greatest Generation, who stood up against fascism, authoritarianism and the forces that were trying to bring about totalitarianism all across Europe and to the rest of the world. We can learn and be inspired by the courage, the character and the conviction of the Tuskegee Airmen. And it’s unfortunate that some in this administration are trying to erase their history. But that history is not just Black history. It’s American history. We will never let it be erased. We must continue to be informed by it, encouraged by it and inspired by it.

As I was thinking about this on the way over—I’m certainly so thankful to Congressman Shomari Figures for his leadership in advancing this legislation and for continuing in every possible way to stand up for his constituents of every race in the great state of Alabama. As I was thinking about the Tuskegee Airmen and the greatest generation who rescued the world from Adolf Hitler, Nazi Germany and fascism, I thought how ironic it is that we’re on the Floor today debating legislation with respect to Russia, Vladimir Putin and their horrific invasion of Ukraine. Now, House Democrats, led by Speaker Pelosi and Leader Hoyer and many others, have been at the forefront of standing up for the people of Ukraine, pushing back against the effort to run them over, pushing back against tyranny and propaganda and the horrors that have been inflicted on them by Vladimir Putin and this war of aggression that Russia has launched.

We will continue to, at all times, stand behind the Ukrainian people, support their courage and their bravery in their fight, an existential one, against Vladimir Putin and Russia. We believe it’s a fight not just for their territorial integrity, but it’s also a battle between the forces of democracy versus the forces of autocracy, the forces of freedom versus the forces of tyranny, the forces of truth versus the forces of propaganda. And the United States of America has always stood on the side of democracy, freedom and truth, which is why we must always continue to stand on the side of the Ukrainian people. And that’s our pledge as House Democrats. We’ve been there with the Ukrainian people from the very beginning. But this legislation that will be before us today, unfortunately, in my view, does not accomplish the objectives that some may, in good faith, in this House or over in the Senate be trying to accomplish.

All of us, I believe, certainly as House Democrats, will continue to stand up for the Ukrainian people. But the manner in which this bill has been written doesn’t require the President of the United States to impose sanctions on Russia. In fact, there are so many loopholes written into the bill, I believe, that it’s very unlikely that the sanctions relief contemplated in the legislation will ever see the light of day. That’s particularly the case because President Trump has shown great reluctance over the 10 years that he’s been in our faces here in the United States of America to actually side with the Ukrainian people. He recently blamed Ukraine for the increase in diesel prices. No, Mr. President, diesel prices have increased because of your reckless and costly war of choice in Iran. He suggested that somehow President Zelenskyy, who has been a brave and courageous wartime leader, and the Ukrainian people have visited the horror, the terror, the war upon themselves. No, one person bears responsibility for it: Vladimir Putin.

Many of us wonder why the President has been so reluctant to aggressively confront the bully of Eastern Europe. One of the things we’ve learned from the Tuskegee Airmen, from the great leaders of that time, from the Greatest Generation, from FDR, from Churchill, is that you have to confront the bully, not appease the bully. So we find ourselves once again, in 2026, just like the Tuskegee Airmen found themselves in the early to mid-1940s in the FDR, Churchill versus Chamberlain moment: you either are going to confront the bully or appease the bully. That’s what Chamberlain did. And when you appease the bully, it doesn’t work out. We learned that lesson, or should have, in 1939. And yet we find ourselves at this moment in time, some, including the highest reaches of the federal government in the executive branch, seemingly more interested in appeasing Vladimir Putin, not confronting him. And that’s why I’ve got real concerns, and I’m not in a position to support this legislation, notwithstanding the fact that I’m proud to represent more Ukrainian Americans than any other Member of Congress in the country back home in South Brooklyn, in Coney Island and in Brighton Beach, an incredible patriotic community.

I say to my constituents: we will continue to stand with the Ukrainian people in Ukraine until victory is won, but this legislation does not provide a path to secure that. Worse yet, what this legislation will do is give Donald Trump perhaps unfettered authority to unleash tariffs on the American people in ways that have already cost everyday Americans thousands of dollars in additional expense per year. Why in the world, in the middle of an affordability crisis that is not a hoax, it’s very real—far too many people in this country, working hard, playing by the rules, can’t thrive, can barely survive in this failed economy. Life way too expensive in the United States of America. Why in the world would this Congress or the People’s House give this President unfettered authority to visit more tariffs on the world that will have an adverse economic impact on the American people? I can’t do it, because I’m standing up for everyday Americans who are suffering in this failed economy with a president who promised to lower costs on day one. Costs haven’t gone down in America. Costs have gone up. And one of the reasons they’ve gone up is because of the Trump Tariffs that have increased costs on everyday Americans. Thousands of additional dollars in expense per year on groceries, on goods, on cars, even on homeownership. And so why in the world would this Congress give this President additional authority to visit that kind of economic harm on the American people?

And so, respectfully, Mr. Speaker, I cannot support the bill…because, substantively, it will not accomplish the objective, which is to stand with the American people, stand with the Ukrainian people, stand with democracy, stand with freedom, stand with truth and push back against tyranny. And this bill at the same time could give the President an additional tool to visit economic harm on the American people. I thank you for yielding. I thank the distinguished gentleman from Alabama for bringing this legislation honoring the Tuskegee Airmen. And at this moment in time, when we see renewed tyranny coming out of Eastern Europe by Vladimir Putin and Russian aggression, let’s summon the courage, the character and the conviction that the Greatest Generation showed and not appease the bully, but confront the bully until victory is won.

Full Floor remarks can be watched here.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES: “WE ARE COMMITTED TO THIS FIGHT FOR AN AFFORDABLE AMERICA UNTIL WE WIN THIS FIGHT FOR THE AMERICAN PEOPLE”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries held a press event with the House Democratic Caucus and advocates on the Capitol steps, where he emphasized that as people continue to struggle with the high cost of living due to failed Republican policies, House Democrats are committed to fighting for an affordable America.

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand here today on the steps of the United States Capitol, alongside Whip Katherine Clark, Dr. Raul Ruiz, Nikema Williams, Yassamin Ansari and distinguished, courageous, fighting Members of the House Democratic Caucus. I want to thank Kat as well as Rebecca from the great state of Arizona, Terri from the great state of Georgia and John from the Great State of Nebraska for bravely sharing your stories and advocating for families, farmers and millions of Americans who are struggling throughout the country.

Far too many people are working hard and playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive and can barely survive. Life is way too expensive. People are drowning in Donald Trump’s failed economy. House Democrats are determined to make life more affordable for the American people. We just need a handful of Republicans to stand up to Donald Trump and join us. Instead, they have decided to cancel votes and run out of town without providing any relief to hardworking American taxpayers.

Republicans have done nothing to lower the high cost of groceries. Nothing to make healthcare more affordable. Nothing to end the reckless war of choice in Iran. Nothing to lower gas prices. Nothing to stop the violent mass deportation machine. Nothing to hold the Trump administration accountable for the unprecedented corruption unleashed on the American people. This is a do-nothing Republican Congress, and it’s about to come to an end.

House Democrats believe that here in America, when you work hard and play by the rules, you should be able to live an affordable life, a comfortable life and a good life. You should be able to own a home, educate your children, see a doctor when you need one, go to the grocery store without being stressed out, take a vacation with your family, save for a rainy day and then retire with grace and dignity. That’s the American Dream. It’s broken right now, but House Democrats are working hard to revive it.

Two years ago, Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans promised to bring down grocery prices on day one. They promised to stop endless wars in the Middle East. They promised to bring energy prices down by 50%. They promised to get gas prices below $2 a gallon. But Republicans have done nothing to make life more affordable for the American people. Instead, they’ve made life more expensive. For two years, Americans have been wondering: were MAGA Republicans lying, indifferent or are they just incompetent? We now have an answer. It’s all of the above.

Democrats know that things need to change dramatically. Our message to the American people is a simple one: we hear you, we see you, we feel you and we’re committed to making life better for you. House Democrats are fighting for an affordable America. House Democrats are fighting to lower the high cost of groceries, gas and housing. House Democrats are fighting to make healthcare affordable because we believe, in this great nation, the wealthiest country in the history of the world, access to high-quality and affordable healthcare can’t simply be a privilege available only to the wealthy, the well-off and the well-connected. Affordable healthcare must be a right available to every single American. We are also here to make clear that it’s time for the corruption to end. Anyone who is stealing from the American people, shortchanging the American people or screwing over the American people, you are now on notice. House Democrats are going to hold the crooks accountable beginning on day one.

Democrats are here. We outside. We are committed to this fight for an affordable America until we win this fight for the American people. We will continue to show up, we will continue to stand up and we will continue to speak up until we end this national nightmare and restore prosperity, peace and the promise of America for everyone.

Fighting for an Affordable America.
