title: House Unanimously Passes Strong Bill to Protect American Agriculture from Terrorist Threats
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, the House of Representatives unanimously passed H.R. 9394, the Civil Preparedness for Agroterrorism Exercise Act of 2026, legislation introduced by Representative Dale Strong (AL-05) to strengthen the nation’s ability to prepare for and respond to acts of agroterrorism.

“America’s agriculture and food supply are critical to both our national security and our economy, and we cannot afford to wait until an attack occurs to determine whether we are prepared,” said Representative Strong. “This legislation will ensure our federal, state, and local partners, first responders, and the private sector are prepared to work together to protect our food supply and respond quickly in the event of an agroterrorism attack. I’m proud to see this commonsense legislation pass the House and move one step closer to becoming law.”

The Civil Preparedness for Agroterrorism Exercise Act directs the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to conduct a nationwide exercise focused on preventing, responding to, recovering from, and mitigating an agroterrorism attack on America’s food and agriculture sector. The exercise will bring together federal, state, local, Tribal, and territorial partners, along with private-sector stakeholders, to identify preparedness gaps and strengthen coordination before a real-world incident occurs.

House Committee on Homeland Security Chairman Andrew Garbarino (NY-02) applauded House passage of the legislation:

“A threat to our nation’s agricultural sector is a threat to every American. Our food supply chain is vital not just to our economy, but to our homeland security. I am proud to join my House colleagues in passing Subcommittee Chairman Strong’s ‘Civil Preparedness for Agroterrorism Exercise Act of 2026’ to ensure DHS is working with state and local partners to stay ahead of our adversaries and defend this critical infrastructure from evolving threats.”

The legislation builds on Strong’s work as Chairman of the Emergency Management and Technology Subcommittee to protect critical infrastructure and improve preparedness for emerging threats, including a two-part hearing series last year examining agroterrorism and threats to America’s food and agriculture sector.

Passage of H.R. 9394 marks the fifth homeland security bill authored by Strong to pass the House during the 119th Congress. The bill now heads to the Senate for consideration.

###

title: Suozzi (D-NY), Knott (R-NC), and over a Dozen National Religious Organizations Urge Passage of Bipartisan, Bicameral Right to Worship Act
text:
Washington, D.C.—Congressman Tom Suozzi (D-NY) today held a press conference with Right to Worship Act co-lead Congressman Brad Knott (R-NC) and supporters from national endorsing organizations to urge the House and Senate to advance the buffer zone legislation this Congress.

The Right to Worship Act would establish a 100-foot, protest-free buffer zone around houses of worship during religious services, making it unlawful to knowingly disrupt or impede people from attending. The bill prohibits conduct that knowingly “hinders,” “deters,” “threatens,” or “intimidates” worshippers trying to enter religious services and would impose civil fines for violations. It authorizes individuals, the U.S. Attorney General, and state attorneys general to sue violators. Peaceful expression protected by the First Amendment is excluded from the bill’s prohibited activities.

“Exercising your right to worship should not require you to exhibit particular courage as you enter your synagogue, church, mosque, temple, mandir, or gurdwara,” said Congressman Suozzi. “I will always stand up for people’s right to protest peacefully, but attendees of religious services should not be harassed, threatened, intimidated, or targeted for practicing their faith. I am proud to lead this bipartisan and bicameral Right to Worship Act that both protects free speech and the freedom to worship.”

“The breadth of support for the Right to Worship Act is very gratifying. So many groups recognize the horrifying reality that the threat to the freedom to worship is not unique to any one faith or congregation. Every religious community feels it, which is why this bill will protect everybody,” Suozzi continued. “I’m proud to stand with such a broad coalition of faith leaders united behind this essential legislation to safeguard the right to worship for every religious community on Long Island, in Queens, and across America.”

“Whether you’re in conservative America, liberal America, red America, or blue America, our Constitution considers your individual right to worship as you see fit. In every corner of this country, that right is being threatened. If people in the United States cannot worship, we do not have a First Amendment. And the right to worship is under attack,” said Congressman Brad Knott (R-NC). “I commend Representative Suozzi for his monumental effort in assembling this team behind us and across the country that was so valuable in crafting this legislation that protects the rights of people who want to speak and protest peacefully. And it protects the rights of those who want to worship.”

Congressman Suozzi’s Right to Worship Act follows his earlier introduction of the SACRED Act in April 2026. Suozzi worked with colleagues in both parties and chambers to build bipartisan, bicameral support for his buffer zone legislation, introducing the Right to Worship Act in the House with Congressman Brad Knott (R-NC) last month alongside a companion measure in the Senate by Senators Cruz (R-TX) and Slotkin (D-MI). Suozzi also expanded the coalition of organizations supporting the legislation, securing the endorsement of more than 30 national groups across faiths for the Right to Worship Act.

Congressman Suozzi and Congressman Knott were joined by representatives from Anti-Defamation League, National Association of Evangelicals, Jewish Federations of North America, American Muslim and Multifaith Women's Empowerment Council, Hindu American Foundation, UNITED SIKHS, American Jewish Committee, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Orthodox Union, Coalition of Hindus of North America, Hadassah, Agudath Israel of America, StandWithUs, and Combat Antisemitism Movement.

“No one should have to push through a hostile crowd or shout over a bullhorn in an attempt to pray. ADL has championed safe worship zone legislation from the beginning, working hand in hand with lawmakers and other key stakeholders to build support and consensus around a critical bipartisan solution. The Right to Worship Act is the product of that work. We are grateful to Senators Cruz and Slotkin and Representatives Knott and Suozzi for their commitment to ensuring everyone, regardless of their faith, can worship freely and safely,” said Jonathan Greenblatt, CEO of ADL.

“Guaranteeing the right for all citizens to worship and freely practice their faith without fear or intimidation is one of the greatest achievements of our nation. Representatives Brad Knott and Tom Suozzi, and Senators Ted Cruz and Elissa Slotkin are to be commended for their proactive leadership to protect this precious blessing for current and future generations,” said Galen Carey, Vice President of Government Relations for the National Association of Evangelicals.

“According to American Jewish Committee’s (AJC) State of Antisemitism in America 2025 Report, 28% of American Jews say that at least one Jewish institution they are affiliated with has been a target of antisemitic incidents in the last five years, and 55% of American Jews altered their behavior in the past year out of fear of antisemitism. At a time of rising threats against Jewish institutions, we applaud Representatives Knott and Suozzi for introducing the bipartisan Right to Worship Act to ensure safe access to houses of worship,” said Ted Deutch, CEO of American Jewish Committee.

“Every community deserves to gather safely in their house of worship. Too often, we've seen Jewish Americans and other faith communities targeted or intimidated simply for practicing their faith. The Right to Worship Act gives law enforcement and communities the tools they need to prevent these disruptions before they escalate, while still respecting every American's First Amendment rights. Safety and religious freedom aren't in tension; this bill shows how we can protect both,” said Hon. Eric D. Fingerhut, President and CEO of Jewish Federations of North America.

“As an American Muslim, I believe religious freedom is the birthright of every American. No one—Jewish, Christian, Muslim, Hindu, Sikh, or of any other faith—should ever be intimidated or afraid simply for entering a house of worship. The Right to Worship Act affirms that protecting people while they pray is not a partisan issue; it is an American responsibility,” said Anila Ali, President and CEO of American Muslim and Multifaith Women's Empowerment Council (AMMWEC).

"The Hindu American community commends Representative Tom Suozzi (D-NY) for his bipartisan leadership in spearheading the Right to Worship Act, which is a critical step in safeguarding our places of worship. In recent years, we have seen a disturbing rise in the harassment of devotees and disruption of services at Hindu mandirs across America, which has deeply shaken the sense of safety for our families and devotees. By making it unlawful to intentionally disrupt or harass individuals within 100 feet of a religious establishment and establishing civil penalties, this legislation ensures that our mandirs remain the sacred spaces of peace and community they are meant to be. No American should have to exercise their First Amendment right to pray under the shadow of intimidation or fear,” said Suhag Shukla, Esq., Executive Director at the Hindu American Foundation.

“Protecting religious freedom and protecting freedom of expression are not mutually exclusive. Both are essential to a free, diverse, and democratic society. The right to worship freely and the right to express oneself freely go together,” said Gurvinder Singh Gill, International Aid Director of UNITED SIKHS.

“BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha welcomes the bipartisan Right to Worship Act, which will help protect houses of worship, including Hindu mandirs, from disruption and intimidation. Four of our mandirs have been vandalized in recent years, and a family should never have to think twice before walking through the door of a house of worship. We are grateful to Representatives Knott and Suozzi for their leadership on this; protecting worship is a fundamentally American issue,” said Mukesh Swaroop, Director of Government Relations for BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

“Tom Suozzi has been an outstanding leader in fighting antisemitism, supporting Israel and standing with American Jewry. His work with Congressman Knott to protect our right to worship is exactly the kind of bipartisan leadership we need. There is no greater friend to the Jewish community than Tom Suozzi,” said Nathan Diament, Executive Director of Advocacy of the Union of Orthodox Jewish Congregations of America (Orthodox Union).

"Few rights are as cherished in America as our freedom to practice the religion of our choosing. But for the American Hindu community that foundational right has felt challenged as more than a dozen temples across the country have faced physical desecration. Since 2022, Hindu temples have seen multiple acts of vandalism, threats and in one case, gunfire, while devotees were inside the temple. These repeated incidents of harassment send a chilling message to the broader Hindu community—s--shattering the sense of solace that should embody a place or worship. Coming amid rising Hinduphobia in the country, this has led to serious concerns among American Hindus about basic security. Thank you, Congressman Tom Souzzi and Congressman Brad Knott, for introducing the Right to Worship Act. This a much-needed step to help ensure that devotees of every faith can visit their places of worship and pray without fear of being targeted or intimidated for simply exercising their First Amendment rights. We appreciate Rep. Suozzi for supporting our community in past years when our temples in New York came under attack, and for responding to our concerns,” said Hitesh Trivedi, COO and NJ Chapter Director of Coalition of Hindus of North America.

"Hadassah has heard from women across the country who have said they are afraid to worship at their synagogues and when they do they spend much of the time anxiously watching the doors for signs of danger. Many of them have been verbally accosted on their way to and from services. We are grateful to Senators Cruz and Slotkin and Representatives Knott and Suozzi for their leadership in introducing the bipartisan Right to Worship Act to address this critical issue. The legislation would establish a 100-foot ‘protection zone’ outside houses of worship and prohibit conduct that impedes entry or disrupts services. We urge Congress to advance this legislation as quickly as possible. Americans should never feel unsafe when practicing their faith,” said Carol Ann Schwartz, National President of Hadassah.

“Religious liberty cannot exist only on paper. It must exist in practice. Because the freedom to worship means very little without the freedom to worship without fear,” said Rabbi Yossie Charner, Director of Congressional Affairs at Agudath Israel of America.

“StandWithUs spends much of its time defending the First Amendment, which protects both the right to speak and the right to worship. It does not ask Americans to choose between them, and neither does this bill. The Right to Worship Act draws a clear and narrow line: say what you want, but you may not drown out a religious service or frighten a family away from the door. We are grateful to Congressman Suozzi, Congressman Knott, and Senators Cruz and Slotkin for this bipartisan bill that protects both parts of our first freedom, and we urge Congress to pass it this year,” said Hadas Alterman, Director of Legislative Strategy at StandWithUs.

“America was founded by individuals who came seeking religious freedom. The right to worship, free from harassment and discrimination, was paramount. More recently, however, in America, harassers have been emboldened, while the faithful have been abandoned. This is particularly true for Jews in America who, in the aftermath of October 7th, have had to endure violent threats and intimidating harassment just to enter synagogues to practice their faith and gather as a community. The Right to Worship Act protects two First Amendment rights – to speech and to the free exercise of religion. By balancing both of these rights, the bill ensures that Jews, and members of all faiths, are able to worship and study in peace. We commend Representatives Suozzi and Knott and Senators Cruz and Slotkin for their bipartisan leadership and look forward to Congress swiftly advancing this common-sense measure into law,” said Alyza Lewin, President of US Affairs at Combat Antisemitism Movement.

title: PASSED COMMITTEE: Lee, Horsford Bipartisan Bill to Restore Full Gaming Loss Deduction
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the House Ways and Means Committee passed the FULL HOUSE Act, led by Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) and Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04). The legislation would restore the long-standing rule allowing the full deduction of gaming losses against winnings.

“Last summer, Republicans limited the gambling loss deduction in their so-called Big Beautiful Bill to help pay for tax cuts for the wealthy. Meanwhile, our workers and small businesses pay the price. Nevadans have been clear: you shouldn’t pay taxes on money you never earned — that’s exactly why we fought to reverse this harmful provision,” said Congresswoman Susie Lee. “I’m glad to see our fix pass out of the House Ways and Means Committee and move one step closer to the finish line. Rest assured, we won’t stop fighting until it’s signed into law.”

For decades, the Internal Revenue Code allowed taxpayers to deduct gaming losses up to the full amount of winnings. However, a last-minute provision in Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act reduced that deduction to 90%, forcing people to pay taxes on money they never actually earned. This change threatens Nevada’s gaming industry, tourism sector, and broader economic activity. The FULL HOUSE Act restores the original law, allowing losses from wagering transactions to be deducted in full, ensuring tax liability reflects actual economic reality.

title: Rep. Sykes Announces $175,000 Grant for Akron Canton Regional Airport Authority
text:
CANTON, OH — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced that the Akron-Canton Regional Airport Authority will receive $175,000 in federal funding through the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) FY26 Airport Improvement Program.

The grant will fund the acquisition of 35 new vehicle movement area transponders, bringing the airport into conformity with current federal safety standards. Vehicle movement area transponders track ground vehicles operating on runways, taxiways, and other restricted airfield surfaces, giving air traffic controllers real-time visibility into airfield activity and reducing the risk of runway incursions.

The funding comes through the FAA's Airport Improvement Program, which provides federal grants to public-use airports for projects related to safety, capacity, and infrastructure. Akron-Canton Regional Airport serves as a key transportation and economic hub for Summit and Stark counties, supporting commercial passenger service, cargo operations, and general aviation.

“This federal investment in Akron-Canton Airport strengthens safety for everyone who works and travels through the airport. I'm proud to have helped secure this funding, and I'll keep working to bring resources home to Ohio's 13th District,” said Congresswoman Sykes. “Every dollar we bring home for projects like this one means a safer, stronger airport for the families and businesses that depend on it.”

“We are grateful to Congresswoman Sykes for her continued commitment to aviation and for helping secure this Airport Improvement Program grant,” said Ren Camacho, President and CEO of the Akron-Canton Airport. “This funding will allow CAK to equip our airfield vehicles with Vehicle Movement Area Transponders, adding another important layer of safety by improving visibility and situational awareness across the airfield.”

This announcement follows Congresswoman Sykes' ongoing efforts to secure federal infrastructure funding for Ohio's 13th District, including previous investments in transportation, aviation, and public safety projects across Summit, Stark, and Portage counties.

title: Rep. Sykes Votes Yes on War Powers Resolution for Sixth Time, Demands President Trump End Unauthorized Iran War
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – For the sixth time, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) voted in favor of a war powers resolution directing the withdrawal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran.

Seven months after President Trump launched unauthorized military strikes, Rep. Sykes continues to demand an end to the war with Iran that has cost American service members their lives and placed additional financial strain on families already struggling to make ends meet.

“President Trump rushed our country into another endless war without a vote from Congress, without a clear plan to bring it to an end, and without answering to the American people,” said Rep. Sykes. “Eighteen service members have already been killed, and hundreds more have been wounded because of this reckless decision. This war has already cost American taxpayers billions of dollars, and President Trump is asking for billions more to continue a conflict he cannot explain and a strategy he cannot defend. Meanwhile, families in Ohio’s 13th Congressional District and across the country are feeling the strain as costs continue to rise and their budgets get tighter. The American people deserve answers, and Congress must act to end this unauthorized war.”

The resolution passed the House and now goes to the Senate for consideration.

title: Congressman Taylor Votes to Shield Ohioans from Rising Data Center Energy Costs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Dave Taylor (OH-02) released the following statement on today’s passage of H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act. This bill would establish a federal standard for protecting American consumers from surging energy costs resulting from local large-load electricity users like AI data centers.

“Ohio is rapidly emerging as a national hub for digital infrastructure, and Buckeye families should not have to bear rising energy costs resulting from local data center development,” said Congressman Taylor. “Today, I was proud to vote in support of the Ratepayer Protection Act to ensure data centers pay their fair share and shield consumers from soaring prices. Winning the AI race against adversaries like China should not come at the expense of Americans’ pocketbooks, and I encourage local, state, and federal officials to continue working collaboratively to enhance transparency in the development process, establish Ohio as a national energy leader, and ensure our state remains an affordable place to live and raise a family for generations to come.”

The bill text of the Ratepayer Protection Act is available here.

title: Congresswoman Tenney Highlights Fort Ontario Legislation at House Natural Resources Committee Hearing
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) today highlighted her Fort Ontario Holocaust Refugee Shelter National Historical Park Establishment Act (H.R. 1031) during a House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Federal Lands legislative hearing, where Oswego County Clerk Terry Wilbur, a lifelong resident of Oswego County, testified in support of preserving Fort Ontario’s historic legacy for future generations.

Fort Ontario has played an important role in American history, including during the French and Indian War and the War of 1812. From 1944 to 1946, the site also served as “Safe Haven,” the only refugee shelter established in the United States for victims fleeing the Holocaust, providing refuge to 982 predominantly Jewish refugees escaping Nazi persecution. Tenney’s legislation would bring national recognition and permanent federal support to this history by establishing parts of Fort Ontario within the National Park System. The proposal would preserve the State Historic Site under state management and maintain the central role of the City of Oswego, Oswego County, and local organizations in preserving and interpreting the site.

“Fort Ontario holds a remarkable place in both Oswego County’s history and our nation’s history, and its story deserves to be preserved for generations to come,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “As the number of Holocaust survivors continues to decline, we have a responsibility to ensure the story of the 982 refugees who found safety in Oswego is never forgotten. Today’s hearing is an important step toward giving Fort Ontario the national recognition it deserves. I am especially grateful to Oswego County Clerk Terry Wilbur, a lifelong resident of our community, for bringing Oswego County’s voice to Congress and demonstrating the strong local commitment to protecting this historic site.”

“Fort Ontario is an important part of Oswego County’s history and the story of Jewish refugees who escaped Nazi persecution and found safety here,” said Oswego County Clerk Terry Wilbur. “I was honored to represent our community and testify before the House Natural Resources Subcommittee in support of H.R. 1031. Federal recognition would help preserve their stories, teach future generations about the dangers of antisemitism, and bring national attention to this part of our county’s history. I thank Congresswoman Tenney for her leadership in moving this legislation forward.”

This legislation is supported by the American Jewish Committee, Jewish Federation of North America, Anti Defamation League, Combat Antisemitism Movement, and Zionist Organization for America:

“At a moment when antisemitism is rising and Holocaust knowledge is fading, preserving places of witness is an urgent national responsibility. AJC’s State of Antisemitism in America 2024 Report found that Americans with greater knowledge about the Holocaust are much more likely to recognize antisemitism and to see it as a problem. Fort Ontario is an irreplaceable site of American Holocaust and refugee history, and establishing it as a National Historical Park will both preserve the story of the refugees who sheltered there and help future generations understand the impact of antisemitism. AJC thanks Representatives Tenney and Suozzi for their bipartisan leadership on this initiative,” said Julie Rayman, Senior Vice President of Policy and Political Affairs, American Jewish Committee.

“At a time when firsthand witnesses to the Holocaust are becoming fewer, preserving the places and stories that document this history is increasingly important. Fort Ontario offers future generations a tangible connection to the experiences of Holocaust refugees who found safety on American soil, highlighting the consequences of persecution and the importance of providing refuge to those fleeing it. Jewish Federations of North America are proud to support H.R. 1031 and thank Representatives Claudia Tenney and Tom Suozzi for their leadership in preserving this important chapter of American and Jewish history,” said Eric D. Fingerhut, President and CEO, Jewish Federations of North America.

“Fort Ontario is one of the few remaining places in America that can tell the story of Holocaust survivors’ experience firsthand. As the number of living survivors dwindles and Holocaust denial and distortion spread online, preserving sites like Fort Ontario is essential. ADL strongly supports the passage of H.R. 1031, which would conserve the site for generations to come,” said Lauren Wolman, Senior Director of Government Relations and Strategy, Anti-Defamation League (ADL).

“As antisemitism continues to rise in the United States and around the world, and fewer Holocaust survivors remain to share their stories, we must preserve historical sites like Safe Haven at Fort Ontario for generations to come. The Holocaust Refugee Shelter at Fort Ontario provided sanctuary during one of history’s darkest moments, and it deserves recognition in the National Park System. In 1944, Fort Ontario became home to 982 refugees (almost all of whom were Jewish) fleeing Nazi persecution and the horrors of the Holocaust. Designating it a National Historical Park will ensure future generations encounter this history firsthand, long after the last survivors are gone. The Combat Antisemitism Movement commends Rep. Claudia Tenney for her leadership on the Fort Ontario Holocaust Refugee Shelter National Historical Park Establishment Act and for spearheading this important effort to preserve Fort Ontario’s legacy,” said Alyza D. Lewin, President of U.S. Affairs, Combat Antisemitism Movement (CAM).

“As antisemitism continues to rise in the United States and around the world, and fewer Holocaust survivors remain to share their stories, we must preserve historical sites like Safe Haven at Fort Ontario for generations to come. The Holocaust Refugee Shelter at Fort Ontario provided sanctuary during one of history’s darkest moments, and it deserves recognition in the National Park System. In 1944, Fort Ontario became home to 982 refugees (almost all of whom were Jewish) fleeing Nazi persecution and the horrors of the Holocaust. Designating it a National Historical Park will ensure future generations encounter this history firsthand, long after the last survivors are gone. The Combat Antisemitism Movement commends Rep. Claudia Tenney for her leadership on the Fort Ontario Holocaust Refugee Shelter National Historical Park Establishment Act and for spearheading this important effort to preserve Fort Ontario’s legacy,” said Morton A. Klein, President, Zionist Organization of America (ZOA).

title: Representatives Shri Thanedar, Bonnie Watson Coleman Introduce Legislation to Strengthen ICE Reporting Standards
text:
Washington, DC - Yesterday, Representative Shri Thanedar and Representative Bonnie Watson Coleman introduced the No ICE Deaths in the Dark Act, comprehensive legislation that will ensure that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) reports quickly and transparently on any deaths that occur in ICE custody. In a reversal from previous policy, ICE is no longer required to report certain deaths that occur within 30 days after release from custody, even when ICE detention or release conditions may have contributed to the death. This legislation would codify Biden-era reporting rules that required full reporting on these and all other deaths in ICE custody.

“Since President Trump took office, ICE has gotten out of control, detaining a record number of Americans in horrific conditions,” said Representative Shri Thanedar. “It is beyond unacceptable that detainees are dying in custody and ICE is refusing to report their deaths. I’m proud to introduce this necessary legislation with Representative Bonnie Watson Coleman to ensure ICE finally acts with the transparency the American people deserve and to protect the lives of those in detention centers.”

“ICE has had free reign to attack people in front of cameras, so it’s imperative we demand to see what is going on behind closed doors,” said Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman. “Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, one of my constituents, was denied medical care and died in ICE custody. How many other detainees have suffered from medical neglect while in custody, only to die once released? These people deserve justice too.”

This legislation is co-sponsored by Representatives Steve Cohen, Herb Conaway, Jasmine Crockett, Danny K. Davis, Veronica Escobar, Adriano Espaillat, Jesus G. “Chuy” Garcia, Dan Goldman, Al Green, Hank Johnson, Betty McCollum, LaMonica McIver, Analilia Mejia, Seth Moulton, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Jan Schakowsky, Bennie G. Thompson, Rashida Tlaib, and Mike Quigley. It has also been endorsed by the following organizations: Asian Americans Advancing Justice, Coalition on Human Needs, Emgage Action, ICE Out of NJ Collective, Make the Road NJ, New Jersey Alliance for Immigrant Justice, Public Citizen, and the Vera Institute of Justice.

The full text of the legislation can be seen here.

Congressman Shri Thanedar proudly represents Michigan's 13th Congressional District, which includes Detroit, Downriver, and the Grosse Pointes. As a champion for working families, Shri is committed to advancing economic opportunities, education, healthcare access, and entrepreneurship for underserved communities. Drawing from his journey from poverty to success, he works tirelessly to uplift Metro Detroit, ensuring every resident has the resources and support they need to thrive.

title: Thompson, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Strengthen Medicare Payments for Community Health Centers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.), Michael Rulli (R-Ohio), Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.), Dave Taylor (R-Ohio), Troy Carter (D-La.), Gus Bilirakis (R-Fla.), Greg Landsman (D-Ohio), August Pfluger (R-Texas), Nanette Barragán (D-Calif.), Jill Tokuda (D-Hawaii) and Lori Trahan (D-MA) introduced the bipartisan Community Health Center Reforms Enabling Better Access for Seniors and Elders Act, or the CHC REBASE Act.

This legislation will modernize how Medicare pays for Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and ensures seniors and underserved patients can continue accessing the care they need close to home.

“Primary care today often includes telehealth visits, remote patient monitoring, and other advancements in healthcare that did not exist 12 years ago when this policy was last reviewed,” Rep. Thompson said. “I am proud to support this bipartisan legislation that accounts for these updates, establishes Medicare payment parity for Federally Qualified Health Centers, and updates health centers’ payment methodology. Seniors in rural areas should have access to comprehensive primary care regardless of where they reside.”

"Community health centers are the backbone of rural healthcare in Ohio's 6th District," Rep. Rulli said. "In communities across Eastern Ohio, they are often the only option families and seniors have. The federal government should be making it easier to keep those doors open, not harder. This bill brings the payment system into the real world and establishes telehealth parity for services that our rural communities depend on. It is commonsense legislation that puts patients first."

"Community Health Centers are an invaluable resource for Medicare patients, providing low-cost and accessible primary care in underserved locations. This bipartisan bill will fill a growing gap in the Medicare reimbursement process to keep these centers both affordable and efficient. I believe every American has a right to quality healthcare, and this bill pushes us closer to that goal," Rep. Dingell said.

“LA-02’s 18 Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) serve around 250,000 patients," Rep. Carter said. “As more seniors turn to Federally Qualified Health Centers for primary care, we must ensure that these centers are modernized, accessible, and do not face unnecessary burdens to providing care. This bill would take critical steps to strengthen and update the financial infrastructure of our FQHCs - which has not been updated in years - and provide these critical safety net providers with the support and resources they need to keep their doors open and continue connecting communities and seniors to care.”

“Community Health Centers (CHCs) provide comprehensive primary care that improves outcomes and saves taxpayer dollars, serving over 4 million seniors in 2025 alone. Yet Medicare's reimbursement policy for CHCs has not kept pace with new innovations in care delivery. This makes it difficult for CHCs to serve the patients who rely on them, especially in rural areas where Medicare is an important payor. The CHC REBASE Act would modernize CHCs' Medicare reimbursement, reduce red tape so seniors can choose Medicare Advantage coverage while keeping their trusted CHC provider, and protect seniors' access to telehealth by providing payment parity. The National Association of Community Health Centers (NACHC) thanks Representatives Rulli, Dingell, and other bipartisan leaders for championing this important legislation," said Kyu Rhee, MD, MPP, President and CEO of NACHC.

"Our community health center members see every day how outdated Medicare payment policies make it harder for community health centers to meet the needs of a growing population of older adults,” said Amanda Pears Kelly, CEO of Advocates for Community Health. “The CHC REBASE Act addresses the real challenges health centers face by modernizing Medicare reimbursement, protecting telehealth access and improving the Medicare Advantage wraparound payment process. These practical reforms will help our members continue providing seniors, especially those in rural and underserved communities, with the comprehensive, high-quality care they deserve.”

Federally Qualified Health Centers are often the first and only point of care for millions of Americans, including seniors, rural residents, and low-income families. Yet the Medicare payment system that reimburses these centers has not kept pace with the real cost of delivering care. The CHC REBASE Act fixes that by outlining a process to update the Protective Payment System bundle of services, establishing telehealth parity, and closing gaps in Medicare Advantage coverage for patients at FQHCs.

title: Rep. Dina Titus Fix for Gambling Loss Deduction Passes Out of Committee
text:
WASHINGTON – Today Congresswoman Dina Titus’s provision restoring the 100 percent tax deduction on gambling losses passed out of committee. She is now urging House leadership to expeditiously bring her fix to the floor.

“After 14 months of fighting to get this commonsense, bipartisan fix through committee, we must now encourage the House to approve this measure before Jan. 1, 2027. This would stop the reduction to 90 percent from taking effect and ensure gamblers across the nation do not pay this tax on phantom money they never won,” Congresswoman Titus said. “Altering the tax code was a ruse in the One, Big, Beautiful Bill at the expense of recreational and professional gamblers. As I have said many times, it must be fixed.”

Congresswoman Titus was the first member of Congress to recognize the injustice of ending the full deduction and introduced her bipartisan FAIR BET Act on July 7, 2025, to correct it. Since then, other measures have been introduced mirroring the language in her bill. The House Ways and Means Committee included one of those measures today in approving H.R. 10357, the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act.

“I am disappointed it took the House committee so long to take action,” Congresswoman Titus said. “I spoke at a Ways and Means Committee field hearing in Las Vegas in July 2025 to bring the consequences of reducing the deduction to their attention. Over the next several months, I wrote letters to the committee urging it to include the fix in an upcoming package. Nothing happened until now, when the House will be out of session until after the election. The Republican House leadership must bring this provision to the floor, and the Senate must also expeditiously pass it if we are to prevent the tax from taking effect and harming gamblers nationwide.”

The FAIR BET Act, which has bipartisan support from 25 co-sponsors, also has backing from the

American Gaming Association, MGM, Draft Kings, FanDuel, Caesars, Wynn, the Nevada Resort Association, and the National Thoroughbred Racing Association. In addition, there has been an outpouring of support for the legislation by gamblers on social media.

title: Rep. Dina Titus Introduces Legislation for More Transparency and Environmental Review of Data Centers on Federal Land
text:
Congresswoman Titus today introduced the Public Lands Accountability Act to ensure the public has a say in the federal permitting process for data centers on public lands and environmental effects are thoroughly evaluated.

“Data centers are proliferating in Nevada and other states having large expanses of federal land,” Congresswoman Titus said. “We need to make sure the public’s voice is heard and that the effects on the environment, water resources and the electric grid are thoroughly assessed and made public.”

A data center has been proposed in Boulder City, Nevada, and would be the first data center in the nation built on BLM land.

“How this project is handled will have immense consequences for data center development in Nevada and beyond,” Congresswoman Titus said, noting there are currently 76 data center projects in Nevada in place or being proposed. “The public should be involved and the environment should be protected.”

Congresswoman Titus’s legislation prevents a federal agency from amending any existing right-of-way permits on BLM land to allow the construction of a data center without going through a new environmental permitting process. As part of the environmental permitting process for proposed data centers on BLM land, the bill requires that the BLM consider the impact of the project on regional water supply. It also requires a data center developer to submit a workforce plan detailing how many local jobs the project will create and whether these jobs will pay prevailing wages.

The bill explicitly prohibits data center projects on public lands from being eligible for categorical exclusions under the National Environmental Permitting Act (NEPA) process, closing potential loopholes that could allow the federal administration to skirt environmental review. The Trump administration is aggressively pushing for the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers through executive actions.

On June 26, 2026, BLM’s Las Vegas Field Office quietly approved an application to amend an existing Right-of-Way (ROW) grant held by Townsite Solar 2, LLC. The original ROW grant authorized Townsite Solar 2, LLC to construct a 19 MW solar photovoltaic power generating facility with battery storage on an 80-acre parcel. The revised ROW grant that BLM approved allows Townsite Solar 2 to construct and operate a data center on the BLM parcel. BLM approved the application for the data center project without conducting a new environmental review or gathering community input, despite the fact the project scope had significantly changed.

Boulder City residents raised concerns about the potential impact of the project on dwindling water resources, extreme heat, and grid resilience, among other environmental concerns and filed an appeal with the BLM. On Sept. 1, 2026, Administrative Judge David Gunter granted a stay halting the data enter development, saying in his ruling, "Appellants have made a persuasive showing that BLM violated NEPA and acted arbitrarily or capriciously when it determined that the data center project is 'substantially the same' as the solar plant project for purposes of its NEPA analysis."

title: Congresswoman Dina Titus Secures Several Water Wins in the Water Resources Development Act of 2026
text:
WASHINGTON – The House of Representatives passed the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 to fund the Army Corps of Engineers for the next two years. Congresswoman Dina Titus (NV-01) helped craft this package as a senior member of the House Transportation & Infrastructure Committee. The bill includes provisions proposed by Rep. Dina Titus to strengthen water conservation efforts. It now faces consideration in the Senate.

“The prolonged drought and the shrinking Colorado River make it imperative that we think outside the box and use every tool possible to mitigate our water supply crisis,” Congresswoman Titus said. “This legislation strengthens the ability of the Army Corps of Engineers to protect dwindling water supplies. It includes provisions I championed to create an Office of Water Supply, Water Conservation, and Drought Resilience that would promote water conservation and drought resiliency measures at federal water projects such as those to optimize reservoir storage, support aquifer storage and recharge, and institute nature-based solutions in drought-prone areas.”

Another provision Congresswoman Titus led in the package would direct the Army Corps to consider the impact of data centers on water supply and conservation projects.

“We need to better understand the effects data centers will have on water supplies, particularly in desert areas like Southern Nevada prone to drought,” she said. “Two-thirds of proposed data centers are in drought-prone regions, and over 70 of those are in Nevada. WRDA 2026 will help strengthen transparency about how this influx of data centers will impact the water supply.”

The WRDA 2026 bill also includes provisions championed by Congresswoman Titus to create a pilot program to use natural infrastructure in dryland streams in arid and desert regions.

This program will be beneficial in Nevada, where 88 percent of streams are ephemeral, including the Amargosa River which has been labeled one of the most endangered rivers in the United States.

Provisions led by Congresswoman Titus in the legislation are:

· Strengthening the Army Corp’s Focus on Water Supply: Builds upon the provisions in WRDA 2024 intended to elevate water supply issues at the Corps of Engineers by establishing a new Office of Water Supply, Water Conservation, and Drought Resilience. The purpose of the office is to promote water supply, water conservation, and drought resiliency at water resource development projects.

· Drought Resiliency Projects: Establishes two new continuing authorities programs to carry out small-scale projects for drought resiliency and for flood control structure enhancement.

· Dryland Streams Pilot Program: Directs the Army Corp to research and test the effectiveness of natural infrastructure in dryland streams in arid, semi-arid, and drought-prone areas. This will be beneficial in Nevada, where 88 percent of streams are ephemeral, including the Amargosa River which was recently labeled one of America’s most endangered rivers.

· Dam Safety: Reauthorizes the dam safety program through 2031 and includes key changes to give states the flexibility they need to protect communities. This is based on the DAMS Act (H.R.5414), a bill Rep Titus co-lead with Rep Van Drew.

· Truckee River Flood Control Project: Provides needed deauthorizations to ensure continued implementation of the Truckee River Flood Management Project (TRMA). Through this project, the cities of Reno and Sparks, Washoe County, and numerous other stakeholders are working together to reduce the devastating impacts of flooding along the Truckee River in Washoe County, Nevada.

title: Rep. Tokuda Leads Hawaiʻi Congressional Delegation in Demanding USPS Restore Direct Mail Delivery to Rebuilt Lahaina Properties
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Jill N. Tokuda (HI-02) led the Hawaiʻi Congressional Delegation in demanding that the United States Postal Service (USPS) immediately halt its unilateral decision to stop direct home mail delivery for Lahaina families returning to rebuilt properties.

In a joint letter sent to Postmaster General David Steiner, Rep. Tokuda, Senators Brian Schatz (D-HI), Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI), and Representative Ed Case (HI-01), pressed USPS leadership to reverse policies that classify rebuilt properties in Lahaina as "new developments" and subject to centralized delivery to community mailboxes rather than restoring their home delivery. The lawmakers also expressed strong opposition to a feasibility study that could permanently close the Downtown Lahaina Post Office, which has been under emergency suspension since the August 2023 wildfires.

"Lahaina residents are not moving into new subdivisions. They are returning to a historic community and to homes rebuilt on the same properties and at the same delivery points that existed before the fire," the delegation wrote. "Lahaina’s survivors have already borne extraordinary burdens in the aftermath of the wildfires. They should not be expected to shoulder additional burdens, costs, and disruptions resulting from changes to postal services that USPS has failed to adequately communicate, plan for, or implement."

The delegation called on USPS to take immediate corrective steps:

Reverse the classification of rebuilt Lahaina properties as "new developments" and restore pre-disaster direct mail delivery.

Ensure affected residents have reasonable access to mail without additional costs or unnecessary disruptions while permanent delivery arrangements are established.

Disclose full administrative, legal, and operational records detailing why direct delivery was cut before replacement infrastructure was ready.

Explain why the Downtown Lahaina Post Office lease was not renewed, along with USPS’s efforts to secure a new location.

Hold meaningful, accessible public meetings with residents and local businesses before making permanent changes.

The full letter to Postmaster General Steiner is available here.

title: Tonko, Heinrich & Budzinski Introduce Good Energy Jobs Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — U.S. Representatives Paul D. Tonko (NY-20), Nikki Budzinski (IL-13), and U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-NM) today introduced the Good Energy Jobs Act, legislation that would codify labor and community benefit requirements, mandating that financial assistance delivered by the Department of Energy (DOE) supports high-quality jobs, broad community benefits, domestic manufacturing, and investment in small and disadvantaged communities

During the Biden administration, the Department of Energy delivered significant financial assistance contingent on strong labor standards, including support for disadvantaged communities and more. The result was a boom in private sector energy investments, resulting in massive growth in high-quality construction and energy technology manufacturing jobs throughout the county. The Good Energy Jobs Act would build upon this progress.

“I’ve always believed that investing in people and communities is the surest way to strengthen our economy,” Congressman Tonko said. “Our Good Energy Jobs Act takes that principle to heart, building on the successes of our Inflation Reduction Act and Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act with strong labor standards that create good-paying, union jobs and drive community development. Our legislation envisions a future where the Department of Energy isn’t just an ATM for project developers, but a partner in building a more prosperous economy for everyone. I’m thankful to my colleagues for standing with me to introduce this legislation, and urge Congress to join us in advancing this commonsense bill.”

"If we want to build the next generation of American energy infrastructure, we need to empower the union men and women who are going to build it,” Congresswoman Budzinski said. “This legislation ensures that workers are paid family-sustaining wages and have a fair shot at organizing, while also ensuring that projects drive local economic development on the front-end through clear, binding commitments. I’m honored to lead this bill with Congressman Tonko and Ranking Member Heinrich and proud to have the support of so many labor unions who see the impact this bill will have on America's workforce and the communities their members call home.”

“My dad was an IBEW lineman, and he spent his career helping keep the lights on for our community. His union job gave him the ability to provide for our family, buy a home, and give my siblings and me opportunities that neither of my parents had growing up. That's what a good energy job can do: it doesn’t just power our homes and our economy — it can power the American dream,” said Heinrich. “That’s why, when we invest taxpayer dollars in America’s energy future, those investments should create good-paying jobs, strengthen American manufacturing, and deliver real benefits to the communities where projects are built.”

This legislation is endorsed by several of the nation’s leading labor and environmental organizations, including: BlueGreen Alliance, Communications Workers of America; International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART); International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers; International Brotherhood of Teamsters; Iron Workers International; Laborers' International Union of North America; League of Conservation Voters; National Wildlife Federation; ReImagine Appalachia; Sierra Club; and United Steelworkers.

title: Trahan, Beyer Lead Bipartisan Push for House Leaders to Act Immediately on Artificial Intelligence
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (D-MA-03), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, and Congressman Don Beyer (D-VA-07), a member of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee, led a bipartisan group of 10 congressional leaders on Artificial Intelligence (AI) in pressing House leadership to take immediate, urgent action to address risks posed by this rapidly advancing technology. The push came in the wake of the OpenAI agent cyberattacks on Hugging Face and subsequent warnings from leaders and researchers at prominent AI companies about the societal and existential risks posed by unrestrained advances in the technology.

In addition to Trahan and Beyer, the letter was signed by Representatives Jay Obernolte (R-CA-33), Ted Lieu (D-CA-36), Scott Franklin (R-FL-18), Sara Jacobs (D-CA-53), Gabe Amo (D-RI-01), Valerie Foushee (D-NC-04), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01), and Veronica Escobar (D-TX-16).

“We call for your joint leadership on an urgent Congressional response to recent incidents involving advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models that have profound implications for economic and national security. Congress has a singular opportunity to respond swiftly and effectively to these warning shots before true catastrophes occur,” the lawmakers wrote. “Congress must urgently advance legislation to mitigate the risk of more serious incidents, especially those that could threaten critical infrastructure, our financial system, and other institutions that every American depends on.”

“The House of Representatives could and should immediately take up legislation that would strengthen AI oversight, security, and transparency. There currently exist dozens of bipartisan bills that committees of jurisdiction have reported. Members of both parties have also worked in recent months to fast-track bipartisan legislation that is ready to be considered by committees of jurisdiction. We believe these bills should be carefully and urgently advanced through the legislative process,” the lawmakers continued.

A copy of the letter sent today can be accessed HERE.

In July, Trahan and Obernolte introduced the FRONTIER Act, bipartisan legislation that would set the first federal safety rules for the most powerful AI systems, requiring the companies that build them to be transparent about the risks, submit to independent safety reviews, and report dangerous incidents to the government. The proposal has been endorsed by a broad coalition of independent AI safety organizations, industry stakeholders, and others.

###

title: Trahan Votes to Protect Ratepayers from Data Center Price Hikes
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, voted to pass the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act, legislation that gives state utility regulators clear standards to make sure large-load customers, including new data centers or information storage facilities, pay for the infrastructure they need. It requires companies to cover the full cost of any additional grid upgrades over time and provide financial guarantees, protecting ratepayers if a data center scales back its operations or shuts down entirely. Trahan also helped pass the legislation when it was considered in the Energy and Commerce Committee in July.

“Families are being squeezed by rising costs across the board. The last thing they need is a data center driving up their utility bills and making it even harder to make ends meet,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “The Ratepayer Protection Act says that if you build a data center, you pay for the data center, including the infrastructure and utility costs that too often get passed onto residents. Communities across the country have made it clear they aren’t going to tolerate these facilities driving up their utility costs and impacting their quality of life. Congress should build on this progress by codifying Governor Healey’s effort to ensure communities have a real say in if and when these facilities.”

Large scale data centers or information storage facilities that use 100 megawatts or more require extensive cooling systems that are necessary to keep servers from overheating. These cooling systems can account for as much as 40% of a data center's total electricity use. These data centers can use even more electricity during summer months or during heat waves where electric grids are already under strain and electricity is under more demand. Recent studies examining the impact of growing data center demand found that wholesale electricity prices increased by 6% to 29% on average nationwide, with increases of up to 57% in the regions most affected, compared with projected prices without that growth in demand.

“Right now, families across our country are afraid to open up their electric bills. The number keeps climbing, and their paycheck isn't keeping pace. They're doing the math at the kitchen table, wondering what they might have to cut next just to keep the lights on. That fear is real, and too many families have stopped believing that anyone in Washington is listening,” Congresswoman Trahan said when the bill was marked up in the Energy and Commerce Committee in July.

The Ratepayer Protection Act now moves to the Senate for consideration.

title: Representative Tran Votes to Protect Families from Rising Utility Costs Associated with Data Centers
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran’s (CA-45) voted in favor of H.R. 9340, the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act, to protect Americans from the costs of energy and electrical grid upgrades required to build data centers.

“We have a responsibility to be mindful and fully aware of the risks associated with A.I., including rising utility costs for consumers and small business owners. As a former consumer protection attorney, I am deeply concerned that our communities are currently the ones who pay the price for new data centers. The Ratepayer Protection Act protects hardworking families from these costs by ensuring that the data centers are the ones who pay for energy and grid upgrades, not the other way around,” said Representative Tran.

The Ratepayer Protection Act was introduced by Representatives Kathy Castor (D-FL-14) and Gabe Evans (R-CO-08), and passed the House by a vote of 417 - 3. The bill requires state utility regulators to establish policies to ensure that community members don’t pay for the costs of building large-load customers, such as data centers, including building new power generation, transmission lines, and other upgrades.

Representative Tran is committed to safeguarding Southern California families from the negative impacts of Artificial Intelligence. On September 15, Representative Tran joined a letter with over 100 colleagues to Speaker Mike Johnson, requesting that the House stay in session and pursue urgent action to address the catastrophic risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence. On September 16, Representative Tran also helped to introduce the Reverse Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act, a bill to prevent data centers from taking advantage of tax cuts implemented by the Republican-led “One Big Beautiful Bill Act.”

title: Representatives Tran, Williams Celebrate Committee Passage of Bipartisan Bill to Protect Small Businesses from Foreign Threats
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran’s (D-CA-45) announced today the successful advancement of bipartisan legislation to protect small businesses against threats from foreign adversaries. Tran helped introduce H.R. 10329, the Combating Foreign Threats to Main Street Act of 2026, a bill to provide assistance to small businesses facing threats from foreign adversaries, including intellectual property theft, cyberattacks, counterfeit goods, and other threats.

“Small businesses are extremely vulnerable to being targeted by foreign adversaries. It’s no secret that the foreign adversaries, like North Korea and the Chinese Communist Party, are waging an organized global campaign to undercut American influence and steal American intellectual property. To be clear, this bill does not single out any ethnicity or national origin. I will be watching to ensure that the execution of this bill stands in line with its purpose: to protect small businesses because too many lack the legal and cybersecurity resources needed to adequately fight these threats. I’m proud to support this common-sense legislation that connects small businesses to the SBA’s expertise to protect American businesses," said Representative Tran.

Introduced alongside House Small Business Committee Chair Representative Roger Williams (R-TX-25), the bill was reported out of committee unanimously. In particular, the bill requires educational material for small businesses that describes potential threats, identifies best prevention and response practices, and provides government resources for small businesses to effectively respond to threats and protect their bottom lines. It specifically focuses on threats from foreign adversaries, including the People's Republic of China; Cuba; Iran; North Korea; Russia; and the Maduro Regime in Venezuela.

As a former small business owner and Ranking Member of the House Small Business Committee Subcommittee on Oversight, Representative Tran has remained dedicated to uplifting small businesses in Congress. Tran has co-led several bipartisan pieces of legislation, which passed the House with overwhelming majorities, to ensure that small businesses across the country have the resources necessary to succeed:

H.R. 4775, the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Foreign Interference Safeguard Act, introduced alongside Representative Don Bacon (R-NE-02) will extend small businesses’ due diligence programs that identify and mitigate the risk of intellectual property theft by foreign entities like the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).

H.R. 5788, the 504 Program Risk Oversight Act, introduced alongside Representative Jimmy Patronis (R-FL-01), would increase transparency and efficiency in the SBA’s 504 loan program to support small businesses’ continued access to capital;

H.R. 787, the Plain Language in Contracting Act, introduced alongside Representative Nick LaLota (R-NY-01), would require contracting opportunities for small businesses to be written in clear, accessible language;

H.R. 832, the Small Business Advocacy Improvements Act, introduced with Representative Roger Williams (R-TX-25), would ensure that the Office of Advocacy of the Small Business Administration represents the interests of American small businesses before foreign governments, and

H.R. 1642, the Connecting Small Businesses with Career and Technical Education Graduates Act, co-led with Representative Roger Williams, would make it easier for small businesses to recruit and retain a strong workforce of graduates from career and technical education programs.

National security also remains a top priority for Tran. He voted in favor of H.R. 881, the DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act, to safeguard U.S. research and innovation and protect against Chinese intellectual property theft. Representative Tran is also a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee, overseeing the Department of Defense, and serves as Co-Chair of the House Democratic National Security Task Force.

title: Bipartisan TWICE Act Championed by Reps. Carter, Higgins Passes in the House
text:
Today, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA) announced that the bipartisan TWIC Efficiency (TWICE) Act introduced by himself and Congressman Clay Higgins (R-LA), passed in the U.S. House of Representatives. This legislation will improve access to the Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) program by assisting those currently in Federal, State, or local prisons through the TWIC card application process to gain this credential needed for specific transportation sector jobs.

“I am incredibly proud that my colleagues passed the TWICE Act, a bill which I know will have a lasting impact in Louisiana and across the country,” said Rep. Carter. “So many jobs in the United States require a TWIC card just to work behind a secure facility’s gate, and this bill gives returning citizens a fair shot and ensures that workforce training can improve people’s lives.”

“A man’s character shouldn’t be measured by how he falls, it should be measured by how he stands back up. By cutting red tape and streamlining access to the TWIC program, this legislation will address maritime and transportation workforce shortages in the Gulf of America and Louisiana waterways while extending a second chance to formerly incarcerated Americans,” said Rep. Higgins. “I commend Congressman Carter for his leadership on this effort and hope my Senate colleagues will swiftly deliver these reforms to President Trump’s desk.”

Background

The TWICE Act would require the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to:

Develop guidelines to improve returning citizens' access to the TWIC program.

Develop guidelines to assist individuals in custody to pre-apply for TWIC cards and to assist those requesting an appeal or waiver after issuance of a “Preliminary Determination of Ineligibility.”

Provide a briefing to Congress within a year on improvements to access to the TWIC program.

The Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) program was created by the Maritime Transportation Security Act (MTSA) of 2002 as a response to September 11th and extenuating concern over national security. TWIC remains critical to national security by regulating access to maritime facilities and vessels. Across the country, there are 13,825 vessels and 3,270 facilities under MTSA’s jurisdiction. These facilities are often major employment hubs – ports, terminals, factories, refineries, power plants, and more.

TWIC assists in controlling workers’ access, like those involved in the surface transportation of containers in or out of ports or those involved in the construction, maintenance, or operation of adjacent facilities and their associated infrastructure. The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) manages TWIC card applications. In total, 2.3 million Americans have TWIC cards, and about 500,000 Americans enroll per year.

TWIC cards are often required for employment in high-demand professions for which labor is in low supply. Facilities within MTSA’s jurisdiction are critical to the supply chain yet are egregiously affected by labor shortages. Nationally, as of October 2023, there is a 2-million-person gap between job openings and unemployed workers, and the labor participation rate has fallen from 67% in 2000 to 62% today.

Before issuing a TWIC card, TSA will conduct a security threat assessment to determine a person’s eligibility. Applicants with criminal records, depending on the offense, will be temporarily or permanently disqualified from the TWIC program. According to TSA, individuals in the custody of Federal, State, and local prisons are not eligible until after they are released from custody. After, they will receive a “Preliminary Determination of Illegibility” for one-year post-release, regardless of offense. Applicants may appeal a preliminary determination and go through a redress process, and TSA issues a waiver in most circumstances.

Based on a TSA-verified sample, approximately 98% of applicants are issued a TWIC card, including redress cases. However, approximately 62% of applicants do not respond to redress notifications. Only 0.1% of those requesting redress are denied due to TSA standards. The redress process is burdensome and often takes months for TSA to review conviction details, circumstances, and proof of rehabilitation. Assisting applicants with the redress process – and minimizing the number of applicants going through this process – can accelerate hiring, increase the labor pool, and reduce TSA’s administrative burden.

Nearly 30% of American adults have a criminal record, yet adult incarceration nationally has declined by 30% in the past decade. Just in Louisiana, about 13,000 formerly incarcerated persons are released back into communities each year.

The TWICE Act is endorsed by American Trucking Association, American Waterways Operators, American Association of Port Authorities, World Trade Center of New Orleans, Transportation Institute, Center for Employment Opportunities (CEO), GNO Inc., Right on Crime, IMTT, The Cooper Group, Cooper Consolidated, Prison Fellowship, Riverview Boat Store - St. Louis barge company, We Work the Waterways, Central Ohio River Business Association (CORBA), Bayaud Enterprises, Bridgeways, Church World Service, Commercial Drivers License of California, Community Kitchen Pittsburgh, Conservation Corps of Long Beach, First 72+, JOB1 Business & Career Solutions, Justice & Accountability Center of Louisiana, JustUS Coordinating Council, Michigan Collaborative to End Mass Incarceration, National Skills Coalition (NSC), New York Association of Training & Employment Professionals, REDF, Repowered, The Fortune Society, Trade Institute of Pittsburgh, The Los Angeles Regional Reentry Partnership, Valeo Vocation, Jobs for the Future, JustLeadershipUSA, and Reentry Working Group.

title: Turner: House Passage of Russia Sanctions ﻿Increases Pressure on Putin
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Congressman Mike Turner has made it his longstanding mission to impose meaningful economic pressure on Vladimir Putin and force an end to Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine. Today, that effort reached a major milestone as the U.S. House passed the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, bipartisan legislation Turner worked to advance as an original cosponsor. The legislation passed the house 262 to 159, and now moves to the President's desk to be signed into law.

"Today, Congress sent Vladimir Putin a clear message; he cannot outlast Ukraine and the free world. This legislation gives President Trump another powerful tool to target the revenue fueling Russia's war machine, punish those helping Moscow evade sanctions, and increase the pressure on Putin to come to the negotiating table. It also extends critical sanctions against Iran, whose regime has provided significant support for Russia's war against Ukraine," Congressman Turner said.

"Lindsey Graham spent his final months building bipartisan support for this legislation because he understood that the path to peace requires raising the cost of continued aggression for Putin and those financing his war against Ukraine," Turner continues.

"Passing this legislation honors Lindsey's legacy and strengthens America's hand in the pursuit of a durable peace. I was proud to work for this legislation as an original cosponsor, and I am pleased to see Congress carry his work forward."

The legislation imposes sanctions targeting Russian officials, financial institutions, oligarchs, energy interests, and vessels used to evade international sanctions. It also authorizes additional tariffs against major purchasers of Russian oil and gas and countries facilitating sanctions evasion, while providing exceptions and waiver authorities established in the legislation.

The bill also strengthens sanctions targeting Russia's energy sector and extends the Iran Sanctions Act, which restricts investment and other activity supporting Iran's energy sector and its ability to finance malign activities. The broader package is intended to reduce revenues available to Moscow and Tehran and increase the economic consequences for governments and entities supporting Russia's war against Ukraine.

The Senate passed the legislation by an overwhelming bipartisan vote of 86–11 on August 7. Turner joined Congressman Michael McCaul, Congressman Steny Hoyer, and a bipartisan group of House members as an original cosponsor of the House legislation.

title: Congressman Van Drew's PROOF Act Passes House to Crack Down on Fraud in Federal Programs
text:
Washington, DC -Today, Congressman Van Drew announced that H.R. 10326, the Preventing Rip-offs and Obtaining Oversight of Funds (PROOF) Act, has passed through the U.S. House of Representatives. This bill would give federal investigators a direct way to obtain records from states when investigating fraud in programs like the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Medicaid, unemployment benefits, disaster assistance, and other federally funded programs.

"To me, it is simple. If taxpayer money is being stolen, investigators should be able to get the records they need to find out where it went," said Congressman Van Drew. "Right now, that does not always happen. We just saw four states refuse twice to provide SNAP data, to the point where the Justice Department had to take them to court just to get the information. Meanwhile, the states that did cooperate provided data that showed billions of dollars a year going to overpayments and fraud.

"The PROOF Act fixes this problem. If the Attorney General is investigating fraud involving federal taxpayer dollars, the state has to provide the records needed for that investigation. We also made sure there are strong privacy protections in place to ensure that the information is only used for the investigation. Every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar not going to a family, senior, or individual counting on that help. It is our responsibility to make sure that these programs are working as they were intended."
