title: Welch Hosts 2026 Women’s Economic Opportunity Conference
text:
WEOC featured keynote remarks from Vermont Entrepreneur and GameTheory Founder Marguerite Dibble, Senator Welch, and Margaret Cheney, followed by interactive skills-building workshops

RANDOLPH, VT – U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) and his wife, Margaret Cheney, hosted the 2026 Women’s Economic Opportunity Conference this weekend. The event was held at Vermont State University in Randolph, and included interactive workshops on growing economic opportunity, cultivating new audiences, fostering business skills, and more. The conference opened with remarks from Senator Welch and Vermont entrepreneur Marguerite Dibble, who was interviewed by Margaret Cheney.

“In really hard times we have to remember that we have agency, that we can act and that we change things for the better. Just five short decades ago, Gloria Steinem was ridiculed for talking about equal pay and reproductive freedom. Without her fight, it wouldn’t be possible for us to be here today, offering opportunities that help everyone to pursue their dreams and make a difference in their own lives and communities. That’s why, at its heart, the Women’s Economic Opportunity Conference has always been about collective effort in the feminist movement,” said Senator Welch.

“WEOC is so fortunate to have such an amazing network of innovative organizations and hardworking business leaders and dreamers who are committed to supporting not only their own personal growth, but the growth of their communities—it’s what makes this event such a huge success year after year,” the Senator continued. “The message from our keynote speaker, entrepreneur Marguerite Dibble, and Margaret was uplifting and empowering. Through shared goals, we can support one another in these unprecedented times. I’ll continue to champion community-building efforts that help more Vermonters achieve their professional and personal aspirations.”

View photos from the event below:

Vermont’s nearly 25,000 women-owned businesses—which make up 43% of all businesses in Vermont—employ more than 40,000 Vermonters and add nearly $2.5 billion to the state’s revenue.

The Women’s Economic Opportunity Conference was created by former Senator Patrick Leahy and his wife, Marcelle, and has been a Vermont tradition for decades. Senator Welch and his wife, Margaret Cheney, have continued this tradition of bringing Vermonters together to learn, network, and build economic opportunity for Vermonters. The event was held in partnership with the Vermont Women’s Fund and the Vermont Community Foundation.

Interactive workshops included: The One Sentence That Changes How You Show Up; AI Guardrails and Policies That Protect Your Business; Turning Potential into Impact: From Aspiration to Action; The Price Is Right: What Will Customers Actually Pay?; Metalsmithing 101, presented by Generator Makerspace; Invisible No More: How to Get Found in the Age of AI Search; 2026 Women, Work & Wages Report: Using data to advance gender equity in Vermont; Your Business Checkup: Are All the Pieces in Place?; and Scam Prevention Through a Multigenerational Lens: Protecting People & Businesses. Learn more and read the full list here.

Workshop leaders included: Margaret Romney, Dorien Morin-van Dam, Akua Smith, Heather Turner, Veronica Newton, Rachel Donegan, Mimi Damm, Rhoni Basden, Cary Brown, Emily Bush, Tamie-Jo Dickinson, Crystal Baldwin, and Sheri Rockcastle. The closing panel featured Elizabeth Roma, Janet Lee, Kristin McCole and was facilitated by Mercy Connections business leader Ruchi Nadkarni.

Learn more about Senator Welch’s work and upcoming events by visiting his website or by following him on social media.

title: Wyden, Merkley Demand Trump Administration Release Energy Bill Assistance for Low-Income Americans
text:
Key federal heating assistance program targeted for budget, staffing cuts by Trump administration as energy costs soar

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley today said they joined Senate colleagues in urging the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to release all available funds for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) ahead of the November 1, 2026 deadline as cold weather sets in.

LIHEAP is a lifeline that provides financial assistance to low-income homeowners and renters to help cover the cost of energy bills. This program is more important than ever as energy costs continue to skyrocket under Trump’s war in Iran, and cancellation of new wind and solar energy projects.

Donald Trump has repeatedly tried to undermine LIHEAP. Last year, he fired the federal employees overseeing the program. The previous two years, Trump’s budget has zeroed out funding for the program entirely. Earlier this year, legislators appropriated roughly $4 billion in federal LIHEAP funds available for the coming year that must be released no later than November 1, 2026.

“As you know, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (P.L. 119-103) requires the Department of Health and Human Services to distribute no less than 90 percent of its total LIHEAP allotment by November 1, 2026. Given the extraordinary pressure consumers will face this winter, we ask that you make this distribution well before the deadline,” the senators wrote to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert Kennedy, Jr.

Nationwide, an estimated 6 million households received assistance with heating and cooling costs through LIHEAP over the last year, and more households may need heating assistance this winter as temperatures drop while the cost of oil, gas, propane, and other residential fuels rise. Heating oil costs are projected to soar by 31.3 percent this winter, the largest increase among the major heating fuels. Overall, the average U.S. household is projected to spend an average of $1,030 to heat their homes this winter, an 8.7 percent increase over last year.

The letter was led by U.S. Senators Jack Reed, D-R.I., Susan Collins, R-Maine, and Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska. In addition to Wyden and Merkley, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Angela D. Alsobrooks, D-Md., Cory Booker, D-N.J., Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., Chris Coons, D-Del. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., Mark Warner, D-Va., Edward J. Markey, D-Mass., Peter Welch, D-Vt., Angus S. King, Jr., I-Maine, Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., Catherine Cortez Masto, D-N.M., Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., Mazie K. title: Ahead of Xi White House Meeting, Congresswoman Chrissy Houlahan Joins Democratic Veterans in Demanding Trump Hold Beijing Accountable for Providing Key Intelligence to Iran Resulting in U.S. Troop Deaths
text:
On July 17th, an Iranian missile struck a U.S. base in Jordan killing three servicemembers and injuring four others; Wall Street Journal reporting has confirmed that Iran acquired high-resolution satellite imagery of the base – used to carry out the attack – from Chinese entities

Ahead of the September 23rd White House meeting between Trump and Xi, twelve Trump hold Xi accountable for Beijing’s role in U.S. troop deaths

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Chrissy Houlahan and 12 fellow Democratic veterans in Congress called on President Trump to publicly condemn China's support for Iranian forces that are killing U.S. troops, ahead of his White House meeting with President Xi Jinping later this month.

On July 17th, an Iranian missile struck a U.S. base in Jordan killing three servicemembers and injuring four others. Recent reporting from the Wall Street Journal confirms that Iran acquired high-resolution satellite imagery of the base from Chinese entities.

Ahead of the September 23rd White House meeting between Trump and Xi, Houlahan and fellow Democratic veteran colleagues demandTrump hold Xi accountable for Beijing’s role in U.S. troop deaths, and that he publicly condemn China’s support for IRGC operations.

“22 brave Americans have lost their lives in Trump’s war with Iran. We now know that at least three of those deaths directly resulted from President Xi sharing key intelligence about U.S. positions with Iran. Instead of holding China accountable, Trump is rolling out the red carpet,” said Congressman Pat Ryan who led the initiative. “I served 27 months in combat in Iraq as an Army Intelligence Officer – I know just how critical and sensitive this information is, and how dangerous it can become in the wrong hands. What’s worse is that Trump knows, too, and hasn’t done a thing to stop it. He said he thinks Xi has been ‘well behaved.’ We disagree. From intelligence sharing to assistance with weapons manufacturing, President Trump must send a strong clear message to Beijing that aiding the IRGC to kill U.S. troops will not be tolerated.”

The letter to President Trump, sent from Democratic Congresspeople including Houlahan, Pat Ryan, Salud Carbajal, Gilbert Cisneros, Herbert Conaway, Jason Crow, Chris Deluzio, Maggie Goodlander, Ted Lieu, Seth Moulton, Mike Thompson, Derek Tran, and Eugene Vindman – is included here, and in full below:

Dear President Trump,

Ahead of President Xi Jinping’s upcoming visit to the White House, we implore you to use your meeting to strongly condemn China’s sharing of satellite information that resulted in the deaths of three U.S. servicemembers in Jordan on July 17th, and demand that President Xi cease any support, cooperation, and information sharing with Iran and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

On July 17th, an Iranian ballistic missile struck sleeping quarters at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, killing three American soldiers and wounding four others. The Wall Street Journal has since reported that Iran acquired high-resolution satellite imagery of the base from Chinese entities both before and after the attack, intelligence that U.S. officials say was directly connected to the strike that killed our troops.

Your administration knew this coordination was happening. In May, the State Department sanctioned three China-based firms for supplying Iran with satellite imagery of American and allied military facilities. Senior officials in your administration reportedly spent months warning their Chinese counterparts that companies in their country were arming Iran with the targeting data.

The satellite imagery is only one piece of China’s material support to Iran; Chinese firms have supplied key raw materials for the production of Iranian Shaheds, delivered chipmaking equipment to the IRGC, and sold Iran shoulder-launched missile systems, including the weapon that was likely responsible for the downed American F-15E Strike Eagle.

Rather than hold Beijing accountable, you downplayed these findings. When asked aboard Air Force One whether you would raise the issue with President Xi, you told reporters, “I think he’s behaved reasonably well." That is a direct and egregious betrayal of our troops.

Our servicemembers are paying the price in blood for this administration's pathetic refusal to confront Beijing. That must end now. Your meeting with President Xi presents an important opportunity to condemn China's role in arming and enabling Iran, and to demand an end to their support.

As veterans, we know what it means to send Americans into harm's way, and we know what is owed to them in return: the truth, and a Commander-in-Chief willing to hold accountable anyone and everyone who might do harm to our troops.

title: House VAT Chairman Robert Aderholt Calls on China to Release Political Prisoners

title: Alford, Real Estate Caucus Call on Copyright Office to Reconsider Fee Increase for Multiple Listing Services
text:
Congressman Mark Alford (MO-04) led a letter with his Congressional Real Estate Caucus Co-Chairs—Reps. Lou Correa (CA-46), Tracey Mann (KS-01), and Brittany Petersen (CO-07)—to the U.S. Copyright Office. The Real Estate Caucus is urging the Copyright Office to reconsider its fee increase on non-photographic databases, which include many Multiple Listing Services (MLSs).

At a time when high prices driven many hardworking families farther away from the American Dream of homeownership, Congress has made housing affordability a bipartisan priority. Yet, this misguided fee increase would undermine this progress by reducing transparency and increasing costs.

Reps. Ryan Mackenzie (PA-07), Jack Bergman (MI-01), Monica De La Cruz (TX-15), and Jimmy Patronis (FL-01) joined the Real Estate Caucus Co-Chairs in sending the letter.

Read the full letter here or below:

“Dear Register Perlmutter:

“We write as Co-Chairs and members of the Bipartisan Congressional Real Estate Caucus to express our concern with the U.S. Copyright Office's final fee schedule submitted to Congress on July 14, 2026. In particular, the proposal would increase the fee for group registration of updates and revisions to non-photographic databases - the category used by many Multiple Listing Services (MLSs) - from $500 to $700 per filing. This comes only six years after the same fee increased from $85 to $500. We urge the Office to reconsider this additional increase before it takes effect.

“MLSs are a critical part of America's housing market. These organizations maintain the property information used every day by buyers, sellers, real estate professionals, lenders, and appraisers. They are also generally small, local, subscriber-supported organizations, not large corporations that can simply absorb repeated cost increases. Because MLS databases are continuously updated, many MLSs must register multiple times each year to maintain meaningful copyright protection against unauthorized scraping, copying, and misuse.

“The proposed increase is especially difficult to justify because MLSs remain stuck using a more expensive paper-based registration process while nearly all other copyright applicants can file electronically. The Office's own analysis reportedly places the cost of processing an MLS registration at approximately $500, yet the proposed fee is $700. It makes little sense to charge MLSs above the reported cost of providing the service while denying them access to the lower-cost, modern filing system available to other registrants. Local MLSs should not be forced to subsidize a bureaucratic process they cannot avoid or modernization efforts from which they do not yet benefit.

“We support a modern, efficient Copyright Office and recognize the need to recover reasonable costs. But fees should be fair, recover the reasonable cost of the service being provided, and structured to encourage -- not discourage -- copyright registration. Stakeholders have warned that MLS registrations are price sensitive and have already declined as fees have increased. At a time when Americans are facing serious housing affordability challenges, Washington should be looking for ways to reduce unnecessary costs in the housing market, not add to them.

“Accordingly, we respectfully ask the Copyright Office to:

Reconsider or delay the proposed increase from $500 to $700 and explain how that amount is justified when the Office's reported processing cost is approximately $500, including how the fee complies with the fair-and-equitable requirements of 17 U.S.C. § 708(b)(4);

Explain how the Office interprets 17 U.S.C. § 708(b) and H. Rept. 105-25 to permit charging MLS registrants more than the Office's reported cost of processing MLS registrations, and identify the principles the Office applies in determining when and by how much a fee may exceed cost;

Explain why the Office lacks authority to delay or modify the proposed MLS fee increase, despite having done so for other proposed fees in prior proceedings, and explain any legal or procedural constraints that would prevent it from doing so in this case;

Provide a concrete plan and timeline for allowing MLS registrations to be filed electronically, including any technological or administrative barriers that remain; and

Explain how the Office accounted for stakeholder evidence that MLSs are generally small, local organizations, that registrations are price sensitive, and that prior fee increases have already reduced participation.

“Congress has a 120-day review period, through November 12, to approve or disapprove the new fee schedule. During that time, we urge the Office to work with MLS stakeholders on a reasonable alternative that lowers processing costs, expands electronic access, and preserves strong copyright protections without imposing another disproportionate fee increase.

“Please respond within 14 days of receipt of this letter. We appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and look forward to working with you.”

title: After Denial of Emergency Aid for Blizzard, Amo, Friedman Introduce Bill to Stop Trump’s Politicization of Disaster Aid
text:
Washington, DC – Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI-01) and Vice Ranking Member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings, and Emergency Management, Congresswoman Laura Friedman (D-CA-30) introduced the Disaster Relief Fairness Act to prevent the president from maliciously denying disaster assistance to states and communities that meet the criteria to qualify.

The bill comes after Trump denied Rhode Island’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration following the historic February blizzard, despite more than $19 million in direct storm damages, which was more than nine times the threshold required for a declaration. President Trump denied Rhode Island’s request on the same day it approved disaster declarations for several Republican-led states.

During President Trump’s second term, the White House has approved 89% of disaster aid requests from Republican governors and 23% from Democratic governors. These politicized denials negatively impact state, city, and town budgets and property tax rates for residents.

“Our state was battered by record-breaking snow and dangerous power outages last February. Instead of helping Rhode Island recover, Trump is playing politics with disaster aid,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI-01). “Who you voted for should not impact whether or not the federal government steps in to help communities dig out after disaster. I’m proud to work with my delegation colleagues to prevent the President from using disaster assistance as political leverage.”

"When a disaster hits American families, the only question should be how fast help arrives, not how your neighbors voted," said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (D-CA-30). "Angelenos saw it firsthand when this administration turned wildfire relief into a bargaining chip, and states across our country are seeing it now. If the White House gets to pick and choose who recovers, no community in America is safe. Our bill ends that for good and ensures disaster aid is about recovery and nothing else."

This bill is cosponsored by Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR-01), Steve Cohen (D-TN-09), Jim Costa (D-CA-21), Seth Magaziner (D-RI-02), and Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL-25).

Senators Jack Reed and Sheldon Whitehouse lead the Disaster Relief Fairness Act in the Senate.

Background

On February 22–23, 2026, Rhode Island experienced a severe snowstorm that dropped more than three feet of snow in 24 hours in parts of the state. It was the state’s highest one-day snowfall on record. The storm caused widespread power outages, emergency room visits, and disruptions to transportation, utilities, businesses, and public services.

Under current law, disaster requests must be based upon a finding that the situation is beyond the capability of the state and affected local governments or Indian tribal governments. The Disaster Relief Fairness Act would ensure that disaster assistance requests made during Trump’s presidency are approved if they meet FEMA’s established requirements and thresholds.

The denial is part of a broader pattern of Rhode Islanders being forced to fight for the federal support they deserve. Amo pressed the Trump administration over rising energy costs and challenged Energy Secretary Chris Wright over statements to Congress, while continuing to push federal agencies to deliver for Rhode Island.

In July, Amo joined Senators Reed and Whitehouse and Congressman Magaziner in calling on FEMA to explain why Rhode Island’s request for assistance was denied. The lawmakers also urged the state to appeal the decision.

After the state’s appeal was denied in September, the Rhode Island Delegation denounced Trump’s politicization of disaster aid and opened a probe to investigate and expose the Trump administration’s blatant and unwarranted politicization of federal disaster aid.

title: Amo Celebrates the Advancement of Reforms to Strengthen America’s Diplomatic Corps
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – House Foreign Affairs Committee Vice Ranking Member Gabe Amo (D-RI) celebrated the House passage of the Foreign Service Modernization Act, which will strengthen America’s diplomatic corps and give Foreign Service Officers the tools they need to meet today’s national security challenges. Congressman Amo helped secure several key provisions in the legislation and spoke on the House floor in support of the bill. The measures Amo secured inclusion of strengthen training to combat antisemitism and support implementation of the Australia United Kingdom United States (AUKUS) security partnership.

“Our diplomats dedicate their lives to representing the United States abroad, often making tremendous personal sacrifices in service to our country,” said Vice Ranking Member Gabe Amo. “We owe them the training, protections, and support they need to do their jobs. I’m proud to have helped secure provisions that strengthen our diplomatic corps and support our key alliances. Our foreign policy is stronger when we invest in the people who carry it out.”

WATCH HERE: Congressman Amo speaks on House floor in support of bipartisan legislation which includes key provisions he championed to strengthen diplomatic training and support AUKUS

Background

The Foreign Service Modernization Act marks the first comprehensive review of the Foreign Service Act, which codifies personnel matters for Foreign Service Officers, since it was signed into law in 1980.

The legislation would:

Provide Ambassadors with increased authority and oversight in carrying out US foreign policy at their posts overseas,

Create a pilot program for a Diplomatic Reserve Corps, modeling the reserve functions of the armed services, that would surge diplomats to the front lines in response to emergencies and crises abroad,

Enhance expeditionary diplomacy in austere posts to advance American interests outside of the confines of embassy walls,

Align State Department human resources technology and training to meet modern national security demands, and

Increase pathways for military veterans to join the Foreign Service.

Amo championed several provisions included in the final legislation, including:

Strengthening training for Foreign Service Officers to better identify and combat antisemitism.

Helping ensure Foreign Service Officers have access to the trainings and briefings they need to implement the trilateral security partnership with Australia and the United Kingdom.

title: Reed, Whitehouse, Amo Call for Federal Assistance to Help Tiverton Families Following Forever Chemical Water Contamination
text:
Providence, RI – Senators Jack Reed (D-RI) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) called on Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin to move quickly to help support Tiverton families whose private wells have been contaminated with dangerous levels of PFAS, or “forever chemicals.”

In a letter to Administrator Zeldin, the lawmakers wrote:

“We are writing to alert you to an urgent public health matter affecting our constituents in Tiverton, Rhode Island, due to dangerous levels of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in private wells. More than half of the private wells tested to date have exceeded Rhode Island’s 20 parts-per-trillion standard, and testing is still underway. With some wells registering PFAS concentrations above 4,000 parts per trillion, Tiverton families urgently need help accessing safe drinking water and determining the scope and source of this contamination.”

“For these families, the harm is not abstract. They rely on private wells for the water they drink, cook with, bathe in, and use every day. Residents are relying on bottled water and emergency supplies while confronting uncertainty about whether the water in their homes is safe.”

“Tiverton residents should not have to wait for the next round of testing, the next funding cycle, or another agency to determine responsibility before they can have safe water in their homes. The immediate priority of all levels of government must be to protect residents and get clean drinking water to families who need it as quickly as possible.”

The full letter can be found here.

Background

Tiverton is facing elevated levels of PFAS, also known as ‘forever chemicals’, in private wells, threatening residents’ drinking water.

More than half of the private wells tested to date have exceeded Rhode Island’s 20 parts-per-trillion standard, and testing is continuing. Some wells have registered PFAS levels above 4,000 parts per trillion, more than 19,900 times the state standard.

Congressman Amo recently met with Tiverton residents and local leaders to hear directly about the impact of the contamination and discuss the federal resources needed to get families safe drinking water. He is urging the EPA to work with federal, state, and local partners to ensure Tiverton residents can access safe drinking water at home.

Residents in the affected zones, including those living in homes on Crandall Road, Bulgarmarsh Road, and Stafford Road, cited elevated PFAS levels in their private wells, reaching over 4,000 parts per trillion (ppt), more than 19,900% above the state’s safety limit of 20 ppt.

Testing from the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (RIDEM) as of September 16 shows that 87 of 157 private wells have exceeded safety limits.

Senators Reed and Whitehouse and Congressman Amo called for the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) to expeditiously approve federal funding for a new water line.

Tiverton residents can find resources and updates on PFAS contamination and ongoing remediation efforts here.

title: Baumgartner Announces $2.23 Million Grant to Spokane County to Support Fairchild Air Force Base Transportation Access
text:
September 21, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Michael Baumgartner (WA-05) announced that the Office of Local Defense Community Cooperation has approved a federal grant for $2,236,500 to Spokane County to undertake a $3,195,000 project for the reconstruction of Thorpe Road. This directly supports Fairchild Air Force Base by constructing better transportation access.

“This is a major win for the operational resilience of Fairchild Air Force Base (FAFB), the beating heart of the Spokane community,” said Congressman Baumgartner. “This is a crucial investment in national security that will enhance timely response and grant Air Force personnel easier access to one of the most strategic military installations in the US Air Forces’s inventory – Fairchild Air Force Base – home to the largest US air refueling wing in the world.”

Currently, Fairchild relies on a single access gate to manage the flow of personnel, goods, and vehicles. This bottleneck not only creates significant congestion and delay, but undermines core principles of military readiness, emergency responsiveness, and base security. This project will reconstruct and modernize Thorpe Road to fully enable the operation of a secondary access gate. The resulting benefits are substantial: improving response times during recalls and emergencies, enhancing quality of life for service members and families, reducing base-related congestion, and strengthening disaster resiliency.

“I also want to recognize the incredible work of Commissioner Al French and Spokane County Director of Public Works Kyle Twohig in securing this funding,” said Congressman Baumgartner. “They saw the need for this project and worked to get it across the finish line. This is exactly the kind of partnership we need between local leaders and the federal government to strengthen Fairchild, improve access for our service members, and make our community more resilient.”

Getting through the main gate at Fairchild can be a challenge, even outside of rush hour. The current gate is only two travel lanes wide, creating unnecessary congestion and delays. By comparison, installations on the west side of the state, including McChord Field and Fort Lewis, have entry points that are four lanes wide or more. Building the Thorpe Road access and secondary gate to accommodate greater traffic capacity will significantly improve the speed and ease of entry while reducing congestion at the main gate.

title: Baumgartner Bill Holds Foreign Officials Accountable for Discriminating Against Washington State Businesses
text:
September 16, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Michael Baumgartner’s (WA-05) No Racketeers on Our Shores Act (H.R. 9834) was approved by the House Judiciary Committee by a vote of 15 to 8. This clears the bill to be considered by the full House of Representatives.

“American companies should not be unfairly targeted or subjected to discriminatory treatment by foreign governments, and that is especially important for companies from Washington state like Coupang, Microsoft and Amazon,” said Congressman Baumgartner. “The No Racketeers on Our Shores Act gives our diplomats another targeted tool to hold foreign officials accountable without immediately escalating to the use of tariffs to address trade disputes.”

The legislation responds to a growing pattern uncovered by the House Judiciary Committee: foreign governments using coercive powers to target successful Washington state companies while protecting their favored domestic competitors:

Background:

Microsoft is one of the companies singled out under Europe’s Digital Markets Act. Its Windows operating system and its LinkedIn service have been designated as one of seven “gate keepers,” placing them under special EU mandates backed by fines up to 10 percent of the company’s worldwide revenues–20 percent for repeat violations. Six of the seven companies initially targeted by the EU for this discriminatory treatment were US firms;

Coupang, a Washington state headquartered company, is facing a whole of government assault by the South Korean government. South Korean agencies launched 40 investigations after a data breach that culminated in a $410 million fine, harming American investors and the U.S. business that sell goods through Coupang to the South Korean market.

title: Congressman Bell Introduces Bipartisan Legislation to Cut Bureaucratic Red Tape, Delivering Disaster Relief Without Delay
text:
Today, Congressman Wesley Bell announced the introduction of his bipartisan Relief Without Delay Act

The bill keeps disaster aid flowing during shutdowns, cuts bureaucratic delays, and invests in tornado preparedness

The legislation builds on Bell’s previous efforts to overhaul the disaster aid process

Congressman Bell: “When a disaster tears through your community, the last thing you should have to worry about is whether Washington's dysfunction will delay your recovery needs”

From STLPR: Bell pushes disaster response package as St. Louis seeks more federal aid

Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) and Jeff Hurd (R-CO-03) led 20 of their colleagues in introducing the Relief Without Delay Act, a bipartisan bill that would ensure the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) disaster aid continues flowing to families and communities during a government shutdown.

Additionally, the bill would bring new transparency to how disaster relief dollars are spent, and strengthen the nation's tornado detection, warning systems, and community storm shelters.

"When a disaster tears through your community, the last thing you should have to worry about is whether Washington's dysfunction will delay your recovery needs," said Congressman Wesley Bell. "I've seen this devastation firsthand in St. Louis. Families who’ve lost everything need help to come fast, not get caught up in bureaucratic red tape. The Relief Without Delay Act makes sure disaster aid never stops, brings real transparency to how those dollars are spent, and invests in tornado warning systems and storm shelters that save lives. Recovery isn’t a partisan issue. It is a promise we keep to every American, no matter what."

“When disaster strikes, families, local governments, and first responders should be able to count on the federal government to do its job, regardless of what is happening in Washington,” said Congressman Jeff Hurd. “Communities across Colorado’s Third District know how important a timely and reliable federal response is when facing wildfires, floods, and other natural disasters. I’m proud to be an original cosponsor of the Relief Without Delay Act to help ensure FEMA can continue supporting disaster response and recovery without interruption, while bringing greater transparency and accountability to how federal disaster dollars are delivered.”

After the devastating tornadoes in Missouri last year, Rep. Bell has repeatedly pushed to hold the Trump Administration accountable and to ensure families receive the necessary post-disaster recovery assistance.

In October 2025, he introduced the FEMA Operations Continuity Act to ensure FEMA can continue providing disaster relief during lapses in government funding. In February 2026, he introduced the FEMA Accountability Act, requiring FEMA to publicly report monthly on disaster relief fund expenditures.​ Most recently, Congressman Bell introduced the Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) Automated Assessment Act, “CDBG AAA,” which seeks to improve how the federal government identifies and addresses unmet housing, infrastructure, and economic recovery needs after major disasters.

In addition to Representatives Bell and Hurd, cosponsors supporting this measure include Representatives Jared Moskowitz (D-FL-23), Troy A. Carter (D-LA-02), Sanford D. Bishop (D-GA-02), Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07), Brad Sherman (D-CA-32), Cleo Fields (D-LA-06), Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL-25), Christian D. title: Rep. Bera Secures $155 Million for Sacramento River Basin
text:
SACRAMENTO, CA — Last week, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 by a strong bipartisan vote of 415-9. title: Beyer Statement On Trump Arch Announcement
text:
Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA), who represents a Northern Virginia district in the U.S. House that includes Arlington National Cemetery and Ronald Reagan National Airport (DCA), issued the following statement after President Trump declared via social media post that his proposal for a gigantic arch intended to serve as a monument to himself would “convert” the site “to house, store, and… use large numbers of drones, plus snipers, …and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition,” supposedly for national security reasons:

“Putting a drone launching site directly in the landing path for DCA is a stupid, dangerous, and unworkable idea. But if Trump wants to pursue it, the FAA’s prior work over the past six months to rubber stamp this proposal with a dubious safety study will be obsolete, and they will have to do it all over again.

“Likewise, Trump’s notion to make his vanity arch an ammunition depot for ‘snipers’ in a location where snipers have never been needed would place a large weapons cache within feet of thousands of tourists, pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers on major commuter traffic thoroughfares and Metro’s Blue Line. Such work would necessitate a redo of all prior impact studies, some of which remain unreleased if they were ever done at all.

“Of course, Trump is not serious about any of this. He just wants this massive monument to his own ego built by any means available, and he has been told that he is likely to lose court challenges. He hopes to use national security as a ludicrous pretext to force construction through, just as he did with his wildly expensive White House ballroom boondoggle. The overwhelming local opposition to Trump’s illegal and disrespectful vanity arch will not be defeated by this chicanery. The Narcissist in Chief is not fooling anyone.”

Last Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a doubtful “determination of no hazard to air navigation” for the President’s arch proposal. The FAA’s determination did not contemplate the structure’s use as a launch pad for “large numbers of drones.”

The FAA document’s political influence was especially apparent in the closing section, which overruled a prior FAA requirement of flashing red lights for the arch in favor of “a non-standard eternal flame” “continuously floodlighted by searchlight projectors.” The National Park Service similarly issued documentation finding the arch would have substantial adverse effects on regional historic sites, but approving it anyway.

Rep. Don Beyer is leading congressional efforts to block construction of Trump’s arch. His Northern Virginia district includes the Arlington National Cemetery, where his parents, grandparents, and sister are buried. He is the author of the Arlington National Cemetery Viewshed Protection Act, which would explicitly prohibit construction of the arch. He previously raised concerns about the projects impacts on traffic in the region, which the Trump Administration has yet to address. The arch has been a consistent source of anger and concern to Beyer’s constituents, who like much of the country, vociferously oppose the project.

RELEASE: Carter welcomes new 14-day red snapper season following efforts to expand fishing access
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Rep. Earl L. “Buddy” Carter (R-GA) today welcomed NOAA Fisheries’ announcement of a new 14-day recreational red snapper fishing season for eligible Georgia anglers from October 9 through October 22, 2026.

The announcement follows efforts led by Rep. John Rutherford (R-FL), alongside Carter and other South Atlantic lawmakers, to expand recreational fishing access after litigation halted the states’ planned summer seasons.

“Georgia’s fishermen deserve greater access to the waters they know best, and this 14-day season is an important step forward,” said Rep. Carter. “I want to thank Congressman John Rutherford for his leadership on this issue, along with President Trump, Secretary Lutnick, NOAA, Governor Kemp, and the Georgia Department of Natural Resources for their work to get our anglers back on the water. I’m proud to have worked alongside them to fight for our fishermen and coastal communities, and we’re going to keep pushing for even greater access.”

In June 2025, Carter led members of Georgia’s House Republican delegation in urging Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to support efforts by Georgia, Florida, and South Carolina to secure greater authority over recreational red snapper management.

Under NOAA’s newly issued permits, eligible Georgia anglers will have access to the October 9–22 season. NOAA and participating states will review harvest data afterward to determine whether an additional fishing opportunity may be available in December.

title: Carbajal Announces Funding for Central Coast Water Projects Passed House
text:
U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24) announced the House of Representatives passed a bipartisan bill containing more than $66 million for Central Coast water projects. The Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) of 2026 will now need to be considered by the Senate for final passage.

Click here for legislative text and here for a summary of WRDA 2026.“Climate change and population growth are straining the Central Coast’s aging water infrastructure. We need strong federal investments to upgrade the water pipes, treatment plants, and sewer systems that serve our region,” said Rep. Carbajal, a senior member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. “Now that the House has passed the Water Resources Development Act, this bill is heading to the Senate carrying key investments I secured for our local infrastructure. I will continue working closely with my colleagues in Congress to ensure this critical legislation is signed into law and delivers for our communities.”

The following projects and authorizations have been included in the committee-passed bill.

$6,300,000 for the City of Lompoc. The City’s projects include the modernization of the City’s water treatment plant and construction of a stormwater treatment and flood control system.

$30,000,000 for the Los Olivos Community Services District (LOCSD). The funding will be used for a new septic-to-sewer project. Once completed, the proposed project will collect wastewater from the LOCSD and send the waste approximately 3.5 miles to a connection point with the City of Solvang. The City of Solvang will then treat and dispose of the LOCSD’s wastewater at their regional facilities.

$25,000,000 for the City of Ojai. The project would replace the metal pipes that service the City’s storm water collection system. These pipes are at the end of their expected life, having been in place since the early 1960s.

$3,200,000 for Summerland Sanitary District to upgrade water and wastewater infrastructure.

$2,000,000 for the City of Solvang to improve its water and water supply infrastructure, including the distribution systems.

Authorization of the City of Morro Bay’s seawall repair and harbor enhancements project.

In July 2026, Carbajal announced WRDA advanced out of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. Below are quotes from Central Coast leaders on the bill's advancement.

“The City of Solvang is grateful for Congressman Carbajal’s leadership and continued advocacy for Solvang. His support helps advance important infrastructure priorities that are essential to the long-term health, reliability, and resilience of our community,” said Mayor David Brown.

“The legislative language advocated by Congressman Salud Carbajal will ensure the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers lives up to its responsibility to repair and maintain breakwater, revetment, and seawall infrastructure that is vital to ensuring safe navigation and operations in Morro Bay Harbor. We appreciate Rep. Carbajal’s leadership and his hard work in Washington, D.C. on behalf of Morro Bay and California,” said Mayor Carla Wixom.

“The Summerland Sanitary District is incredibly grateful to Congressman Carbajal for his continued advocacy for our coastal infrastructure. Securing this $3.2 million authorization in the draft WRDA bill is a vital milestone in rehabilitating our ocean outfall. This federal partnership establishes the critical pathway we need to protect our local environment and ensure reliable wastewater services for our community,” said Diantha Glaser, General Manager of the Summerland Sanitary District.

“Building a sewer system to solve a problem that has persisted for more than 50 years isn't glamorous, and it certainly is not easy. We are deeply grateful to Congressman Salud Carbajal for his leadership and support in helping secure funding for this critical community infrastructure. This investment gives Los Olivos a once-in-a-generation opportunity to build the solution our community has long supported while ensuring that local decisions remain in local hands. It allows us to move forward with a project that reflects the needs and priorities of the people who live and work here,” said Los Olivos Community Services District President Julie Kennedy.

“Congressman Carbajal’s work to continue advancing the Lower Mission Creek Flood Control Project through WRDA 2026 is a very welcome shot in the arm. He has been an essential and long-time champion of the project. With construction now over 50% complete, renewed Federal investment is critical to finishing this complex and urgently needed project to protect our densely developed urban core from recurring flooding,” said Santa Barbara County Public Works Director Chris Sneddon.

“Safety and infrastructure have been central priorities for this Council and City staff, with enhanced public participation, deferred maintenance budgeting, and focused timelines as key progress indicators. We are extremely grateful for our Federal agencies in partnering with the City of Ojai to bring our storm systems to proper order, helping to sustain a community that can remain resilient, safe, and efficient now and for decades to come,” said Ojai’s Mayor Andy Gilman.

The Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) authorizes the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to carry out critical water infrastructure projects nationwide, including flood risk reduction, ecosystem restoration and navigation improvement. WRDA is biennial legislation crafted by the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. By authorizing these projects through WRDA, Congress helps unlock future federal funding.

title: RELEASE: Casar Leads 100+ Members Demanding Medical Care, Not Deportation, for Man Shot by ICE in Austin
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Greg Casar and over 100 Members of Congress demanded that ICE release Wilber Rafael Garces Perez from detention to allow him to receive medical treatment and stop its efforts to deport him. Mr. Garces Perez is a 28-year-old DoorDash driver who was shot in the back by an ICE agent in Austin on September 20th.

In a letter authored by Casar to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Acting ICE Director David Venturella, the Members demand that:

ICE release Mr. Garces Perez from detention so he can receive medical treatment;

ICE abandon efforts to swiftly deport him or remove him from Texas;

The ICE agent responsible remain in Texas; and

DHS preserve all available evidence related to the shooting and share all evidence with parties that have jurisdiction to conduct a full, independent, and transparent investigation.

Mr. Garces Perez is being held at "the South Texas Detention Complex in Pearsall, Texas, which has a documented history of medical neglect," the Members write. "According to his lawyers, he 'still has the bullet lodged in his body. He's received no pain medication and had to sleep on the floor.'" On September 21, after a visit from Congressman Joaquin Castro's staff, he was briefly taken to a hospital before being returned to detention. According to his cellmate, he was "roughly handled and handcuffed" beforehand, and he has since "reported losing sensation on the left side of his body."

"Mr. Garces Perez is a key witness to this shooting, and given ICE's history of obscuring the facts in similar investigations, he must not be removed," the Members write.

The Members request answers by Monday, September 28th. Their questions include:

Why did agents use deadly force?

ICE's use of force policy requires officers to render medical aid, and video suggests they did not. Why was that policy not followed?

What is Mr. Garces Perez's current medical condition? What treatment is he receiving in immigration detention?

Will ICE release all bodycam footage?

The letter was copied to FBI Director Kash Patel and DHS Inspector General Joseph V. Cuffari.

The full letter can be viewed here.

The letter was signed by U.S. Representatives Yassamin Ansari, Becca Balint, Nanette Barragán, Wesley Bell, Donald Beyer, Everton Blair, Brendan Boyle, Shontel Brown, Janelle Bynum, André Carson, Greg Casar, Joaquin Castro, Judy Chu, Gilbert Cisneros, Yvette Clarke, Lou Correa, Joe Courtney, Jasmine Crockett, Jason Crow, Sharice Davids, Madeleine Dean, Diana DeGette, Christopher Deluzio, Mark DeSaulnier, Maxine Dexter, Lloyd Doggett, Veronica Escobar, Adriano Espaillat, Lizzie Fletcher, Laura Friedman, Maxwell Frost, John Garamendi, Jesús García, Robert Garcia, Sylvia Garcia, Daniel Goldman, Jimmy Gomez, Al Green, Adelita Grijalva, Steven Horsford, Chrissy Houlahan, Val Hoyle, Jared Huffman, Jonathan Jackson, Sara Jacobs, Pramila Jayapal, Julie Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Robin Kelly, Ro Khanna, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Summer Lee, Teresa Leger Fernandez, Sam Liccardo, Seth Magaziner, Sarah McBride, Betty McCollum, Morgan McGarvey, James McGovern, LaMonica McIver, Analilia Mejia, Christian Menefee, Robert Menendez, Kweisi Mfume, Dave Min, Gwen Moore, Kelly Morrison, Eleanor Norton, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ilhan Omar, Frank Pallone, Brittany Pettersen, Mark Pocan, Nellie Pou, Ayanna Pressley, Mike Quigley, Delia Ramirez, Emily Randall, Luz Rivas, Andrea Salinas, Mary Gay Scanlon, Lateefah Simon, Adam Smith, Eric Sorensen, Melanie Stansbury, Mark Takano, Bennie Thompson, Mike Thompson, Dina Titus, Rashida Tlaib, Jill Tokuda, Paul Tonko, Ritchie Torres, Lori Trahan, Derek Tran, Gabe Vasquez, Marc Veasey, Nydia Velázquez, James Walkinshaw, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, and Bonnie Watson Coleman.

title: The Washington Times Op-Ed by Rep. Smith'A presidential appeal to release unjustly detained U.S. citizens'
text:
By Rep. Christopher H. Smith - Tuesday, September 22, 2026

Political prisoner in China Jimmy Lai illustration by Linas Garsys / The Washington Times

OPINION:

President Trump and General Secretary Xi Jinping will meet in Washington this week with trade, technology, Taiwan and Iran on a crowded agenda.

These critical, wide-ranging disputes require intense focus and attention but are unlikely to be resolved in a single day. Yet, the summit can produce one immediate result: bringing home Americans unjustly detained in China and political prisoners such as Jimmy Lai, whose time behind bars must come to an end.

Mr. Xi should leave the U.S. knowing four names by heart: Nelson Wells Jr., Dawn Michelle Hunt, Youlin Chen and Min Zin.

Mr. Trump already understands why detention cases require leader-level diplomacy. In May, Mr. Trump personally raised the case of Mr. Lai, the 78-year-old Hong Kong publisher nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize, who is serving a 20-year sentence for his peaceful advocacy. We hope the president will raise Mr. Lai again. Only Mr. Xi can approve a release of that political significance. Only Mr. Xi can do the same for Americans whose cases have already become U.S. priorities.

Mr. Wells and Ms. Hunt have spent more than 12 years behind bars. Mr. Wells is a Louisiana-born father of three. Ms. Hunt is a Chicago artist. They were prosecuted in a judicial system controlled by the Communist Party. Testimony at hearings I have chaired has documented failures of evidence, legal defense and due process in these cases.

Mr. Wells was first sentenced to life; his sentence was later reduced to 22 years, which could keep him imprisoned until 2041. Ms. Hunt received a death sentence with a two-year reprieve, which was later commuted to life. Their health is now deteriorating.

Mr. Wells’ family reports seizures, diabetes and high blood pressure. He also has endured physical attacks in prison.

Ms. Hunt needs blood transfusions, has experienced sexual abuse and mistreatment while in prison, and has severe, untreated medical problems, including tumors in her uterus and ovaries. Her father died this year without seeing her come home.

The administration has already asked China to release Mr. Wells and Ms. Hunt on humanitarian grounds. Family advocates say Chinese officials have indicated Beijing is prepared to consider release if the request comes from a sufficiently senior level. More than a year of diplomatic work has therefore brought these cases to the point where only political intervention can move them. That leaves the essential appeal for the summit: to make these requests directly to Mr. Xi.

After all, the final decision is Mr. Xi’s. Beijing can choose clemency, medical parole, commutation or transfer, but no Chinese judge, foreign minister or Politburo member can authorize the release of two Americans sought by the U.S. president without approval from the top. That is how authority works in China’s autocratic system.

The president was recently asked by a reporter about Mr. Wells and Ms. Hunt. He had their names repeated and said he would speak with Mr. Xi about many matters.

Thank you, Mr. President. These names are worth repeating until Mr. Xi no longer needs the reminder. This is not for rhetorical effect. It is to ensure that imprisonment remains a top U.S. concern and an irritant in bilateral relations until they are home.

Tragically, Mr. Chen and Mr. Zin now require the same attention. Mr. Chen, a Boston-area seismologist who worked on U.S.-funded research, has been held since November 2024 after Chinese authorities stopped him at Beijing’s airport as he tried to return from a family visit. He was accused of “espionage” and has been held without charge.

Mr. Zin, a respected scholar of Burma-China relations, was invited to an academic gathering by Chinese hosts and detained upon arrival. He also faces a bogus espionage accusation. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has designated both men as “wrongfully detained” and promised to use State Department resources to secure their release.

There may be U.S. officials and pundits who object to using presidential time to raise these cases, but their objections would not be persuasive here. Raising these cases does not require trading away a tariff concession, a technology restriction or a security interest to secure the release of a U.S. citizen. Mr. Wells and Ms. Hunt are already the subjects of a humanitarian request; Mr. Chen and Mr. Zin are formally designated wrongful detention cases by our State Department. Presidential attention simply takes existing U.S. policy to the level where a decision can be made.

The release of unjustly detained U.S. citizens is a tangible result of a meeting that every American understands and will celebrate.

title: Opening statement of Co-Chairman Smith at CECC hearingThe Faces of Repression: Prisoners, Families, and Communities Targeted by the CCP
text:
The following are excerpts of Co-Chairman Chris Smith’s (R-NJ) opening statement at the Congressional-Executive Commission on China’s (CECC) September 22nd hearing, entitled “The Faces of Repression: Prisoners, Families, and Communities Targeted by the CCP”:

Behind every statistic about political prisoners is a person with hopes and dreams, and a life filled with isolation and pain. Behind every person in a Chinese prison is a family waiting, praying, and hoping that someone will not forget them. And behind many of those families is an entire community that feels threatened and intimidated.

Perhaps, that is what the Chinese Communist Party wants. It wants the prisoner isolated. It wants the family frightened. And it wants everyone watching to conclude that speaking out is either futile or simply too costly.

But today, we are here to say: we will not look away. The real cost is failing to speak out. Silence is not an option. Today, we appeal to Xi Jinping to release women and men of conscience and goodness—as a tangible good faith expression of good will, benevolence, respect, and strength. We appeal to Xi Jinping’s heart.

We again ask President Trump—who helped Pastor Ezra Jin gain his freedom—to appeal to Xi Jinping to show compassion and courage.

Pastor Jin founded Beijing Zion Church, which grew to a congregation of approximately 1,500 people before Chinese authorities forcibly shut down its sanctuary in 2018. Even after the physical church was closed, the congregation continued to meet, worship, teach, and evangelize across China. By 2025, Zion Church had nearly 100 meeting points in 40 cities.

The response from the Chinese Communist Party was a nationwide crackdown. In October 2025, authorities carried out arrests in 11 cities, taking approximately 30 pastors and church leaders into custody. Eighteen were ultimately criminally detained. Pastor Jin was one of them. His amazing daughter, Grace, came before this Commission and told us what his imprisonment meant for him and their family.

Both Congress and the President listened and acted. The House passed my resolution, H.Res. 1259, asking the President to help secure Pastor Jin’s release during engagement with Xi Jinping. President Trump personally pushed for Pastor Jin’s freedom, and he was released and reunited with his family this summer. That is something worth celebrating.

Pastor Jin himself has said that he believes the direct intervention of President Trump with President Xi was instrumental in securing his freedom. And he returned to America after eight months apart from his family. But Pastor Jin’s freedom also reminds us of the people who are still behind bars. Eight of his Zion Church colleagues remain detained.

And according to our Commission, their families have raised concerns about extreme temperatures, malnutrition, inadequate medical care, and mistreatment in detention. Even the lawyers attempting to defend them have faced pressure.

We also must remember Americans who remain imprisoned in China. Nelson Wells, Sr. has been here before, almost two years to the day. On September 18th, 2024, he testified at the CECC hearing, “Bringing Home Americans Detained in China,” I chaired about his son, Nelson Wells Jr., who has now spent more than a decade imprisoned in China.

Nelson Jr. was arrested in 2014 after traveling to China for medical treatment. He was initially sentenced to life imprisonment; that sentence was later reduced to 22 years, leaving him incarcerated until 2041. His family has also reported serious and debilitating medical problems.

Mr. Wells’ testimony was heartbreaking. He told us about the call that changed his family’s life—the call telling them that their son had been arrested in China. And he told us about the deterioration of Nelson’s health. His father and mother have spent years trying to bring their son home.

The tragedy of Dawn Michelle Hunt’s imprisonment has also taken a devastating toll on her family. After more than 12 years without his daughter, Dawn’s father, Gene Hunt, passed away on January 25, 2026, without ever seeing her come home.

Her brother, Tim Hunt, is with us today and has continued the fight their father began, promising to do everything he can to bring Dawn back to her family. Dawn is reportedly in declining health, making the family’s plea for her humanitarian release all the more urgent.

Gene’s greatest wish was to see his daughter free; his family now carries that hope forward and asks that Dawn be given the opportunity to come home. That is why I introduced HR 5491—the Nelson Wells Jr. and Dawn Michelle Hunt Unjustly Detained in Communist China Act. The legislation recognizes that we need more than expressions of concern—we need a coordinated American response.

The bill would strengthen the government’s ability to identify Americans unjustly detained in China, coordinate their cases, engage with their families, pursue humanitarian releases and prisoner transfers, and identify additional tools for holding responsible Chinese officials accountable. Because when an American is unjustly detained, that person’s family should not have to navigate the Chinese Communist Party’s system alone.

And this repression is not limited to Christians, Americans, or any one community. Last week, our Commission heard a compelling appeal from Jimmy Lai’s son, Sebastien. Both Sebastien and his sister, Claire, are asking that their heroic father be freed.

Gulshan Abbas is a retired Uyghur doctor, who was detained in Xinjiang and sentenced to 20 years in prison. Her detention came just days after her sister, Rushan Abbas—who will testify today—spoke publicly here in Washington about the persecution of Uyghurs. Gulshan’s case is an example of transnational repression because of the obvious connection between her detention and her sister’s advocacy in the United States.

We must also remember the Falun Gong practitioners, who have endured decades of persecution. Falun Gong was banned by the Chinese government in 1999, and practitioners who refuse to renounce their beliefs have faced imprisonment, forced organ harvesting, and other forms of repression. The Commission’s 2025 annual report identified 485 Falun Gong practitioners among cases of active detention.

But once again, the repression does not necessarily end at the prison gate. Falun Gong practitioners living here in the United States have reported surveillance, harassment, threats, physical assaults, property damage, and reprisals against relatives in China. The Justice Department has also prosecuted individuals for acting as agents of the People’s Republic of China in efforts targeting Falun Gong practitioners in the United States.

Today’s hearing is a heartfelt appeal to Xi Jinping.

Let these wonderful people go.

###

title: OSV News article on Smith hearing'Ezra Jin Mingri, lawmakers call on Trump to push Xi to free prisoners of conscience'
text:
By Kate Scanlon

Published September 22, 2026 at 5:03 PM

WASHINGTON (OSV News) — Ezra Jin Mingri, founder and pastor of an underground church in China and a former prisoner of conscience in that country, called for the release of other individuals imprisoned for their religious beliefs Sept. 22 at a hearing by the Congressional-Executive Commission on China.

With his daughter Grace Jin Drexel acting as translator, Jin said in remarks at the hearing that “reuniting with my family after eight years apart and watching the fireworks together on America’s 250th Independence Day felt like a dream.”

“Even as I rejoice and enjoy such freedom and joy with my family, I cannot stop thinking and worrying about my eight fellow church leaders who remain in prison,” he said.

Jin was released from imprisonment and reunited with his family in the U.S. shortly before Independence Day. President Donald Trump previously sought his release during a May summit with China’s President Xi Jinping.

U.S. Rep. Chris Smith, R-N.J., is seen on Capitol Hill in Washington March 10, 2021. (OSV News photo/Ken Cedeno, Pool via Reuters)

Ezra Jin Mingri, founder and pastor of an underground church in China and a prisoner of conscience in that country until his release, is pictured in a 2018 file photo in Beijing. Mingri arrived in Los Angeles July 3, 2026, after he was released from imprisonment and reunited with his family in the U.S. shortly before Independence Day, U.S. officials said. (OSV News photo/Thomas Peter, Reuters)

Ezra Jin Mingri calls for release of pastors

As Trump prepared to host Xi for a state visit in Washington, advocates have urged him to again push for the release of additional prisoners of conscience and political prisoners of interest to the U.S., including Jimmy Lai, Hong Kong’s prominent Catholic and pro-democracy campaigner. Lai remains in prison, where he is serving a 20-year sentence.

“I sincerely hope that the members of Congress will continue to pay attention to religious persecution and human rights within China,” Jin said. “I hope that this meeting between the two heads of state can produce genuine consensus and a breakthrough in improving China’s human rights situation and ending the persecution of religious believers.”

In 2018, Jin, the founder of Zion Church, and his family moved to the U.S. amid pressure on the church from Chinese officials. But Jin later returned and was prohibited from leaving China. He was among dozens of members imprisoned in a crackdown by Chinese authorities on his church in October 2025. Some other members of his religious community remain imprisoned.

Jin stressed that if he, as the “main leader of our church,” was released, then it should “also be the case that my coworkers, those other leaders of my church, should also be released without any guilt.” He also called for the release of other Christian pastors held in China.

Hong Kong protesters hold East Turkestan Uyghur flags at a rally in support of Xinjiang Uyghurs’ human rights, in Hong Kong Dec. 22, 2019. (OSV News photo/Lucy Nicholson, Reuters)

Catholic lawmakers speak out

At the hearing, two Catholic lawmakers, Reps. Chris Smith, R-N.J., co-chair of the CECC, and Jim McGovern, D-Mass., one of the commissioners, called for the release of those who were “unjustly detained” by the Chinese government, including Lai.

Smith called on Trump to raise the issue of the release of these prisoners “eyeball to eyeball” with Xi during their meeting.

“This summit is a golden opportunity for the president to speak out and to do so boldly,” Smith said.

Smith said at the hearing that behind every such prisoner there “is a family waiting, praying, and hoping that someone will not forget them, and behind many of those families is an entire community that feels threatened and far too intimidated.”

“Perhaps that is what the Chinese Communist Party wants,” he said. “It wants the prisoner isolated. It wants the family frightened, and it wants everyone watching to conclude that speaking out is either futile or simply too costly. But today we are here to say we will not look away. The real cost is failing to speak out. Silence is not an option.”

U.S. President Donald Trump meets with Chinese President Xi at the start of their bilateral meeting at the G20 leaders summit in Osaka, Japan, June 29, 2019. Trump and Xi are scheduled to meet on Sept. 24, 2026, at the White House in Washington. (OSV News photo/Kevin Lamarque, Reuters)

‘A clear and unified message’ for Trump

McGovern said, “We convene with a clear and unified message to President Trump: advocate for the release of prisoners of conscience in China.”

“Pastor Jin is proof that this goal is achievable,” he said. “We sincerely hope for more releases.”

McGovern also urged Trump not to “abandon human rights in our foreign policy.”

title: The Washington Stand article featuring Smith's commentary'Advocates, Lawmakers Press Trump to Uphold Prisoners of Faith, Conscience during Xi Visit'
text:
By Dan Hart

Published September 22, 2026

With President Trump set to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday as part of a state visit to Washington, human rights advocates and lawmakers are urging the commander in chief to champion the cause of Christians and other citizens who are imprisoned in China simply for practicing their faith or for advocating for freedom.

A large-scale crackdown on non-government approved churches is being carried out by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) over the past year. Last October, almost two dozen pastors and other workers from a single church called Zion Church were arrested, including founder and head pastor Ezra Jin. But in July, the power of personal advocacy was put on display as Xi’s communist regime released Jin following a personal appeal to Xi from Trump in May for Jin’s release.

Now, human rights advocates such as Voice of the Martyrs’ Todd Nettleton are highlighting the plight of other imprisoned pastors such as John Cao. As detailed by Family Research Council’s Bob Fu, Cao “spent seven years in a Chinese prison for conducting humanitarian work along the China-Myanmar border,” but even two years after completing his sentence, he is still being prevented from reuniting with his family in the U.S. by the CCP. Others are urging Trump to fulfill a promise to secure the freedom of Jimmy Lai, a Hong Kong media mogul and champion of democracy.

As Fu catalogs, the list of the wrongfully imprisoned in China goes on and on: Gao Zhisheng, a human rights lawyer; Dr. Wang Bingzhang, a leader of the overseas Chinese democracy movement who was kidnapped by CCP agents in Vietnam; Zhang Zhan, a citizen journalist who exposed the truth about COVID-19. Then there are the eight pastors and members of Ezra Jin’s Zion Church who remain imprisoned, as well as Elder Li Yingqiang, Pastor Yang Rongli of Golden Lampstand Church, and Pastor Wang Yi of Early Rain Covenant Church. These Christians are imprisoned simply for refusing to surrender the authority of their churches to the Communist Party, Fu notes.

Lawmakers like Rep. Chris Smith (R-N.J.), who serves as co-chair of the Congressional Executive Commission on China, say that advocating on behalf of Christians and other prisoners of conscience is especially important now as persecution by the CCP “is getting far worse.”

“[T]he reason why Ezra Jin’s church got targeted [is because] they refused to allow surveillance cameras into their churches,” he pointed out during “Washington Watch with Tony Perkins” Monday. “It’s one of those things where the Communist Party is ubiquitous, they want to be everywhere. And for the slightest perceived infraction, they will then arrest pastors and horribly mistreat them. So this is the time for the United States, I believe, and every freedom loving country to pivot and say, ‘Religious freedom matters.’ Human rights are at the core of our relationship and should be with a dictatorship like China. Raise it and make it stick. Link it to other things, including trade.”

Smith went on to emphasize that for Christians, advocating for those in prison is a direct command from God.

“Our Lord said, ‘did you visit me when I was in prison’ in Matthew 25? ‘How about when you had the opportunity? Did you try to get me out of prison?’” he underscored. “I’ve met so many wonderful pastors and people over the years, including in the Soviet Union going back to 1981. My first trip there was in ’82 on behalf of religious freedom. … Ronald Reagan always raised religious freedom. He always had a list of people that he was asking — in this case, the Russian or Soviet leadership — to allow to go free. And we need to persist and tell this dictatorship, ‘This is a priority. [If] you want other things, [if] you want more trade, … well, this is the linchpin. This opens up the door.”

Smith further stressed how critical the stakes are for those caught in the CCP’s brutal prison system. “If you’re arrested in China, political or religious prisoner, you’re almost always going to be tortured, and I mean horribly tortured. I had a number of hearings on what the Chinese government actually does to people, and you can’t even repeat some of it [because] it is so, so horrific. And that leaves scars on that individual, the likes of which we can’t even fathom. So I would ask all of us to be praying.”

Smith, who serves as a senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and as co-chair of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, recalled what Wei Jingsheng, a father of China’s democracy movement, once told him about how powerful the West’s advocacy efforts are for those in China’s prisons.

“[H]e told me something I will never forget. He said, ‘When you Americans and the West kowtow and try to be all nicey-nice with these dictators, they beat us more in prison.’ He said, ‘When you are tough, when you are well-founded in your knowledge about what’s going on, and you’re able to present a case and do so right from the heart, but also filled with facts, they beat us less and it effectuates the freedom of people from these gulags.’ So it’s it works. But we have to be serious. … [Secretary of State] Marco Rubio, who used to chair the China Commission … he knows this like the back of his hand. He should be raising it.”

Smith additionally detailed how decades of pro-China trade policies by the U.S. has undercut America’s ability to effectively fight against the CCP’s human rights abuses.

“[I]n 2005 [and] 2006 … Google, Microsoft, and Yahoo were conveying all of this technology to the Chinese Communist Party to surveil their own people to limit what can be searched on a Google search engine, for example, in China,” he explained. “… [O]ur technology has seriously enabled their public security police, their military, their command and control, and then the entirety of their weapons systems to be state of the art. I fault our Big Business for that. … Bill Clinton was the worst of all when it came to conveying all of that. [He] lost China on human rights for the purposes of trade, and that means technology transfers that have dual use that are military. We gave them the store, and we wonder why we’re now worried about a potential conflict vis à vis Taiwan and beyond.”

The congressman also pointed out that the measures that the U.S. has taken to combat illicitly-made Chinese goods ending up in the U.S. have not been effective, which has further hampered human rights.

“Bill Clinton had a memorandum of understanding on enforcement of the Smoot-Hawley Act [which says] we can’t import gulag-made goods. And it wasn’t worth the paper it was printed [on]. I went over to China and I said to our people in our embassy, ‘How do you enforce this? You can’t get to the factories where they’re making these things. There’s no on-site inspection. They don’t allow unfettered access.’ … So all these things are being produced by forced labor, including child labor [and it] ends up in our department stores.”

title: El Representante García se une a más de 70 legisladores de las Américas para exigir el fin de los ataques a embarcaciones y las ejecuciones extrajudiciales por parte de EE.UU.
text:
Washington, D.C. — En una acción interparlamentaria conjunta sin precedentes que reúne a más de 70 legisladores de 13 países de las Américas, incluyendo los Estados Unidos, y Puerto Rico, el Representante Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), junto con los Representantes Andre Carson (IN-07), Greg Casar (TX-35), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Summer Lee (PA-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-00), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), y Nydia Velázquez (NY-07) emitieron una declaración exigiendo el cese inmediato de los ataques del gobierno de Estados Unidos contra embarcaciones en el mar Caribe y el Pacífico Oriental, los cuales han provocado al menos 234 ejecuciones extrajudiciales. Asimismo, los firmantes reclaman justicia para las víctimas de estos ataques e instan a los demás gobiernos de la región a abstenerse de facilitar acciones que, según expertos jurídicos, organizaciones de derechos humanos y miembros —actuales y retirados— de las fuerzas armadas de Estados Unidos, constituyen violaciones del derecho internacional.

Los legisladores señalan que el propio gobierno estadounidense ha determinado que estas operaciones no han reducido significativamente el flujo de cocaína hacia el país. Destacan que el derecho a la vida y al debido proceso, así como las garantías frente al uso arbitrario de la fuerza, son principios fundamentales del Estado de derecho democrático. Advierten que las acusaciones de narcotráfico, por graves que sean, no anulan ni prevalecen sobre estas protecciones. Ante el anuncio de la administración Trump de continuar con estas operaciones y extenderlas a objetivos terrestres, los legisladores manifiestan su compromiso de utilizar sus “facultades legislativas y de fiscalización para promover la transparencia y la rendición de cuentas en torno a estas ejecuciones extrajudiciales”.

La declaración completa y la lista de firmantes están disponibles en este enlace.

"Donald Trump está lanzando bombas en el Caribe y el Pacífico en flagrante violación de la ley y de los derechos humanos fundamentales", afirmó el congresista Jesús "Chuy" García. "Esto no ha servido para detener el tráfico de drogas ni para aumentar la seguridad de los estadounidenses. Por el contrario, ha dejado cientos de muertos, familias destrozadas y comunidades sumidas en el miedo. Llamemos a estos ataques por su nombre: ejecuciones extrajudiciales ilegales. Me enorgullece unirme a legisladores de todo el hemisferio para oponerme a estos graves crímenes".

"Ante el silencio institucional y la censura gubernamental en Ecuador, esta coalición de parlamentarios de toda América Latina es fundamental para romper el secretismo que rodea a las operaciones encubiertas en nuestras aguas", señaló María Verónica Iñiguez Gallardo, miembro de la Asamblea Nacional de Ecuador. "Esta declaración transnacional representa un paso decisivo hacia la rendición de cuentas y la transparencia para nuestros pueblos".

“Estados Unidos debe poner fin a sus ataques en el Caribe y el Pacífico’, declaró Iván Cepeda Castro, senador de Colombia. “La lucha contra el narcotráfico no puede justificar el sacrificio de vidas humanas ni la vulneración del derecho internacional. América Latina y el Caribe deben actuar unidos para defender nuestra soberanía y el derecho de nuestra región a la paz, libre de las pretensiones de dominación hemisférica de cualquier potencia”.

“La campaña de bombardeos de Donald Trump en el Caribe y el Pacífico es a la vez criminal y cruel, y no ha contribuido en nada a hacer nuestra región más segura”, afirmó Don Davies, miembro de la Cámara de los Comunes de Canadá. “Los canadienses sabemos lo que significa ver nuestra soberanía amenazada por nuestro vecino del sur. Por ello, me solidarizo con los pueblos de todo el hemisferio en el rechazo a estas ejecuciones ilegales”.

Esta declaración ha sido apoyada por los siguientes grupos: Latin America Working Group (LAWG), Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC), Washington Office on Latin America (WOLA), Friends Committee on National Legislation (FCNL), Center for Economic and Policy Research (CEPR), Colombia Acuerdo de Paz NGO, Maryknoll Office for Global Concerns, Alianza Americas, Witness at the Border, Minnesota Cuba Committee, The United Methodist Church – General Board of Church and Society, Center for Engagement and Advocacy in the Americas (CEDA), Mennonite Central Committee U.S., MADRE, Unitarian Universalist Service Committee, ImPact Coalition on Strengthening International Judicial Institutions, Andean Information Network.
