title: Alaska Delegation Welcomes $315 Million Contract for Coast Guard Infrastructure in Kodiak
text:
Projects Will Support Arrival of New Icebreakers, Offshore Patrol Cutters

WASHINGTON—U.S. Senators Dan Sullivan and Lisa Murkowski and Congressman Nick Begich (all R-Alaska) today welcomed news that the Coast Guard has awarded a $315 million contract for the design and construction of a cutter mooring and new fuel pier at Coast Guard Base Kodiak. The Alaska congressional delegation helped secure the funding necessary for the projects in the 2025 Working Families Tax Cuts Act, FY 2023 Major Acquisition Systems Infrastructure legislation, and the 2022 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

“The historic build-up of the Coast Guard in Alaska and Kodiak continues today with $315 million coming for shoreside infrastructure projects in this great Coast Guard community,” said Sen. Sullivan, chair of the Senate Commerce Coast Guard, Maritime, and Fisheries Subcommittee. “My delegation colleagues and I worked hard in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act to deliver the largest investment in the Coast Guard in history—$25 billion—much of which is coming to our great state. These investments are great news for our Coast Guard, Alaska’s economy, and the hard-working families of Kodiak. I was glad to tour the site for this new berth and fuel pier this summer with the Coast Guard Commandant and the Homeland Security Secretary, both of whom understand the importance of Kodiak to the Coast Guard and our national security. I look forward to seeing these projects break ground as Kodiak prepares to welcome major new Coast Guard assets, including two new icebreakers, two offshore patrol cutters, and hundreds of new Coasties and their families.”

“Alaska is a cornerstone of American defense; investments like this from the Coast Guard are critical as we work to improve infrastructure on bases across the state to maintain our national security,” said Sen. Murkowski. “The construction of a new fuel pier, which will also allow for the berthing of two Arctic Security Cutters, bolsters Base Kodiak’s capability to carry out Coast Guard missions in the Arctic. I’m proud to have helped the Coast Guard leverage these historic investments to strengthen infrastructure and operations in Alaska as we support our Coast Guard men and women, as well as their families.”

“Base Kodiak is critical to America’s long-term Arctic strategy,” said Congressman Begich. “As we bring new cutters and personnel to Alaska, we must have the strategic infrastructure in place to support them. Congress made a historic commitment to rebuilding and modernizing the Coast Guard, and this project represents the next phase of that investment. This new fuel pier and major cutter mooring will strengthen force readiness and ensure our Coast Guard has the infrastructure necessary to carry out its mission across Alaska and the Arctic.”

According to the Coast Guard, the project includes waterfront improvements, including grading work to improve ground stability; construction of a new fueling utility building; installation of utilities, cutter shore ties, and other site amenities, including information technology, water and sewage and safety equipment; and unexploded ordnance removal.

Below is an overview of the delegation’s work to bring more Coast Guard assets, personnel, vessels, infrastructure, and investments to Alaska.

Securing U.S. Coast Guard Construction and Infrastructure Funding for Alaska Installations:

Since 2015, Congress has appropriated about $1.408 billion for infrastructure and construction-related projects in Alaska to support new and existing Coast Guard assets, giving many communities throughout Alaska significant investments in their infrastructure and local housing.

Securing Historic Investments in America’s Icebreaker Fleet:

Through the 2025 Working Families Tax Cuts Act, the Alaska congressional delegation secured $4.3 billion for the procurement of two new Polar Security Cutters, with substantial progress toward a third, marking the most significant expansion of heavy icebreaking capability in U.S. history. The delegation also worked to deliver $3.5 billion to procure three Arctic Security Cutters, the nation’s next-generation medium polar icebreakers. Additionally, they championed $816 million for more than ten new light and medium domestic icebreaking cutters.

On June 11, 2026, the Coast Guard announced that two of the three new icebreakers committed to Alaska will be homeported in Kodiak, with the third slated for Seward.

Beyond icebreakers, the WFTCA included major investments across the Coast Guard’s fleet: $1 billion for approximately 10 Fast Response Cutters (FRC), $4.3 billion for approximately 9 Offshore Patrol Cutters (OPC), $2.2 billion for approximately 40 MH-60 helicopters, and $1.1 billion for approximately 6 HC-130 aircraft. Critically, these efforts are backed by over $3 billion for shoreside infrastructure to support the homeporting of these assets, including the $300 million for the homeporting of the Storis in Juneau.

title: Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit, Bera Urges Trump to Stand Firm on Taiwan and Establish AI Crisis Guardrails
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Ahead of President Trump’s meeting with President Xi Jinping of the People’s Republic of China (PRC), U.S. Representative Ami Bera, M.D. (CA-06), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific, is urging President Trump to maintain longstanding U.S. commitments in the Indo-Pacific while using direct diplomacy with Beijing to address the emerging national security risks posed by artificial intelligence and reduce the risk of dangerous miscalculation.

Ranking Member Bera joined East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee Chair Young Kim (CA-40) in a bipartisan letter outlining priorities for the Trump-Xi summit, including upholding America’s longstanding policy toward Taiwan and supporting Taiwan’s self-defense, securing the release of wrongfully detained Americans, disrupting the fentanyl trade, and reducing Beijing’s leverage over critical mineral supply chains.

In a separate letter, Bera, House Foreign Affairs Committee Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (NY-05), and House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Africa Ranking Member Sara Jacobs (CA-51) led 26 other House Democrats in calling for sustained dialogue between the United States and the PRC focused on artificial intelligence safety and risk.

“President Trump must make clear that the United States will not compromise its commitments to peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific for the sake of reaching a broader deal with Beijing. That means standing firm on Taiwan, pressing for the release of wrongfully detained Americans, combating the networks fueling the fentanyl crisis, and reducing dangerous supply-chain dependencies,” said Representative Bera.

“At the same time, the President should seek agreement on implementing AI guardrails and establishing reliable channels of communication that reduce the risk of miscalculation and provide mechanisms to deconflict during a crisis. During the Cold War, the United States and the Soviet Union developed similar mechanisms to communicate during moments of heightened tension. Washington and Beijing need those channels in place to address current and emerging threats,” Bera continued.

Standing Firm on Taiwan and Advancing U.S. Security Priorities

In the Bera-Kim letter, the lawmakers urge President Trump to maintain America’s longstanding One-China policy, guided by the Taiwan Relations Act, the three U.S.-China Joint Communiqués, and the Six Assurances. They specifically call for continued efforts to strengthen Taiwan’s self-defense capabilities and for the President to make clear that the United States will not consult with Beijing over arms sales to Taiwan.

“Maintaining America’s decades-long policy on Taiwan – guided by the Taiwan Relations Act, the three U.S.-China Joint Communiqués, and the Six Assurances – by increasing Taiwan’s self-defense capabilities, including through additional arms sales, is essential to U.S. security,” Bera and Kim wrote. “We urge you to make clear that the U.S. will not consult with the PRC on arms sales to Taiwan consistent with the U.S. One-China policy.”

The Kim-Bera letter also urges President Trump to press for the release of wrongfully detained U.S. citizens Min Zin and Youlin Chen, expand law-enforcement cooperation to target fentanyl precursor chemicals and the networks supporting the fentanyl trade, and reduce U.S. dependence on the PRC for critical minerals and key pharmaceutical inputs.

Read the full Bera-Kim letter here.

Establishing AI Guardrails and Crisis Communications

In the Bera-Meeks-Jacobs letter, the lawmakers led more than two dozen U.S. House Democrats in calling for a sustained dialogue between the United States and the PRC focused on AI safety and national security risks. The letter calls for shared standards and red lines around dangerous uses of AI, a standing crisis communications channel, mechanisms to report consequential AI incidents, and discussions on maintaining human control over nuclear weapons decisions and preventing advanced AI capabilities from reaching dangerous non-state actors.

“The purpose of a U.S.-China dialogue on AI should be focused and practical: reduce risks of miscalculation and address the dangers that neither country can manage alone,” the lawmakers wrote.

The Bera-Meeks-Jacobs letter also calls for a standing channel that both countries could use to report anomalous AI events and prevent misunderstandings, work on technologies that could help verify claims about AI activities, and narrowly scoped engagement between American and Chinese AI researchers focused on safety and risk while protecting U.S. technology and intellectual property.

“The promise and risks of AI are too great for the United States and China to not talk,” the lawmakers added.

Read the full Bera-Meeks-Jacobs letter here.

title: REP. BOEBERT CALLS FOR MORTGAGE UNDERWRITING AND CREDIT SCORE REFORM AND LOWERING THE BARRIER TO HOMEOWNERSHIP
text:
Lone Tree, CO — Congresswoman Lauren Boebert (CO-04) sent a letter to Housing and Urban Development Secretary Scott Turner, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins calling for underwriting and credit-score reform so qualified Americans can buy a home without being locked out by outdated down-payment and credit rules.

“Affordability is what families talk about around the kitchen table in the heartland,” Rep. Boebert wrote. “Republicans in Congress cut taxes. Next, we need to reform the home-buying process."

Rep. Boebert is seeking to work with the departments to develop new policy that changes who qualifies for credit, cuts process costs, and modernizes mortgage rules without weakening the loan itself. She argued that a rigid 20 percent down payment knocks working families out of homeownership, and that on-time rent history and real-world income patterns should count.

“Asking a buyer to put down hundreds of thousands of dollars knocks many out of the chance to buy and grow their wealth,” she wrote. "I intend to work in a bipartisan manner with my colleagues to eventually introduce legislation."

Rep. Boebert said the federal mortgage system still judges borrowers through a narrow lens: a traditional credit score built on revolving debt and a steady W-2 paycheck. That approach shuts out renters with years of on-time payments but thin credit files; farmers and ranchers whose income arrives at harvest; tradesmen, contractors, seasonal workers, and small-business owners whose earnings vary by design; and commission earners punished for volatility instead of credited for income.

On an $833,000 jumbo loan, she noted, 20 percent down is about $167,000, while 5 percent is about $42,000. In many parts of the country, a jumbo loan is the only path to a primary residence. "Keeping the bar at 20 percent does not automatically make the loan safer,” she wrote. “It just delays homeownership and keeps people renting longer."

Rep. Boebert asked for a more flexible down-payment standard for jumbo or conventional loans, including a 5 percent option or a percentage tied to true income and credit history, paired with sound underwriting. Debt-to-income limits, credit scores, employment history, cash reserves, and appraisals should stay rigorous. The change, she said, is about the cash-to-close barrier, not ignoring risk.

“Families need our help to reduce arbitrary barriers in lending,” Rep. Boebert wrote.

title: Congresswoman Bynum: “A racial slur is not trash talk. It’s not a rivalry. It’s straight up racist.”
text:
Today, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum (OR-05) released the following statement following the alleged use of a racial slur during a recent Oregon high school football game.

“Football is supposed to be about teamwork, healthy competition, and kids getting the chance to do something they love,” said Rep. Bynum. “A kid should be able to put on their jersey, take the field, and worry about the next play – not whether someone is going to attack them on their race, sex, religion, or any other distinguishing feature. A racial slur is not trash talk. It’s not a rivalry. It’s straight up racist. In the state legislature, I sponsored legislation to make sure incidents like this couldn’t just be swept under the rug. We can’t ask young people to speak up and then fail them when they do. We need to teach our kids that reporting incidents like these will be taken seriously, investigated, and appropriately addressed based on the findings.

“The Oregon School Activities Association must step up and double down on eliminating these incidents. I have no tolerance for our kids being harmed in competition by racial slurs. And I have no patience for mealy-mouthed adults who throw their hands up and say there’s nothing we can do. If OSAA does not act, the governor and legislature should consider taking up a stronger set of sanctions sooner, rather than later.”

As a state legislator, Congresswoman Bynum introduced HB 3409, requiring a process for reporting and responding to harassment and hateful language during school sports and activities. The legislation was in response to a 2019 racial slur incident at Parkrose High School during a girls varsity basketball game, as well as other reports from students around the state.

###

title: Congresswoman Bynum Statement on Knight’s $1 Billion Donation to University of Oregon
text:
Today, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum (OR-05) released a statement in response to Phil and Penny Knight’s announcement of a $1 billion donation to the University of Oregon to help start an engineering school.

“This is exactly what investing in the next generation looks like – and I’m not just saying that because I’m an engineer,” said Rep. Bynum. “This generous and game-changing donation should be the standard for how we invest in getting our kids ready for the future and for how philanthropy can partner with local, state, and federal government to drive innovation. I’m fighting everyday in Congress to make that a reality. Go Ducks!”

title: NEWS: After Detention Visit, Casar Says Man Shot by ICE Still Has Bullet in His Body, Needs Surgery
text:
SAN ANTONIO, TEXAS – Today, Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35) visited Wilber Rafael Garces Perez at the South Texas ICE Processing Center in Pearsall, three days after Garces Perez was shot by a federal immigration officer in North Austin. Staff members from the office of Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) joined the visit.

Casar reported that Garces Perez saw a specialist for the first time today, and that the specialist said he needs surgery to remove the bullet still lodged in his body.

Casar inspected the wound where the bullet entered Garces Perez's back, just below his neck, and saw heavy bruising across his chest. Garces Perez told Casar the following:

He was discharged from the hospital within hours of the shooting, without speaking to his physician.

He did not learn the bullet was still inside him until more than a day after the shooting.

He spent his first night in a processing facility with no bed, in his hospital gown, cold and in intense pain.

He finally received stronger pain medication by injection just one hour before the scheduled congressional visit.

“I saw the conditions of Wilber’s injuries, and just like anybody that had been shot three days ago, he needs a doctor — not a deportation or a detention center,” said Congressman Casar (D-Texas). “My message to ICE is very clear: release Wilber from detention to get him the medical care he desperately needs.”

“ICE's treatment of Wilber amounts to torture. After being shot in the back, he has received next to no medical care — despite being in excruciating pain and losing movement on his left side. He should be in a hospital, not held in isolation at the South Texas Immigration Processing Center,” said Congressman Joaquin Castro (D-Texas). “He had permission to work in the U.S. and was delivering for DoorDash to support his family. Wilber must be released into medical care immediately. There must be an independent investigation, and the officers who shot him in the back must be held accountable. An agency that tortures a man like this should be disbanded.”

Casar called for a full, transparent investigation into the shooting by local, state, and federal law enforcement. The agents from the shooting scene are scheduled to be interviewed tomorrow, and local law enforcement has requested to be included. That request has not been fulfilled, and Casar called for the federal government to cooperate fully with local law enforcement.

Casar also called for the release of body camera and dash camera footage and answers on why Garces Perez was removed from the hospital. Casar has also requested a briefing from DHS Secretary Mullin by Monday, September 28.

###

Congressman Greg Casar represents Texas’s 35th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, which runs down I-35 from East Austin to Hays County to the West Side of San Antonio. A labor organizer and son of Mexican immigrants, Casar serves as the Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus for the 119th Congress. He also serves on the Committee on Education and Labor and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability.

title: NEWS: Casar, Sanders Introduce Legislation to Create New Federal Agency to Ban Artificial Superintelligence, Pause Advanced AI Development
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas) and Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act — legislation to stop artificial intelligence (AI) oligarchs from building machines humans cannot control and to pause advanced AI development until we have put in place rigorous federal testing and oversight to ensure AI does not harm humanity.

“Experts are warning that AI superintelligence, wielded by the wrong humans or by rogue AI, could kill countless numbers of people. But Donald Trump says he wants to encourage it. Something has to change,” Congressman Casar said. “Our bill bans the development of artificial superintelligence and pushes for international agreements so that no one, anywhere, builds AI too powerful for humans to control. Furthermore, our bill would immediately halt other dangerous AI capabilities, such as the capacity to develop biochemical weapons, or the capacity for AI to develop new AI instead of humans.”

“When you are racing towards a cliff, you don’t just ease up on the gas pedal. You hit the brakes. When the future of humanity is at stake, we need binding international safety rules, not voluntary standards from the industry,” Senator Sanders said. “Scientists have been clear: AI is an existential threat to humanity. It must be treated as such. This legislation will permanently ban the development of artificial superintelligence and would put in place an immediate pause on advanced AI development until we have clear safety rules in place — developed by the most knowledgeable scientists in our country. Congress must act now before it is too late.”

The Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act will protect humanity by:

Banning Artificial Superintelligence. No person or entity may develop or deploy Artificial Superintelligence — an AI that exceeds human cognitive performance and capabilities across most domains, or has sufficient capabilities to destroy or disempower humanity, including by overthrowing the federal government.

Pausing Advanced AI development until a new, federal AI regulatory body is up and running and has established clear rules and model review process to ensure safe and secure development and deployment of AI.

Establishing a new cabinet-level federal agency, the Department of Artificial Intelligence, to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence, including by enforcing a prohibition on artificial superintelligence. This agency will be advised by the most knowledgeable scientists in our country to:

Monitor frontier AI systems at all stages of the lifecycle for dangerous capabilities.

Supervise the removal of dangerous capabilities like subverting shutdown commands or conducting unauthorized cyberattacks.

Supervise the destruction of artificial superintelligence.

Setting penalties for any person or entity that attempts to violate or circumvent the pauses and prohibitions laid out in this bill. Entities shall be subject to the corporate death penalty, and persons shall be subject to not more than 20 years in prison, which is similar to existing penalties related to unlawfully developing nuclear weapons.

Working to ban superintelligence around the world by setting the international policy of the United States to pursue international agreements, allied coordination, and policies such as export controls to prevent the development of artificial superintelligence anywhere in the world.

title: Castro Statement on Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez
text:
Pearsall, TX — Today, staff from the Office of Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) shared the following statement on behalf of Congressman Castro, after members of his staff and Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35) visited Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez at the South Texas ICE Processing Center (STIPC) in Pearsall, Texas:

"My apologies for not being with you today. An hours-long flight delay kept me from joining Congressman Casar in visiting Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez. As the Congressman for Austin, Wilber's home, Greg's unyielding pursuit of truth and justice in this matter has been admirable. Thank you, Congressman, for that work.

“ICE's treatment of Wilber thus far has amounted to torture. That is not an exaggeration in this case. After being shot in the back and handcuffed without first aid, he was allowed to stay in the hospital for only a few hours before being taken to a detention center while in excruciating pain and made to lie on the floor. The medical facilities at the South Texas ICE Processing Center (STIPC) in Pearsall are not equipped to handle a patient who has experienced that kind of trauma. ICE knew this but took him there anyway. It got so bad that he had to be taken back to the hospital, but again he was allowed to remain only hours before being returned to STIPC. He told ICE agents about his excruciating pain and told them that he could no longer move the left side of his body. Yet they let him suffer with their bullet still in his body.

“This immigrant man, a Venezuelan, fled a regime that President Trump himself declared a terrorist one, just as millions of Venezuelans have fled over the past several years. He had permission to enter the United States and to work. And that's what he was doing when ICE shot him in the back, delivering food for DoorDash to support himself and his family. In fact, he told my staff that he had been working in the area for quite some time and that all the restaurants in the area know him. He also asked my staff to tell his wife and mother that he was doing okay, as not to worry them. This is who ICE is targeting.

“ICE has shot and killed people before, including U.S. citizens, and lied about it. They have discredited themselves. There must be an independent investigation, and the ICE officers who shot Wilber in the back should be held accountable. Finally, this system known as ICE, which has allowed a man to be tortured, should be disbanded.”

title: The Epoch Times article on Smith hearing'Families Call for Release of Loved Ones in China as Xi Visits US'
text:
By Eva Fu

Published September 23, 2026

WASHINGTON—These are the faces that Beijing doesn’t want the world to see.

They are political prisoners, ranging in age from their early 20s to nearly 80, each held behind bars because their beliefs or speech do not align with the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).

Each of them is a father or a mother, a son or a daughter. In the United States and elsewhere, someone is thinking of them, waiting for the day they will be allowed to go home.

Among those waiting are a mother of an 8-year-old, and a daughter undergoing chemotherapy, wishing to hold her father’s hand.

As the U.S.–China summit looms over Washington, advocates see an opening to make that happen.

One phone call to Beijing from the Oval Office, they argue, and these detainees could walk free.

On Capitol Hill, the plight of the political prisoners has galvanized bipartisan lawmakers ahead of the bilateral talks.

House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said at a presser that he believes the “release of the hostages” is on the agenda.

Five Democratic lawmakers have also presented the president with the names of 22 prisoners he could bring up with Chinese counterparts.

Rep. Chris Smith (R-N.J.) hosted two hearings this month championing their cause.

“It’s like that could be me. That could be my wife if she lives in China,” he told The Epoch Times.

“We’re all God’s children. If we don’t raise [this cause], who will?”

Butterfly in the Kitchen

On the kitchen counter of her Florida home, Ziba Murat keeps an embroidered image of a swallowtail butterfly.

It’s a small, tangible piece of Gulshan Abbas, Murat’s reticent mother, who’s now in Chinese jail under a 20-year sentence on terrorism-related charges. The United States has deemed those accusations as unfounded.

Ziba Murat holds a photo of her mother, Dr. Gulshan Abbas, at Murat's home in Virginia in 2024.

Ziba Murat keeps a framed image of a butterfly that was cross-stitched by her mother, jailed political prisoner Dr. Gulshan Abbas, in her kitchen.

It was hard for Murat to connect the person she knows so intimately with the reality of life in prison. Abbas, as Murat remembers, smiled quietly at jokes and embroidered for hours with a patience Murat never possessed.

Even after retiring, Abbas continued to go out of her way to help Uyghur patients, getting up early to meet them at the hospital just so they could see the right doctor and have everything they needed, Murat told The Epoch Times.

Murat misses her. She misses her mother’s humming in the kitchen and the wonderful stir-fries she cooked during the months she spent visiting the United States.

When it was time for Abbas to leave in 2016, Murat wanted her to stay.

She remembers her mother telling her: “I have a 10-year-visa. I can come back anytime I want.”

Murat said she had a sinking feeling as she watched her mother disappear through airport security. That was the last time they saw each other in person.

(L–R) Ziba Murat; her mother, Dr. Gulshan Abbas; and her younger sister Zamira Murat during a 2015 visit to the United States by Abbas, in this file photo.

For the next two years, the two talked on the phone every day. Then in 2018, days after Abbas’s sister Rushan made a public speech denouncing the Party’s mass detention of Uyghurs, Abbas became unreachable. It took two years for her family to learn of her imprisonment and sentencing in a secret trial.

Holding her baby daughter, Murat walked around Congress frantically looking for help. Never a news junkie, she became glued to the screen, scanning for the slightest hint of change in U.S.–China policy.

Guilt gnawed at Murat as she wondered what she could have done, thinking about how she was here in the United States living her life while her mother was suffering in a Chinese jail.

Murat still can’t bring herself to tell the truth to her 8-year-old daughter.

When the girl saw a photo of Rushan holding a photo of Abbas, she asked Murat what was going on.

Murat responded that her grandmother was “very far away” and that they were asking people to bring her back.

Through all these years, Murat said, the girl hasn’t hugged her grandmother. She knows her grandmother through stories, photographs, and the hope that one day they will finally meet.

“That’s the cruelty of transnational repression,” Murat said at a Sept. 16 event on China’s religious freedom. “It did not harm only one person. It steals birthdays. It steals holidays, ordinary family moments that you can never get back.”

Dr. Gulshan Abbas's image is shown during a congressional hearing by the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party titled “The Chinese Communist Party's Ongoing Uyghur Genocide,” in Washington on March 23, 2023.

Ziba Murat with House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) during a visit for the State of the Union address in Washington on Feb. 24, 2026.

Ziba Murat with Rep. John Moolenaar (R-Mich.), head of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, in Washington in March 2026.

A Card From Jail

Alisa Zhou experienced that cruelty when she was around 7 years old.

It was 2000, one year after the Chinese regime went all out against her faith, Falun Gong.

The meditative practice spread widely by word of mouth in the 1990s, reaching an estimated 70 million practitioners by decade’s end. Then, in 1999, the Chinese leadership ordered a full-fledged eradication campaign. Overnight, the practitioners became outlaws.

Zhou was too young to make sense of it all, and her father tried to shield her from the hard reality. When her mother, Wang Youmei, vanished suddenly, he told Zhou that she had gone on a business trip far away.

But the persecution found a way to reach Zhou. After her mother’s arrest, Zhou’s best friend, with whom she walked to and from school every day, stopped playing with her. Then her father took her to an unfamiliar place.

Her mother was there. She handed Zhou a bag of snacks and a handwritten card.

One message is etched into her memory: her mother’s wish that her children “grow up healthy and happy.”

The young Zhou cried as she took in the words. Some time later, she grasped that her mother was in jail.

There were a lot more tears during those nights when Zhou was alone. To encourage herself, she wrote down “truthfulness, compassion, and forbearance”—the three core principles of Falun Gong—and hung it on her bedroom wall.

More than two decades later, the same three words keep Zhou going after her mother’s fifth arrest this April.

She had learned about it while driving to Virginia Beach for a weekend retreat. Back at work on Monday, she burst into tears when her boss greeted her with “How was your weekend?”

Zhou is now an American citizen. But despite living in the free world, the persecution follows her like a shadow, she said.

“There’s not a moment where I can shake it off,” she told The Epoch Times. Whenever she trawls the internet for information on China, she’s haunted by revelations of new arrests and deaths.

Believing in truthfulness, compassion, and forbearance poses no threat to anyone, Zhou said, but if the CCP is out to get someone, “there’s no shortage of excuses.” She said she can’t fathom how a state could turn on its own people.

Neither can Smith, the co-chair of the bicameral Congressional-Executive Commission on China that monitors human rights in the communist country.

“I’ve been in Congress for 46 years. I don’t get it,” he said.

“These [people] are assets to your country. ... This is the salt of the earth—Christian believers, Falun Gong practitioners, the Uyghurs, Tibetan Buddhists. Why would you look to hurt these people?

“Let them thrive, and your nation thrives.”

To Hold a Daughter’s Hand

It’s difficult to know how many political prisoners there are in China. The Chinese regime doesn’t provide such information and asserts that it doesn’t hold them.

A database from human rights nonprofit Dui Hua Foundation, last updated in December 2025, recorded more than 50,000 entries. The Congressional-Executive Commission on China has tracked more than 11,000 cases. Neither comes close to the true number, advocates say.

“It’s millions of people that have to go through that,” Sam Brownback, former ambassador at large for international religious freedom, told The Epoch Times. “These are people that have families like I do, and they’ve just done what they believe is right and stood up for freedom.”

In Hong Kong, the number of political prisoners has also been rising over the six years since Beijing imposed a national security law to crush dissent.

One of the most prominent is Jimmy Lai, founder of one of the largest pro-democracy newspapers in Hong Kong, which folded following a 500-strong police raid in 2021.

His daughter Claire was diagnosed with cancer weeks ago and just started chemotherapy in London.

Lai received the news at the maximum-security prison where he’s serving a 20-year sentence.

At a Sept. 16 hearing highlighting Lai’s case, Claire’s brother Sebastien pleaded for compassionate release so that their father could “sit beside his daughter in her hardest moment” and hold her hand.

“She wants nothing more than to have him with her for this fight,” Sebastien Lai said.

Sebastien Lai said he hears about his father’s health declining every single day.

In a report two days before the hearing, the Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong Foundation found that Hong Kong prison guards have rehearsed Jimmy Lai’s death.

“It’s really scary to hear,” Sebastien Lai said.

The Hong Kong authorities’ actions against his father are a “real disgrace,” he said. “They went through all this kangaroo court show trial and found nothing. His record is unblemished, yet they still keep going.”

The Long Game

Jimmy Lai is one of an estimated 2,000 Hong Kong pro-democracy figures ensnared under the national security law.

Former student leader Joshua Wong is currently awaiting sentencing for “foreign collusion” for lobbying Western lawmakers, and potentially faces life in prison.

For democracy activist Frances Hui, who has a HK$1 million (about $127,000) bounty on her head, the word that comes to mind is “horror.”

“I knew [Wong] when he was 16; I don’t know if he will ever come out alive, or if I will ever be able to see him,” she told The Epoch Times.

Wong was already serving a four-year, eight-month prison term. Seven months before Wong was due to be released, prosecutors began a second trial.

“They waited until the very end to come up with this charge. It’s just so apparent that they are trying to keep him behind bars for as long as they can,” Hui said.

The two met when they were both teenagers campaigning for Hong Kong’s democratic freedoms. Wong, in Hui’s telling, had a lot of energy, taking interviews even while on hunger strike and physically frail.

“He inspires so many of us,” Hui said, suggesting that the Party authorities are acting out of fear.

“They are afraid that if he gets out next year, he will create something that they can’t control.”

The regime is playing the long game, she said, betting that over time, the outside world will “forget the prisoners as they slowly go quiet.”

The families of the prisoners fear forgetting, too.

At a recent human rights panel, Uyghur lawyer Rayhan Asat held up a photo of her brother, Ekpar, who was detained upon returning from a 2016 U.S. exchange program.

They had seen each other that March. She was studying at Harvard Law School and expecting to see him at her graduation ceremony in two months. She regrets not taking many videos of them together. After 10 years of separation, it’s now difficult to imagine what he sounds like.

“That’s a very painful thought,” she said.

Hope for a Miracle

The release of Pastor Ezra Jin in July is helping to keep their hopes alive.

After nearly nine months in custody, the Zion Church leader walked onto a plane bound for the United States and was reunited with his family.

Chinese authorities charged him with fraud and illegal business operations—allegations frequently used to prosecute religious activities in China. They told him they could imprison him for 15 years but would be lenient if he pleaded guilty. He refused.

On July 3, he was pulled from prison and sent in an empty train car to the airport. Even after stepping onto the plane, Jin said, he had no idea where he was going. He had no paperwork or visa.

He arrived on July 4—America’s 250th birthday. It felt like a dream. The previous day, he was a prisoner. The following evening, he was sitting by the seaside, watching fireworks with family he hadn’t seen in eight years.

Many had thought it was mission impossible, he said, as he accepted an award in July celebrating his freedom. He thanked Trump and many human rights advocates for their support.

“When we stand together, changes do happen,” he said.

This article was published on September 23, 2026 and can be found online at:

title: On the eve of Trump-Xi meeting in Washington, D.C.Capitol Hill hearing features heartfelt appeals to Xi Jinping: let these wonderful people go
text:
At yesterday’s Capitol Hill hearing chaired by Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ), lawmakers heard compelling, emotional testimony about the people imprisoned and persecuted by the Chinese government, the families and religious communities working for their freedom, and the retaliation faced by those who speak out on their behalf in China.

“Behind every statistic about political prisoners is a person with hopes and dreams, and a life filled with isolation and pain. Behind every person in a Chinese prison is a family waiting, praying, and hoping that someone will not forget them. And behind many of those families is an entire community that feels threatened and intimidated,” Smith said during his opening remarks.

“Today, we appeal to Xi Jinping to release women and men of conscience and goodness—as a tangible good faith expression of good will, benevolence, respect, and strength. We appeal to Xi Jinping’s heart,” continued Smith, the Co-Chair of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China (CECC).

“We again ask President Trump—who helped Pastor Ezra Jin gain his freedom—to appeal to Xi Jinping to show compassion and courage.”

At the hearing—entitled “The Faces of Repression: Prisoners, Families, and Communities Targeted by the CCP”—members of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China (CECC) heard from multiple highly anticipated witnesses, including Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri, the founder and pastor of China’s underground Zion Church, who was recently released from Chinese detention after spending more than 260 days in custody.

During the first panel of witnesses, Pastor Jin—accompanied by his daughter and translator, Grace Jin Drexel—testified before Congress for the first time since his long-awaited release in July. Pastor Jin described the persecution, harassment, and intimidation inflicted upon his church and congregants by the Chinese government, explaining that “the government put pressure on the landlords to terminate our leases, police came to stop church activities and demanded that attendees register their ID cards, [and] police came and cut off the water and power of our meeting place.”

Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri and his daughter and translator, Grace Jin Drexel, testify before the CECC at their September 22nd hearing.

Eventually, after years of relentless harassment, the Chinese government “mobilized several hundred police to forcibly shut down the Zion Church sanctuary, and the congregation was scattered,” according to Pastor Jin. Zion Church’s services were then moved to online platforms, such as Zoom, where their number of congregants only grew.

Shortly thereafter, however, Pastor Jin and other church leaders were arrested and detained by Chinese authorities on the bogus charge of “illegal use of the internet.” The charges were later changed to “illegal business operations” and “fraud.”

“During detention, our basic rights were severely restricted. We were not able to have normal correspondence with our families. The only channel for communicating with the outside world was through lawyers,” said Pastor Jin.

“On July 3, without any notice whatsoever, I was taken out of the detention center and brought to Guangzhou Airport, where the prosecutor’s office withdrew the indictment against me, and I was put on a plane bound for the United States,” he continued. “It was only through the U.S. Embassy’s consular officer that I learned this happened because President Trump had specifically requested my release from President Xi Jinping during his visit to China!”

Concluding his testimony, Pastor Jin called upon U.S. Congress to “continue to pay attention to religious persecution and human rights within China,” and he expressed hope that “this meeting between the two heads of state can produce genuine consensus and breakthroughs in improving China’s human rights situation and ending the persecution of religious believers.”

The hearing’s second panel contained other high-profile witnesses, including Nelson Wells Sr., the father of detained American citizen Nelson Wells Jr.; Tim Hunt, the brother of detained American citizen Dawn Michelle Hunt; Rushan Abbas, the sister of detained Chinese political prisoner Dr. Gulshan Abbas and the founder and Executive Director of the Campaign for Uyghurs; and Erping Zhang, a spokesperson for Falun Gong and the Director of Government and Advocacy at the Falun Dafa Information Center.

Nelson Wells Jr., an American citizen from Louisiana, was arrested in China in 2014 and sentenced to 22 years in prison after being duped by a so-called friend into carrying bags allegedly containing narcotics. “For that one mistake—that one betrayal, his life, his wife’s life, his children’s lives, and our lives will never be the same,” said Nelson Wells Sr.

Nelson Wells Sr., the father of detained American citizen Nelson Wells Jr., speaks to lawmakers at the CECC's September 22nd hearing.

Testifying before the Commission, Wells Sr. described his son’s declining health, as well as the abusive treatment he endures while in prison:

“Over the years, Nelson has been targeted as one of the few Americans and the only Black American in the prison, which has exposed him to harsher treatment and sometimes physical attack. He has suffered from debilitating chronic pain, seizures (a Chinese MRI report shows he has brain atrophy), malnutrition, internal issues, dental pain, severe depression and thoughts of self-harm… And now, as of a few weeks ago, we discovered that he has been diagnosed with Hepatitis C—the news of which has devastated Nelson and our family.”

Through tears, Wells Sr. continued, “We need President Donald Trump, our President, a father himself, to personally advocate on Nelson’s behalf to President Xi when the two meet this week. We have come a long way and are at the last mile. We believe that he—and perhaps only he—can bring Nelson, can bring Dawn home.

“When our country asked us to serve, my wife and I did so unreservedly and without hesitation. I even served hardship posts, including during the Gulf War. President Trump, now I am asking for your help—father to father—on behalf of my child. He is a man, but as every parent here knows, he is still my child, and I cannot leave him behind. I am asking you also not to leave him—an American citizen—behind,” he concluded.

Tim Hunt—whose sister, Dawn, an American citizen from Chicago, was also arrested in China in 2014 and sentenced to life imprisonment after being lured into a fraudulent sweepstakes scheme—spoke powerfully and movingly about the hardships his sister and his family have endured since her arrest.

“She has aged dramatically. Her posture is that of someone much older. She is slumped over. She is frail. Her teeth have yellowed and shifted. Her hair is much grayer than it was just two years ago. Those are the things I could see,” said Hunt.

Hunt revealed that in January, Gene Hunt—his and Dawn’s father—sadly passed away at 92 years old, “with his only daughter still in prison.”

Tim Hunt, the brother of detained American citizen Dawn Michelle Hunt, speaks to lawmakers at the CECC's September 22nd hearing.

“Our father died knowing that his little girl was incarcerated. Dawn was not home when he died. She could not be there with him. He could not tell her that he loved her one last time. He could not see her one last time. He could not give her words of encouragement. He could not help her prepare for a life of freedom. And he could not be there for her if she struggled after twelve years of incarceration,” stated Hunt.

Towards the end of his testimony, Hunt urged lawmakers to push for and secure Dawn’s and Nelson’s releases: “Please use your voices. Please ask President Trump to ask President Xi to release Dawn. And please ask for the release of Nelson Wells Jr. as well… I need help for the average American. The two-job American. The three-job American. The American who served his country with honor and pride.”

Rushan Abbas, a prominent Uyghur activist, discussed how her sister, Dr. Gulshan Abbas, was punished by the Chinese government for Rushan’s advocacy in the United States. “I come before you first and foremost as a sister to an innocent woman who has been jailed in China for the past 8 years in retaliation for my advocacy in the U.S. as an Uyghur American,” said Rushan.

“Her imprisonment is a blatant act of transnational repression—an attempt to punish me for speaking the truth and to send a chilling message to Uyghurs everywhere: speak out, and your family will pay the price,” she continued.

“But Beijing’s cruelty did not silence me. It transformed the course of my life. I walked away from my professional career and became a full-time advocate for my people, determined to turn the pain they inflicted on my family into a relentless fight for freedom, justice, and accountability.”

Abbas urged Congress to pass three bills authored and introduced by Rep. Smith—the Transnational Repression Policy Act (HR 4829), the Stop Forced Organ Harvesting Act of 2025 (HR 1503), and the Uyghur Genocide Accountability and Sanctions Act of 2025 (HR 4830)—which, together, would strengthen the United States’ framework for addressing, preventing, and prosecuting many of China’s human rights abuses.

Witnesses Rushan Abbas and Erping Zhang speak at the CECC's hearing, "The Faces of Repression: Prisoners, Families, and Communities Targeted by the CCP."

Erping Zhang, a spokesperson and advocate for Falun Gong—a spiritual practice in the Buddhist tradition that has been the subject of decades-long persecution and repression at the hands of the CCP—echoed Abbas’ recommendations and urged the United States to continue speaking up for Falun Gong practitioners.

“The Party has tried all means to bankrupt us, to silence us, and to delegitimize us… What it has done to Falun Gong is one of the most comprehensive demonstrations available of how the Party behaves when it believes it is threatened,” said Zhang.

“It is therefore one of the best available predictors of how it will behave toward the United States which the CCP regards as its ultimate adversary. We believe that Falun Gong matters, more than ever, to China, to the United States, and to the world, and thus hope the CCP’s repression of our community can receive the attention it deserves,” he concluded.

Throughout the hearing, Rep. Smith and various witnesses raised the importance of his bipartisan Nelson Wells Jr. and Dawn Michelle Hunt Unjustly Detained in Communist China Act (HR 5491), which would mandate a coordinated U.S. government response to the unjust imprisonment of American citizens in China—and the use of family members as hostages to silence or punish American citizens critical of the CCP.

“The bill would strengthen the government’s ability to identify Americans unjustly detained in China, coordinate their cases, engage with their families, pursue humanitarian releases and prisoner transfers, and identify additional tools for holding responsible Chinese officials accountable,” said Smith.

“Because when an American is unjustly detained, that person’s family should not have to navigate the Chinese Communist Party’s system alone.”

title: The Epoch Times article on Smith hearing'"Bring Them Home": Americans Push to Free Loved Ones Jailed in China'
text:
By Eva Fu

Published September 23, 2026

WASHINGTON—With the U.S.–China summit approaching, Americans who have loved ones detained in China are pleading with President Donald Trump not to forget them.

One of them is 20-year U.S. Army veteran Nelson Wells, whose son, Nelson Wells Jr., has been in Chinese prison for 12 years on charges that the family says are dubious.

At a hearing held by the Congressional-Executive Commission on China on Sept. 22, Wells appealed to the U.S. president “father to father.”

Weeks ago, his son was diagnosed with hepatitis C. He is set to be released in 2041. But with Wells Jr.’s deteriorating health, including chronic pain, high blood pressure, diabetes, and seizures, Wells said he’s not sure whether his son could last that long.

“He’s sick. His family has suffered. There’s no justice in allowing him to die in prison,” Wells said.

He said Wells Jr.’s daughter, now 12, “has never seen her father outside photographs” and prays at night “for someone who can bring him home.”

Trump can be that someone, he said.

Rep. Chris Smith (R-N.J.), who hosted the hearing, agreed that the United States cannot look away.

Freeing political prisoners needs to be on the U.S.–China summit agenda, he told The Epoch Times.

“It has to be—period,” he said.

The congressman said he hopes the president can convey “a sense of urgency and compassion” for “these suffering individuals.”

Seated next to Wells at the witness table was Tim Hunt, whose sister, Dawn Michelle Hunt, like Wells’s son, was arrested in China in 2014 for alleged drug smuggling. Both families deny the accusations.

While visiting his sister in July, Hunt said, he didn’t recognize the sibling he had last seen two years ago.

“She has aged dramatically. Her posture is that of someone much older. She is slumped over,” he said. He noticed how her teeth had yellowed and shifted, and how her hair had grayed.

When they met, he said, she kept asking when she would be freed, and he couldn’t give her an answer.

In January, their father passed away at age 92.

“He lived a long life before he died, with his only daughter still in prison,” Hunt said, tears rolling down his face. “He could not see her one last time.”

Wells put his arm around Hunt while wiping off his own tears.

His deepest hope is to “bring them home alive, and bring them home this year,” Wells said.

‘Can’t Delay It Further’

More than 200 Americans are currently detained in China, according to the Dui Hua Foundation, a human rights group focused on the country.

The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has also heavily suppressed religious and ethnic minority groups, such as Uyghurs, Christians, and practitioners of the spiritual practice Falun Gong, subjecting them to arbitrary arrests, harsh sentences, and other forms of abuse.

Those imprisoned include many who have families in America.

Rushan Abbas, executive director at Campaign for Uyghurs, described the case of her sister, Gulshan Abbas, as an example of the CCP’s transnational repression.

Gulshan Abbas disappeared days after Rushan Abbas spoke in public about the mass detention and torture of Uyghurs in China’s Xinjiang region. The former was sentenced to 20 years in prison in a secret trial.

“Behind every statistic is a human being, a family torn apart, and a voice the CCP is trying to silence,” Rushan Abbas said.

Erping Zhang, a spokesperson for Falun Gong, noted the case of Alisa Zhou, a Maryland accountant in the audience whose mother has been detained in China since April.

Her mother’s arrest followed months of covert Chinese police surveillance of two Falun Gong study groups, Zhang noted in his written testimony.

American Grace Chen, who’s in the U.S. Army, was a teenager when the Chinese authorities arrested her parents in 2020. Only after their release in 2025 did Chen learn about the “horrors” that her father experienced, Zhang said at the hearing. Chen’s father was denied sleep, scalded with hot water, and forced to drink urine, according to Zhang.

Her parents are still in China.

Trump in July helped Pastor Ezra Jin of Beijing’s Zion Church gain his freedom. Jin also testified at the hearing, with his daughter, Grace Jin Drexel, as the translator.

He said later in an interview that he considers the upcoming meeting between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping to be the best shot to raise the political prisoners’ case.

“We can’t delay it further,” Jin said. He added that he hopes the freedom he enjoys can soon extend to many others who still don’t have it—including eight church fellows arrested at the same time as him in October 2025 and two Light of Zion Church leaders, Gao Quanfu and his wife, Pang Yu.

Wells has about 10 minutes of call time with his jailed son each month. He has saved this month’s allotment for after the summit, hoping to deliver some good news, he told The Epoch Times.

Hunt said he is cautiously hopeful. Speaking slowly at the hearing, he told the audience that if his sister and Wells’s son can’t come home at the same time, he hopes that Wells’s son gets the priority.

“He still has a mother and a father that are alive. He still has that family that can support him. He needs that,” Hunt said.

title: The Epoch Times article on Smith hearing'Congress Warned About Beijing's Repression on US Soil'
text:
By Eva Fu

Published September 23, 2026

WASHINGTON—The Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP’s) sweeping repression targeting one faith group is creating a challenge to the United States and allowing Beijing to expand its toolbox to persecute other communities, a Falun Gong spokesperson testified to Congress.

Erping Zhang described a wide spectrum of Beijing-linked tactics targeting the spiritual community, playing out in America—including assault, anonymous violent threats, spying, disinformation, and frivolous lawsuits.

The tactics can be used against “any group the CCP decides is a problem,” Zhang told the Congressional-Executive Commission on China on Sept. 22.

“The regime’s actions undermine the basic rights of Americans and the rule of law,” he said in his written testimony.

“The impact of this activity reaches far beyond our own community, creating a playbook of tactics that the regime can use against other targets while undermining U.S. democracy, freedom, and sovereignty.”

Zhang pointed to a June report by the Falun Dafa Information Center, which identified more than 600 cases of transnational repression incidents across 30 states.

Falun Gong practitioners have faced these threats for simply practicing their faith in the United States, Zhang said.

Falun Gong, also known as Falun Dafa, is a meditation practice with spiritual teachings based on the core tenets of truthfulness, compassion, and forbearance. In the 1990s, 70 million to 100 million people began practicing, with many crediting Falun Gong for uplifting their physical and mental well-being. In 1999, the Chinese communist regime marked it for eradication.

Organizations monitoring the persecution have verified thousands of deaths, which they say represent a drop in the ocean.

Between March and April, nearly 800 practitioners in China reported experiencing harassment, arrest, or house raids, according to Minghui.org, a clearinghouse for such information. The oldest of them was 94.

Since 1999, Falun Gong practitioners have been “detained by the millions, tortured, sexually abused, forced into producing goods that reached American shelves, subjected to forced organ harvesting,” Zhang said. “That apparatus was later turned onto the Uyghurs.”

Several Chinese officials hit with U.S. sanctions for repressing Uyghurs in China’s Xinjiang region have a history of persecuting Falun Gong, an Epoch Times review of their records found.

Rep. Chris Smith (R-N.J.), who chaired the congressional hearing, noted that the repression doesn’t end at the prison gate.

To see “spiritual disciplines like Falun Gong suffer so horribly in China underscores that we have to do more, not less,” he said.

Be it Falun Gong practitioners, Christians, or Uyghurs, Smith said, “they are the best citizens imaginable.”

“Very often, they have a code of conduct that’s written on their hearts,” he told The Epoch Times. “Why wouldn’t you want more of that? I don’t get it.”

Beyond China, the Falun Gong community has become a top target for the regime’s “unrestricted war” against religious freedom, Zhang said in his written testimony.

In 2023, the Department of Justice charged two Chinese agents for trying to bribe an IRS official to act on a fake whistleblower complaint against Shen Yun Performing Arts, a New York-based arts company founded by Falun Gong practitioners. John Chen, one of the alleged agents acting under Chinese authorities’ orders, stated his goal was to help the regime “topple” Falun Gong, according to court documents. Both Chen and the other Chinese national pleaded guilty.

Since March 2024, more than 300 anonymous death threats and bomb threats linked to Chinese individuals have been sent, targeting Falun Gong and Shen Yun, as well as lawmakers supportive of Falun Gong, and several civil institutions, according to Falun Dafa Information Center.

The center also counted dozens of cases in which individuals impersonated Falun Gong practitioners to make fake threats.

In late January, foreign influence research group Graphika flagged a cluster of websites linked to Chinese companies that push Beijing’s propaganda overseas while masquerading as legitimate Western media, corroborating an Epoch Times report finding similar operations on X.

Zhang said Falun Gong has long served as a target of Beijing’s repression tactics.

title: Courtney Responds to GAO Report on Submarine Repairs
text:
NORWICH, CT – Today, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, issued the following statement after sending a letter to his colleagues on the Armed Services Committee in response to the recent Government Accountability Office (GAO) report on Navy submarine repairs. “I agree that the past track record of submarine repairs is unsatisfactory and that GAO’s recommendation to create more efficient ways to decommission submarines without interfering with maintenance of operational submarines is extremely helpful,” Courtney said. “My letter to my colleagues on the Armed Services Committee includes more up-to-date information regarding of the latest inventory of Virginia-class submarines and corrects the report’s omission of Seawolf submarines, which, as the original follow-on to the Los Angeles-class fleet, are a premier cohort the U.S submarine attack fleet.

“My letter also noted that because of Congress’ swift authorization of the AUKUS security agreement, the U.S. Navy’s submarine fleet will have new intermediate repair capacity forward-deployed in the Indo-Pacific at a new repair facility in Western Australia. title: Rep. Crane’s House-Passed Border Tunnel Bill Gains Momentum with Senate Companion
text:
On March 10, 2025, the House of Representatives passed the Subterranean Border Defense Act, legislation introduced by Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) and Rep. Lou Correa (D-CA) to strengthen congressional oversight of illicit cross-border tunnels. The bill earned strong bipartisan support with a 402-1 vote on the House floor.

Last week, Sen. Rick Scott (R-FL) introduced a companion bill in the Senate, marking key progress in the effort.

Since 1990, law enforcement has discovered more than 200 illicit tunnels along the southwest border. Transnational criminal organizations rely on these passages to smuggle drugs, weapons, currency, and people.

Earlier this year, a Homeland Security Task Force investigation uncovered a nearly 2,000-foot tunnel stretching from Tijuana to a storefront near the Otay Mesa Port of Entry and reaching a depth of 55 feet. The operation led to the seizure of more than a ton of cocaine valued at an estimated $45 million. Rep. Crane believes that as enforcement above ground drives down unlawful entries, traffickers and cartels will continue to adapt by turning to unconventional methods of evading frontline personnel.

The Subterranean Border Defense Act builds on Section 7134 of the Fiscal Year 2023 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). That provision directed the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), in coordination with the Department of Homeland Security’s Under Secretary for Science and Technology, to develop a strategic plan to counter illicit cross-border tunnel operations. Under the law, the plan was required to address the following:

Setting risk-based criteria to prioritize the identification, breach, assessment, and remediation of tunnels

Promoting innovative technologies to carry out that work while reducing the impact on surrounding communities

Establishing processes for sharing tunnel location, operations, and technical information

Providing Border Patrol sector chiefs with periodic indicators of the tunnel types found in their sectors to educate field personnel

Assessing technology and staffing needs, including position descriptions, specialized skills, and full-time personnel levels by Border Patrol sector for counter-tunnel operations

However, the NDAA required CBP to report to Congress on the plan’s implementation only once. Rep. Crane’s bill would close this gap by converting that one-time requirement into an annual one. The legislation would direct CBP to submit a report to the House Committee on Homeland Security and the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs every year. As a result, lawmakers would receive regular updates on CBP’s efforts to counter tunnels infiltrating the United States, allowing them to craft policy based on the latest findings rather than outdated information.

title: Congressman Deluzio Celebrates Federal Funds for Next-Generation Cancer Treatment Research Based in O’Hara Township
text:
CARNEGIE, PA — Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) announced that the U.S. Department of Health & Human Services has awarded a $306,756 grant to KaliVir Immunotherapeutics of O’Hara Township, PA for cancer treatment research. This federal funding is a Small Business Innovation Research Grant (SBIR) – Phase II from the National Cancer Institute.

KaliVir Immunotherapeutics develops next-generation, viral-based therapies (oncolytic viruses) that both directly destroy tumor cells as well as attract and activate an anti-tumor immune response.

“I’m proud to announce federal funding to support cutting-edge research for cancer treatment right here in Western PA,” said Congressman Deluzio. “KaliVir does life-saving work—and I’m excited to see the discoveries they make with this grant.”

“KaliVir Immunotherapeutics is grateful to Congressman Duluzio and his colleagues for voting to restore funding for the SBIR program,” said KaliVir’s Chief Executive Officer Helena Chaye, PhD, JD. “The STEALTH-001 study is a first-in-human, open-label, Phase 1/1b dose-escalation and expansion trial evaluating VET3-TGI, both as a monotherapy and in combination with atezolizumab in patients with pathologically confirmed, advanced, unresectable or metastatic solid tumors. The SBIR award will allow KaliVir to further strengthen the scientific foundation of our programs, and the full amount of the grant will directly impact the economy in the greater Pittsburgh area.”America's Seed Fund, including funding for SBIR Phase II Grants, provides technology-focused entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses with funding to develop their ideas and a pathway to commercialization. Powered by a network of federal agencies, entrepreneur support organizations, and the Small Business Administration (SBA), America's Seed Fund advances federal missions and fosters a culture of innovation in the United States.

The Trump Administration’s efforts to freeze funding and pause federal grants has created significant uncertainty for grantees, varying by agency and program. As of now, courts have paused many of these freezes. However, Congressman Deluzio’s office will continue to monitor these developments and fight to make sure this congressionally authorized funding keeps going to projects that make life better for Western Pennsylvanians. If you are the recipient of a federal grant and have been notified that this funding is no longer available to you or are experiencing other issues accessing your lawfully appropriated funds, please share your concerns with Congressman Deluzio’s office at PA17Grants@mail.house.gov.

title: Fedorchak, Majority Leader Scalise highlight North Dakota's role in strengthening America’s defense supply chain
text:
Fargo, ND — Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak (R-ND) welcomed U.S. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-LA) to Fargo Tuesday for a tour of Badland Batteries’ new battery-cell manufacturing facility and a discussion about strengthening domestic manufacturing, reducing reliance on foreign supply chains, and supporting America’s national defense.

Fedorchak and Scalise toured the company’s new 80,000-square-foot plant, viewed its completed production line, and received an update from Packet Digital CEO Terri Zimmerman on the company’s plans to increase production. The Fargo facility will manufacture battery cells for use in Packet Digital battery packs that power unmanned aircraft systems, autonomous systems, and other defense and commercial technologies.

“North Dakota is proving that the advanced technologies essential to America’s economic and national security can be developed and manufactured right here at home,” Fedorchak said. “The batteries produced at this Fargo facility will power unmanned and autonomous systems used by our military while helping reduce our dangerous reliance on foreign supply chains. I’m grateful to Leader Scalise for coming to North Dakota to see this exciting work and to Terri Zimmerman and the entire Packet Digital team for investing, innovating, and creating new opportunities in our state.”

“It was great to join Congresswoman Fedorchak and see firsthand the cutting-edge work happening at Packet Digital,” said Scalise. “For too long, America allowed so much of our manufacturing base to move overseas, including technologies that are critical to our national security. Packet Digital is helping reverse that trend by building these advanced batteries right here in Fargo, while creating good jobs for North Dakota families. We need more American companies making these investments, creating good jobs, and ensuring the United States continues to lead the world in innovation.”

Packet Digital is a Fargo-based technology company specializing in batteries and power systems for unmanned aircraft and autonomous systems. The company established Badland Batteries in 2023 and selected the north Fargo site for its battery-cell manufacturing facility in 2024. Badland Batteries launched its first commercial unmanned aircraft system battery products in 2025.

Fedorchak previously toured the facility in September 2025 while it was under development. Tuesday’s visit offered an opportunity to see the completed plant and production line ahead of its grand opening on October 8.

title: Hoeven, Fedorchak introduce legislation extending FCHIP to improve health care in rural areas
text:
WASHINGTON – Senator John Hoeven (R-N.D.) and Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak (R-N.D.) today introduced legislation to extend the Frontier Community Health Integration Project (FCHIP) for five years. The FCHIP program develops and tests health care delivery and reimbursement models for Critical Access Hospitals (CAH) in hyper-rural counties to improve health outcomes for patients and save Medicare costs. In the Senate, the legislation is cosponsored by Senators Kevin Cramer (R-N.D.), Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.) and Steve Daines (R-Mont.).

Currently there are five CAHs participating in the program, including the following North Dakota CAHs:

Jacobson Memorial Hospital Care Center in Elgin.

McKenzie County Healthcare Systems in Watford City.

Southwest Healthcare Services in Bowman.

“Critical Access Hospitals play a key role in ensuring that North Dakotans, regardless of their zip code, have improved access and better health care services. Our bicameral legislation extends this demonstration program for five years to help strengthen the care available to Medicare beneficiaries in rural areas while helping find ways to save on Medicare costs,” said Senator Hoeven.

“North Dakotans should be able to get quality care close to home, even in our most rural of communities,” said Congresswoman Fedorchak. “Critical Access Hospitals are lifelines for rural families. Extending FCHIP will give participating hospitals more flexibility to provide skilled nursing care, expand telehealth, and sustain ambulance services. I’m glad to partner with Senator Hoeven on a practical way to strengthen rural health care while testing ways to save Medicare dollars.”

“For families across rural America, having access to a local health care provider can make all the difference,” said Senator Cramer. “But low patient volumes and government restrictions can make it difficult for rural hospitals to keep their doors open and provide the care their communities need. Our bill to extend the FCHIP Demonstration will give rural hospitals greater flexibility to deliver essential services and help preserve access to quality health care for families in rural North Dakota.”

“Since 2016, the Frontier Community Health Integration Project (FCHIP) has provided Montana’s Critical Access Hospitals with unique flexibility, allowed them to implement critical innovations, and improved access to and quality of care in rural areas. By keeping some of our most rural hospitals afloat through innovative payment models that enable community-based care, the program has served Montanans that might otherwise be overlooked. I strongly support extending FCHIP and am proud to cosponsor this crucial legislation,” said Senator Sheehy.

“Montanans deserve access to top-quality health care, no matter where they live. Oftentimes, our rural communities face challenges in delivering that care- that’s why I’m proud to work with Senator Hoeven to extend the Frontier Community Health Integration Program (FCHIP) which will help Montana’s Critical Access Hospitals continue to test new ways to ensure access to high quality care in rural communities,” said Senator Daines.

Specifically, FCHIP provides a waiver to Medicare payment rules that allows hospitals to increase the number of available Skilled Nursing Facility or Nursing Facility beds, cover the costs required to facilitate and grow telehealth programs and pay the expenses of providing ambulance services at each participating Critical Access Hospital.

The legislation is endorsed by the National Rural Health Association, North Dakota Hospital Association, and the Montana Hospital Association.

title: Congressman Chuck Fleischmann Applauds $2.5 Million for Tennessee Wesleyan University’s Health Science, STEM Education
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Chuck Fleischmann (TN-03) is proud to announce that he has secured $2,500,000 in federal funding for Tennessee Wesleyan University to enhance its Health Science and STEM education programs. The funding will support major renovations, and equipment upgrades at the university’s Fisher Hall of Science in Athens, Tennessee.

“This $2.5 million investment is about building a brighter future for East Tennessee,” said Congressman Fleischmann. “Modernizing Fisher Hall of Science empowers our students, including many from first-generation and underserved backgrounds, to excel and launch successful careers right here at home. These graduates are essential to meeting the workforce needs in advanced manufacturing, nuclear technologies, and artificial intelligence, vital to our region’s economic growth. This is a win for our students and for our region’s future.”

The project will modernize the 30,000-square-foot Fisher Hall of Science, which has not been significantly updated since its completion in 1968. Planned improvements include new flooring, laboratory countertops, HVAC system upgrades, network cabling, and advanced scientific equipment. The initiative will also provide faculty training and implement systems to track student progress from enrollment through job placement.

With these enhancements, Tennessee Wesleyan University aims to increase student enrollment and research participation in biology, chemistry, and environmental science, while also improving student outcomes such as graduation rates and job placements. The upgrades will particularly benefit first-generation and low-income students who rely on the university’s science programs, as well as regional employers seeking a pipeline of highly skilled graduates.

title: Fong Announces Over $34 Million for Central Valley Water Projects
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) announced that over $34 million in federal grants has been awarded to two Central Valley water projects. The South Valley Conveyance and Storage Project (South Valley Project) in Kern County will receive $25 million and the Seaborn Reservoir Project in Tulare County will receive $9.28 million. Both grants come from the Bureau of Reclamation's Small Storage Grant Program.

Congressman Fong led a letter with Congressman David Valadao in May 2026 urging the Bureau of Reclamation to fund the critical South Valley Project. The two also wrote an earlier letter in February 2026 requesting the Bureau include $25 million for the project in its FY2027 budget request.

"Water is life in the Central Valley, and this investment of $34 million is vital for our farms, businesses, and families," said Congressman Fong. "These projects will expand water storage, improve groundwater levels, and give our region the tools it needs to capture and store water so that it is available when communities need it most. The Central Valley feeds America, and this funding is integral in helping us continue putting food on families’ plates across the country."

“Today’s critical funding means we will be able to break ground on the South Valley Conveyance and Storage Project,” said Paul Cook, General Manager of the Irvine Ranch Water District, and Dan Bartel, General Manager of the Rosedale – Rio Bravo Water Storage District. “The Project will create 375 cubic feet per second of new conveyance capacity from the California Aqueduct across the San Joaquin Valley to new and existing groundwater banking facilities to capture water in wet years. We want to thank the Bureau of Reclamation for recognizing the water supply benefits this project provides to both the Central and Southern California, and our Congressional delegation for helping to secure the funding to move this water reliability project forward. We also want to specifically thank Rep. Fong and Rep. Valadao for their leadership and steadfast support for this project that will improve water conveyance and storage for the entire region.”

“The Tulare Irrigation District’s receipt of funding from the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation for the Seaborn Reservoir Project marks a major milestone in securing a more reliable and sustainable water future for the Central Valley,” said Aaron Fukuda, General Manager, Tulare Irrigation District. “We are grateful to our staff, consultants, congressional partners, and the Bureau of Reclamation for their tireless efforts and shared commitment to moving this critical project forward. Seaborn Reservoir is more than an investment in water storage—it is an investment in the farms, jobs, and communities that sustain our region. Regional storage projects like Seaborn are essential to strengthening water supply reliability, achieving groundwater sustainability, and ensuring that our agricultural communities remain vibrant and productive for generations to come.”

California's farmers supply 40% of the United States' fruits and vegetables, meaning reliable water infrastructure in the Central Valley and across the state is a food security and national security imperative. Both the South Valley Project and Seaborn Reservoir Project will create additional groundwater sources and new conveyance facilities to boost storage capacity, enhance flood flow capture, increase water supply reliability during drought periods and times of emergency, and improve long-term water sustainability in the region.

This funding builds on Congressman Fong’s long-standing commitment to Central Valley water. Since being elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, he has:

Secured $1 billion in western water infrastructure funding in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, with $540 million going specifically to California dams, canals, and water projects.

Secured $5 million to combat invasive golden mussels in the FY2027 Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Bill.
