title: Rep. Craig Cosponsors Bipartisan Legislation to Reform America’s Immigration System, Hold ICE Accountable
text:
EAGAN, MN – Today, U.S. Representative Angie Craig officially cosponsored bipartisan legislation that would make meaningful reforms to our country’s broken immigration system.

The DIGNITY Act would grant legal status and protections to certain undocumented immigrants, reform the asylum screening process to provide legal options for asylum seekers, invest in border security and modernize ports of entry, create new regional processing centers for asylum seekers, mandate accountability for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and provide a pathway to citizenship for our country’s Dreamers.

The DIGNITY Act was originally introduced by Reps. Veronica Escobar (D-TX) and Maria Elvira Salazar (R-FL).

“America is a country of immigrants, yet for too long, our broken immigration system has made it too hard for folks who come to this country looking for a better life to stay here,” said Rep. Craig. “It’s time to create a humane immigration system that actually works and provide a pathway to legal status for those who work, pay taxes and contribute to our economy. I’m proud to support this critical bill, which makes meaningful reforms to our immigration system without compromising our communities’ safety and security. It’s a win-win”

Rep. Craig has always advocated for a legal pathway to citizenship for our nation’s Dreamers and Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipients. She has repeatedly cosponsored the bipartisan American Dream and Promise Act, which would provide a pathway to citizenship to Dreamers, recipients of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) and Deferred Enforced Departure (DED) beneficiaries. She is also a cosponsor of the America’s Children Act, which would provide a pathway to legal permanent residency for individuals who were brought to the U.S.as children and have since graduated from an institution of higher education.

Rep. Craig has also been a fervent defender of the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program in the face of President Trump’s repeated attacks on TPS holders.

In July, she introduced the Temporary Protected Status Review Act, which would require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to follow a clear, evidence-based process before terminating TPS and allow Congress to reverse TPS terminations under the Congressional Review Act.

title: Rep. Crockett Demands Abbott Release Texas Maternal Mortality Report Before the Midterms
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett (TX-30) called on Texas Governor Greg Abbott, Texas Department of State Health Services Interim Commissioner Imelda Garcia, and Texas Maternal Mortality and Morbidity Review Committee Presiding Officer Dr. Carla Ortique to immediately release Texas’s latest maternal mortality report, warning that withholding these findings until after the midterm elections would prevent Texans from the opportunity to examine the state’s maternal health record before casting their ballots.

“Texas mothers are dying, and instead of giving us answers, Abbott’s administration is hiding that data, right before the midterms,” said Crockett.

In her letter, Crockett cites recent research documenting worsening maternal health outcomes following the enactment of Senate Bill 8 in 2021, which effectively banned abortion after six weeks of pregnancy. The letter also highlights the state’s decision to forgo analysis of pregnancy-related deaths during the two years immediately following the law’s enactment.

Recent independent analyses cited in the letter found significant increases in serious pregnancy complications following Texas’s abortion restrictions, including increases in sepsis among women hospitalized during second-trimester pregnancy loss, emergency room visits for early miscarriage, and blood transfusions during miscarriage-related emergency room visits.

“As the most uninsured state in the country, Texas is already failing women — especially our mothers. And burying that truth to silence families' stories does not erase their reality. Texans deserve the truth. They deserve transparency. And this administration has a legal obligation to give it to them,” said Crockett.

With early voting scheduled to begin October 19, Crockett called on state officials to release the MMMRC’s findings without further delay and fulfill the committee’s statutory responsibility to examine pregnancy-related deaths and help prevent maternal deaths in Texas.

The full letter can be found here.

title: Davids, Cole Introduce Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Survivors of Indian Boarding Schools
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representatives Sharice Davids (D-KS-03) and Tom Cole (R-OK-04), Co-Chairs of the Congressional Native American Caucus, introduced a bipartisan House Resolution designating the week of September 27 through October 3, 2026, as Indian Boarding School "National Week of Remembrance."

The resolution aims to formally honor the thousands of American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian children who were forcibly removed from their families and communities to attend government-funded and church-run Indian boarding schools, while acknowledging the enduring intergenerational trauma experienced by survivors and their descendants.

"I would not be here today if not for the strength and resilience of my ancestors, including my grandparents who survived federal Indian boarding schools," said Representative Sharice Davids (D-KS-03), Member of the Wisconsin Ho-Chunk Nation. "These boarding schools were explicitly designed to strip Indigenous children of their languages, cultures, and identities — causing harm that continues to ripple through Native families and communities today. Designating this week isn't just about acknowledging a dark chapter in our history; it is about honoring the survivors, remembering the children who never returned home, and committing to healing for future generations."

“For many years, Indian boarding schools were created to forcibly remove Native children from their homes, strip them of their heritage, and, sadly, in some cases, take their lives,” said Representative Tom Cole (R-OK-04), Member of the Chickasaw Nation of Oklahoma. “However, this history is not often spoken about or taught in curriculum. Recognizing this week as Indian Boarding School National Week of Remembrance can bring light to this dark chapter in our nation’s history. I would like to thank Representative Sharice Davids of Kansas, who I co-chair the Congressional Native American Caucus with, for her work on this legislation, as it is critical that we remember and honor these boarding school survivors and those who did not make it home.”

Starting with the Indian Civilization Fund Act of 1819, the United States government enacted policies that established or funded more than 526 Indian boarding schools across 38 states. By 1926, an estimated 83 percent of Native American children were enrolled in these institutions, where physical, psychological, and spiritual abuse were widespread.

Loss of Life and Unmarked Graves: Untold numbers of children died from disease, abuse, or while trying to escape. Recent ground-penetrating radar research has uncovered evidence of unmarked graves, off-campus cemeteries, and unrecorded casualties.

Lasting Intergenerational Trauma: Studies show that survivors and their descendants experience disproportionate rates of post-traumatic stress disorder, chronic health conditions, and intergenerational trauma stemming from the systematic disruption of Tribal family structures and cultural identity.

State Impact: In Kansas alone, there were 14 federal Indian boarding schools — including the Shawnee Indian Manual Labor School in Fairway (now preserved as the Shawnee Indian Mission State Historic Site in Kansas' Third District). In Oklahoma, 76 federal boarding schools operated, accounting for roughly 19 percent of all known boarding schools nationwide.

"The National Week of Remembrance calls on us to reflect on the history that forever changed our Native families, communities, and generations. We honor those who were taken from their families, survivors who carried the weight of the boarding school experience throughout their lives, and, with reverence, those who never returned to their homes," said Nikki Santos, Chief Executive Officer (Coeur d'Alene Tribe), National Native American Boarding School Healing Coalition (NABS). "We honor the children. Their lives matter, and their stories and their truth belong in the history of this nation. Remembrance Week calls on all of us to ensure that experiences of Native children and families are never again forgotten or erased."

This resolution builds directly on Davids and Cole's ongoing bipartisan work to address the history of federal assimilation policies. The co-chairs have also introduced the bipartisan Truth and Healing Commission on Indian Boarding School Policies Act, legislation that would establish a formal federal commission to investigate, document, and report on the full extent of abuses and lingering impacts of Indian boarding school policies.

title: Dingell, Moolenaar Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Strengthen Senior Care
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and John Moolenaar (R-MI-02) introduced bipartisan legislation to strengthen the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE). The PACE Improvement Act would support the expansion of current PACE programs and facilitate the establishment of new ones by giving PACE programs greater flexibility to enroll beneficiaries throughout the year, remove limitations on when entities may apply to become PACE organizations, make PACE a mandatory service under Medicaid, address outdated limitations and unnecessary constraints on the potential for the growth and expansion of PACE organizations, and more.

“The PACE model has been successful in helping seniors and Americans with disabilities age and live with dignity. As the third-largest PACE state, Michigan’s PACE providers deliver critical long-term services for individuals wishing to remain in their homes. But too many Americans continue to sit on waitlists to receive home and community-based services,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “We must do more to ensure Americans have the option to live independently in the comfort of their own homes. With this bipartisan bill, we can put these long-term supports in reach for those who need them the most.”

“Michigan seniors should have more choices when it comes to receiving the care they need, including the option to receive home care. This is especially true in rural communities where long-term care options can be limited,” said Congressman Moolenaar. “This bipartisan legislation expands access to the PACE program, cuts unnecessary red tape, and gives more seniors the opportunity to receive high-quality care closer to home. I am proud to support this commonsense bill and will continue working to strengthen care for seniors across our state.”

The legislation is supported by the National Pace Association, PACE of Southeast Michigan, Alzheimer’s Association, Alzheimer’s Impact Movement, American Association on Health and Disability, CommunicationFIRST, Community Catalyst, Lakeshore Foundation, LeadingAge, National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys, National Disability Rights Network, and Village to Village Network.

“There is an incredible need for the life changing care PACE provides. More than 350,000 Michiganders are dually eligible for Medicare and Medicaid, and thousands more are already receiving long-term care because their needs have reached a nursing facility level of care. Yet PACE currently serves only about 6,500 people across our entire state. That gap represents an enormous opportunity to help more older adults remain independent, stay connected to their communities and receive the care they need,” said Brandon Young, President and CEO of PACE Southeast Michigan. “We see every day what happens when people are given that opportunity. They regain strength, increase their independence and find a meaningful sense of belonging. We are incredibly grateful to Congresswoman Dingell for recognizing the need and taking action to make PACE easier to access.”

"I don't know where I'd be without PACE,” said Carol Jackson, a PACE Southeast Michigan participant who lives in Trenton, Michigan. “The people here are like a family – my PACE family is my family. The elderly need places like PACE to survive on their own and be able to keep doing a lot with their lives. The people at my PACE center help all of us so much. No matter what we’re going through, they’re there for us. I'm so grateful that Debbie is supporting PACE by bringing this bill forward. I hope it passes, because there's so many more people out there who need PACE."

The Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE) is a model of care that integrates Medicare and Medicaid benefits for eligible beneficiaries. It provides comprehensive medical and social services to seniors and individuals living with disabilities that enables them to live in their homes and communities rather than receiving care in an institutional setting. Congresswoman Dingell, a co-chair of the Bipartisan Disabilities Caucus and the 21st Century Long-Term Care Caucus, and Congressman Moolenar first introduced legislation on PACE in 2023.

Bill text can be viewed HERE.

title: De La Cruz Leads Fight Against Mealybug
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz (TX-15) introduced the Combatting Pasture Mealybug Act. The bill directs the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) to study the impact of the pasture mealybug and provide Congress with recommended strategies that the Federal Government can quickly deploy to contain the invasive pest.

Original co-sponsors of the legislation include Representative Brian Babin (TX-36), Michael Cloud (TX-27), Jake Ellzey (TX-06), Pat Fallon (TX-04), Brandon Gill (TX-26), Lance Gooden (TX-05), Morgan Luttrell (TX-08), Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), Beth Van Duyne (TX-24), Randy Weber (TX-14), Roger Williams (TX-25), Kat Cammack (FL-03) and David Valadao (CA-22).

"The pasture mealybug poses a major threat to Texas agriculture. After hearing from Texas farmers, it's clear we must act now. That's why I am proud to lead the fight in stopping this new pest and working alongside Secretary Rollins to deploy effective solutions. Protecting Texas agriculture is my top priority, and I will fight to secure a strong future for Texas." - Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz

The legislation is supported by the following organizations: Texas & Southwestern Cattle Raisers Association, Texas Farm Bureau, Texas Citrus Mutual, Texas Vegetable Association, Texas International Produce Association, Mississippi Cattlemen's Association, and Florida Farm Bureau.

“Pasture mealybug poses a serious threat to our grazing land resources and the future of cattle operations in Texas and the Southwest. With no viable eradication option for pasture mealybug, it is crucial that we ramp up our response efforts now. By directing USDA to study and report on strategies, the Combating Pasture Mealybug Act is imperative to ensuring long-term viability of our grasslands and forages."

- Stephen Diebel, Texas & Southwestern Cattle Raisers Association President

"The Texas International Produce Association (TIPA) supports Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz’s Combating Pasture Mealybug Act. While our members primarily represent the fresh fruit and vegetable industry, the strength of every agricultural sector—including livestock, forage, sod, and other crop production—contributes to the health of our overall agricultural economy. Emerging pests that threaten our farmers, ranchers, sod producers, and agricultural lands can have consequences extending well beyond a single commodity. We appreciate Congresswoman De La Cruz’s leadership in bringing attention to this threat and working to protect the long-term strength and resilience of American agriculture." - Texas International Produce Association

“Texas Farm Bureau supports the Mealybug Eradication Act. Pasture mealybug poses a serious threat to productive grazing lands and the livestock industry, and we must be prepared to respond. This bill will help strengthen our understanding of the pest, improve preparedness and response capabilities, and identify strategies to contain and eradicate it. We thank Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz for her leadership and support of Texas agriculture.” - Russell Boening, President, Texas Farm Bureau

Background:

First spotted in the United States in 2025, the pasture mealybug is an invasive pest that feeds on plant sap in forage grasses, attacking both above- and below-ground parts of key forage, row, and turf crops. As of September 2026, the bug has been identified in counties across Texas, Louisiana, Florida, and Georgia.

Pasture mealybug infestation causes pasture dieback and major economic losses in livestock, sugarcane, turfgrass, and row-crop sectors. Damages caused by the pasture mealybug are estimated to cost billions of dollars in the long term.

title: Deluzio, Padilla, Ruiz Launch Effort to Prohibit Firearms at Polling Places, Protect Voters and Election Workers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – With midterm elections just around the corner and threats to our elections at an all-time high, U.S. Representative Chris Deluzio (D-PA-17), U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA), and Congressman Raúl Ruiz (D-CA-25) introduced bicameral legislation to protect voters and election workers from intimidation and threats of violence at polling places.

The Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act of 2026 would help ensure that every voter and election worker has the right to cast their ballot and conduct their official duties free from fear and intimidation. It would update existing anti-intimidation provisions of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 to limit the presence of visible firearms at locations where voters cast their ballot or election workers perform their official duties, empowering poll workers and election officials to continue safely administering elections.

“The right to vote is foundational to America's democracy, and part of protecting that right is keeping official ballot drop sites and polling places free from intimidation,” said Congressman Deluzio. “With the rising risk of political violence and ongoing threats to our democratic system, we need to strengthen the sanctity of our elections. The Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act of 2026 would help protect the rights of America’s voters and election workers so that they can vote and perform their official duties free from violent threats and intimidation. I’m proud to reintroduce this bill today alongside Senator Alex Padilla and Representative Ruiz.”

“No voter should have to walk past a gauntlet of firearms to exercise their right to vote, and no election worker should have to risk armed threats just to do their job,” said Senator Padilla. “Intimidation and violence have no place at our polls. These threats disenfranchise voters, undermine the fairness of our elections, and prevent nonpartisan election workers from doing their jobs. Our bill will keep visible firearms and other forms of violence away from polling places, ensuring every eligible voter can exercise their fundamental right safely, freely, and without intimidation.”

"With the midterms just weeks away, every American should be able to cast their ballot, and every election worker should be able to do their job without fear for their personal safety,” said Congressman Dr. Raul Ruiz. “That is why I am proud to join Congressman Deluzio and Senator Padilla introducing the Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act. This legislation aims to help keep our polling places safe and more secure and protect the voters and election workers who make our democracy possible."

The right to vote is fundamental to American democracy, but rising threats of political violence against voters and election workers threaten election security. As of April 2026, 32 percent of local election workers have reported experience threats, harassment, or abuse. Armed groups such as the Proud Boys and Oath Keepers who were involved in the January 6, 2021 assault on the U.S. Capitol have threatened to patrol polling places in recent elections. While intimidation is illegal under existing law, this new legislation is important to provide a clearer standard and further ensure safe polling locations.

Specifically, the Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act would:

Amend Section 11(b) of the Voting Rights Act to establish a rebuttable presumption that a person carrying a visible firearm while engaging in election-related activities is engaging in voter intimidation;

Provide civil remedies for individuals who experience this type of intimidation, including an emergency injunction that would allow the voter or election official to carry out their duties in peace; and

Recognize an exception for law enforcement officers acting within their official duties.

The Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act is endorsed by organizations including the Brennan Center, Defend the Vote Action Fund, and the Fair Elections Center.

"Congress must pass the Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act. We are grateful to Representative Deluzio, Senator Padilla, and other members of Congress for their work to keep our elections safe for everyone involved in the process. This legislation would bolster federal protections that empower voters, election officials, and election workers to seek legal recourse if they are intimidated. The bill would help protect our democracy by keeping intimidation and violence out of voting." — Sean Morales-Doyle, Senior Director of the voting rights program, Brennan Center for Justice at NYU Law.

"Our ability to hold elected leaders accountable to the people depends on ensuring every voter can access the ballot free from intimidation or harassment, and that election workers can run those elections without interference. Defend The Vote Action Fund applauds Rep. Deluzio and Sen. Padilla for their leadership on this critical bill that protects voters' rights to cast their ballots free from interference, while ensuring that poll workers and election officials can safely oversee and administer our elections." — Brian Lemek, Executive Director of Defend the Vote Action Fund.

"To fully realize our civil rights, we need stronger protections against intimidation to make sure that election officials can do their jobs without fear, and that no American is stopped from exercising their right to vote. The Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act is one way we can defend our voting rights in the face of those who want to take power away from the people." — Rebekah Caruthers, President and CEO of the Fair Elections Center.

This bill was first introduced in 2024. Full text of the 2026 bill is available HERE.

title: CONGRESSMAN DOWNING'S BILL CROW TRIBE WATER RIGHTS SETTLEMENT AMENDMENTS ACT PASSES BOTH CHAMBERS OF CONGRESS, HEADS TO PRESIDENT’S DESK
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025, passed the U.S. Senate. Senator Steve Daines spearheaded the bill in the Senate, while Congressman Troy Downing championed it in the House of Representatives. The legislation updates the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 to provide the Crow Tribe with greater flexibility to develop water infrastructure and keep long-overdue projects on the reservation moving forward.

The original settlement ratified the water rights compact between the Crow Tribe and the State of Montana. It authorized the Bureau of Reclamation to rehabilitate the Crow Irrigation Project (CIP) and construct a Municipal, Rural, and Industrial (MR&I) water system.

S. 240 modernizes that framework by converting the MR&I component from a single centralized project into a more flexible, localized approach. Instead of one large system, the legislation allows the Tribe to develop smaller water and wastewater projects tailored to the needs of individual communities across the reservation.

In addition, the legislation extends the Crow Tribe's exclusive right to develop a hydropower project at the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam for five years, through 2030, helping support future energy development on the reservation.

“Today, S. 240, the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025, passed the U.S. Senate. This legislation gives the Crow Tribe greater flexibility to develop critical water infrastructure and keep long-overdue projects moving forward on the reservation. We must continue honoring our commitments to the Crow Tribe and strengthening Montana’s water infrastructure," said Congressman Downing. "Thank you to Senator Daines for leading this bill in the Senate and sending it to the President’s desk."

“This bill is a necessity for the Crow Tribe and surrounding communities and will ensure the tribe has the resources they need to deliver safe, reliable access to clean water to the reservation and complete a hydropower project to bring new baseload generation to the region. I’m grateful for Representative Downing’s work to get this passed in the House and am thrilled to see it pass the Senate- let’s get it across the finish line!” said Senator Steve Daines.

“The federal government must ensure tribal water settlements work as intended. S. 240 gives the Crow Tribe greater flexibility to complete critical drinking water and irrigation projects while extending its exclusive right to pursue hydropower development at Yellowtail Afterbay Dam. I commend Senator Daines and Rep. Downing for championing a practical solution that strengthens tribal self-determination and supports long-term economic growth on the Crow Reservation,” said House Committee on Natural Resources Chairman Bruce Westerman.

title: ICYMI: DOWNING OP-ED IN THE WASHINGTON EXAMINER: Inherit a million? You can invest. Have an economics doctorate? The SEC says you’re too dumb
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Congressman Troy Downing penned an op-ed in the Washington Examiner highlighting his new bill, H.R.9574, The Informed Investor Access Act. The legislation would break down barriers to capital markets by creating a new route to accredited-investor status for a specific transaction when an individual receives personalized investment advice or a recommendation from a registered investment adviser or registered broker-dealer.

Read the Washington Examiner op-edHERE.

September 22, 2026

Are some people simply not rich enough to build the American dream?

America’s capital markets are the most dynamic in the world. They are ripe with opportunity. Our nation’s business ecosystem is better because of them.

The American dream of entrepreneurship and prosperity is possible through our robust capital markets. Too many people are locked out of important parts of those markets for one simple reason: They are not rich enough.

Most investors can only directly invest in publicly traded companies, which make up less than 1% of all U.S. businesses. They have virtually no access to nonpublic, or private, investment opportunities. In other words, they have no access to investments that help the rich get richer.

The number of publicly available stock investment options has declined by nearly 50% since the 1990s, which means fewer investment opportunities for hardworking Montanans. That is the effect of the outdated “accredited investor” framework.

Publicly traded companies are subject to the highest degree of disclosure requirements from the Securities and Exchange Commission. The strict requirements, along with their direct costs to the investor, create a transparent but also very expensive option, which is why everyone has access.

Nonpublic companies are not subject to these same rules, so the federal government has long held that only “sophisticated” investors are allowed to participate in these markets. The problem is the false equivalency between sophistication and wealth. This foreclosure on access by anyone but the wealthiest among us is one reason the rich get richer and ordinary people are often left behind.

Under current SEC rules, anyone can access the private markets by being an accredited investor, which is defined by having more than $1 million in net worth, not including one’s residence, or by earning more than $200,000 per year for two consecutive years. The rules include other qualifications, but for most people, wealth remains the gatekeeper.

This leaves many “ordinary” people on the sidelines — many of whom understand the risks of investing and have built strong portfolios or financial plans either independently or with a financial adviser. A high net worth does not automatically make someone a knowledgeable investor, just as falling below an arbitrary threshold does not make someone incapable of understanding risk. In other words, a person who inherits $1 million but has no idea about how money works may qualify, but someone with a doctorate in economics with only $100,000 to invest is generally not qualified.

I have seen our capital markets from nearly every angle. I began my career as an educator and research scientist before founding a tech company that later merged with Yahoo. I went on to build multiple businesses, structure alternative investments, and raise capital through independent broker-dealers. Later, as Montana state auditor and commissioner of securities and insurance, I served as our state’s chief securities regulator. Today, I serve on the House Financial Services Committee.

Those experiences taught me that capital formation and investor protection should not be seen as competing goals. Well-designed rules can advance both.

That is why I introduced the Informed Investor Access Act. My legislation would create a new route to accredited-investor status for a specific transaction when someone receives personalized investment advice or a recommendation from a registered investment adviser or registered broker-dealer.

This is not an invitation to throw open the doors without guardrails. Registered investment advisers are bound by a fiduciary duty, and broker-dealers must comply with Regulation Best Interest. These professionals are required to consider a client’s financial circumstances and risk tolerance when making recommendations.

The current framework creates a self-reinforcing barrier: Often, people are required to meet the wealth threshold to access investments that may help them build wealth. Meanwhile, entrepreneurs in private businesses lose potential sources of capital that could help them innovate and expand.

Access must improve on both sides of the marketplace. I recently led a congressional letter urging SEC Chairman Paul Atkins to finalize the commission’s Registered Offering Reform proposal.

Among its provisions, the proposal would remove duplicative state registration and qualification reviews for certain public companies, reducing unnecessary costs while maintaining disclosure and anti-fraud protections.

This matters across the country, but especially in rural states such as Montana. Entrepreneurs and growing businesses should not be forced to move their business to a major financial center to find capital. Likewise, Montanans who work, save, and plan responsibly should not be excluded from considering an investment simply because they don’t meet the wealth threshold.

Modernizing these rules does not guarantee returns, eliminate risk, or make every investment suitable. Nor should it. These are investments without training wheels, and they should be carefully scrutinized.

Giving everyday people access gives them an opportunity to make informed choices with professional guidance, while allowing businesses to reach a broader pool of potential investors.

Building wealth should not be reserved for those who were given a head start or who are already wealthy. Congress and the SEC can preserve strong protections while replacing outdated barriers with standards that recognize individual circumstances. This is how we strengthen capital formation in America and keep America’s markets the strongest in the world.

title: Elfreth Joins Maryland Delegation in Announcing $8.6 Million to Increase Safety and Security in Places of Worship
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks, and Representatives Steny Hoyer, Kweisi Mfume, Andy Harris, Jamie Raskin, Glenn Ivey, April McClain Delaney, and Johnny Olszewski announced $8,627,091 in federal funding to strengthen security at 49 religious institutions and community centers across Maryland.

“Marylanders of all faiths deserve to both be safe and feel safe in their houses of worship. Since coming to Congress, I have continued to prioritize increased security funding for nonprofit and religious institutions – both in Washington in the budget and through our Interfaith Advisory Council – which is why it is so great to join Team Maryland in announcing this $8 million in federal funding for 49 houses of worship, religious institutions, and community centers across our state. Especially as religious institutions spend more and more on security and the number of hate crimes continues to rise, Congress has an important responsibility to ensure the safety of all of our neighbors,” said Congresswoman Elfreth.

“Every Marylander deserves to be able to exercise their right to religious freedom and worship without fear for their safety. Our faith institutions also help build community in many ways, from providing spiritual services to offering youth programs to supporting local families. As that work continues, we have also seen an appalling increase in threats against faith-based organizations across the state, and we know that more federal funding and reforms are necessary to meet the growing security measures needed to keep community members safe. We will continue working to increase funds for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program and to see that these investments go where they are needed most, in light of recent changes to this program,” said Senator Van Hollen.

“All Marylanders deserve to feel safe in their homes, schools, communities – and especially in places of worship. It was critical that Team Maryland fight to secure over $8 million in federal funding to strengthen security at religious centers in our state. And I won’t stop fighting until all Marylanders feel and are safe,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

“The Nonprofit Security Grant Program has become an essential tool for protecting our houses of worship, schools, community centers, and early-childhood programs. With the alarming rise in antisemitism and other forms of hate, it is critical that everyone feels safe when gathering with their communities and congregations. I’m proud that Team Maryland was able to secure this funding, and I will continue working with our delegation to push for further federal support for nonprofit security,” said Congressman Steny H. Hoyer.

“No matter what your faith or religion is, every American should feel safe and secure in their ability to worship peacefully,” said Congressman Kweisi Mfume. “With this injection of over $8 million in Federal funding, dozens of faith-based institutions across Maryland will be able to improve their security systems and protocols, ensuring that houses of worship remain sanctuaries for practitioners of all beliefs.”

“Marylanders should be able to practice their faith without worrying about their safety. This funding will improve security at religious institutions across the First District, from Harford County to the Eastern Shore. Thank you to President Trump and the Department of Homeland Security for helping Maryland’s religious organizations improve security and protect our communities,” said Congressman Harris.

“Amidst an alarming increase in antisemitism, Islamophobia and other forms of toxic hate, Team Maryland is surging more than $8.6 million in federal Nonprofit Security Grants to protect our people,” said Rep. Jamie Raskin (MD-08). “No American should become a target of senseless violence and intimidation, especially in their house of worship.”

“Every Marylander should be able to worship and gather without fear,” said Congressman Ivey. “Team Maryland fought together to secure this federal funding so that faith communities across our state have the resources they need to strengthen security and protect the people they serve. I’m proud of our delegation’s work to deliver these investments and help keep Marylanders safe.”

“Whether you are walking into a church, synagogue, mosque, temple, or community center, you should never have to fear for your safety. Freedom of religion means the freedom to worship without fear. This $8.6 million investment will help 49 institutions across Maryland strengthen security and protect the communities they serve. I’ll keep working with Team Maryland to ensure our faith communities have the resources they need to keep people safe,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney.

“Our faith communities are critical community anchors and bring so many Marylanders together,” said Congressman Johnny Olszewski (MD-02). “This funding gives 49 religious institutions and community centers across our state the resources they need to worship, learn, and gather without fear. Team Maryland will keep fighting to make sure our houses of worship have what they need to stay safe.”

title: Emmer Attends Monticello Water Treatment Plant Ribbon Cutting
text:
MONTICELLO, MN – Yesterday, Congressman Tom Emmer attended the Ribbon Cutting Ceremony for Monticello's new Water Treatment Plant. September 23, 2026 marked the start of construction of the new facility to provide safe drinking water to the surrounding community.

“This much-needed Water Treatment Plant will make a difference for Monticello and the surrounding communities,” said Congressman Emmer. “We’re grateful for the local leaders who have worked so hard to get this project underway. It’s great to know that those who live and work in Monticello will continue to have access to safe, clean water for years to come.”

Background

Monticello, Minnesota is a growing city in Wright County with a population of approximately 14,600 residents, located roughly 41 miles northwest of Minneapolis. Monticello residents connected to city water are served by five municipal wells that feed water into the distribution system. While Monticello's wells meet all Safe Drinking Water Act Standards, testing shows an elevated level of manganese. Because of this, the city is building a new filtration system and water treatment plant.

title: Representatives Escobar, Bacon Introduce Bill to Prevent Military Families from Losing Access to Nutrition Benefits
text:
Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) and Congressman Don Bacon (NE-2) introduced the Nutrition Continuity for Military Families Act of 2026. This bill would ensure that at-risk military families do not lose access to crucial supplemental nutritional benefits through the Women, Infant, and Children (WIC) program while conducting military required permanent changes of station (PCS).

"Receiving orders to move around the country or the world is one of the most stressful sacrifices a military family can make," said Congresswoman Escobar. "It's critical that when families conduct a permanent change of station, Congress and the military make this drastic change as smooth as possible. The last thing they should be worried about is the transferring of their nutrition assistance. My bipartisan bill addresses this by ensuring military families have the resources and tools at their disposal to ensure they have food on the table.”

"Food costs are one of the biggest financial pressures on military families right now, and WIC benefits are a lifeline for many of them," said Shannon Razsadin, Military Family Advisory Network CEO. "Our own research backs that up: the Military Family 360° Survey found 41.2% of military families report low or very low food security, up from 15.6% just two years ago, and families who've recently moved due to military orders are among the hardest hit. Families report WIC benefit coverage gaps when they relocate, and some don't even know they qualify in the first place. This legislation fixes both problems: it helps families know what they're eligible for and ensures those benefits don't lapse just because they got new orders. That's real financial stability for the families who need it most, and it strengthens the readiness of our all-volunteer force."

The Nutrition Continuity for Military Families Act of 2026 ensures that the Department of Defense (DoD) provides the necessary resources and tools to fend off military family food insecurity. Specifically, this bill will:

Require the DoD to notify service members upon receipt of PCS orders, if they are likely to fall within the category of income eligibility for WIC based on their grade/rank and time in service. The target category include:

enlisted service members undergoing a PCS with one or more dependents

pregnant enlisted service members

enlisted service members with pregnant spouses

enlisted servicemembers who meet the following service criteria:

serving an initial term of enlistment

serving in a paygrade of E-4 of below or,

have completed less than 10 years of service and is serving in the paygrade of E-5 or E-6.

Require that state agencies issue a Verification of Certification card to covered members at the time of certification or recertification, ensuring their continued access to program benefits

Require DoD to ensure that every military installation is staffed at least three days a week by a DoD employee knowledgeable of the WIC program and with resources to direct families to local agencies to complete enrollment and manage benefits. These offices will provide readily available resources to military families who may be challenged to access local agencies located off the installation.

title: Leger Fernández Calls for Pause on Data Center Development, Unveils “No Blank Checks for Data Centers” Principles
text:
SANTA FE, NM — Today, Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03) unveiled her No Blank Checks for Data Centers Principles, a set of clear standards to protect New Mexico families, water, land, and local communities as companies seek to build massive data centers across the state. The Congresswoman called for a moratorium on new data center development in New Mexico until companies meet the principles she laid out.

“The role of government is to protect us from greedy corporations,” said Congresswoman Leger Fernández. "Data centers want our water, our land, and our power. Communities may want the jobs they could bring to New Mexico. But we will not give them a blank check. I will only support data centers that pay their own way, protect our precious water, create good-paying union jobs, use clean energy, and earn the support of the communities where they want to build. Data centers must work for New Mexico, not the other way around. Communities must know how much water and electricity these projects will use, who will pay for them, and what residents will receive in return. If a project cannot answer those questions, it should not move forward. Congress must act to regulate data centers with these principles in mind. We cannot let AI and data centers regulate themselves.”

The Congresswoman’s platform requires data centers to meet six principles:

No Blank Checks for Data Centers Principles

Don’t hike up electric bills. Data centers must pay for their own electricity and infrastructure without passing their costs on to New Mexico families.

Don’t negatively impact water resources in the area.

Use energy sources that meet New Mexico’s renewable energy and zero-carbon requirements.

Create good-paying union jobs.

Get community approval and do consultation before permitting and building.

No taxpayer subsidies, projects must provide community benefits.

“Our water. Our land. Our power. Our say,” said Leger Fernández. “Those are New Mexico’s terms.”

Leger Fernández also linked her data center standards to a broader call for federal oversight of artificial intelligence. In a post earlier this week, she said:

“Trump called AI concerns “a HOAX.” He said opponents of data centers “want to end up being backwards and poor.” No, Mr. President, Americans want Congress and you to do your job protecting humanity, protecting our utility bills, and protecting us from out-of-control, corrupt greed.

A principal role of government is to protect the American people. Safety must always be our first mandate. It is also the government’s job to protect the American people from unmitigated greed. The billionaires that you are listening to now would prefer the government stay on the sidelines. But the U.S. government knows how to regulate corporate greed and how to address new technologies that could destroy our world.

What we do now will matter. We cannot just let AI and data centers regulate themselves or depend on their goodwill to lower utility costs and limit the most destructive possibilities inherent in this rapidly evolving technology. We must let local communities have a say in what is built in their neighborhoods so they can protect their water, environment, and cost burdens.

But Congress must act. There must be a strong, enforceable national regulatory framework. We must have civil and criminal liability. We must protect the local and national financial interests of working families.

It is not a hoax, Mr. President. And we have a job to do.”

title: Figures, Booker, Hayes, Ezell to Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Cover College and Trade School Costs for Families of America’s First Responders, Teachers, and Social Workers
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Rep. Shomari C. Figures (AL-02), Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ), Rep. Jahana Hayes (CT-05), and Rep. Mike Ezell (MS-04) will introduce the bipartisan Public Service Educational Assistance Act, a bill to support the families of critical public service employees by covering the full cost of higher education and training opportunities for the dependents of educators, first responders, and social workers.

"Educators, first responders, and social workers show up for us in our classrooms, our emergencies, and our hardest moments, year after year," said Booker. "Their families carry that sacrifice too, often quietly, through long hours and stretched budgets. After 20 years of service, the least we can do is make sure their kids can go to college without drowning in debt."

“Teachers, social workers, and first responders dedicate their lives in service to our communities, oftentimes unable to provide opportunities they fight so hard for others to enjoy, to their own children,” said Hayes. “I am pleased to introduce the Public Service Educational Assistance Act alongside Congressman Figures to honor the work of public servants and make it easier for their own families to pursue higher education."

“As someone who spent more than four decades in law enforcement, I know the sacrifices that come with a career dedicated to serving your community—not just for the individual wearing the badge, but for their entire family,” said Ezell. “The Public Service Educational Assistance Act recognizes that commitment by helping provide educational opportunities for the children of those who have devoted decades of their lives to public service. I’m proud to help introduce this legislation to support the families of our law enforcement officers, first responders, educators, and others who dedicate their careers to serving their neighbors.”

This legislation establishes a federal education assistance program covering the full cost of postsecondary education and training opportunities – including those enrolled in trade schools and vocational programs – for the dependents of educators, first responders, and social workers who have completed at least 20 years of qualifying service.

This bill is endorsed by the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, the National Association of Social Workers, the International Association of Fire Fighters, and the Major Cities Chiefs Association.

title: Finstad Calls for Increased USPS Communication Regarding Closure of Glenville Post Office
text:
September 24, 2026

ROCHESTER, MN – Today, Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) sent a letter to District Manager of the United States Postal Service’s Minnesota-North Dakota District Angela Bye, requesting clarity and increased communication following the closure of the Glenville Post Office.

On June 28, 2026, a vehicle struck the Glenville Post Office, causing damage to the front of the building. The next day, Postal Service operations were halted and customers were informed mail could be picked up at the Albert Lea Post Office, about seven miles away. Since then, city officials and residents of Glenville have received minimal updates on a reopening date or timeline of resumed operations.

The letter reads:

“Dear District Manager Bye,

“I am writing regarding the continued closure of the Glenville Post Office located at 220 W. Main Street in Glenville, Minnesota following a vehicle collision that damaged the building. I am concerned about the length of the closure and the impact it is having on residents, businesses, and other postal customers in the Glenville community. It is important that you communicate clearly with the City of Glenville about the timeline and process of reopening the post office.

“On June 28, 2026, a vehicle struck the Glenville Post Office building, leaving damage to the front of the building. Since then, the Postal Service has halted operations at this location with no indication to the local community on the status of restoring postal operations. Residents should not be left without convenient access to postal services for an extended and indefinite period, particularly without clear information about what is being done to restore services.

“Numerous constituents of mine have contacted my office stating that they have had no correspondence with the Postal Service on a reopening date or a timeline for resumed operations. While I understand that unforeseen circumstances can complicate the repair of a damaged postal facility, the residents of Glenville deserve transparency regarding the status of their post office and a clear understanding of when normal service will return.

“Local residents rely on their Post Office for essential mailing services. This includes receiving medications, bill payments, stamps, shipping packages, and regular correspondence. Further, this closure can have a profound impact on Glenville’s Main Street businesses that rely on the Post Office to connect with customers and remain competitive.

“I respectfully request information on the following questions:

What is the current status of the Glenville Post Office following the vehicle collision?

What repairs or other corrective actions are required before the facility can reopen?

How is the Postal Service communicating with the City of Glenville about the closure and anticipated reopening, and how will you communicate with City officials going forward?

What temporary measures has USPS implemented to ensure Glenville residents continue to have reasonable access to postal services?

“I respectfully urge USPS to work with the local postmaster to reopen the Glenville Post Office as soon as possible and keep the local community informed on the steps being taken to do so. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

“Sincerely,

title: RELEASE: Rep. Friedman, Bipartisan & Bicameral Coalition Announce Legislation to Create a National Film Tax Credit
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, September 24, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) announced the bipartisan, bicameral Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, legislation to create a national film tax credit and bring hundreds of thousands of good-paying production jobs back to the United States.

A one-pager on the bill is available here. Full text is available here.

The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act will create 143,500 full-time equivalent jobs annually across the country by establishing a 20% tax credit on labor expenses for American workers on qualifying film and television productions, with bonus credits worth up to 30% for productions that hire in rural or federal disaster areas, work across multiple states, or bring work home from overseas. The bill is led by Representatives Laura Friedman, Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), Linda Sánchez (CA-38) (CA-30), Brian Jack (GA-03), David Kustoff (TN-08), Judy Chu (CA-28), Mike Carey (OH-15), and Tom Suozzi (NY-03) in the House. In the Senate, the bill is led by Senators Tim Scott (SC) and Adam Schiff (CA).

“For over a year, I’ve worked to build a coalition of unions, studios, Republicans & Democrats, and the White House, because we knew that a national film tax credit would bring hundreds of thousands of jobs back to our country,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “This bill is a result of that coalition. It tells every country that has been outbidding us for American work that we are done losing”

WHAT THE BILL DOES:

A 20% credit on American labor expenses. Feature films, television pilots, and television seasons that cost more than $1 million qualify if at least 75% of their principal photography days happen in the United States.

Bonus credits that reward hiring where it is needed most. Productions can earn an additional 5% each, up to a 30% total credit, for shooting at least 30% of their days in a rural opportunity zone or a federally declared disaster area, for independent productions, for spending at least $10 million in qualified wages across 10 or more states, and for increasing domestic production relative to what a company shoots abroad.

Includes post-production and visual effects work. Domestic post-production and VFX qualify as long as at least 75% of those costs are incurred in the United States, with the same 5% bonuses available.

Usable by independent producers, not just major studios. The credit is transferable, meaning a producer who doesn't owe enough in federal taxes to use it can sell it to a company that does and get the cash up front.

Takes effect quickly. The credit applies to productions that begin in taxable years starting after December 31, 2026.

A one-pager with more details can be found here

FRIEDMAN’S WORK TO GET AMERICA A NATIONAL FILM TAX CREDIT:

Spent more than a year building the coalition behind this bill, sitting down with Rep. Brian Jack, Jon Voight, industry unions, studios, producers, and more to make the case for a national film tax credit before the issue had political momentum, as Variety reported in May 2025.

Co-founded the Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus with Rep. Brian Jack (GA-03), Rep. Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), Rep. Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Rep. Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11), and Rep. Tom Suozzi (NY-03), building the bipartisan bloc that will help carry this bill, as reported by Deadline and The Hollywood Reporter.

Helped stand up the U.S. Film & TV Production Coalition with the Motion Picture Association, Jon Voight, IATSE, the DGA, and the industry’s unions, appearing at the September 2026 press conference where MPA Chairman and CEO Charles Rivkin released the study behind these numbers, as covered by TheWrap.

“Having worked in a movie theater growing up, I saw early on how films can move and inspire generations of Americans. Films like ‘The Notebook’ bring us to tears, and films like ‘Forrest Gump’ inspire us to see the world differently. That is the power of film, and South Carolina is blessed to serve as the backdrop for both of these iconic American stories,” said Senator Tim Scott (SC). “We cannot stand by as more and more American film production moves overseas, taking jobs, investment, and an important source of American cultural influence with it. This legislation will create jobs in communities across America, support local economies, and help ensure that the next generation of iconic American films is made right here in America.”

“For years, I’ve been championing a federal film tax credit to stop the exodus of tv and film production leaving the United States for countries offering higher incentives. Now, we have the best opportunity in decades to get it done. The direct and indirect jobs created by this creative and talented workforce are enormously important, and we want to make sure they stay in this country. With the support of the White House, our bill will create an overdue federal program to bring the movie magic back to America while creating thousands of jobs and spurring local economic growth across the nation. This legislation has bipartisan, bicameral support, and it’s time we get this passed,” said Senator Adam Schiff (CA).

“When a production comes to a community—from rural East Texas to urban New York—that money doesn't just benefit the production company. It helps the local caterer, the hardware store, the hoteliers, and every tradesman in between who makes film and television production possible. Those jobs are going overseas right now simply because other countries are offering bigger handouts. If we want to keep American storytelling in America, we have to level the playing field, and that's exactly what this bill does. This isn't about subsidizing Hollywood—it's about supporting the American worker, one story and one production at a time. I'm proud to work with Senator Scott and our bipartisan group in both chambers to get this done, and I'm grateful to Ambassador Jon Voight and Sean Astin for the work they've put into pushing this forward,” said Congressman Nathaniel Moran (TX-01).

“My Congressional District is home to Trilith Studios, and I proudly represent the craftsmen, electricians, and carpenters who work hard to create movies that inspire generations of Americans. Study after study has demonstrated that American film production delivers substantial economic benefits to communities across our country by creating jobs, supporting local businesses, and generating millions of dollars in local economic activity. I applaud President Trump's leadership in calling for a legislative solution to bring film production back to the United States, and I look forward to working with him and my colleagues in Congress to advance our legislation and achieve this important goal,” said Rep. Brian Jack (GA-03).

“The United States is losing good-paying union jobs because it’s become too expensive to film here. This isn’t about the actors who star in films and can travel for a shoot. It’s about the production crews and set builders, the backbone of the film industry. Our bill would create incentives to bring those jobs back home and boost local economies, not just in California, but across the country,” said Congresswoman Linda Sánchez (CA-38).

“For generations, Southern California has been the heart of America's film and television industry, supporting thousands of workers and small businesses in the San Gabriel Valley and across our region. But today, too many productions are leaving for other countries, taking good-paying jobs and economic opportunity with them. We cannot stand by while communities across the United States lose these productions and the jobs they support. That's why I am so proud to co-lead the bipartisan, bicameral Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, which will create a new federal tax credit to incentivize film and television production here in America. This bill will help bring productions and jobs back home, support our creative workforce, and keep Southern California the entertainment capital of the world,” said Congresswoman Judy Chu (CA-28).

“Ohio has a rich history in film production, from ‘The Deer Hunter’ and ‘The Shawshank Redemption’ to ‘The Avengers’ and ‘A Christmas Story.’ Many of these filming locations have become tourist attractions and are economic drivers to this day. The film industry provides high-paying jobs for artists, small businesses, and union workers. As other countries implement beneficial tax incentives to draw production away from the United States, Congress must work to ensure the United States stays competitive. I would like to commend Representative Moran for introducing this important legislation. As Chairman of the Humanities Caucus and a member of the tax-writing committee, I am confident this bill will help the United States maintain its global influence, as well as the high-paying jobs, associated with film production,” said Congressman Mike Carey (OH-15).

“The film and TV industry is an economic engine in New York. It supports thousands of good jobs at good wages,” said Congressman Tom Suozzi (NY-03). “America is the entertainment leader of the world and this bill incentivizes filmmakers and studios to hire American workers. I'm proud to help lead this commonsense, bipartisan effort.”

“I want to thank President Trump for bringing national attention to the urgent need for a federal film and television production tax credit and for calling on Congress to act,” said Hollywood Ambassador Jon Voight. “I also want to thank Senators Tim Scott and Adam Schiff, along with Representatives Nathaniel Moran, Linda Sánchez, Brian Jack, Laura Friedman, Mike Carey, Judy Chu, David Kustoff, Tom Suozzi, and the growing list of supporters, for their work on this bipartisan effort to bring productions and jobs back to the United States. The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act will restore the American film and television industry, put crews back to work, support productions at all levels, and create economic opportunities in communities nationwide. All Americans want to bring our iconic film industry home, and we can do it by working together to get this important legislation passed quickly.”

Endorsed by: American Federation of Musicians, American Society of Composers, Authors, and Publishers (ASCAP), Coalition for American Production (CAP), CreativeFuture, Directors Guild of America (DGA), FilmUSA, Independent Film and Television Alliance (IFTA), International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees (IATSE), Motion Picture Association (MPA), Paramount, Producers Guild of America (PGA), Screen Actors Guild – American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA), Teamsters, Television Academy, Writers Guild of America East (WGAE), Writers Guild of America West (WGAW).

Statements of support from endorsing organizations can be found here.

The American film and television industry supports more than two million jobs, pays $202 billion in wages, and is made up of more than 162,000 businesses in all 50 states, the vast majority of them small businesses. But more than 100,000 production jobs have disappeared since the industry’s peak in October 2022, a decline of roughly 36% through February 2026.

While U.S. high-budget production spending fell 20% in 2025, the United Kingdom grew 15%, and Germany, Hungary, and the Czech Republic grew a combined 78%. Sixty-five countries now offer production incentives, and no single state can outbid a foreign government.

title: Fulcher Announces $26 Million Returned to Idahoans Through Casework
text:

title: Gluesenkamp Perez Announces 2026 Bigleaf Maple Big Leaf Contest
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03) announced her fourth annual Bigleaf Maple Big Leaf Contest to encourage residents of Washington’s Third District to get out in the woods and find the biggest Bigleaf Maple leaf they can.

Last year’s winner, James Owen, shows off his 21in leaf found in east Lewis County

title: New Gooden Bill Cracks Down on Synthetic Kratom Products
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Lance Gooden (TX-05) announced the End Gas Station Heroin Act, legislation to protect Americans from dangerous synthetic opioids sold in gas stations and smoke shops.

The bill permanently schedules synthetic opioids and analogs sold in synthetic kratom products, commonly known as “gas station heroin.” It also creates a special federal enforcement mechanism to address new and emerging substances before manufacturers can evade enforcement.

“Dangerous synthetic opioids powerful enough to fuel addiction and destroy lives should not be sitting on convenience store shelves next to snacks and energy drinks,” said Rep. Gooden. “My bill permanently schedules these drugs, closes loopholes, and targets the entities putting them into our communities.”

The issue has taken on renewed urgency following the deaths of two University of Mississippi students earlier this week. Synthetic kratom products were reportedly found at the scene, though authorities have not determined the official cause of death.

Existing enforcement mechanisms have struggled to keep pace as new synthetic compounds enter the market across the country. The Drug Enforcement Administration has taken temporary action to schedule certain synthetic substances, but those measures are limited and do not provide a permanent framework for addressing new compounds as they emerge.

The End Gas Station Heroin Act would:

Permanently schedule several dangerous synthetic opioids and analogs, including synthetic 7-OH.

Create a mechanism to treat future emerging synthetic opioids as scheduled for manufacturers and distributors, helping prevent minor molecular alterations from being used to evade enforcement.

Target manufacturers and distributors who introduce these drugs into the stream of commerce.

The bill was featured in an exclusive article by the Washington Reporter and is cosponsored by Reps. Rich McCormick (GA-07), Barry Moore (AL-01), Mariannette Miller-Meeks (IA-01), and Randy Fine (FL-06). Senator Bernie Moreno is leading the companion in the Senate.

Read the bill text here.

title: Goodlander Joins Democratic Veterans in Demanding Trump Hold China Accountable for Support to Iran
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), a Navy Reserve veteran and member of the House Armed Services Committee, joined Congressman Pat Ryan (NY-18) and 12 fellow Democratic veterans in a letter urging President Trump to confront China over its support to Iran. The lawmakers sent the letter ahead of President Xi Jinping’s visit to the White House this week.

On July 17, an Iranian ballistic missile struck sleeping quarters at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, killing three U.S. soldiers and wounding four others. The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran obtained high-resolution satellite imagery of the base from Chinese entities before and after the strike, and that U.S. officials connected that intelligence to the attack.

The lawmakers demanded Trump hold Xi accountable for Beijing’s role in U.S. troop deaths, and that he publicly condemn China’s support for IRGC operations.

“As veterans, we know what it means to send Americans into harm’s way, and we know what is owed to them in return: the truth, and a Commander-in-Chief willing to hold accountable anyone and everyone who might do harm to our troops,” the veterans wrote.

The lawmakers wrote: “We implore you to use your meeting to strongly condemn China’s sharing of satellite information that resulted in the deaths of three U.S. servicemembers in Jordan on July 17th, and demand that President Xi cease any support, cooperation, and information sharing with Iran and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).”

The letter also cited May State Department sanctions on three China-based firms for supplying satellite imagery of U.S. and allied military facilities to Iran.

They continued, “In May, the State Department sanctioned three China-based firms for supplying Iran with satellite imagery of American and allied military facilities. Senior officials in your administration reportedly spent months warning their Chinese counterparts that companies in their country were arming Iran with the targeting data. […] Your meeting with President Xi presents an important opportunity to condemn China’s role in arming and enabling Iran, and to demand an end to their support.”

Goodlander joined the letter alongside Democratic Veterans Caucus Chair Rep. Pat Ryan and Reps. Salud Carbajal, Gilbert Cisneros, Herbert Conaway, Jason Crow, Chris Deluzio, Chrissy Houlahan, Ted Lieu, Seth Moulton, Mike Thompson, Derek Tran, and Eugene Vindman.

Read the full letter here.

title: Rep. Grijalva, Sen. Wyden Introduce Bill to Protect Social Security  Benefits from Garnishment
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva and Senator Ron Wyden introduced the Protection of Social Security Benefits Restoration Act, legislation to restore protections for Social Security and other earned benefits from garnishment.

The bill would repeal provisions added in 1996 that allowed the federal government to reduce Social Security benefits to collect delinquent federal non-tax debts, such as student loans. The legislation would restore the protections originally provided under the Social Security Act and extend those protections across Social Security, Railroad Retirement, and Black Lung benefits.

“Social Security is not a handout — it is a benefit earned over decades of hard work. Retirees deserve to know that money will be there when they need it,” said Rep. Grijalva. “At a time when the cost of living continues to rise, seniors living on fixed incomes can’t afford to have their Social Security benefits taken away. I’m proud to introduce this legislation with Senator Wyden to protect these critical benefits that retirees have earned.”

“Social Security should not be able to garnish benefits that American workers earned over a lifetime of hard work on account of outstanding student debt or other federal loans,” said Senator Wyden. “With inflation and rising costs of living, Congress must take the financial burden off struggling seniors and Americans with disabilities at risk of seeing their Social Security benefits cut. That's why I am proud to introduce legislation that will ensure that Americans’ benefits are protected from garnishment, providing greater peace of mind to seniors in their retirement."

By the numbers:

For millions of adults, Social Security is their sole source of income and for more than 63% it makes up over half of their retirement income. Garnishment can be financially devastating.

According to the CFPB, the total amount of Social Security benefits the Department of Education collected between 2001 and 2019 through the offset program increased from $16.2 million to $429.7 million.

In 2019, the average amount collected from individual beneficiaries was $186 per month.

The bill has been endorsed by the following organizations: Social Security Works, National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare (NCPSSM), AFL-CIO, Justice in Aging, the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE), National Organization of Social Security Claimants' Representatives (NOSSCR), and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT).

title: Rep. Hageman Introduces Bill to Bring Transparency to Federal Settlement Payments
text:
Washington, D.C. - Congresswoman Harriet Hageman (R-WY) introduced the Clearer Liability Expenditure and Access to Reporting (CLEAR) Act to require greater transparency in federal agencies’ use of taxpayer dollars to pay final court judgments or compromise settlements arising from litigation against the government.

The Judgment Fund is a permanent, indefinite appropriation of taxpayer dollars that covers these payments with minimal oversight from Congress, effectively constituting a blank check. While the Treasury Department provides some details online, concerns about public access and searchability of this information persist. That secrecy has allowed agencies to shield their actions in settling with certain favored groups, a tactic known as sue-and-settle,” whereby an outside group sues an agency and, instead of fighting the case, it uses taxpayers’ money to pay the group and its legal bills. The American people have a right to easily access the records showing exactly how their tax dollars are being spent.

"Taxpayers are on the hook when the federal government settles a lawsuit, but the information on where that money goes is difficult to track,” said Rep. Hageman. “The CLEAR Act shines a light on every payment, shows who collects the money, and gives Congress the information to detect sue-and-settle schemes."

title: Congressman Johnson Hosts Two Panels at CBCF ALC 55
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- At the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation’s 55th Annual Legislative Conference, Congressman Hank Johnson (GA-04) held two panel discussions.

His first panel, “Protect The Culture: Stopping the Assault on Black Voices, Talent, and Influence”, explored legislative pathways and industry strategies to end targeted assaults on Black voices, ensuring Black journalists can report freely, Black athletes are protected from plantation exploitation, and Black entertainers can create without fear of their work being weaponized against them.

The event was moderated by media personality Dr. Rashad Richey and included Georgia State Representative (D-108) and Democratic nominee for Georgia’s 13th Congressional District, Dr. Jasmine Clark; respected journalist and author April Ryan; and Executive Director of Athletes.org, Brandon Copeland, as panelists.

“Music artists have their lyrics used as evidence in court against them,” said Congressman Johnson, who is the author of the RAP Act that would put guardrails on the use of lyrics in criminal prosecutions. “Journalists receive threats for telling the truth. Black athletes like Colin Kaepernick, who spoke by taking a knee for justice, are blackballed – which sends a message to keep your mouth shut.”

WATCH HERE

His second panel, Judiciary/Justice for All Braintrust, explored that if our democracy is to survive the delicate system of checks and balances that has undergirded our system for 250 years must be restored. Congressman Johnson is the author of several court reform bills, including requiring SCOTUS justices to adhere to a binding code of ethics, setting term limits for justices at 18 years and expanding the court from nine to 13 justices.

“Our democracy is under great threat,” said Congressman Johnson. “In my opinion, the greatest threat is not Donald Trump. It’s not the legislative branch under Republican control. It’s the Supreme Court. Our country was founded on the principles of three co-equal branches of government each operating as a check and balance on the other. This framework worked well for 250 years, but it’s being dismantled by the Supreme Court that is granting itself and the executive branch more power at the expense of the legislative branch.”

The panel discussion was led by moderator The Nation journalist Elie Mystal and included panelists Nikolas Bowie, Louis D. Brandeis Professor of Law at Harvard Law School; Michele Goodwin, Linda D. & Timothy J. O’Neill Professor of Constitutional Law and Global Health Policy at Georgetown Law; and Maya Wiley, President/CEO at the Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights.
